VECTOR_SEARCH · “Current docs” (v3 index)

SELECT TOP (10) WITH APPROXIMATE t.id, s.distance
FROM VECTOR_SEARCH(TABLE = dbo.T AS t, COLUMN = Vec,
                   SIMILAR_TO = @qv, METRIC = 'cosine') AS s
WHERE t.CategoryID = 5     -- iterative filter
ORDER BY s.distance;
  • Returns columns from TABLE + distance (t.col, s.distance).
  • WITH APPROXIMATE requires ORDER BY distance ASC: without ORDER BY → Msg 42248; other columns or DESC → 42271; TOP_N → 42274.
  • Without APPROXIMATE → exact kNN; without TOP/ORDER BY → full scan; without a compatible index → warning + kNN.
  • Hint WITH (FORCE_ANN_ONLY) after the alias: requires index + TOP … WITH APPROXIMATE.
  • Not in views; window / GROUP BY / DISTINCT / UNION → subquery; CROSS APPLY → TOP inside the APPLY.

VECTOR_SEARCH · “Learn” (Jul 2026, previous index)

SELECT TOP 10 t.ProductID, s.distance
FROM VECTOR_SEARCH(TABLE = dbo.Products AS t, COLUMN = Vec,
                   SIMILAR_TO = @qv, METRIC = 'cosine',
                   TOP_N = 50) AS s
WHERE t.CategoryID = 5     -- filtered AFTER the 50
ORDER BY s.distance;
  • TOP_N = k (positive integer): deprecated in the docs; with a v3 index → Msg 42274.
  • Learn lab: PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON + ALLOW_STALE_VECTOR_INDEX = ON + TYPE = 'DISKANN' + TOP_N.
TopicLearn (Jul 2026)Current docs (Oct 2026)
ANN syntaxVECTOR_SEARCH(…, TOP_N = k)SELECT TOP (N) WITH APPROXIMATE … ORDER BY distance; TOP_N deprecated
DML / requirementsread-only table; clustered int PKv3: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE, ≥ 100 rows; read-only and int PK only in the previous one
WHERE filterpost-filteringv3: iterative
Status“currently in preview”GA Azure SQL DB / Fabric / MI AUP (Sep 29, 2026); Preview SQL Server 2025
BaseType / max. dim“always float”; 1,998also float16 (3,996)
BM25FREETEXTTABLE o CONTAINSTABLEonly FREETEXTTABLE

Hybrid + RRF

-- RRF(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d))
COALESCE(1.0 / (@k + ks.keyword_rank), 0.0)
+ COALESCE(1.0 / (@k + ss.vector_rank), 0.0) AS rrf_score
  1. Query embedding (same model as the data).
  2. Keyword CTE: FREETEXTTABLE → TOP (@topN) by [RANK] DESC → RANK(). Vector CTE: VECTOR_DISTANCE / VECTOR_SEARCH → TOP (@topN) by distance ASC → RANK().
  3. FULL OUTER JOIN + COALESCE(…, 0.0) → ORDER BY rrf_score DESC.
  • No native function; does not normalize scores (uses ranks); weight: 2.0 / (@k + vector_rank). Initial @topN 50; filters before the RRF.

Evaluate vector / hybrid search

  • Query set with known relevant results: full-text only, vector only and hybrid (hybrid: higher recall, little loss of precision, slower).
  • Precision = relevant results returned / results returned · Recall = relevant results returned / existing relevant results · MRR = mean of 1 / rank of the first relevant result · Recall@k (ANN) = |ANN ∩ exact| / k.
  • Cost: SET STATISTICS TIME, IO ON, actual plan, Query Store.
Memorize: 1,998 (float32) · 3,996 (float16) · header 8 B · page 8,060 B · cosine 0–2, dot negative · ENN < 50,000 vectors · index ≥ 100 rows (Msg 42266), only type DiskANN, ALTER on the table · RRF k = 60 (1/61 + 1/63 = 0.0323) · RANK 0–1000, BM25 only FREETEXTTABLE · errors 42266 / 42274 · PREVIEW_FEATURES default OFF, FULLTEXT_INDEX_VERSION default 2.
Learn vs docs and traps:
  • Question with TOP_N, read-only table or int PK → previous index (Learn); current Azure SQL DB / Fabric → v3 with TOP (N) WITH APPROXIMATE. Recognize both.
  • Only VECTOR_SEARCH uses the index (VECTOR_DISTANCE never does). Different metric or column → warning + kNN.
  • 1 / (60 + rank) with integers gives 0: use 1.0 /. TOP without ORDER BY (module CTE) returns arbitrary rows.

⚡ M11 · RAG with SQL — the essentials

RAG pattern in T-SQL

  • Retrieve → Augment → Generate; the LLM runs outside (Azure OpenAI): SQL only retrieves, formats, calls and parses
  • AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS → VECTOR_DISTANCE / VECTOR_SEARCH → FOR JSON → JSON_OBJECT + JSON_ARRAY → sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint → JSON_VALUE
  • 4 RAG signals (Learn): changing data · traceable answer · privacy (only the context per request) · domain questions
  • Grounding: rules in system; context + question in user

sys.sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint — signature

ParameterTypeDefault · values
@urlnvarchar(4000)required · HTTPS only
@payloadnvarchar(max)NULL · JSON / XML / text
@headersnvarchar(4000)NULL · flat JSON
@methodnvarchar(6)POST · GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE HEAD
@timeoutsmallint30 s · 1–230
@credentialsysnameNULL · DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL
@responsenvarchar(max) OUTPUTJSON envelope (or XML)
@retry_counttinyint0 · 0–10
  • Return value: 0 = HTTP 2xx · other = HTTP code · exception = call could not be made

Limits and rules

FOR JSON

FOR JSON { AUTO | PATH } [, ROOT('x')]
    [, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES] [, WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER]
  • AUTO: SELECT shape (1:N join → array with the alias of the child) · PATH: you define names with 'a.b'
  • NULLs omitted by default · unnamed ROOT = "root"
  • ROOT + WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER → Msg 13620; multiple rows + WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER = invalid JSON
  • 0 rows → NULL: ISNULL(@ctx, N'[]') · as a result set it is split into rows of 2033 chars
  • Lean context: TOP (3–5), LEFT(text, 400), without rowguid/IDs/dates

JSON_OBJECT · JSON_ARRAY · JSON_ARRAYAGG

JSON_OBJECT('k': v [, …] [NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL] [RETURNING json])
JSON_ARRAY(v [, …] [NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL] [RETURNING json])
JSON_ARRAYAGG(v [ORDER BY …] [NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL] [RETURNING json])
  • Default: OBJECT = NULL ON NULL · ARRAY and ARRAYAGG = ABSENT ON NULL
  • OBJECT/ARRAY: SQL Server 2022+ · ARRAYAGG: SQL Server 2025 (0 rows → NULL)
  • 'ctx': JSON_QUERY(@json) inserts an object/array unescaped; content is always a string
  • CAST(1 AS bit) → true · automatic escaping of " \ / and control characters

Chat completions payload (@payload)

{ "model": "<deployment>",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "system", "content": "reglas de grounding" },
    { "role": "user", "content": "<context>[…]</context> Question: …" } ],
  "max_completion_tokens": 800 }

  • Per deployment: /openai/deployments/<d>/chat/completions?api-version=2024-10-21 (without model; api-version required)
  • Roles system · user · assistant; developer = system in reasoning (do not mix)
  • temperature 0–2 (Learn: 0.3–0.5 = factual) · response_format: text | json_object | json_schema

@response and JSON_VALUE paths

{ "response": { "status": { "http": { "code": 200, "description": "OK" } }, "headers": {} },
  "result": { "choices": [ { "index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "…" } } ],
              "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0 } } }
  • $.result.choices[0].message.content (null if filtered) · .finish_reason: stop · length · content_filter · tool_calls · function_call
  • $.result.usage.total_tokens · $.result.error.message (non-2xx) · $.response.status.http.code
  • result is missing with HTTP 204 · with Accept: application/xml, @response is XML
  • JSON_VALUE = nvarchar(4000): > 4000 chars → NULL (lax) / Msg 13625 (strict) → OPENJSON … WITH (c nvarchar(max) '$.choices[0].message.content')
  • Incorrect: $.response.message.content · $.result.content

  • Msg 31643 option OFF · 8189 no permission · 31630 credential does not cover the URL · 31644 MI OFF · 11558 invalid JSON · 31629 timeout · 31610 not HTTPS

Module 1Domain 1 · 35–40%

Design and implement database objects with SQL

Tables (data types, sizes, columns, rowstore and columnstore indexes), specialized tables (in-memory, temporal, external, ledger, graph), JSON, constraints, SEQUENCE and partitioning in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL and SQL database in Fabric. Exact syntax, numeric limits and which feature exists on each platform are tested.

Skills measured covered:
  • Design and implement tables, including data types, size, columns, indexes, and column store indexes
  • Design and implement specialized tables, including in-memory, temporal, external, ledger, and graph
  • Design and implement JSON columns and indexes
  • Design and implement database constraints, including PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, and DEFAULT
  • Design and implement SEQUENCES
  • Design and implement partitioning for tables and indexes

SQL platforms: what to choose and which feature exists where SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric

Same T-SQL engine on all of them, but control (IaaS vs PaaS) and the available objects change. In PaaS, Azure manages hardware, OS, patches and engine; you design tables, indexes, constraints and data.

SQL Server (on-premises / Azure VM)

  • IaaS: control of OS, instance and version; maximum compatibility
  • SQL IaaS Agent extension: automatic backups and patches, Key Vault
  • Multiple filegroups and all instance features

Azure SQL Database

  • PaaS; General Purpose, Business Critical, Hyperscale tiers; serverless compute (autopause: use connection retries and avoid long transactions)
  • SLA 99.99%; only the PRIMARY filegroup; no cross-database queries (use elastic query) or SQL Agent (use elastic jobs)

Azure SQL Managed Instance

  • Nearly 100% compatibility with SQL Server Enterprise; engine always up to date
  • Instance features: SQL Server Agent, Service Broker, linked servers, cross-database (three-part names), Database Mail; native VNet
  • MI link (distributed AG) synchronizes SQL Server → Azure; update policy: SQL Server 2022 / SQL Server 2025 / Always-up-to-date

SQL database in Fabric

  • Azure SQL Database engine + automatic mirroring to OneLake (Delta Parquet) and a read-only SQL analytics endpoint
  • Microsoft Entra users only (no logins); only PRIMARY; CI/CD with SqlPackage and Git; GraphQL API

Memorize: SQL database in Fabric does NOT create in-memory tables, ledger (or its history) or Always Encrypted, and does not allow partition SWITCH. Azure SQL DB and Fabric: only the PRIMARY filegroup.

Data types and sizes: reference table GA

Choose the smallest type that covers the range and precision: it reduces storage, index size, backups and JOIN cost. Changing the type in production usually forces a table rebuild.

Numeric types

TypeSize / rangeNotes
tinyint · smallint1 byte (0–255) · 2 bytes (−32,768 to 32,767)tinyint is the only unsigned integer
int · bigint4 bytes (±2,147,483,647) · 8 bytes (−2^63 to 2^63−1)Typical surrogate key: int/bigint IDENTITY
decimal(p,s) = numeric5 B (p 1–9) · 9 B (p 10–19) · 13 B (p 20–28) · 17 B (p 29–38)p 1–38 (default 18); s 0–p (default 0). Each (p,s) is a different type. Exact: use it for money
money · smallmoney8 B · 4 B4 decimal places; truncation risk in calculations → use decimal with ≥ 4 decimal places
float(n) · realn 1–24 → 4 B, ~7 digits (real = float(24)) · n 25–53 → 8 B, ~15 digitsDefault n = 53. Approximate: avoid = and <>; not for financial data

Strings and collations

TypeSizeNotes
char(n) · varchar(n)n = bytes, 1–8,000; varchar takes data + 2 Bvarchar(max) up to 2 GB. Default length: 1 when declared, 30 in CAST/CONVERT
nchar(n) · nvarchar(n)n = byte pairs, 1–4,000; takes 2n B (+2 B in nvarchar)UTF-16: a supplementary character uses 4 B (fewer than n fit). Unicode literals with the N'…' prefix
_UTF8 collationE.g. Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8char/varchar store full Unicode in UTF-8: ASCII 1 B, 128–2047 2 B, 2048–65535 3 B, the rest 4 B. Best for ASCII/Latin; East Asian text takes 3 B (UTF-16: 2 B). SQL Server 2019+, Azure SQL, Fabric SQL DB
varchar(max) / nvarchar(max)Each non-null column adds 24 B of fixed allocationThey count against the 8,060 B limit in sorts and clustered key updates (error 512)

Date/time and other types

TypeSizeNotes
date3 B0001-01-01 a 9999-12-31
time(p)3 B (p 0–2) · 4 B (p 3–4) · 5 B (p 5–7, default 7)100 ns precision
smalldatetime · datetime4 B · 8 Bsmalldatetime: 1900-01-01 to 2079-06-06, 1 minute. datetime: from 1753, rounds to .000/.003/.007 s (legacy)
datetime2(p)6 B (p < 3) · 7 B (p 3–4) · 8 B (p 5–7)p 0–7, default 7. No time zone. Type of PERIOD columns
datetimeoffset(p)8 B (p 0–2) · 9 B (p 3–4) · 10 B (p 5–7, default)Stores the offset −14:00 to +14:00; is not aware of time zones or DST
uniqueidentifier16 BNEWID() random; NEWSEQUENTIALID() only in DEFAULT. Only comparisons and IS NULL
rowversion (timestamp)8 BBinary counter per database, one column per table; not a date/time; timestamp is a deprecated synonym in DDL
varbinary(max) · xml · jsonUp to 2 GBtext, ntext, image are deprecated → varchar(max), nvarchar(max), varbinary(max)
Exam: float for money ✗ → decimal. Random GUID as clustered key ✗ (16 B, fragmentation) → int/bigint IDENTITY, SEQUENCE or NEWSEQUENTIALID(). datetime2 over datetime; multi-time-zone data → datetimeoffset.
Memorize: decimal 5-9-13-17 B (p ≤ 9/19/28/38) · datetime2 6-7-8 B · datetimeoffset 8-9-10 B · varchar n = bytes, nvarchar n = byte pairs.
Learn vs Docs: the Learn estimation example annotates Salary DECIMAL(10,2) -- 5 bytes; this is incorrect: DECIMAL(10,2) uses 9 bytes (5 B only up to p = 9). Learn also lists IMAGE as a recommended binary type, but it is deprecated.

Columns: IDENTITY, computed, SPARSE and row size GA

CREATE TABLE dbo.Product
(
    ProductID   int IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,            -- (seed, increment): both or neither
    ProductGuid uniqueidentifier NOT NULL
        CONSTRAINT DF_Product_Guid DEFAULT NEWSEQUENTIALID(),
    Name        nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,
    Price       decimal(10,2) NOT NULL,
    Qty         int NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_Product_Qty DEFAULT 0,
    Total       AS (Price * Qty) PERSISTED,            -- computed and stored
    Notes       nvarchar(400) SPARSE NULL,             -- SPARSE: always nullable
    RowVer      rowversion,                            -- one per table
    CONSTRAINT PK_Product PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (ProductID)
);
PropertyVerified rules
IDENTITY [(seed, increment)]Default (1,1); both or neither are specified; one per table; the property cannot be removed. In memory-optimized: only (1,1). Does not guarantee uniqueness (use PK/UNIQUE), consecutive values or absence of gaps (rollback, failure, restart, cache); values are not reused
Computed columnVirtual unless PERSISTED [NOT NULL]. Indexable if deterministic and precise (PERSISTED extends this to imprecise/CLR). Does not accept DEFAULT; CHECK, FOREIGN KEY and NOT NULL require PERSISTED (error 8183; the doc says “nor FOREIGN KEY”, but an FK on a PERSISTED column was created without error in SQL Server 2025). Cannot be the target of INSERT/UPDATE. Requires SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON when indexing
SPARSESaves space on NULLs (consider it if the savings are ≥ 20–40%); costs more for non-null values. Must be nullable; no DEFAULT, IDENTITY or ROWGUIDCOL; not in a clustered key or PK; incompatible with compression; not text/ntext/image/timestamp/UDT/geometry/geography. Column set: XML COLUMN_SET FOR ALL_SPARSE_COLUMNS
NEWSEQUENTIALID()Only as the DEFAULT of uniqueidentifier; cannot be combined with other operators. Predictable → do not use if privacy matters

Table and row limits

LimitValueNotes
Columns per table1,024Up to 30,000 with column sets
Bytes per row8,060varchar/nvarchar/varbinary/sql_variant/CLR can overflow to ROW_OVERFLOW_DATA (the widest first), leaving a 24 B pointer; each ≤ 8,000 B. char, int… must fit in 8,060 B including ~7 B of overhead (error 1701: char(8000) + char(53) fits; + char(54) does not)
LOB ((max), xml)Exempt from 8,060In-row if they fit; otherwise, a 16 B pointer to LOB_DATA (table option large value types out of row)
Extent8 contiguous pagesAllocation unit
Exam: “I need the number before the INSERT, to share it across tables, to restart it or to reserve ranges” → SEQUENCE; “simple auto-number for one table” → IDENTITY. “Many columns almost always NULL” → SPARSE.
Watch out: a clustered index key cannot contain a varchar with data already in ROW_OVERFLOW_DATA; an INSERT/UPDATE that pushes the data off-row fails.

Rowstore indexes: clustered, nonclustered, unique, filtered, covering GA

CREATE [ UNIQUE ] [ CLUSTERED | NONCLUSTERED ] INDEX index_name
    ON <object> ( column [ ASC | DESC ] [ ,...n ] )
    [ INCLUDE ( column_name [ ,...n ] ) ]
    [ WHERE <filter_predicate> ]
    [ WITH ( <relational_index_option> [ ,...n ] ) ]
    [ ON { partition_scheme_name ( column_name ) | filegroup_name | "default" } ];
-- Covering: the query is resolved without a key lookup
CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Product_Category
    ON dbo.Product (Category) INCLUDE (ProductName, Price)
    WITH (FILLFACTOR = 90, PAD_INDEX = ON, DATA_COMPRESSION = PAGE);

-- Filtered + unique: "UNIQUE" that allows many NULLs
CREATE UNIQUE NONCLUSTERED INDEX UX_Customer_Email
    ON dbo.Customer (Email) WHERE Email IS NOT NULL;
CriterionClusteredNonclustered
LeafFull row (defines the physical order)Only keys + INCLUDE + row locator (clustered key or RID)
Per table1 (without it, the table is a heap)Up to 999 (includes the PK/UNIQUE ones)
Maximum key size900 bytes1,700 bytes (before 2016: 900)
Created implicitly withPRIMARY KEY (if there is no other clustered)UNIQUE constraint
Use it forMain access path, ranges, narrow/static/increasing keySelective lookups, joins, query coverage

Rules and limits

  • Key: up to 32 columns; INCLUDE columns do not count. Cannot be key columns: ntext, text, image, varchar(max), nvarchar(max), varbinary(max), xml, json. INCLUDE accepts everything except text/ntext/image.
  • Ideal clustered key: narrow, unique, static, increasing. If it is not unique, the engine adds a 4 B uniqueifier; a GUID takes 16 B.
  • Filtered: nonclustered only; simple predicates joined with AND (=, <>, IS [NOT] NULL, IN, <, >…); no computed columns/UDT/spatial/hierarchyid; use IS NULL, not = NULL; does not support IGNORE_DUP_KEY.
  • Create the clustered index first: creating it rebuilds the existing nonclustered ones. CREATE INDEX … ON partition_scheme on a clustered index moves the table.
  • Without ON, the index of a partitioned table is aligned with it. Creating/rebuilding non-aligned indexes with > 1,000 partitions is possible but not supported.

Options (WITH) and defaults

OptionDefaultNotes
PAD_INDEXOFFApplies FILLFACTOR to intermediate pages; only useful with FILLFACTOR
FILLFACTOR0 (= 100)1–100; only when creating/rebuilding (not maintained); < 100 increases space usage
SORT_IN_TEMPDBOFFIn Hyperscale always ON except resumable; not supported with RESUMABLE
IGNORE_DUP_KEYOFFON: only the duplicate rows are rejected (warning). Not on non-unique indexes, filtered indexes or views
DROP_EXISTINGOFFAllows nonclustered → clustered; not clustered → nonclustered (error 1925). The doc does not allow CCI → rowstore either, but in SQL Server 2025 CCI → clustered rowstore did work (CCI → nonclustered did not)
ONLINEOFFON: only IS in the main phase; Sch-M when creating/dropping a clustered index or rebuilding. In SQL Server it depends on the edition
RESUMABLE / MAX_DURATIONOFFRequires ONLINE = ON. CREATE INDEX: SQL Server 2019+; ALTER INDEX … REBUILD: 2017+. MAX_DURATION > 0 and ≤ 10,080 min
ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS / ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKSONWith page locks OFF, REORGANIZE is not possible
OPTIMIZE_FOR_SEQUENTIAL_KEYOFF2019+; reduces PAGELATCH_EX contention on the last page
MAXDOP0Maximum 64; 1 suppresses parallelism
DATA_COMPRESSION—NONE | ROW | PAGE (rowstore); COLUMNSTORE | COLUMNSTORE_ARCHIVE (columnstore). Each nonclustered index has its own compression
 
ALTER INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product
    REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON (WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY (MAX_DURATION = 5 MINUTES, ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS)));

ALTER INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product
    REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON, RESUMABLE = ON, MAX_DURATION = 240 MINUTES);
ALTER INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product PAUSE;
ALTER INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product RESUME WITH (MAXDOP = 4);
ALTER INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product ABORT;   -- cannot be resumed afterwards
Exam: “avoid key lookups” → INCLUDE (covering). “Index only a subset of rows / unique with NULL” → filtered. “Rebuild without blocking” → ONLINE = ON; “pause and resume” → RESUMABLE = ON. ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = NONE | SELF | BLOCKERS (BLOCKERS requires ALTER ANY CONNECTION; SELF not with MAX_DURATION = 0).
Watch out: RESUMABLE does not apply to ALTER INDEX REBUILD ALL, ALTER TABLE REBUILD, columnstore, filtered or disabled indexes, or inside an explicit transaction. WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY in CREATE INDEX: SQL Server 2022+ and Azure SQL.
Memorize: 900 B (clustered) · 1,700 B (nonclustered) · 32 key columns · 999 nonclustered · FILLFACTOR 0 = 100.
Sources: Learn · Optimize with indexes · Docs · CREATE INDEX · Docs · ALTER INDEX · Docs · Index design guide · Docs · Maximum capacity

Columnstore indexes: CCI, NCCI, ordered and archive GA Azure SQL: all tiers except Basic and Standard < S3

CriterionClustered columnstore (CCI)Nonclustered columnstore (NCCI)
RolePrimary storage for the ENTIRE table (replaces the clustered rowstore)Secondary columnar copy of selected columns on a rowstore table
ScenarioDW fact tables, historical data, reportingReal-time operational analytics on OLTP (rowstore + NCCI)
Per table11 per rowstore table; supports WHERE (filtered)
IntegrityPK/UNIQUE/FK are enforced with rowstore indexes (B-tree NCIs can be added)The base rowstore table keeps PK/UNIQUE
Restrictions—≤ 1,024 columns; no INCLUDE, ASC/DESC or SPARSE columns; no LOB (max); not constraint-based
ConceptValue
Maximum rows per rowgroup1,048,576; each column is compressed separately (column segment)
Direct bulk load to columnstoreBatches of ≥ 102,400 rows; fewer rows (or the final remainder) go to the deltastore
Delta rowgroupTemporary clustered B-tree; becomes CLOSED upon reaching 1,048,576 rows; the tuple-mover compresses the CLOSED ones. Since SQL Server 2019 / Azure SQL, a background merge task compresses old OPEN deltas and merges rowgroups with many deleted rows
States (state_desc)INVISIBLE (0) · OPEN (1) · CLOSED (2) · COMPRESSED (3) · TOMBSTONE (4)
DELETE / UPDATEDELETE in columnstore = logical delete (space freed on reorganize/rebuild); UPDATE = logical delete + INSERT into delta
MaintenanceREORGANIZE (online) physically removes the deleted rows from a rowgroup with ≥ 10% deleted and merges rowgroups; COMPRESS_ALL_ROW_GROUPS = ON forces OPEN and CLOSED ones into the columnstore
CompressionCOLUMNSTORE (default) · COLUMNSTORE_ARCHIVE (smaller, slower; archival) · COMPRESSION_DELAY default 0 min · cannot be combined with ROW/PAGE
 
CREATE CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX CCI_SalesHistory ON dbo.SalesHistory;

CREATE NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX NCCI_Orders
    ON dbo.Orders (OrderDate, Amount, Region)
    WHERE OrderDate >= '2025-01-01'                 -- filtered NCCI
    WITH (COMPRESSION_DELAY = 10 MINUTES);

-- Ordered CCI (SQL Server 2022+; ordered NCCI: SQL Server 2025+ and Azure SQL)
CREATE CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX CCI_SalesHistory
    ON dbo.SalesHistory ORDER (SaleDate) WITH (DROP_EXISTING = ON, MAXDOP = 1);

ALTER INDEX CCI_SalesHistory ON dbo.SalesHistory
    REORGANIZE WITH (COMPRESS_ALL_ROW_GROUPS = ON);
ALTER INDEX CCI_SalesHistory ON dbo.SalesHistory REBUILD
    WITH (DATA_COMPRESSION = COLUMNSTORE_ARCHIVE);   -- archival

SELECT OBJECT_NAME(object_id) AS tbl, state_desc, total_rows, deleted_rows, size_in_bytes
FROM sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats
WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('dbo.SalesHistory');

Option availability by version

OptionCCINCCI
COMPRESSION_DELAY, DATA_COMPRESSIONSQL Server 2016SQL Server 2016
WHERE (filtered)n/aSQL Server 2016
ONLINESQL Server 2019SQL Server 2017
ORDERSQL Server 2022SQL Server 2025
Exam: fact table with millions of rows + aggregations → CCI. Analytics on an OLTP table without changing its schema → NCCI. Small table (< 1 M rows), frequent updates/deletes or single-row lookups → rowstore.
Learn vs Docs: Learn says the tuple-mover compresses a delta rowgroup with “at least 102,400” rows. In Docs, 102,400 is the minimum size of a bulk load batch to compress directly; the delta rowgroup closes at 1,048,576. Learn recommends REBUILD to improve compression; since SQL Server 2016, REORGANIZE is usually enough. In Fabric SQL DB the CCI is created with the table (otherwise, error 35354 with Change Feed). Syntax verified on SQL Server 2025: the CCI accepts ORDER (…) WITH (…) and rejects WITH (…) ORDER (…) (Msg 156); the doc grammar for SQL Server lists WITH before ORDER (looks like a doc error). NCCI: ORDER → WHERE → WITH; only 1 columnstore index per table (error 35339).
Memorize: 1,048,576 (rowgroup) · 102,400 (direct bulk minimum) · 10% deleted (REORGANIZE cleans the rowgroup) · states OPEN→CLOSED→COMPRESSED (+TOMBSTONE).
Sources: Learn · Optimize with indexes · Docs · Columnstore indexes overview · Docs · CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX · Docs · ALTER INDEX · Docs · sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats

In-memory OLTP: memory-optimized tables SQL Server Azure SQL DB Premium/BC · MI BC Fabric

Data lives in RAM with optimistic concurrency (no locks or latches); the log on disk provides durability. It is accessed with interpreted T-SQL or natively compiled procedures. Ideal for: session state, cache, staging/ETL, high-throughput OLTP.

-- SQL Server only: one MEMORY_OPTIMIZED_DATA filegroup per database
ALTER DATABASE imoltp ADD FILEGROUP imoltp_mod CONTAINS MEMORY_OPTIMIZED_DATA;
ALTER DATABASE imoltp ADD FILE (NAME = 'imoltp_mod1', FILENAME = 'C:\data\imoltp_mod1') TO FILEGROUP imoltp_mod;   -- FILENAME = folder (container)
GO
USE imoltp;
GO

CREATE TABLE dbo.SessionState
(
    SessionId int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED HASH WITH (BUCKET_COUNT = 1000000),
    UserId    int NOT NULL,
    LastSeen  datetime2 NOT NULL,
    INDEX IX_UserId NONCLUSTERED (UserId)
) WITH (MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON, DURABILITY = SCHEMA_ONLY);
-- CREATE PROCEDURE must be the 1st statement in the batch:
GO

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.usp_TouchSession @SessionId int, @LastSeen datetime2
WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING
AS BEGIN ATOMIC WITH (TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL = SNAPSHOT, LANGUAGE = N'us_english')
    UPDATE dbo.SessionState SET LastSeen = @LastSeen WHERE SessionId = @SessionId;
END;
Option / ruleValue
DURABILITY = SCHEMA_AND_DATA (default)Durable schema and data (log + data/delta files); requires PRIMARY KEY; with delayed durability recent commits can be lost in a crash
DURABILITY = SCHEMA_ONLYOnly the schema persists; data is lost on restart or failover; no data I/O → sessions, staging, temp
IndexesEvery table needs ≥ 1 index (explicit or via PK/UNIQUE). PK/UNIQUE must be NONCLUSTERED or NONCLUSTERED HASH. Up to 999 per table (2017+ and Azure SQL; previously 8). Nonclustered key ≤ 2,500 B declared
Rows, IDENTITY8,060 B in-row; LOB and large columns go off-row since 2016 (8 B pointer). IDENTITY only (1,1)
Requirements and quotas64-bit; SQL Server 2016 SP1+ in all editions (Standard: 32 GB per DB; Express: 352 MB per DB). One memory-optimized filegroup per DB (since SQL Server 2025 it can be removed). Azure SQL: XTP quota per service objective → out-of-quota error if exceeded
Native modulesWITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING and BEGIN ATOMIC with TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL and LANGUAGE required; schema-qualified objects and no SELECT *
CriterionHash indexNonclustered (memory-optimized)
Equality seekYes, but needs equality on ALL the key columnsYes, does not require the full key
Ranges, inequality, ORDER BYNo (scan)Yes
BUCKET_COUNT≈ 1–2× distinct key values; rounded up to the next power of 2 (1 – 1,073,741,824; required for hash)—
Many duplicatesBad if rows/unique ≥ 10 (long chains)Best option
Monitoring / recommendationsys.dm_db_xtp_hash_index_stats: avg_chain_length ideal 1 (up to 10 acceptable); ~33% of buckets empty when the count equals the distinct valuesRecommended as a starting point when migrating
Exam: temporary/session data that can be lost → SCHEMA_ONLY; data that cannot be lost → SCHEMA_AND_DATA. Point lookups by key → hash; ranges/ordering → nonclustered. Dataset larger than RAM → do not use in-memory.
Learn vs Docs: Learn says memory-optimized tables do not support VARCHAR(MAX)/NVARCHAR(MAX)/VARBINARY(MAX); the current doc does support them (SQL Server 2016+, off-row; verified on SQL Server 2025: they are created without error). Not supported (error on create): datetimeoffset, geography, geometry, hierarchyid, json, rowversion, sql_variant, vector, xml, text/ntext/image and UDT. Also unsupported: compression, partitioning, or being a MERGE target (error 10794); indexes are added with ALTER TABLE … ADD INDEX (CREATE INDEX does not work). Azure SQL: not available in General Purpose/Standard/Basic (you cannot scale or restore to them with in-memory objects).
Sources: Learn · Use specialized table types · Docs · Memory-optimized tables · Docs · Indexes for memory-optimized tables · Docs · Hash indexes · Docs · Data types · Docs · Memory-optimized filegroup · Docs · Natively compiled procedures · Docs · In-memory in MI

Temporal tables (system-versioned) SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL Fabric GA

CREATE TABLE dbo.Employee
(
    EmployeeID int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED,          -- PK required
    Salary     decimal(10,2) NOT NULL,
    ValidFrom  datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START HIDDEN NOT NULL,
    ValidTo    datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END   HIDDEN NOT NULL,
    PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (ValidFrom, ValidTo)
)
WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_TABLE = dbo.EmployeeHistory,
                              HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD = 6 MONTHS));
ALTER TABLE dbo.InsurancePolicy ADD
    ValidFrom datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START HIDDEN
        CONSTRAINT DF_Policy_From DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME(),
    ValidTo   datetime2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END HIDDEN
        CONSTRAINT DF_Policy_To DEFAULT CONVERT(datetime2, '9999-12-31 23:59:59.9999999'),
    PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (ValidFrom, ValidTo);
ALTER TABLE dbo.InsurancePolicy SET (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_TABLE = History.InsurancePolicy));

SELECT * FROM dbo.Employee FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF '2025-01-01T00:00:00' WHERE EmployeeID = 1;  -- UTC
ALTER TABLE dbo.Employee SET (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD = 9 MONTHS));
ALTER DATABASE [MyDb] SET TEMPORAL_HISTORY_RETENTION ON;
FOR SYSTEM_TIME clauseRows returned
AS OF tValidFrom <= t AND ValidTo > t
FROM a TO bValidFrom < b AND ValidTo > a (excludes those that start exactly at b)
BETWEEN a AND bValidFrom <= b AND ValidTo > a (includes those that start at b)
CONTAINED IN (a, b)ValidFrom >= a AND ValidTo <= b (opened and closed within the range)
ALLUnion of current + history

Rules, retention and limits

  • PK required; exactly one PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME with two datetime2 columns (ROW START/ROW END) always NOT NULL (declaring them NULL fails). Values in UTC = start of the transaction. HIDDEN avoids breaking SELECT * and INSERT without a column list.
  • History: same schema (number, names, order and types), same DB, schema-qualified name (HISTORY_TABLE = schema.table). Anonymous: MSSQL_TemporalHistoryFor_<object_id>, rowstore with PAGE compression and a clustered index (end, start). Custom: cannot have PK, FK, unique, constraints or triggers; for analytics use clustered columnstore.
  • HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD = n { DAYS | WEEKS | MONTHS | YEARS }; default INFINITE. Requires the DB flag is_temporal_history_retention_enabled (ON; it switches to OFF after a point-in-time restore) and a history table with a clustered rowstore that starts with the period-end column, or a clustered columnstore. Cleanup in batches of up to 10,000 rows. SYSTEM_VERSIONING = OFF does not keep the retention period.
  • Cleanup alternatives: partitioning (sliding window), a custom script (with SYSTEM_VERSIONING = OFF).
  • No TRUNCATE TABLE with versioning ON; no INSTEAD OF triggers (AFTER only on the current table); INSERT/UPDATE cannot reference the PERIOD columns; no FILESTREAM/FileTable; node/edge tables cannot be temporal; ALTER COLUMN is not online; FOR SYSTEM_TIME does not work over linked servers or external tables; partitioning is not copied to the history table (it uses the default filegroup).
  • When converting a table: the start DEFAULT cannot be in the future; the end DEFAULT = the maximum datetime2 value with the same precision; DATA_CONSISTENCY_CHECK validates the data (OFF skips it).
Exam: “automatic history / auditing / value at a past date / revert changes / SCD type 2 without triggers” → temporal. Cost: ~double the storage.
Memorize: GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START/END + PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME + SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON. FROM…TO excludes the upper bound; BETWEEN…AND includes it.
Sources: Learn · Use specialized table types · Docs · Temporal tables · Docs · Create a system-versioned temporal table · Docs · Manage retention · Docs · Considerations and limitations

External tables and data virtualization SQL Server 2022/2025 Azure SQL DB Preview MI Fabric Preview

They query data where it lives (lake, blob, other DBs) without moving it; read-only. Order: master key (if there is a SECRET) → credential → external data source → external file format → external table.

CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL LakeCred WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity';   -- without SECRET: no master key required
-- SAS: WITH IDENTITY = 'SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE', SECRET = 'sv=...'  (without the leading '?'; Read + List permissions)

CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE LakeSource
WITH (LOCATION = 'abs://container@account.blob.core.windows.net/sales', CREDENTIAL = LakeCred);

CREATE EXTERNAL FILE FORMAT ParquetFF WITH (FORMAT_TYPE = PARQUET);

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dbo.ExternalSales
(OrderID int, CustomerID int, OrderAmount decimal(10,2), OrderDate date)
WITH (LOCATION = 'year=*/month=*/*.parquet', DATA_SOURCE = LakeSource, FILE_FORMAT = ParquetFF);
CriterionSQL Server 2022/2025Azure SQL DatabaseAzure SQL MISQL database in Fabric
Mechanism / statusPolyBase / data virtualization (GA)Data virtualization and elastic query (Preview)Data virtualization (GA); CETAS disabled by defaultData virtualization (Preview)
Sources (LOCATION)abs://, adls://, s3://, sqlserver://, oracle://, teradata://, mongodb://, odbc:// (HDFS retired as of 2022)abs://, adls://; other DBs with TYPE = RDBMS (elastic query)abs://, adls://OneLake only (abfss://…dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/…)
Formats (FORMAT_TYPE)DELIMITEDTEXT, PARQUET, DELTA (1.0); ORC and RCFILE no longer apply as of 2022 (Hadoop only, retired)CSV, PARQUET, DELTA (1.0)PARQUET, CSVPARQUET, CSV
AuthenticationCredential (SAS, S3 key; managed identity with Azure Arc in 2025)Managed Identity, SAS, User IdentityManaged Identity, SASMicrosoft Entra pass-through (Lakehouse access)
  • SQL Server 2022+: PolyBase is no longer needed for Parquet, Delta, ABS, ADLS and S3, but it is still needed for Oracle, Teradata, MongoDB and ODBC (sp_configure 'polybase enabled'). SQL Server 2025: CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE … (LOCATION, CONNECTION_OPTIONS, CREDENTIAL, PUSHDOWN = ON | OFF), without TYPE.
  • The https:// prefix = bulk operations only (BULK INSERT / OPENROWSET (BULK …) with SAS), not external tables; in MI the generic https:// is disabled. Folder LOCATION: in Azure SQL DB/MI it does not traverse subfolders (SQL Server/PolyBase does by default); in all of them, hidden folders and files that start with _ or . are ignored; wildcards are supported.
  • Azure SQL/Fabric: read-only (SQL Server exports with CETAS after enabling allow polybase export): no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE or DEFAULT; allowed DDL: CREATE/DROP TABLE, STATISTICS and VIEW. Columns must match the files (otherwise, rows are rejected). No geography, geometry, hierarchyid, image, text, ntext, xml, json or UDT in Azure SQL/Fabric.
  • Non-deterministic results; no parallelism in elastic query; no RLS. Fabric: row ≤ 1 MB; CSV is queried with a schema-qualified name.
  • Permissions for CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE: CREATE TABLE, ALTER ANY SCHEMA, ALTER ANY EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE, ALTER ANY EXTERNAL FILE FORMAT; ALTER ANY EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE grants access to all the credentials in the DB.
CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE RemoteRef
WITH (TYPE = RDBMS, LOCATION = 'remoteserver.database.windows.net',
      DATABASE_NAME = 'RemoteDb', CREDENTIAL = RemoteCred);
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dbo.CustomerInformation
(CustomerID int NOT NULL, CustomerName varchar(50) NOT NULL)
WITH (DATA_SOURCE = RemoteRef);   -- SCHEMA_NAME / OBJECT_NAME map to a different remote name
Exam: “query Parquet/CSV in the lake without ETL” → external table + data virtualization; “query another Azure SQL Database” → elastic query (TYPE = RDBMS); “import the data” → SELECT INTO from the external table.
Watch out: elastic query in SHARD_MAP_MANAGER mode loses support on Mar 31, 2027. In Azure SQL DB, CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE AS SELECT is not available. The Learn example (LOCATION = '/raw/sales/', ParquetFormat) is generic: in Azure SQL use abs:///adls://; in Fabric, abfss:// to OneLake.

Ledger tables SQL Server 2022+ Azure SQL DB MI Fabric

Tamper-evident tables: each modified row is hashed (SHA-256) into a Merkle tree per transaction and the transactions are chained into blocks (blockchain). A digest is the hash of the last block saved in trusted storage; verifying recalculates the hashes and compares them with the digests. Both the table and the database can be ledger; a ledger table cannot be reverted to a regular table.

Updatable ledger table

  • INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; previous versions move to a history table
  • It is system-versioned: SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON + LEDGER = ON (does not require PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME; it can also be temporal)
  • 4 GENERATED ALWAYS columns: ledger_start/end_transaction_id and ledger_start/end_sequence_number
  • Anonymous history: MSSQL_LedgerHistoryFor_<GUID> according to the doc (SQL Server 2025 generates MSSQL_LedgerHistoryFor_<object_id>)

Append-only ledger table

  • INSERT only; no history table
  • LEDGER = ON (APPEND_ONLY = ON)
  • 2 columns: ledger_start_transaction_id and ledger_start_sequence_number
  • Ideal for SIEM, access logs or blockchain replica
CREATE SCHEMA [Account];                -- the schemas must exist
GO
CREATE SCHEMA [AccessControl];
GO
CREATE TABLE [Account].[Balance]      -- updatable
(CustomerID int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED, Balance decimal(10,2) NOT NULL)
WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_TABLE = [Account].[BalanceHistory]), LEDGER = ON);

CREATE TABLE [AccessControl].[KeyCardEvents]   -- append-only: APPEND_ONLY goes INSIDE the parentheses
(EmployeeID int NOT NULL, [Timestamp] datetime2 NOT NULL)
WITH (LEDGER = ON (APPEND_ONLY = ON));

CREATE DATABASE MyLedgerDB WITH LEDGER = ON;   -- irreversible; every new table = updatable ledger without writing WITH (…); LEDGER = OFF → error 37420

-- History: query the ledger view (not the history table) and join with the transaction
SELECT t.commit_time, t.principal_name, l.CustomerID, l.Balance, l.ledger_operation_type_desc
FROM [Account].[Balance_Ledger] AS l
JOIN sys.database_ledger_transactions AS t ON t.transaction_id = l.ledger_transaction_id;

EXECUTE sp_generate_database_ledger_digest;    -- manual digest (JSON) and closes the current block

DECLARE @digest_locations nvarchar(max) =
  (SELECT * FROM sys.database_ledger_digest_locations FOR JSON AUTO, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES);
EXECUTE sys.sp_verify_database_ledger_from_digest_storage @digest_locations;   -- requires configured digest storage (otherwise, @locations NULL → error 37365)
-- With your own digest: EXECUTE sp_verify_database_ledger N'[ ...digest JSON... ]';   -- both require snapshot isolation on the DB (Msg 37498)
ConceptDetails
Ledger view<table>_Ledger by default (LEDGER_VIEW = schema.view customizes it): ledger_transaction_id, ledger_sequence_number, ledger_operation_type (1 = INSERT, 2 = DELETE; an UPDATE = DELETE + INSERT) and _desc
Database ledgersys.database_ledger_transactions (user and commit time) and sys.database_ledger_blocks (Merkle root + hash of the previous block). A block is closed ≈ every 30 s with automatic digest storage (if there were transactions), when a manual digest is generated, or on reaching 100 K transactions
Where to store digestsAzure Blob with a locked immutability policy (container sqldbledgerdigests; no LRS accounts) or Azure Confidential Ledger (stronger guarantee against privileged admins). SQL Server 2022: Azure Storage only (manual container + SAS credential). Azure SQL: the server/MI identity needs Storage Blob Data Contributor (Blob) or Contributor (Confidential Ledger)
PermissionsIn the catalog: ENABLE LEDGER (create ledger tables/DB), ALTER LEDGER, ALTER LEDGER CONFIGURATION (digest storage) and VIEW LEDGER CONTENT (view the ledger and run sp_verify_database_ledger). sp_generate_database_ledger_digest is executable by public; the digest management doc cites a “GENERATE LEDGER DIGEST” permission that does not exist in sys.fn_builtin_permissions
LimitsAn existing table cannot be converted (data must be migrated); no TRUNCATE, in-memory, sparse column sets, partition SWITCH, graph, FileTable or full-text; no xml, sql_variant, UDT, FILESTREAM, vector or json (error 37379 in SQL Server 2025); no nonclustered rowstore index when there is a clustered columnstore (error 37439); a transaction can update ≤ 200 ledger tables; added columns count toward the 1,024; old data is not deleted (neither from append-only tables nor from history)
Exam: “cryptographic proof that not even a DBA altered the data” → ledger. Need auditable UPDATE/DELETE → updatable; only immutable inserts → append-only. Ledger ≠ temporal: temporal lets you query the past but is not tamper-evident; an updatable ledger can be both.
Memorize: updatable = SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON + LEDGER = ON (4 columns, history + view) · append-only = LEDGER = ON (APPEND_ONLY = ON) (2 columns) · verify with digests in immutable storage.
Learn vs Docs: Learn shows WITH (LEDGER = ON) for the updatable one and WITH (LEDGER = ON, APPEND_ONLY = ON) for the append-only one. Tested on SQL Server 2025: the first fails (Msg 37349: LEDGER = ON requires SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON, even inside a ledger database) and the second is a syntax error (Msg 102). Correct: WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON, LEDGER = ON) and WITH (LEDGER = ON (APPEND_ONLY = ON)); only in a ledger database can you omit the WITH entirely.
Sources: Learn · Use specialized table types · Docs · Ledger overview · Docs · Updatable ledger tables · Docs · Append-only ledger tables · Docs · Database ledger · Docs · Digest management · Docs · Verify a ledger database · Docs · Ledger limitations

Graph tables: node and edge SQL Server 2017+ Azure SQL DB MI Fabric

They model many-to-many relationships and variable-depth hierarchies (“friends of friends”). There is one graph per database (all its node + edge tables, in any schema). They are regular tables (indexes, constraints, MERGE, columnstore) with generated pseudo-columns: node → $node_id; edge → $edge_id, $from_id, $to_id (displayed as JSON; internally graph_id_<hex>).

CREATE TABLE Person     (ID int PRIMARY KEY, name varchar(100)) AS NODE;
CREATE TABLE Restaurant (ID int PRIMARY KEY, name varchar(100)) AS NODE;
CREATE TABLE likes (rating int) AS EDGE;          -- without attributes: CREATE TABLE friendOf AS EDGE;

INSERT INTO Person VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob');          -- $node_id is generated automatically
INSERT INTO Restaurant VALUES (1, 'Taco Dream');
INSERT INTO likes                                            -- edge: $from_id, $to_id, attributes
VALUES ((SELECT $node_id FROM Person WHERE ID = 1), (SELECT $node_id FROM Restaurant WHERE ID = 1), 9);

SELECT p.name, r.name, l.rating
FROM Person AS p, likes AS l, Restaurant AS r
WHERE MATCH(p-(l)->r) AND p.name = 'Alice';
CREATE TABLE bought
(
    PurchaseCount int,
    CONSTRAINT EC_BOUGHT CONNECTION (Customer TO Product, Supplier TO Product) ON DELETE NO ACTION
) AS EDGE;                                                   -- ON DELETE NO ACTION (default) | CASCADE

SELECT Person1.name, STRING_AGG(Person2.name, '->') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Friends
FROM Person AS Person1, friendOf FOR PATH AS fo, Person FOR PATH AS Person2
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(Person1(-(fo)->Person2){1,3})) AND Person1.name = 'Jacob';
TopicRule
MATCHOnly in the WHERE clause; combined only with AND (no OR/NOT). Directions a-(e)->b and a<-(e)-b; an edge alias cannot be repeated within the same MATCH
SHORTEST_PATH (2019+)Only inside MATCH; returns one shortest path (not all of them). Path tables with FOR PATH; + pattern (1 or more, up to the shortest) or {1,n}; projection with STRING_AGG/COUNT/LAST_VALUE … WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH); LAST_NODE() chains patterns
Edge constraints (2019+)CONNECTION (A TO B [, C TO D]): clauses within one constraint = OR; several constraints = AND (to widen the allowed pairs, create a new one with all the clauses and drop the old one). ON DELETE NO ACTION | CASCADE. Without an edge constraint, nothing prevents orphan edges and there is no cascading delete
IndexesIf you do not create a unique constraint/index on $node_id/$edge_id, an automatic unique nonclustered index is created. In OLTP an index on ($from_id, $to_id) is recommended. Metadata: sys.tables.is_node / is_edge
LimitsThey cannot be temp tables, table types/variables, system-versioned temporal or memory-optimized (nor ledger); UPDATE of $from_id/$to_id is not allowed (insert a new edge and delete the old one); $node_id/$edge_id cannot be inserted; no cross-database queries; the pseudo-columns cannot be used as the sort column of an ordered CCI. Fabric SQL DB allows it, but it is not mirrored to OneLake
Exam: many-to-many relationships, deep hierarchies or “shortest path” → graph + MATCH; simple parent-child relationships with referential integrity → regular tables with FK.
Memorize: AS NODE → $node_id · AS EDGE → $from_id + $to_id (filled with $node_id) · MATCH only in WHERE · edge constraint = CONNECTION (A TO B).
Learn vs Docs: the Learn example starts with CREATE TABLE Person AS NODE;, which is a syntax error (Msg 102: a node table needs ≥ 1 column; an edge table can have no columns). It also inserts (1, 'Alice') and queries Person1.name/id without those columns, and INSERT INTO Manages VALUES (1, 2) fails (NULL in internal columns): $from_id/$to_id receive the $node_id of the nodes, not integers.
Sources: Learn · Use specialized table types · Docs · Graph architecture · Docs · Graph sample · Docs · SHORTEST_PATH · Docs · MATCH · Docs · Edge constraints · Docs · CREATE TABLE (SQL Graph)

JSON: json type, nvarchar(max) and indexes SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB / MI Fabric GA

JSON for data that varies per row (preferences, API responses, audit logs, multi-tenant, flexible metadata); predictable data goes in typed columns. JSON functions require compat level ≥ 130 (the json type works at any level).

CriterionNative json typenvarchar(max) + ISJSON
AvailabilitySQL Server 2025, Azure SQL DB, MI (SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date policy), Fabric SQL DBAll versions with JSON functions (2016+)
StoragePre-parsed binary, internal UTF-8 (Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8); up to 2 GBText; up to 2 GB
ValidationAutomatic: object or array only (scalar, null or empty string → error 13609; duplicate keys: keeps the first)Manual: CHECK (ISJSON(col) = 1)
Modifyingcol.modify('$.a', value) (in-place if it fits) or JSON_MODIFYJSON_MODIFY
IndexingCREATE JSON INDEX (the json type cannot be the key of a regular index; it can be used in INCLUDE or in the WHERE of a filtered index)Computed column with JSON_VALUE + regular index
ConversionImplicit from char/varchar/nvarchar/vector; to text, explicit (CAST/CONVERT)—
 
CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders
(
    OrderID      int IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,          -- the JSON index requires a clustering key
    OrderDetails json NOT NULL CONSTRAINT CK_Orders_Basket CHECK (JSON_PATH_EXISTS(OrderDetails, '$.basket') = 1)
);
CREATE JSON INDEX IX_OrderDetails ON dbo.Orders (OrderDetails)
    FOR ('$.customer', '$.basket')                  -- optional; without FOR it indexes the whole '$'
    WITH (OPTIMIZE_FOR_ARRAY_SEARCH = ON);

SELECT OrderID FROM dbo.Orders WHERE JSON_VALUE(OrderDetails, '$.customer.id' RETURNING int) = 16167;
UPDATE dbo.Orders SET OrderDetails.modify('$.status', 'shipped') WHERE OrderID = 1;

CREATE TABLE dbo.Docs (DocID int IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
                       Info nvarchar(max) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT CK_Docs_Json CHECK (ISJSON(Info) = 1));
ALTER TABLE dbo.Docs ADD CustomerName AS JSON_VALUE(Info, '$.Customer.Name');   -- same expression as the queries
CREATE INDEX IX_Docs_CustomerName ON dbo.Docs (CustomerName);                     -- notice: NC key max. 1,700 bytes
CREATE JSON INDEXDetails
SyntaxCREATE JSON INDEX name ON table (json_col) [FOR ('$.a' [, …])] [WITH (…)] [ON filegroup | "default"] (the doc lists ON filegroup, but SQL Server 2025 17.0.1145 rejects it with Msg 156: Verify). Paths are ≤ 128 levels deep, index everything under the path and cannot overlap ($.a and $.a.b → error 13683); changing paths = recreating the index
Options (default)OPTIMIZE_FOR_ARRAY_SEARCH (OFF), FILLFACTOR (0), DROP_EXISTING (OFF), ONLINE = OFF (the only valid option; Sch-M lock), ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS/ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS (ON), MAXDOP (accepted, but it uses 1 CPU), DATA_COMPRESSION (NONE | ROW | PAGE: the doc lists it in the syntax but says in Limitations that it is not supported; in SQL Server 2025 it is accepted and PAGE was applied to the index's internal table)
Requirements and permissionsClustering key on the table (≤ 31 columns and < 128 bytes); ALTER on the table (or db_ddladmin/db_owner/sysadmin)
LimitsOne per json column (≤ 249 per table); not on computed json columns, views, table variables or memory-optimized tables; not in index hints; it can only be created/altered offline. Catalog: sys.json_indexes, sys.json_index_paths
Predicates that use it= operator: JSON_VALUE(col, path [RETURNING type]) (the doc also shows IN and BETWEEN after RETURNING int/decimal), JSON_PATH_EXISTS(col, path) = 1 and JSON_CONTAINS(col, value, path); LIKE and IS [NOT] NULL not yet
FunctionWhat it does / details
JSON_VALUE(expr, path [RETURNING type])Scalar. Without RETURNING: nvarchar(4000) (longer → NULL in lax, error in strict); path defaults to lax. RETURNING: SQL Server 2025+ and only if the input is of type json (with nvarchar/literal → Msg 102); types: integers, decimal/numeric, float/real, char/varchar/nchar/nvarchar (incl. (max)), date, time, datetime2, datetimeoffset
JSON_QUERY(expr, path)Object or array (JSON fragment); OPENJSON(json [, path]) WITH (col type 'path' [AS JSON]) turns it into rows (with CROSS APPLY)
ISJSON(expr [, VALUE | ARRAY | OBJECT | SCALAR])1 / 0 / NULL; the type argument is from SQL Server 2022+. JSON_PATH_EXISTS(expr, path) (2022+) → 1 / 0
JSON_CONTAINS(target, search [, path] [, search_mode])2025+. 1 / 0 / NULL; search_mode 0 = equality (default), 1 = LIKE; path currently required, with a wildcard if it points to an array ('$.a[*]'). The doc allows a json or text target, but in 17.0.1145 a varchar/nvarchar gave a type error: use json (Verify)
json type limits≤ 32,000 unique keys (doc; the engine fails beyond 32,768); key ≤ 7,998 bytes; ≤ 65,535 properties per object or elements per array; 128 levels; no alias type or sql_variant; not in memory-optimized or external tables; drivers without JSONSUPPORT (SqlClient < 6.0, JDBC < 13.2.0) see it as varchar/nvarchar
Exam: indexing a JSON property in nvarchar(max) → computed column with JSON_VALUE + index (same expression as the query); in a json column → CREATE JSON INDEX; requiring a property → CHECK (JSON_PATH_EXISTS(col, '$.x') = 1); JSON_VALUE = scalar, JSON_QUERY = object/array.
Memorize: JSON index = 1 per column, offline only, predicates with = (no LIKE or IS NULL), non-overlapping paths, requires a clustering key. NC key ≤ 1,700 bytes → cast the computed column to the smallest possible type.
Learn vs Docs: Learn marks .modify() as preview and does not mention CREATE JSON INDEX. The doc (Oct 2026) shows GA for the json type, .modify(), JSON_CONTAINS and the JSON index in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL DB, MI (2025/Always-up-to-date policy) and Fabric SQL DB. In Fabric SQL DB, a table with json or vector columns is not mirrored to OneLake and ALTER COLUMN to those types is not possible.
Verify (doc ≠ engine 17.0.1145): (1) CREATE JSON INDEX … ON filegroup: the doc lists it and the engine returns Msg 156; (2) DATA_COMPRESSION on the JSON index: the doc says it is not supported and the engine accepts it (PAGE was applied); (3) JSON_CONTAINS with varchar/nvarchar: the doc allows text and the engine gives a type error; (4) unique keys per document: doc 32,000, the engine fails at 32,768. Confirm them on your version before relying on them.

Constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT SQL Server Azure SQL Fabric

The engine always enforces them (also with bulk import or ad hoc SQL; validation in the app can be bypassed). Name them (CONSTRAINT name): auto-generated names change between environments.

CREATE TABLE dbo.Customer
(
    CustomerID   int IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_Customer PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED,
    EmailAddress nvarchar(100)     NOT NULL CONSTRAINT UQ_Customer_Email UNIQUE,
    CreatedDate  datetime2         NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_Customer_Created DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME(),
    Credit       decimal(10,2)     NULL     CONSTRAINT CK_Customer_Credit CHECK (Credit >= 0)
);
CREATE TABLE dbo.[Order]                      -- Order is a reserved word: brackets
(
    OrderID    int IDENTITY NOT NULL CONSTRAINT PK_Order PRIMARY KEY,
    CustomerID int NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT FK_Order_Customer FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES dbo.Customer (CustomerID)
        ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE NO ACTION
);
CREATE INDEX IX_Order_CustomerID ON dbo.[Order] (CustomerID);          -- the FK does not create an index

ALTER TABLE dbo.Customer ADD CONSTRAINT DF_Customer_Credit DEFAULT 0 FOR Credit;    -- DEFAULT ... FOR column
ALTER TABLE dbo.[Order] WITH NOCHECK ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Order_Id CHECK (OrderID > 0); -- does not validate existing data
ALTER TABLE dbo.[Order] NOCHECK CONSTRAINT FK_Order_Customer;                      -- disable (FK and CHECK only)
ALTER TABLE dbo.[Order] WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT ALL;                           -- re-enable AND revalidate
SELECT name, is_disabled, is_not_trusted FROM sys.foreign_keys;   -- same in sys.check_constraints
ConstraintKey rules
PRIMARY KEY1 per table; NOT NULL columns (implicit if you do not declare nullability; ALTER TABLE … ADD PRIMARY KEY on a nullable column fails); ≤ 32 columns and 900 bytes. Creates a unique index: clustered if the table does not already have a clustered one (otherwise, nonclustered; or an explicit PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED)
FOREIGN KEYReferences a PK or UNIQUE in the same DB. A NULL in the FK skips the check (in composite FKs use NOT NULL). ON DELETE/ON UPDATE: NO ACTION (default: error and rollback) · CASCADE · SET NULL (nullable column) · SET DEFAULT (the FK columns need a DEFAULT; if they are nullable without a DEFAULT, NULL is used). CASCADE/SET NULL/SET DEFAULT not with timestamp or with INSTEAD OF triggers for the same action. Cycles or multiple cascade paths → error 1785. Max. 253 outgoing references; up to 10,000 incoming (compat ≥ 130, with restrictions). Not enforced on temp tables
UNIQUENonclustered unique index by default (clustered only if you specify it); allows NULL but only one per column; can be the target of an FK. Multiple NULLs → filtered unique index WHERE col IS NOT NULL
CHECKRejects only FALSE: NULL (UNKNOWN) passes. At column or table level (several columns); several per column; an empty table always satisfies it; it is not evaluated on DELETE. Avoid type conversions: they can break SWITCH
DEFAULTApplies only on INSERT. One per column; constant, NULL or scalar function; cannot refer to other columns; not on timestamp or IDENTITY. ADD of a NOT NULL column requires a DEFAULT (or an empty table); if it is nullable, WITH VALUES fills the existing rows (otherwise, they stay NULL)
Enabling / trustedNOCHECK CONSTRAINT {name | ALL} only for FK and CHECK (PK, UNIQUE and DEFAULT cannot be disabled). When adding, WITH CHECK is assumed; when re-enabling, WITH NOCHECK → it stays not trusted and the optimizer ignores it until WITH CHECK CHECK CONSTRAINT
Exam: orphans → FK; duplicates → UNIQUE; invalid values → CHECK; value if omitted → DEFAULT; key without duplicates or NULLs → PK. Multiple NULLs in a unique column → filtered unique index. “Load data that violates the FK and then enforce it” → WITH NOCHECK, and then revalidate so that it becomes trusted again.
Memorize: CHECK lets NULL through · UNIQUE allows a single NULL · an FK with NULL is not validated · re-enabling = implicit NOCHECK · PK = clustered by default · UNIQUE = nonclustered by default.
Learn vs Docs: the Learn examples use CREATE TABLE Order / INSERT INTO Order: ORDER is a reserved word and requires [Order].
Sources: Learn · Enforce data integrity with constraints · Docs · Primary and foreign key constraints · Docs · Unique and check constraints · Docs · Default values · Docs · Create foreign key relationships · Docs · Disable FK constraints · Docs · ALTER TABLE · Docs · Error 1785

SEQUENCE objects SQL Server Azure SQL Fabric

A schema object (not tied to a table) that generates numbers according to its specification; the app decides how to use it. Numbers are generated outside the transaction: they are consumed even if there is a rollback (gaps).

CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.OrderNumber AS int
    START WITH 1000 INCREMENT BY 1
    MINVALUE 1000 MAXVALUE 999999
    NO CYCLE CACHE 50;                                  -- CACHE [n] | NO CACHE

INSERT dbo.Invoice (InvoiceNo, CustomerID) VALUES (NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.OrderNumber, 100);
DECLARE @n int = NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.OrderNumber;        -- value BEFORE the INSERT
SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.OrderNumber OVER (ORDER BY CustomerID) AS Seq, CustomerID FROM dbo.Customer;

ALTER TABLE dbo.Invoice ADD CONSTRAINT DF_Invoice_No DEFAULT (NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.OrderNumber) FOR InvoiceNo;

DECLARE @first sql_variant, @last sql_variant;
EXEC sys.sp_sequence_get_range @sequence_name = N'dbo.OrderNumber', @range_size = 100,
     @range_first_value = @first OUTPUT, @range_last_value = @last OUTPUT;

ALTER SEQUENCE dbo.OrderNumber RESTART WITH 1000 INCREMENT BY 2;      -- RESTART [WITH n] INCREMENT MINVALUE MAXVALUE CYCLE CACHE
SELECT start_value, increment, minimum_value, maximum_value, is_cycling, is_cached, cache_size, current_value FROM sys.sequences;
OptionDefault and rules
ASbigint; allowed: tinyint, smallint, int, bigint, decimal/numeric with scale 0 and alias types of those types. The type cannot be changed with ALTER (recreate)
START WITHMINVALUE if ascending (MAXVALUE if descending). CREATE SEQUENCE s; starts at −9,223,372,036,854,775,808
INCREMENT BY1; cannot be 0; negative = descending
MINVALUE / MAXVALUEMinimum / maximum of the type (tinyint → 0); NO MINVALUE / NO MAXVALUE
CYCLEDefault NO CYCLE (raises an error when exhausted). With CYCLE it restarts at MINVALUE (MAXVALUE if descending), not at START WITH
CACHEDefault CACHE (size chosen by the engine). An unexpected shutdown loses the numbers in memory → gaps; NO CACHE writes on every use: fewer gaps, more I/O
NEXT VALUE FORRequires UPDATE on the sequence. OVER (ORDER BY …) only in SELECT and INSERT … SELECT (no PARTITION BY; not in UPDATE/MERGE). Not in subqueries/CTEs/derived tables, views, UDFs, computed columns, CHECK, WHERE, TOP/OFFSET, DISTINCT/UNION, GROUP BY or read-only DBs; in MERGE only via a DEFAULT of the target table (INSERT action)
In DEFAULTSame DB; adding it requires REFERENCES on the sequence; no OVER; several columns using the same sequence in one row get the same value; DROP SEQUENCE is not possible while a DEFAULT uses it
sp_sequence_get_rangeReserves @range_size (bigint) numbers at once; sql_variant outputs: @range_first_value (required), @range_last_value, @sequence_increment, @sequence_min_value, @sequence_max_value; @range_cycle_count (int); error if the range exceeds the limits of a sequence without CYCLE
PermissionsCREATE SEQUENCE, ALTER or CONTROL on the schema
FeatureSEQUENCEIDENTITY
Tied to a tableNoYes (1 column per table)
Sharing across tables/columnsYesNo
Value before the INSERTYesNo
Ranges / ordering with OVER / cyclingYes / Yes / YesNo / No / No
Changing the specificationYes (ALTER SEQUENCE)No
Values protected after insertingNo (use an UPDATE trigger if needed)Yes (they cannot be modified)
UniquenessNot enforced: add UNIQUE—
Exam: number shared by several tables, value before the INSERT, reserving blocks, restarting on reaching a value, ordering the numbers by another column → SEQUENCE. Simple auto-numbering of a table → IDENTITY.
Memorize: default bigint, START = MINVALUE, INCREMENT 1, NO CYCLE, CACHE. Official example with START 125 INCREMENT 25 MINVALUE 100 MAXVALUE 200 CYCLE: 125, 150, 175, 200 and then 100.
Learn vs Docs: the outputs of sp_sequence_get_range are sql_variant (the doc declares sql_variant; Learn uses INT variables and that fails on SQL Server 2025 with “Implicit conversion from data type sql_variant to int is not allowed”: use sql_variant or CAST). The Learn example also inserts into Order (reserved word: [Order]) a column OrderNumber that its CREATE TABLE does not define.
Sources: Learn · Enforce data integrity with constraints (sequences section) · Docs · Sequence numbers · Docs · CREATE SEQUENCE · Docs · ALTER SEQUENCE · Docs · NEXT VALUE FOR · Docs · sp_sequence_get_range

Table and index partitioning SQL Server Azure SQL (all tiers) Fabric

Three pieces: partition function (type + boundaries + LEFT/RIGHT) → partition scheme (filegroups) → table or index ON scheme(column). n boundaries = n + 1 partitions (max. 15,000 partitions = 14,999 boundaries). It is still a single logical table, but the partition key is an almost permanent decision.

CREATE PARTITION FUNCTION PF_OrderDate (date)
    AS RANGE RIGHT FOR VALUES ('2025-01-01', '2025-04-01', '2025-07-01', '2025-10-01');   -- 4 boundaries → 5 partitions

CREATE PARTITION SCHEME PS_OrderDate AS PARTITION PF_OrderDate ALL TO ([PRIMARY]);
-- Several filegroups: AS PARTITION PF_OrderDate TO (fg1, fg2, fg3, fg4, fg5)   (one per partition)

CREATE TABLE dbo.[Order]
(
    OrderID    int IDENTITY NOT NULL,
    OrderDate  date NOT NULL,
    CustomerID int NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT PK_Order PRIMARY KEY (OrderID, OrderDate)        -- PK/UNIQUE must include the partition column
) ON PS_OrderDate (OrderDate);

CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Order_Customer ON dbo.[Order] (CustomerID) ON PS_OrderDate (OrderDate);   -- aligned

SELECT $PARTITION.PF_OrderDate('2025-05-17') AS PartitionNumber;     -- 3: partition no. of any value
SELECT p.partition_number, p.rows FROM sys.partitions AS p
WHERE p.object_id = OBJECT_ID('dbo.[Order]') AND p.index_id IN (0, 1) ORDER BY p.partition_number;
CriterionRANGE LEFT (default)RANGE RIGHT
The boundary value belongs to…the partition on its left (inclusive upper bound)the partition on its right (inclusive lower bound)
FOR VALUES (1, 100, 1000)≤ 1 · 2–100 · 101–1000 · > 1000< 1 · 1–99 · 100–999 · ≥ 1000
Use it forCategories/strings or “up to” ranges (Learn's PF_Region)Dates by month/quarter (date, datetime, datetime2, datetimeoffset): midnight and the first day stay with the rest of the period → precise partition elimination
TopicRules
Partition columnSame type as the function's (including length, precision and scale). No text, ntext, image, xml, timestamp, (max), alias types or CLR UDTs; a computed column must be PERSISTED. NULL values go to partition 1 (the leftmost one)
BoundariesUnordered → sorted (with a warning); duplicates → error. datetime/smalldatetime literals are evaluated as us_english (deprecated): use yyyymmdd
Partition schemeALL TO ([PRIMARY]) (one filegroup; recommended except for tiered storage or per-filegroup backups) or a list of filegroups (n + 1; an extra one is left as NEXT USED). Azure SQL DB and Fabric SQL DB: PRIMARY only
Aligned indexesSame scheme (or an equivalent function: same type, no. of partitions and boundaries). PK/UNIQUE must include the partitioning column; a non-unique clustered index adds it; a non-unique nonclustered index adds it as included. A columnstore on a partitioned table must be aligned (the column is added automatically). Nonaligned only if needed (e.g., unique without the partitioning column)
OtherAn FK from another table to the partitioned PK uses the composite key (OrderID, OrderDate). ALTER TABLE … SET (LOCK_ESCALATION = AUTO) escalates locks per partition. The history of a temporal table does not inherit the partitioning. Catalog: sys.partitions, sys.partition_schemes, sys.partition_functions, sys.partition_range_values, sys.index_columns.partition_ordinal
When / when notYes: ≥ 80% of queries filter on the key, periodic archiving (SWITCH), per-partition maintenance, tiered storage. No: queries that do not filter on the key, point lookups, small tables. Stable key (does not change after the INSERT), balanced distribution, millions of rows per partition
Exam: date-range queries + archiving by period → date partitioning with RANGE RIGHT, PK that includes the date, aligned indexes and SWITCH to archive. Partitioning does not improve queries that do not filter on the key.
Memorize: n boundaries = n + 1 partitions · RIGHT: the boundary opens the right-hand partition · PK/UNIQUE include the partitioning column · Azure SQL DB / Fabric: ALL TO ([PRIMARY]).
Learn vs Docs: Learn says nonaligned indexes “are not supported” with > 1,000 partitions; the docs: creating or rebuilding them “may be possible, but is not supported” (memory consumption and performance).
Sources: Learn · Partition tables for scale · Docs · Partitioned tables and indexes · Docs · Create partitioned tables and indexes · Docs · CREATE PARTITION FUNCTION · Docs · CREATE PARTITION SCHEME · Docs · $PARTITION

Operations: SPLIT, MERGE, SWITCH and sliding window SQL Server Azure SQL Fabric: no SWITCH

-- State: P1 < 2025-01-01 (empty) · P2 Q1 · P3 Q2 · P4 Q3 · P5 ≥ 2025-10-01 (empty)

-- 1) New boundary at the end: reassign NEXT USED before each SPLIT (with a single filegroup it is lost after splitting)
ALTER PARTITION SCHEME PS_OrderDate NEXT USED [PRIMARY];
ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION PF_OrderDate() SPLIT RANGE ('2026-01-01');          -- P5 = Q4 2025 (empty) · P6 ≥ 2026-01-01

-- 2) Load: identical staging table (structure, indexes, filegroup) with a CHECK that bounds the range (if missing → error 4982)
ALTER TABLE dbo.Order_Staging WITH CHECK ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Stg_Q4
    CHECK (OrderDate IS NOT NULL AND OrderDate >= '2025-10-01' AND OrderDate < '2026-01-01');
ALTER TABLE dbo.Order_Staging SWITCH TO dbo.[Order] PARTITION 5;

-- 3) Archive the oldest: SWITCH OUT (metadata only) and then MERGE the boundary
ALTER TABLE dbo.[Order] SWITCH PARTITION 2 TO dbo.Order_Archive
    WITH (WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY (MAX_DURATION = 1 MINUTES, ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = BLOCKERS));
ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION PF_OrderDate() MERGE RANGE ('2025-01-01');          -- must be an existing boundary

TRUNCATE TABLE dbo.[Order] WITH (PARTITIONS (1, 3 TO 4));                    -- syntax: empties specific partitions (aligned indexes); after the MERGE they are renumbered
ALTER INDEX IX_Order_Customer ON dbo.[Order] REBUILD PARTITION = 3;          -- per-partition maintenance
OperationRules
SPLIT RANGE (v)Adds a boundary (n + 1 partitions). Requires a NEXT USED filegroup in all the schemes that use the function; with ALL TO ([PRIMARY]) the NEXT USED is assigned when the scheme is created, but it is consumed by each SPLIT: reassign it with ALTER PARTITION SCHEME … NEXT USED (otherwise the next SPLIT fails). Permission ALTER ANY DATASPACE
MERGE RANGE (v)v must be an existing boundary; it removes that partition and merges its rows into the neighboring one. Affects all objects that use the function
Cost of SPLIT/MERGEWith data, they can generate up to 4× more log and severe blocking: keep partitions empty at both ends (so the split and the merge do not move data)
SWITCH [PARTITION n] TO t [PARTITION m]Metadata only (seconds); takes Sch-M on source and target. The target (table or partition) must exist and be empty; same structure; same filegroup (indexes included); when loading into a partition, the source needs a CHECK within its range. Data inherits the target's security. WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY (MAX_DURATION = n [MINUTES], ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = NONE | SELF | BLOCKERS)
With columnstoreA partitioned table with a clustered columnstore behaves like a partitioned heap: PK/unique and all nonclustered indexes must include the partitioning key to be able to SWITCH. Typical load: staging without columnstore → create the CCI → SWITCH into an empty partition. DATA_COMPRESSION = COLUMNSTORE_ARCHIVE ON PARTITIONS (n) compresses the older ones. With columnstore, SPLIT only splits an empty partition and MERGE does not merge two non-empty partitions (docs + error in SQL Server 2025); alternative: SWITCH to staging, SPLIT/MERGE and SWITCH back. The staging table also needs a CCI (otherwise the SWITCH fails)
Not allowedSWITCH on ledger tables and in Fabric SQL DB (the Fabric limitations doc prohibits SWITCH and per-partition compression; the mirroring one prohibits “Switch/Split/Merge partition” and rebuilding partitions with ROW/PAGE: in Fabric, do not count on SPLIT/MERGE). Constraints with type conversion can break the SWITCH
Exam: load or archive millions of rows in seconds → SWITCH (not INSERT/DELETE). SWITCH fails → non-empty target, different filegroup, different structure or missing range CHECK. Add a period → NEXT USED + SPLIT; retire a period → SWITCH OUT + MERGE.
Memorize: SPLIT: NEXT USED first · MERGE: existing boundary · SWITCH: empty + same filegroup + CHECK · sliding window with RIGHT: SWITCH OUT P2 and MERGE the first boundary.
Learn vs Docs: the Learn example MERGE RANGE ('2023-12-31') is not a boundary of its function (2024-01-01 … 2024-10-01) and fails (“The specified partition range value could not be found”); also, MERGE by itself does not “archive”: first the partition is taken out with SWITCH. Without a prior SWITCH, the rows are merged into the neighboring partition.
Sources: Learn · Partition tables for scale · Docs · ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION · Docs · ALTER PARTITION SCHEME · Docs · ALTER TABLE (SWITCH) · Docs · TRUNCATE TABLE · Docs · CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX · Docs · Fabric SQL DB limitations

Module lab (requires SQL Server 2025+)

  1. CREATE DATABASE EcommerceDB; (the json type requires SQL Server 2025).
  2. Supplier, Category and Product: PK IDENTITY(1,1), UNIQUE, DEFAULT GETUTCDATE(), CHECK (BasePrice > 0), CHECK (StockQuantity >= 0), two FKs and indexes IX_Category/IX_Supplier on them.
  3. Temporal ProductPrice: SysStartTime/SysEndTime GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START/END HIDDEN, PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME, WITH (SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON); after an UPDATE, FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL shows current + historical.
  4. ALTER TABLE Product ADD Metadata JSON; + computed MetadataColor AS JSON_VALUE(Metadata, '$.color') + nonclustered index on it.
  5. Partitioned [Order]: PF_OrderDate (DATE) RANGE RIGHT (2025-01-01, 04-01, 07-01, 10-01), PS_OrderDate … ALL TO ([PRIMARY]), PK (OrderID, OrderDate), aligned index; check with $PARTITION.PF_OrderDate(OrderDate).
  6. OrderLineSequence (START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1) and OrderDetail with a composite FK (OrderID, OrderDate) to [Order], LineTotal AS (Quantity * UnitPrice) and NEXT VALUE FOR in the INSERT.
  7. Verify: an INSERT with BasePrice = -50 must fail because of the CHECK; cleanup: drop EcommerceDB.
Exam: the Learn module assessment asks: change history without a manual table → temporal; unique ProductID + Category with no nulls → PK + NOT NULL; split a large table by date ranges → partitioning.
