Implement programmability objects with SQL

Views, scalar functions, table-valued functions, stored procedures and triggers: exact syntax, options, restrictions and criteria for choosing the object. The exam mainly tests which object to use, what each one does NOT allow and the typical mistakes (multi-row, permissions, performance).

Skills measured covered:
  • Create views
  • Create scalar functions
  • Create table-valued functions
  • Create stored procedures
  • Create triggers

Key comparison: view · TVF · scalar function · stored procedure · trigger SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

CriterionViewInline TVFMulti-statement TVFScalar functionStored procedureTrigger
How it is usedFROM / JOINFROM / JOIN / APPLYFROM / JOIN / APPLYin expressions: SELECT, WHERE, CHECK, computed column (or EXEC)EXEC (INSERT … EXEC to capture rows)automatic (DML / DDL / LOGON)
ParametersNoYes (without OUTPUT)Yes (without OUTPUT)Yes (without OUTPUT)Yes: defaults, OUTPUT, TVP READONLYNo (uses inserted / deleted)
Returnsrowstable (1 SELECT)table (variable @t)1 value (not table, cursor, timestamp)result sets + OUTPUT + int codenothing (result sets: deprecated)
Modifies dataYes, if updatable or with INSTEAD OFNoNo (only its local variable)NoYesYes
Transaction / TRY / dynamic SQLNoNoNoNoYesYes
Optimizationexpanded into the query; indexableexpanded like a view with parametersblack box: fixed 100 rows (interleaved execution since 2017)row by row and serial plan (inlining since 2019)cached plan (compiles on the 1st execution)runs inside the DML's transaction
EXECUTE AS—NoYesYesYesYes
Decision rule:
  • Reusable complex JOIN without parameters, or hiding columns/rows → view (heavy aggregation over stable data → indexed view).
  • Parameterized result used in FROM/JOIN → inline TVF; multi-statement TVF only if procedural logic is needed.
  • A reusable computed value in SELECT/WHERE/computed column → scalar function (ideally inlineable).
  • Multiple statements, transaction, error handling, OUTPUT, DML on several tables → stored procedure.
  • Automatic reaction to DML/DDL/LOGON (auditing, cross-table rule that CHECK/FOREIGN KEY cannot express) → trigger.
Learn vs Docs: unit 7 says multi-statement TVFs and scalar ones are “black boxes” for the optimizer. Since SQL Server 2017 (interleaved execution, actual cardinality) and SQL Server 2019 (scalar UDF inlining) this is no longer always true: see the function topics.
Exam context: these same objects (stored procedures and views) are the ones later exposed through REST/GraphQL with Data API builder and the ones protected with object permissions: grant EXECUTE/SELECT on the module, not on the tables (see the security topic).
Sources: Learn · Choose when to use each option · Docs · User-defined functions · Docs · IQP in detail

CREATE VIEW: syntax, options and rules SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

A view is a virtual table defined by a SELECT: it does not store data (unless indexed) and runs every time it is queried.

CREATE [ OR ALTER ] VIEW [ schema_name. ] view_name [ ( column [ ,...n ] ) ]
[ WITH { ENCRYPTION | SCHEMABINDING | VIEW_METADATA } [ ,...n ] ]
AS select_statement
[ WITH CHECK OPTION ] [ ; ]
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW Sales.vActiveCustomers
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
SELECT CustomerID, CustomerName, Email     -- explicit columns: with SCHEMABINDING, SELECT * raises an error
FROM Sales.Customers                       -- 2-part name required
WHERE IsActive = 1;
GO
GRANT SELECT ON Sales.vActiveCustomers TO ReportingUsers;   -- without permission on Sales.Customers
OptionEffectNotes
OR ALTERCreates the view or alters it if it exists (keeps permissions)SQL Server 2016 SP1+, Azure SQL DB, SQL database in Fabric
ENCRYPTIONObfuscates the CREATE VIEW text (OBJECT_DEFINITION returns NULL)Cannot be published in replication
SCHEMABINDINGBinds the view to the schema of the objects it references2-part names, same DB; no SELECT * (Msg 1054); DROP/ALTER of used columns fails (Msg 5074 / 4922); requirement for indexed views
VIEW_METADATADB-Library, ODBC and OLE DB receive the view's metadata, not the base table'sWith INSTEAD OF INSERT/UPDATE all columns (except timestamp) are updatable
WITH CHECK OPTIONDML performed through the view must still satisfy its WHERESee the updatable views topic
RuleDetails
Max. columns1,024 per view
PositionCREATE VIEW must be the 1st statement in the batch (Msg 111) and only creates in the current DB
ORDER BYProhibited except with TOP, OFFSET or FOR XML (Msg 1033); even then it does not guarantee the output order: put it in the outer query
Not allowedINTO, OPTION clause, temporary tables and table variables (Msg 4508)
AllowedJOIN, subqueries, functions, UNION/UNION ALL, table and join hints, other views
Column namesRequired if the column is an expression/constant or there are duplicate names (join)
Saved SET optionsQUOTED_IDENTIFIER and ANSI_NULLS are saved at create/alter time; those of the querying session are ignored
PermissionsCREATE VIEW in the DB + ALTER on the schema (and read permission on the referenced objects)
SELECT * gets “frozen”: when the view is created, * is expanded to the column list at that moment. After ALTER TABLE … ADD, a view without SCHEMABINDING does not see the new column until EXEC sys.sp_refreshview N'Sales.vStar' or ALTER VIEW (verified: 4 → 5 columns). Same problem in unbound functions/SPs/triggers: sp_refreshsqlmodule.
Exam: “give access to specific columns/rows without giving access to the table” → create the view and grant SELECT on the view (works because view and table have the same owner: ownership chaining). “Backward compatibility when the schema changes” → view that emulates the old table.
Fabric: in SQL database in Fabric views are created but not replicated (mirroring) to OneLake. In Fabric Data Warehouse / SQL analytics endpoint the syntax is more limited (only SCHEMABINDING as an option): do not confuse with SQL database in Fabric.
Sources: Learn · Create views · Docs · CREATE VIEW · Docs · Views

Updatable views, WITH CHECK OPTION and INSTEAD OF SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric

You can INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE through a view only if the engine can trace the change unambiguously to a single base table.

ConditionDetails
1 base tableAll DML must reference columns from a single table. If it affects 2 (or INSERT on a view with JOIN): Msg 4405
Direct columnsModified columns cannot be aggregates (AVG, COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, GROUPING, STDEV, STDEVP, VAR, VARP), calculations or the result of UNION/UNION ALL/CROSS JOIN/EXCEPT/INTERSECT
UngroupedNot affected by GROUP BY, HAVING or DISTINCT
TOPCannot be used in the view together with WITH CHECK OPTION
AlternativesINSTEAD OF trigger (makes the view updatable for that statement) or partitioned view
 
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW Sales.vHighValueOrders
AS
SELECT OrderID, CustomerID, OrderDate, TotalAmount
FROM Sales.Orders
WHERE TotalAmount > 1000
WITH CHECK OPTION;
GO
INSERT Sales.vHighValueOrders (CustomerID, OrderDate, TotalAmount) VALUES (1, '2024-05-01', 500);   -- Msg 550
INSERT Sales.vHighValueOrders (CustomerID, OrderDate, TotalAmount) VALUES (1, '2024-05-01', 5000);  -- OK
CHECK OPTION: only checks DML performed through the view (not DML on the base table) · also applies to underlying views that have it (verified with a view on a view: Msg 550) · T-SQL has no LOCAL/CASCADED · an INSTEAD OF trigger cannot be created on a view with CHECK OPTION (Msg 2112): remove it first with ALTER VIEW.
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW Sales.vCustomerOrders
AS
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName, o.OrderID, o.TotalAmount
FROM Sales.Customers AS c JOIN Sales.Orders AS o ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID;
GO
UPDATE Sales.vCustomerOrders SET CustomerName = N'X', TotalAmount = 1 WHERE OrderID = 1;   -- Msg 4405: 2 base tables
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER Sales.trg_vCustomerOrders_iou
ON Sales.vCustomerOrders INSTEAD OF UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    UPDATE c SET CustomerName = i.CustomerName
    FROM Sales.Customers AS c JOIN inserted AS i ON i.CustomerID = c.CustomerID;
    UPDATE o SET TotalAmount = i.TotalAmount
    FROM Sales.Orders AS o JOIN inserted AS i ON i.OrderID = o.OrderID;
END;
Partitioned views: UNION ALL of member tables with the same structure and non-overlapping CHECK constraints on the partitioning column (local or distributed); they are updatable with conditions. To partition on a single server, Microsoft prefers partitioned tables (tables module).
Sources: Learn · Create views · Docs · CREATE VIEW (Updatable views) · Docs · Modify data through a view · Docs · CREATE TRIGGER

Indexed views: requirements, restrictions and usage SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

An indexed view is a materialized view: when a UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX is created on it, the result is stored (like a table with a clustered index) and the engine maintains it on every DML of the base tables. Useful for queries that aggregate many rows; a bad idea if the base tables change a lot.

  1. Comply with the required SET options (next table) when creating base tables, view and index, in every DML on the base tables and when the optimizer must use the view in a plan.
  2. Define the view WITH SCHEMABINDING: deterministic, 2-part names, only base tables from the same DB (no other views).
  3. With GROUP BY: include COUNT_BIG(*), no HAVING, and SUM only over non-nullable expressions (ISNULL inside the SUM).
  4. Create the UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX first (IGNORE_DUP_KEY = OFF; with GROUP BY, only GROUP BY columns). Then optional nonclustered indexes.
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW Sales.vOrderTotals
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
SELECT CustomerID,
       SUM(TotalAmount) AS TotalSales,    -- TotalAmount is NOT NULL
       COUNT_BIG(*)     AS OrderCount     -- required with GROUP BY
FROM Sales.Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;
GO
CREATE UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX IX_vOrderTotals ON Sales.vOrderTotals (CustomerID);
GO
SELECT CustomerID, TotalSales FROM Sales.vOrderTotals WITH (NOEXPAND);   -- SQL Server Standard: NOEXPAND
SET optionRequired valueDefault OLE DB / ODBC
ANSI_NULLSONON
ANSI_PADDINGONON
ANSI_WARNINGSON (implies ARITHABORT ON)ON
ARITHABORTONOFF (the only one that must be changed with OLE DB/ODBC)
CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULLONON
NUMERIC_ROUNDABORTOFFOFF
QUOTED_IDENTIFIERONON
CategoryNot allowed in the definition
AggregatesCOUNT (use COUNT_BIG), AVG, MIN, MAX, STDEV/STDEVP/VAR/VARP, CHECKSUM_AGG, STRING_AGG, CLR aggregates; SUM of a nullable expression (Msg 8662)
SELECTSELECT * (Msg 1054), DISTINCT (use GROUP BY), TOP, subqueries, CTE, OVER, HAVING, CUBE/ROLLUP/GROUPING SETS, ORDER BY/OFFSET
FROMLEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER JOIN, CROSS/OUTER APPLY, derived tables, self-joins, table variables, TVF (inline and multi-statement), PIVOT/UNPIVOT, TABLESAMPLE, FOR SYSTEM_TIME, rowset functions (OPENQUERY…), other views
Set operators / WHEREUNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, INTERSECT; full-text predicates
Typestext/ntext/image, xml, FILESTREAM, sparse column sets; float in the index key (allowed as a non-key column)
TopicDetails
Automatic useSQL Server Enterprise/Developer, Azure SQL DB and MI: the optimizer uses it even if the query does not name it. In Standard it must be referenced with WITH (NOEXPAND). OPTION (EXPAND VIEWS) prevents its use
CostEvery INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the base tables updates the view: with many or complex ones, DML degrades (or a plan cannot be generated)
LifecycleDropping the view drops its indexes; dropping the clustered index removes the materialized result (it becomes a normal view again). It can be partitioned
Owner and permissionsView and base tables: same owner (ownership chain); whoever runs CREATE INDEX must be the owner of the view (or have ALTER on it/its schema). CREATE VIEW + ALTER on the schema; REFERENCES on the table if it is in another schema
DeterminismCOLUMNPROPERTY(…, 'IsDeterministic' | 'IsPrecise'). Only deterministic and precise expressions (no float) in the key, WHERE and GROUP BY. Date literals: CONVERT(datetime, '05/01/2012', 101) (deterministic style), not implicit conversion
UDF insideSCHEMABINDING, 2-part name, DATA ACCESS = NO SQL and EXTERNAL ACCESS = NO
Verified errors: Msg 1939 (view without SCHEMABINDING) · 10138 (missing COUNT_BIG(*)) · 8662 (nullable SUM) · 1054 (*) · 4513 (reference to a non-schema-bound view) · 1934 (DML with incorrect SET options, e.g. QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF) · 1935 (index on a view created with a SET option OFF).
Traps: sqlcmd starts with QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF (use sqlcmd -I); with OLE DB/ODBC, ARITHABORT ON at the server level is recommended when creating the 1st indexed view. A view that references inlineable scalar UDFs cannot be indexed: disable inlining for those UDFs (WITH INLINE = OFF).
Exam: heavy, repetitive aggregation over tables with many more reads than writes → indexed view. Requirements mnemonic: SCHEMABINDING + deterministic + COUNT_BIG(*) + 2-part names + unique clustered index + SET options.
Sources: Learn · Create views · Docs · Create indexed views · Docs · Scalar UDF inlining

Scalar functions: syntax, options and restrictions SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

Returns a single value and can be used wherever an expression is allowed (SELECT, WHERE, CHECK, computed column). It cannot have side effects.

CREATE [ OR ALTER ] FUNCTION [ schema_name. ] function_name
( [ { @parameter_name [ AS ] [ type_schema_name. ] parameter_data_type
      [ = default ] [ READONLY ] } [ ,...n ] ] )
RETURNS return_data_type
    [ WITH { ENCRYPTION | SCHEMABINDING | RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT | CALLED ON NULL INPUT
           | EXECUTE AS clause | INLINE = { ON | OFF } } [ ,...n ] ]
    [ AS ]
BEGIN
    function_body
    RETURN scalar_expression
END [ ; ]
CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fnDiscount (@price decimal(10,2), @pct decimal(5,2) = 10)
RETURNS decimal(10,2)
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
BEGIN
    RETURN @price * (1 - @pct / 100.0);
END;
GO
SELECT dbo.fnDiscount(100, DEFAULT) AS ok;      -- with a default you must write DEFAULT
GO
SELECT dbo.fnDiscount(100) AS error;            -- Msg 313 (missing arguments)
GO
SELECT OBJECTPROPERTY(OBJECT_ID('dbo.fnDiscount'), 'IsDeterministic') AS is_deterministic;   -- 1
OptionEffectNotes
SCHEMABINDINGBinds the function to the objects it references (2-part names, same DB, requires REFERENCES; referenced views/UDFs must also be schema-bound)Requirement for being deterministic. Avoids spools if the UDF does not access data. Removed with ALTER FUNCTION without the option
RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUTIf any argument is NULL it returns NULL without executing the bodyDefault: CALLED ON NULL INPUT
EXECUTE ASCALLER (default) · SELF · OWNER · 'user_name'With any value other than CALLER it is not inlineable
INLINE = { ON | OFF }Forces/prevents inlining of the UDFSQL Server 2019+, Azure SQL DB. ON on an ineligible UDF → Msg 16203
ENCRYPTIONObfuscates the function textNot replicable
RuleDetails
InvocationAt least a 2-part name (dbo.fn()). If a parameter has a default, DEFAULT must be passed; with EXEC it can be omitted. (≠ stored procedures)
ParametersMax. 2,100; no OUTPUT; no cursor or table (user-defined table types with READONLY are allowed); no timestamp
Return typeAny type except cursor, table and timestamp
Nesting32 levels
Allowed in the bodyDECLARE, assignments, flow control (no TRY/CATCH), SELECT that assigns variables, local cursors, DML on local table variables, calls to extended stored procedures, GETDATE()/GETUTCDATE()
Prohibited (Msg 443)TRY…CATCH, THROW, RAISERROR, SET (e.g. SET NOCOUNT ON), dynamic SQL (EXEC (…)), NEWID(), NEWSEQUENTIALID(), RAND(), TEXTPTR
Other limitsNo temporary tables (Msg 2772); cannot call user SPs (Msg 557 at execution); no FOR XML, no multiple result sets, no OUTPUT INTO to a table; an error inside cancels the function and the statement that called it
Determinism: same input + same DB state → same result, and the function must be SCHEMABINDING (without it IsDeterministic = 0, verified). Required for indexed/persisted computed columns and for indexed views. Deterministic: DATEADD, DATEDIFF, ISNULL, COALESCE, YEAR/MONTH/DAY, ROUND, all string functions except FORMAT. Nondeterministic: GETDATE, NEWID, RAND() without a seed, FORMAT, AT TIME ZONE. To use NEWID() inside a function, wrap it in a view and query the view from the function.
Learn vs Docs: GetEmployeeTenure uses DATEDIFF(YEAR, @HireDate, GETDATE()), but DATEDIFF counts year boundaries, not full years (2023-12-31 → 2024-01-01 = 1). Also, GETDATE() makes it nondeterministic and not inlineable (is_inlineable = 0, verified): pass the reference date as a parameter (@AsOf). Learn also states that functions that reference tables are nondeterministic: CREATE FUNCTION allows local data access in deterministic functions (with SCHEMABINDING), but then UserDataAccess = true and they cannot be used to index computed columns or inside an indexed view.
Inconsistency in Docs: “User-defined functions” still says max. 1,024 parameters; CREATE FUNCTION and Maximum capacity specifications say 2,100 (use 2,100).
Fabric Data Warehouse Preview: there, scalar UDFs are Preview and, to be used in SELECT … FROM over user tables, must be inlineable. Do not confuse with SQL database in Fabric, where the whole CREATE FUNCTION of this topic does apply.
Sources: Learn · Create scalar functions · Docs · CREATE FUNCTION · Docs · Create UDFs · Docs · Deterministic functions

Scalar UDF performance and scalar UDF inlining SQL Server 2019+ Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

Without inlining, a scalar UDF is invoked row by row, runs in an interpreted way (statement by statement, without optimizing across statements), is poorly costed and forces a serial plan (no parallelism). With inlining, the engine turns it into a scalar expression/subquery inside the query (the plan no longer has a UDF operator).

ConceptValue
Enabled byCompatibility level 150 or higher (default 170 in SQL Server 2025 and Azure SQL DB). No changes to UDFs or queries
Disable in the DBALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET TSQL_SCALAR_UDF_INLINING = OFF; (default ON)
Disable for 1 queryOPTION (USE HINT('DISABLE_TSQL_SCALAR_UDF_INLINING')) (verified: the <UserDefinedFunction> node reappears in the plan)
Disable for 1 UDFWITH INLINE = OFF in CREATE/ALTER FUNCTION
Is it eligible?sys.sql_modules.is_inlineable = 1 (also 1 for inline TVF; 0 for multi-statement TVF and the rest). Eligible does not imply inlined: it is decided per query and per UDF
Was it inlined?The XML plan does not contain <UserDefinedFunction>
Side effectsChanges the query hash; previously hidden warnings may surface (division by zero); query-level join hints may stop being valid; the value of SCOPE_IDENTITY()/@@ROWCOUNT/@@ERROR inside the UDF changes (which is why it is blocked if the UDF uses them)

The UDF must NOT have…

  • time-dependent functions (GETDATE()) or with side effects (NEWSEQUENTIALID())
  • EXECUTE AS other than CALLER
  • table variables/TVPs, UDTs, CTEs, @@ROWCOUNT, STRING_AGG, XML methods, WITH XMLNAMESPACES
  • remote tables, encrypted columns, module signature
  • aggregates passed as an argument to another scalar UDF; system views (e.g. OBJECT_ID)
  • more than one RETURN; SELECT … ORDER BY without TOP 1; accumulation SELECT @v += col
  • be native (natively compiled) or a partition function
  • thousands of lines of code: the engine may decide not to inline it

The context must NOT be…

  • the UDF in the query's ORDER BY or GROUP BY
  • computed column or CHECK constraint
  • query with a CTE, GROUPING SETS/CUBE/ROLLUP
  • call from a RETURN
  • DISTINCT with ORDER BY and the UDF in the select list
  • variable assigned in the same query and used as an argument of the UDF (SELECT @y = 2, @x = dbo.f(@y))
SELECT o.name, o.type, m.is_inlineable
FROM sys.sql_modules AS m JOIN sys.objects AS o ON o.object_id = m.object_id
WHERE o.type IN ('FN', 'IF', 'TF');
Typical scenario: slow query that calls a scalar UDF over millions of rows → (1) compat level ≥ 150 and check is_inlineable; (2) if it is not eligible, rewrite it as an inline TVF + CROSS APPLY; (3) if it uses GETDATE(), pass the date as a parameter. Compat level ≥ 140 only gives interleaved execution (MSTVF), not inlining.
Docs vs docs: ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION still marks TSQL_SCALAR_UDF_INLINING in Azure SQL Database as “(feature is in preview)”; Scalar UDF inlining and Intelligent query processing list it without Preview (since compat 150): treat it as GA.
Sources: Docs · Scalar UDF inlining · Docs · User-defined functions · Learn · Create scalar functions

Table-valued functions: inline vs multi-statement and APPLY SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fnCustomerOrders (@CustomerID int)
RETURNS TABLE
AS
RETURN
(
    SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, TotalAmount, Status
    FROM Sales.Orders
    WHERE CustomerID = @CustomerID
);
CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fnOrderSummary (@From date, @To date)
RETURNS @r TABLE (CustomerID int PRIMARY KEY, Orders int NOT NULL, Revenue decimal(18,2) NOT NULL)
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT @r (CustomerID, Orders, Revenue)
    SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*), SUM(TotalAmount)
    FROM Sales.Orders
    WHERE OrderDate BETWEEN @From AND @To
    GROUP BY CustomerID;
    RETURN;                                  -- RETURN without a value
END;
CriterionInline TVFMulti-statement TVF
BodyRETURN ( SELECT … ), without BEGIN…ENDBEGIN … RETURN END, multiple statements
Returned tableInferred from the SELECTDeclared: RETURNS @t TABLE (…) (supports PK, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT)
OptimizerExpanded into the query (like a view with parameters): the optimizer sees and optimizes everything, with real statisticsMaterialized in a table variable: fixed estimate of 100 rows (SQL Server 2014+; 1 before)
Interleaved executionn/aSQL Server 2017+ (compat ≥ 140), Azure SQL: uses the actual cardinality
EXECUTE ASNo (Msg 487)Yes
is_inlineable10
WhenDefaultOnly if you need procedural logic or multiple steps
Interleaved executionDetails
How it worksThe optimizer pauses, runs the MSTVF, captures the actual no. of rows and resumes optimization with that cardinality (verified: estimate 7 instead of 100, IsInterleavedExecuted="1")
EligibilityRead-only statement and arguments that are runtime constants; a plain SELECT * from the MSTVF does not benefit
Cached planKeeps the estimate from the 1st execution; OPTION (RECOMPILE) does not cache it
Disable (DB)SQL Server 2019+/Azure SQL (default ON): ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET INTERLEAVED_EXECUTION_TVF = OFF; · SQL Server 2017 (old name, inverted logic): ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET DISABLE_INTERLEAVED_EXECUTION_TVF = ON;. No effect with compat level ≤ 130
Disable (query)OPTION (USE HINT('DISABLE_INTERLEAVED_EXECUTION_TVF'))
 
-- CROSS APPLY ≈ INNER: only customers that have orders
SELECT c.CustomerName, o.OrderID, o.TotalAmount
FROM Sales.Customers AS c
CROSS APPLY dbo.fnCustomerOrders(c.CustomerID) AS o;

-- OUTER APPLY ≈ LEFT: all customers (NULL columns if there are no orders)
SELECT c.CustomerName, o.OrderID
FROM Sales.Customers AS c
OUTER APPLY dbo.fnCustomerOrders(c.CustomerID) AS o;
Learn vs Docs: the example in the unit INNER JOIN dbo.GetCustomerOrders(c.CustomerID) o ON 1=1 does not work (Msg 4104: cannot bind c.CustomerID). A JOIN cannot pass columns from the left side to a function; you must use APPLY (verified).
APPLY: the right side can use columns from the left side (correlation), never the other way around. Outside APPLY, the arguments of a TVF can only be constants and local variables. A TVF can be used in the FROM of SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
Exam: pick inline TVF unless the question requires multiple statements. “Incorrect row estimate / bad plan with a multi-statement TVF” → rewrite as inline TVF, or compat level ≥ 140 (interleaved execution).

CREATE [ OR ALTER ] { PROC | PROCEDURE } [ schema_name. ] procedure_name [ ; number ]
    [ { @parameter_name [ type_schema_name. ] data_type }
        [ VARYING ] [ NULL ] [ = default ] [ OUT | OUTPUT | [ READONLY ] ] ] [ ,...n ]
[ WITH { ENCRYPTION | RECOMPILE | EXECUTE AS clause } [ ,...n ] ]
[ FOR REPLICATION ]
AS { [ BEGIN ] sql_statement [ ; ] [ ...n ] [ END ] } [ ; ]
OptionEffect
ENCRYPTIONObfuscates the text (OBJECT_DEFINITION = NULL; privileged users with DAC or file access can still see it). Not replicable
RECOMPILEDoes not cache the plan: compiles on every execution (not with FOR REPLICATION or in CLR)
EXECUTE ASSecurity context it runs under (see the security topic)
FOR REPLICATIONReplication filter (type RF); accepts no parameters and does not run on the Subscriber

#proc / ##procLocal / global temporary SP; full name ≤ 116 / ≤ 128 characters (includes #/##)
RuleDetails
CompilationCompiled on the 1st execution, not at creation (at creation only the syntax is validated); then the plan is reused from the cache. That is why it can reference tables that do not exist yet (deferred name resolution: fails at execution, Msg 208)
PositionMust be the 1st statement in the batch (Msg 111)
Limits2,100 parameters · 32 nesting levels (@@NESTLEVEL) · text size: CREATE PROCEDURE says “no predefined maximum size”, but Maximum capacity specifications sets the smaller of the batch size (65,536 × network packet size; default packet 4 KB) and 250 MB
Not allowed in the bodyCREATE AGGREGATE/DEFAULT/RULE/SCHEMA; CREATE/ALTER for TRIGGER, FUNCTION, PROCEDURE, VIEW; USE; SET SHOWPLAN_TEXT|ALL|XML, SET PARSEONLY
Saved SET optionsQUOTED_IDENTIFIER and ANSI_NULLS are saved at creation; any other SET executed inside the SP is reverted when it ends
ArgumentsA function cannot be used as a default, nor can GETDATE() be passed directly in the EXEC (Msg 102): use a variable
Remote instanceIts changes cannot be rolled back (it does not participate in the transaction)
NameAvoid the sp_ prefix (reserved for the system; searched first in master)
PermissionsCREATE PROCEDURE in the DB + ALTER on the schema, or member of db_ddladmin

SET NOCOUNT, plan cache and recompilation

ItemEffect
SET NOCOUNT ONSuppresses the rows-affected messages (DONEINPROC); @@ROWCOUNT is still updated. Put it at the start of the SP
CREATE … WITH RECOMPILEThe SP does not use the plan cache (useful with atypical parameters)
EXEC proc … WITH RECOMPILERecompiles only that execution
OPTION (RECOMPILE)Recompiles a specific statement in the SP
EXEC sys.sp_recompile N'sch.proc'Marks the SP for recompilation on its next execution
Learn vs Docs: unit 3 and its knowledge check talk about “precompiled” procedures: in reality they are compiled on first execution and the plan is cached. On SET NOCOUNT ON, the unit promises better performance; CREATE PROCEDURE says there is no measurable benefit today, while SET NOCOUNT sees it as useful in SPs with many statements or loops: its guaranteed effect is avoiding the count messages.

Optional parameter plan optimization (OPPO) SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB SQL database in Fabric

Improves the WHERE (col = @p OR @p IS NULL) pattern (the one in GetCustomerOrdersByDate in unit 3): a single plan is bad for both cases (seek vs scan). OPPO generates a dispatcher and several variants (PSP Multiplan infrastructure) depending on whether the parameter is NULL or not. Requires compat level 170 + OPTIONAL_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATION (ON by default, verified). Disable: ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET OPTIONAL_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATION = OFF; or OPTION (USE HINT('DISABLE_OPTIONAL_PARAMETER_OPTIMIZATION')).

Natively compiled stored procedures SQL Server 2014+ Azure SQL DB: Premium / Business Critical MI: not in General Purpose SQL database in Fabric: no in-memory tables

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.usp_2 (@c1 int, @c3 nvarchar(5))
WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING
AS BEGIN ATOMIC WITH (TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL = SNAPSHOT, LANGUAGE = N'us_english')
    DECLARE @c2 datetime = GETDATE();
    INSERT INTO dbo.T2 (c1, c2, c3) VALUES (@c1, @c2, @c3);   -- T2: MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON table
END
RequirementDetails
OptionsNATIVE_COMPILATION and SCHEMABINDING required (EXECUTE AS optional, in any order)
Atomic blockThe body is a single BEGIN ATOMIC (not nested) with TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL (SNAPSHOT, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE) and LANGUAGE; optional DATEFIRST, DATEFORMAT, DELAYED_DURABILITY
Inside the blockXACT_ABORT fixed ON and fixed SET options; no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; RETURN commits, THROW rolls back
StyleSchema-qualified names, no SELECT *; NOT NULL on parameters/variables exists only in native SPs
ConversionAn SP created without NATIVE_COMPILATION cannot be altered to native: it must be recreated

Stored procedures: parameters, OUTPUT, RETURN, EXEC and TVP SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

CREATE TYPE dbo.IdList AS TABLE (id int PRIMARY KEY);          -- user-defined table type
GO
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE Sales.uspTotalByIds
    @ids    dbo.IdList    READONLY,                            -- TVP: READONLY required
    @Status nvarchar(20)  = NULL,                              -- default: optional parameter
    @Total  decimal(18,2) OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SELECT @Total = SUM(o.TotalAmount)
    FROM Sales.Orders AS o JOIN @ids AS i ON i.id = o.OrderID
    WHERE @Status IS NULL OR o.Status = @Status;
    RETURN 0;
END;
GO
DECLARE @x dbo.IdList, @t decimal(18,2), @rc int;
INSERT @x (id) VALUES (1), (2), (3);
EXEC @rc = Sales.uspTotalByIds @ids = @x, @Total = @t OUTPUT;   -- @Status takes its default
SELECT @rc AS return_code, @t AS total;
EXEC Sales.uspTotalByIds @x, DEFAULT, @t OUTPUT;                 -- positional + DEFAULT
EXEC Sales.uspTotalByIds @ids = @x, @Total = @t;                 -- without OUTPUT: @t does not change
GO
DECLARE @x dbo.IdList, @t decimal(18,2);
EXEC Sales.uspTotalByIds @ids = @x, N'Open', @t OUTPUT;          -- Msg 119: after @p = value, everything must be named
ItemRule
Input@name type [= default]. Without a default it is required. The default is a constant or NULL (it can be a wildcard pattern for LIKE); not a function
OUTPUT / OUTMust be declared in the SP and specified in the call with a variable (not constants). Without the word OUTPUT in the EXEC, the variable does not change (verified)
Typestext/ntext/image cannot be OUTPUT (CLR only) · cursor only as OUTPUT and with VARYING · a table cannot be OUTPUT
RETURNReturns an int; without RETURN it returns 0 if there was no error; RETURN NULL → warning and 0. Captured with EXEC @rc = proc
CallPositional or @p = value; after using @p = value, all the following ones too (Msg 119). DEFAULT requests the default value (error if none exists). EXEC is optional if it is the 1st statement in the batch
WITH RESULT SETSEXEC … WITH RESULT SETS ((col type, …)) redefines the names and types of the result set; also UNDEFINED or NONE
Capture rowsINSERT table EXEC proc saves the result set of the SP into a table (compatible columns)
Table-valued parameter (TVP)Details
DeclarationCREATE TYPE … AS TABLE; the parameter takes READONLY (otherwise: Msg 352). Input only: no OUTPUT
ModificationINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the TVP inside the SP → Msg 10700. It cannot be the target of SELECT INTO or INSERT EXEC
If omittedThe SP receives an empty table (verified)
PerformancePassed by reference, cached like a temp table, no locks on the initial load from the client; no statistics on its columns; performs well (compared with BULK INSERT) with < 1,000 rows
PermissionsEXECUTE and REFERENCES on the type (or its schema/DB)
Three output channels: result sets (SELECT), OUTPUT parameters and the RETURN code. The docs recommend signaling failures with errors (THROW/RAISERROR), not with return codes, and not returning business data through RETURN.

Transactions and error handling inside a stored procedure SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE Sales.uspInsertOrder
    @CustomerID  int,
    @OrderDate   date          = NULL,
    @TotalAmount decimal(10,2),
    @NewOrderID  int           OUTPUT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT, XACT_ABORT ON;                              -- 1) at the start
    SET @OrderDate = ISNULL(@OrderDate, CAST(SYSUTCDATETIME() AS date));
    BEGIN TRY
        BEGIN TRANSACTION;
        IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Sales.Customers WHERE CustomerID = @CustomerID)
            THROW 50001, N'Customer does not exist.', 1;     -- 2) validate and fail early
        INSERT Sales.Orders (CustomerID, OrderDate, TotalAmount)
        VALUES (@CustomerID, @OrderDate, @TotalAmount);
        SET @NewOrderID = SCOPE_IDENTITY();
        COMMIT TRANSACTION;
        RETURN 0;
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;             -- 3) roll back
        THROW;                                               -- 4) rethrow the original error
    END CATCH;
END;
CriterionTHROWRAISERROR
Error number≥ 50,000 (up to 2,147,483,647); does not need to be in sys.messagesA msg_id must exist in sys.messages; with free text the error is 50000
SeverityAlways 16 (when rethrowing it keeps the original)Explicit parameter
Messagenvarchar(2048); no printf (% reserved: write %%); state 0–255Supports printf formatting
XACT_ABORTHonors it (rolls back the transaction)Does not honor it
RethrowTHROW; with no arguments, only inside CATCHMust be rebuilt with ERROR_MESSAGE() (loses the original number)
SyntaxThe previous statement must end with ;—
UsageNew code (recommended by Microsoft)Legacy
ComponentDetails
SET XACT_ABORT ONAny runtime error rolls back the transaction. Default OFF in statements, ON in triggers and atomic blocks. Verified outside TRY: RAISERROR leaves the transaction open, THROW rolls it back and aborts the batch
XACT_STATE()1 = can be committed · 0 = no transaction · −1 = uncommittable (read-only or ROLLBACK); inside TRY with XACT_ABORT ON errors leave it at −1
ERROR_*()ERROR_NUMBER, ERROR_SEVERITY, ERROR_STATE, ERROR_PROCEDURE, ERROR_LINE, ERROR_MESSAGE (only inside CATCH)
Not caught by TRY…CATCHWarnings (severity ≤ 10); severity ≥ 20 that closes the connection; attentions and KILL; compilation and name-resolution errors at the same level (it does catch them if they occur at a lower level: SP or sp_executesql called from the TRY)
Exam pattern: SET XACT_ABORT ON + BEGIN TRY / BEGIN TRANSACTION … COMMIT + in CATCH: IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK; THROW;. Keep transactions short (shorter locks, fewer deadlocks).
Traps: ROLLBACK TRAN followed by THROW … without a ; in between → THROW is interpreted as a transaction name (Msg 102 near 50001, verified). Learn vs Docs: the unit uses RAISERROR in the CATCH (the docs recommend THROW), and the lab (AddOrderLineItem) uses neither XACT_ABORT nor TRY…CATCH: with XACT_ABORT OFF a statement error between BEGIN TRANSACTION and COMMIT does not roll back the rest.

sp_executesql [ @stmt = ] N'statement'
    [ , [ @params = ] N'@p1 data_type [ OUT | OUTPUT ] [ ,...n ]' ]
    [ , [ @p1 = ] value1 [ ,...n ] ]
DECLARE @sch sysname = N'Sales', @tbl sysname = N'Orders', @cust int = 1, @cnt int, @sql nvarchar(max);
SET @sql = N'SELECT @n = COUNT(*) FROM ' + QUOTENAME(@sch) + N'.' + QUOTENAME(@tbl)
         + N' WHERE CustomerID = @c;';
EXEC sys.sp_executesql @sql, N'@c int, @n int OUTPUT', @c = @cust, @n = @cnt OUTPUT;
SELECT @cnt AS n_orders;
CriterionEXEC (@sql)sp_executesql
ParametersNo: everything is concatenatedYes (@params + values, with OUTPUT)
Plan cacheOne plan per distinct textReuses the plan if the text does not change (performance similar to an SP)
SQL injectionHigh if you concatenate inputLow if the values are passed as parameters
@stmtString; it can be concatenated inside the parenthesesUnicode (N'…'), constant or variable: it cannot be concatenated in the argument (Msg 102); values cannot be expressions
ContextIts own batchIts own batch: does not see the variables of the caller; the DB change lasts only for the statement; parameter order matters
What to wrapWith what
Object name (securable)QUOTENAME(@v) (sysname, ≤ 128)
String literal ≤ 128 charactersQUOTENAME(@v, '''')
String literal > 128 charactersREPLACE(@v, '''', '''''')
Business valuessp_executesql parameters (do not concatenate)
Truncation: QUOTENAME can return up to 258 characters; if you store it in a small variable it is silently truncated and can allow injection. Call QUOTENAME/REPLACE directly inside the dynamic SQL or size the buffer (2 * (LEN(@v) + 1)).
Permissions: ownership chaining does not apply to dynamic SQL: inside an SP, EXEC (…) checks the permissions of the caller on the tables (verified: Msg 229). Solutions: WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER, module signing, or avoiding dynamic SQL.
SQL Server 2025 · OPTIMIZED_SP_EXECUTESQL SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB SQL database in Fabric: ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET OPTIMIZED_SP_EXECUTESQL = ON; (default OFF, verified) serializes the compilation of identical batches with a compile lock, as SPs and triggers do, to avoid compilation storms. It is also recommended to enable asynchronous auto-update statistics and ASYNC_STATS_UPDATE_WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY.

DML triggers: AFTER vs INSTEAD OF, inserted/deleted and multi-row SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

A trigger is a special stored procedure that runs automatically on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against a table or view, once per statement (not per row) and inside the DML transaction.

CREATE [ OR ALTER ] TRIGGER [ schema_name. ] trigger_name
ON { table | view }
[ WITH { ENCRYPTION | EXECUTE AS clause } [ ,...n ] ]
{ FOR | AFTER | INSTEAD OF } { [ INSERT ] [ , ] [ UPDATE ] [ , ] [ DELETE ] }
[ NOT FOR REPLICATION ]
AS { sql_statement [ ; ] [ ...n ] }
Platform: in Azure SQL Database and SQL database in Fabric the documented syntax only supports WITH EXECUTE AS (no ENCRYPTION, NOT FOR REPLICATION or CLR). On memory-optimized tables the trigger is native: WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING, EXECUTE AS (all three required; SCHEMABINDING is not supported on regular tables), only FOR/AFTER and the body is a single ATOMIC block. CREATE TRIGGER must be the 1st statement in the batch and applies to one table/view; the trigger lives in the schema of its table (Msg 2103 if the schema differs). Triggers cannot be created on temporary tables (Msg 167).
CriterionAFTER (= FOR)INSTEAD OF
ObjectsTables only (on a view: error, Msg 8197)Tables and views
When it runsAfter the DML and after constraints (CHECK/FK) and cascading actionsInstead of the DML; constraints are evaluated afterwards, on whatever the trigger does
How manySeveral per eventMax. 1 per INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and object (Msg 2111)
RecursionYes, if RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS ONDoes not call itself: the inner DML is processed as if the trigger did not exist
Restrictions—No DELETE/UPDATE if there is an FK with ON DELETE/ON UPDATE CASCADE; not on views with CHECK OPTION
Ordersp_settriggerorder (First/Last)Not applicable (Msg 15133)
Typical useAuditing, cross-table rules, maintaining aggregatesMaking views updatable; intercepting/redirecting DML
Operationinserteddeleted
INSERTNew rowsEmpty
DELETEEmptyDeleted rows
UPDATENew version of the rowsPrevious version of the rows

They are logical in-memory tables with the structure of the trigger table: they cannot be modified or indexed. With text/ntext/image they cannot be referenced in AFTER; varchar(max), nvarchar(max) and varbinary(max) can. Referencing the “wrong” table does not raise an error, but it is empty.

CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER Sales.trg_OrderLines_UpdateStock
ON Sales.OrderLines
AFTER INSERT
AS
BEGIN
    IF ROWCOUNT_BIG() = 0 RETURN;                 -- 1st statement: exit if 0 rows
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    UPDATE p
    SET QuantityInStock = p.QuantityInStock - i.Qty
    FROM Inventory.Products AS p
    JOIN (SELECT ProductID, SUM(Quantity) AS Qty FROM inserted GROUP BY ProductID) AS i
         ON i.ProductID = p.ProductID;
END;
Learn vs Docs: the trigger tr_UpdateInventory in the unit (UPDATE … FROM Products p JOIN inserted i) fails when inserted contains several rows for the same ProductID: only one is applied (verified: stock 80 instead of 70 when inserting 10 + 20). Always think multi-row, use set-based logic (no cursors) and aggregate before joining.

Detect what changed

CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER Sales.trg_Orders_AuditStatus
ON Sales.Orders
AFTER UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    IF ROWCOUNT_BIG() = 0 RETURN;
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    IF UPDATE(Status)                                            -- TRUE even if the value does not change
        INSERT dbo.Audit (Msg)
        SELECT CONCAT(N'Order ', i.OrderID, N': ', d.Status, N' -> ', i.Status)
        FROM inserted AS i JOIN deleted AS d ON d.OrderID = i.OrderID
        WHERE d.Status IS DISTINCT FROM i.Status;                -- real change, NULL-safe (SQL Server 2022+, Azure SQL)
END;
GO
-- COLUMNS_UPDATED: mask 2^(ordinal-1). In dbo.Prod (ProductID, Name, Price, Stock, Note): Price=4, Stock=8
-- IF (COLUMNS_UPDATED() & 12) = 12 PRINT 'Price and Stock';     IF (COLUMNS_UPDATED() & 12) > 0 PRINT 'Price or Stock';
FunctionDetails
UPDATE(col)TRUE if the column was in the SET / INSERT, even if the value does not change (on INSERT it is always TRUE); does not support computed columns. To detect a real change, compare inserted with deleted (careful: <> does not detect NULL ↔ value)
COLUMNS_UPDATED()varbinary with 1 bit per column: the least significant bit of the leftmost byte is the 1st column; > 8 columns → several bytes (SUBSTRING). On INSERT all bits = 1; outside a trigger it returns NULL. Use COLUMNPROPERTY(…, 'ColumnID'), not ORDINAL_POSITION
ROWCOUNT_BIG()Rows of the triggering statement. Must be the 1st statement: any other (SET, SELECT…) resets @@ROWCOUNT. The trigger fires even if it affects 0 rows
When NOT to use a trigger: if a CHECK/FK/UNIQUE/DEFAULT or a stored procedure solves it (triggers are invisible, hard to debug and hold locks within the transaction). Keep the trigger short and, for heavy work, queue the event (queue table + asynchronous process). Embeddings idea (separate module): a trigger can flag/queue the rows whose text changed (UPDATE(col) + compare inserted/deleted) to regenerate embeddings outside the transaction; synchronously calling an external endpoint from the trigger adds latency, holds locks and makes an external failure roll back the original DML.

Trigger behavior: order, nesting, recursion and ROLLBACK SQL Server Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric GA

TopicDetails
Execution orderINSTEAD OF → constraints (CHECK/FK, cascades) → AFTER. If a constraint fails, the AFTER does not fire
Multiple AFTERsUndefined order, except with sp_settriggerorder: one First and one Last per operation and table. ALTER TRIGGER removes the First/Last attribute (verified)
NestingUp to 32 levels. Server option nested triggers (default 1); at 0 the AFTERs are not chained (the INSTEAD OFs are; the 1st AFTER inside an INSTEAD OF does run) and recursion is also disabled
RecursionALTER DATABASE … SET RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS { ON | OFF } (default OFF, verified). OFF only prevents direct recursion; for the indirect one (T1→T2→T1) you must set nested triggers = 0. Without a guard and with ON → Msg 217 (limit 32)
TRIGGER_NESTLEVEL()TRIGGER_NESTLEVEL( [ object_id ] , [ 'AFTER' | 'IOT' ] , [ 'DML' | 'DDL' ] ): no. of triggers on the stack (without parameters: all). Use it as a guard. With object_id = 0 it counts by type/category
XACT_ABORTON by default inside a trigger: a runtime error rolls back the trigger and the original statement
ROLLBACK in the triggerRolls back the whole transaction, aborts the batch (Msg 3609 “The transaction ended in the trigger”) and no more triggers run. Pattern: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; THROW 50002, N'…', 1; for a controlled error (in CATCH, @@TRANCOUNT = 0)
TRUNCATEDoes not fire DELETE triggers (nor does WRITETEXT)
OUTPUTWith triggers enabled on the table, OUTPUT without INTO fails (Msg 334): use OUTPUT … INTO @table
Result setsA trigger can return them (deprecated). sp_configure 'disallow results from triggers', 1 (default 0) blocks it (Msg 524); logon triggers never allow them
Prohibited statementsIn any DML trigger: CREATE/ALTER/DROP/RESTORE DATABASE, RESTORE LOG, RECONFIGURE. On the table of the trigger itself, also: CREATE/ALTER/DROP INDEX, DROP TABLE and ALTER TABLE that changes columns, partitions, PK or UNIQUE
Enable / catalogDISABLE TRIGGER name ON table | DATABASE | ALL SERVER y ENABLE TRIGGER; sys.triggers (is_disabled, is_instead_of_trigger), sys.trigger_events
Permissions and securityCreate: ALTER on the table/view. By default it runs in the context of the caller (privilege-escalation risk): review sys.triggers/sys.server_triggers and use EXECUTE AS with care
 
EXEC sys.sp_settriggerorder @triggername = N'dbo.trg_TO1_c', @order = N'First', @stmttype = N'INSERT';
EXEC sys.sp_settriggerorder @triggername = N'dbo.trg_TO1_a', @order = N'Last',  @stmttype = N'INSERT';
-- @order: First | Last | None · @stmttype: INSERT | UPDATE | DELETE | LOGON | DDL event · @namespace: DATABASE | SERVER | NULL
GO
ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS ON;               -- default OFF
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER dbo.trg_Rec ON dbo.Rec AFTER UPDATE AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    IF TRIGGER_NESTLEVEL() < 3                                   -- guard against infinite recursion
        UPDATE dbo.Rec SET n = n + 1;
END;
Defaults to memorize: RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS = OFF · nested triggers = 1 · disallow results from triggers = 0 · XACT_ABORT = ON inside triggers · 32 nesting levels · only one INSTEAD OF per operation · one First and one Last per operation.

DDL triggerDetails
WhenOnly after the event (FOR/AFTER); there is no INSTEAD OF for DDL and there are no inserted/deleted tables
Eventsevent_type (CREATE_TABLE, ALTER_TABLE, DROP_TABLE, CREATE_DATABASE…) or event_group (macro that expands into sys.trigger_events). Covers CREATE, ALTER, DROP, GRANT, DENY, REVOKE, UPDATE STATISTICS; some SPs (sp_rename, sp_addtype) also fire them
EVENTDATA()Event XML: EventType, PostTime, ObjectName, TSQLCommand/CommandText… (the schema varies by event: EVENT_INSTANCE_<event_type>). It only returns data if called directly in the trigger (NULL from another routine). Use .value(), not .query()
ScopeDatabase: DB object (sys.triggers). Server: stored in master (sys.server_triggers). They are not schema-scoped: do not use OBJECT_ID/OBJECT_NAME/OBJECTPROPERTY. They do not fire for temporary tables or SPs
ManagementDISABLE TRIGGER name ON DATABASE | ALL SERVER · DROP TRIGGER name ON DATABASE | ALL SERVER
EXECUTE ASDatabase: CALLER | SELF | 'user'. Server/logon: CALLER | SELF | 'login_name'. OWNER is not supported
PermissionsDatabase: ALTER ANY DATABASE DDL TRIGGER. Server and logon: CONTROL SERVER
 
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER trg_ddl_guard
ON DATABASE
FOR DROP_TABLE, ALTER_TABLE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    DECLARE @e xml = EVENTDATA();
    DECLARE @evt nvarchar(100) = @e.value('(/EVENT_INSTANCE/EventType)[1]', 'nvarchar(100)');
    DECLARE @obj sysname       = @e.value('(/EVENT_INSTANCE/ObjectName)[1]', 'sysname');
    DECLARE @cmd nvarchar(max) = @e.value('(/EVENT_INSTANCE/TSQLCommand/CommandText)[1]', 'nvarchar(max)');
    PRINT @evt + N' on ' + @obj + N': ' + @cmd;       -- .value() outside the PRINT: inside it gives Msg 2722
    ROLLBACK;                                          -- rolls back the DDL
    THROW 50010, N'Schema changes are blocked. Disable trg_ddl_guard first.', 1;
END;
GO
DISABLE TRIGGER trg_ddl_guard ON DATABASE;
DROP TRIGGER trg_ddl_guard ON DATABASE;
Logon triggerDetails
TimingAfter authentication and before the session is created. PRINT and errors go to the error log. It does not fire if authentication fails
TransactionImplicit and independent (@@TRANCOUNT = 1): ROLLBACK denies the login (avoid COMMIT). There is also no session if there is an error with severity > 20
RestrictionsNever returns result sets (if it does, the login is denied); no distributed transactions (error 3969)
RiskCan prevent everyone from connecting, including sysadmin: recoverable with the dedicated administrator connection (DAC) or by starting with -f (minimal configuration)
Triggers vs event notificationsThe trigger is synchronous (it can prevent the session); an event notification on AUDIT_LOGIN is asynchronous and cannot
 
CREATE TRIGGER connection_limit_trigger ON ALL SERVER
WITH EXECUTE AS N'login_test'                        -- the login needs VIEW SERVER STATE
FOR LOGON AS BEGIN
    IF ORIGINAL_LOGIN() = N'login_test'
       AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions
            WHERE is_user_process = 1 AND original_login_name = N'login_test') > 3
        ROLLBACK;
END;
Exam: prevent/audit schema changes → DDL trigger; limit sessions or restrict logins by conditions → logon trigger (it does not exist in Azure SQL Database or SQL database in Fabric). Triggers run in the context of the caller by default: a malicious trigger can escalate privileges when an administrator fires it.
Sources: Learn · Create triggers · Docs · DDL triggers · Docs · Logon triggers · Docs · EVENTDATA · Docs · Fabric SQL database limitations · Docs · Azure SQL T-SQL differences

Module security: ownership chaining, EXECUTE AS and signing SQL Server Azure SQL GA

Ownership chainingDetails
ConceptIf the calling module and the referenced object have the same owner (by default, the schema owner), permissions on the referenced object are not checked: EXECUTE/SELECT on the module is enough
LimitationsDML only (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) · same owner · does not apply to dynamic SQL in the module
Breaks ifDifferent owner (verified: SP in dbo over a table in a schema of another owner → Msg 229) · dynamic SQL · TRUNCATE and DDL · another DB (cross-database ownership chaining is disabled by default)
AlwaysEXECUTE on the module is checked, regardless of the EXECUTE AS
EXECUTE ASContext during the moduleNotes
CALLERThe callerDefault (except in queues); needs permissions on the objects if the chain is broken
SELFWhoever created/altered the moduleStored in sys.sql_modules.execute_as_principal_id
OWNERCurrent owner of the module (or of the schema)Singleton account (not role/group); not for DDL/logon triggers; shows as −2
'user_name'That DB userMust exist (not a group, role, certificate or built-in accounts); whoever creates the module needs IMPERSONATE; the user cannot be dropped while a module uses it
'login_name'That loginServer DDL triggers and logon triggers only

Applies to functions (except inline TVF), stored procedures, DML triggers and DDL/logon triggers (also to queues). The context is valid only during the module; inside it you can go back to the caller with EXECUTE AS CALLER / REVERT.

CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.uspChainOk AS SELECT TOP (1) OrderID FROM Sales.Orders ORDER BY OrderID;    -- EXECUTE only
GO
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.uspChainDyn
AS EXEC (N'SELECT TOP (1) OrderID FROM Sales.Orders ORDER BY OrderID');                         -- requires SELECT from the caller (Msg 229)
GO
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.uspChainDynOwner WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER
AS EXEC (N'SELECT TOP (1) OrderID FROM Sales.Orders ORDER BY OrderID');                         -- OK
GO
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.uspTruncateStaging WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER
AS TRUNCATE TABLE dbo.Staging;                                    -- TRUNCATE has no grantable permission
GO
GRANT EXECUTE ON dbo.uspChainOk TO ReportingUsers;                -- repeat for each SP
GRANT EXECUTE ON dbo.uspTruncateStaging TO ReportingUsers;
Platform: Azure SQL Database does not support cross-database ownership chaining, TRUSTWORTHY or EXECUTE AS LOGIN (use EXECUTE AS USER). On Managed Instance, EXECUTE AS USER fails for Entra users whose name differs from the login. Verify (Fabric): the limits page for SQL database in Fabric marks EXECUTE AS = No, but CREATE PROCEDURE/CREATE TRIGGER include the clause for Fabric: check in your environment. With OWNER, the owner must be resolvable by the server (in testing, with an unresolvable domain owner it failed with HResult 0x3C2C).

Module signing (alternative to EXECUTE AS / TRUSTWORTHY)

  1. Create the certificate (in the DB).
  2. Sign the module: ADD [ COUNTER ] SIGNATURE TO module_class::module_name BY CERTIFICATE | ASYMMETRIC KEY … (WITH PASSWORD if the private key is not protected by the database master key).
  3. Create a user without login FROM CERTIFICATE and give it the permissions the module needs.
  4. Grant EXECUTE on the module to the real users (they do not need permissions on the tables).
CREATE CERTIFICATE ModuleCert ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<StrongPassword>' WITH SUBJECT = 'Signs reporting procedures';
GO
ADD SIGNATURE TO dbo.uspChainDyn BY CERTIFICATE ModuleCert WITH PASSWORD = '<StrongPassword>';
GO
CREATE USER ModuleCertUser FROM CERTIFICATE ModuleCert;           -- user without login
GRANT SELECT ON Sales.Orders TO ModuleCertUser;                   -- permission used by the signed SP
GRANT EXECUTE ON dbo.uspChainDyn TO ReportingUsers;               -- the caller only needs EXECUTE
Signature: every character of the module is included in the signature and the signature is removed when the module is modified (it must be signed again). Requires ALTER on the object and CONTROL on the certificate/key. A signed scalar UDF is not inlineable.
ObjectPermission to create / use it
ViewCREATE VIEW in the DB + ALTER on the schema. Use: SELECT (or INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
FunctionCREATE FUNCTION + ALTER on the schema (+ EXECUTE on the UDT used; REFERENCES for SCHEMABINDING). Use: EXECUTE (scalar) or SELECT (TVF)
Stored procedureCREATE PROCEDURE + ALTER on the schema, or db_ddladmin. Use: EXECUTE
DML triggerALTER on the table or view
DDL triggerDatabase: ALTER ANY DATABASE DDL TRIGGER · Server/logon: CONTROL SERVER
User-defined table type (TVP)EXECUTE and REFERENCES on the type (or its schema/DB)

Learn lab flow (AdventureWorksLT, 45 min)

  1. Prerequisites: SQL Server 2019+ or Azure SQL Database, CREATE permissions and the AdventureWorksLT DB. Check with SELECT TOP (5) on SalesLT.Customer, SalesOrderHeader and Product.
  2. CREATE OR ALTER VIEW SalesLT.vCustomerOrders: JOIN of Customer and SalesOrderHeader with CONCAT(FirstName, ' ', LastName).
  3. CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dbo.AddOrderLineItem: SET NOCOUNT ON, BEGIN TRANSACTION, validates ProductID/SalesOrderID (ROLLBACK + THROW 50010/50011), inserts into SalesOrderDetail, recalculates SubTotal and COMMIT.
  4. CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.fnOrderTotal (scalar, ISNULL(@Total, 0.00)) and its use in a SELECT … GROUP BY.
  5. CREATE OR ALTER FUNCTION dbo.GetCustomerOrders (inline TVF) queried directly and with CROSS APPLY.
  6. Table dbo.OrderAudit + CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER SalesLT.trg_LogOrderTotalChange … AFTER INSERT, UPDATE (OldTotal = NewTotal − inserted + deleted); test it with an UPDATE of OrderQty.
  7. Cleanup: delete the AdventureWorksLT DB (closing existing connections).

The exam tests the exact signature (order, optional parameters, defaults), the return type, NULL behavior, the platform/status (GA or Preview) and choosing the right tool.

Skills measured covered:
  • Write common table expressions (CTEs)
  • Write queries that include window functions
  • Write queries that include JSON functions, such as JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_ARRAYAGG, JSON_CONTAINS, OPENJSON, and JSON_VALUE

Common table expressions (CTE) SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

Named result set that lives only for one statement: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE, DELETE or the SELECT of a CREATE VIEW. It is not materialized: each reference re-runs its query.

;WITH VentasCliente (CustomerID, Total) AS      -- optional column list
(
    SELECT CustomerID, SUM(Total) FROM dbo.Orders GROUP BY CustomerID
),
Top1 AS                                         -- comma between CTEs; can use the previous ones
(
    SELECT TOP (1) CustomerID, Total
    FROM VentasCliente
    ORDER BY Total DESC                         -- ORDER BY only with TOP / OFFSET-FETCH
)
SELECT * FROM Top1;                             -- 10 | 175.00
WITH Dup AS
(
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Email ORDER BY CustomerID) AS rn
    FROM dbo.Customers
)
DELETE FROM Dup WHERE rn > 1;                   -- deletes rows from the base table
RuleDetails
Preceding ;If the WITH is not the first statement in the batch, the previous one must end with ; (otherwise, Msg 319).
What can followA single SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/MERGE/DELETE statement that uses the CTE (or CREATE VIEW).
Multiple CTEsA single WITH, CTEs separated by commas. They can reference previous CTEs; forward references are not allowed.
Not allowed in the definitionORDER BY (except with TOP or OFFSET/FETCH), INTO, OPTION with hints, FOR BROWSE, a nested WITH and running a stored procedure.
Name and columnsUnique name within the WITH (it can match a table: the CTE takes precedence). No duplicate columns; the column list must match the number of columns in the SELECT.
FabricWarehouse and SQL analytics endpoint: standard and sequential CTEs are GA; nested: Preview; recursive: no.
Exam: “readability / reusing the same result within the same query” → CTE. “Referenced many times and expensive” → temporary table. “Variable-depth hierarchy” → recursive CTE.
Sources: Learn · Organize queries with common table expressions · Docs · WITH common_table_expression

Recursive CTE and MAXRECURSION SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

An anchor member + UNION ALL + a recursive member that references itself. It ends when an iteration returns no rows; the result is the union of all iterations.

WITH Org AS
(
    -- Anchor: root of the hierarchy
    SELECT EmployeeID, ManagerID, Name, 0 AS Lvl,
           CAST(Name AS nvarchar(400)) AS Path          -- same type in anchor and recursive
    FROM dbo.Employees WHERE ManagerID IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    -- Recursive: references Org only once
    SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.ManagerID, e.Name, o.Lvl + 1,
           CAST(o.Path + N' > ' + e.Name AS nvarchar(400))
    FROM dbo.Employees AS e
    JOIN Org AS o ON e.ManagerID = o.EmployeeID
)
SELECT EmployeeID, Lvl, Path
FROM Org
ORDER BY Path
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 50);        -- hint on the outer statement, not inside the CTE
WITH n AS (SELECT 1 AS i UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 200)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM n
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 0);         -- 200; without the option → Msg 530 when exceeding 100 levels

-- Alternative without recursion (SQL Server 2022+, compat 160):
SELECT value FROM GENERATE_SERIES(1, 200);
ItemValue / rule
MAXRECURSIONOPTION (MAXRECURSION n), n between 0 and 32767. Server default = 100. 0 = no limit. Only one per statement.
When exceededMsg 530 (maximum recursion 100 has been exhausted); the statement's effects are rolled back. 32768 → Msg 310.
Structure≥ 1 anchor and ≥ 1 recursive member; anchors before the first recursive member; only UNION ALL between the last anchor and the first recursive member. Implicit end (empty iteration).
ColumnsSame number and same type/length as the anchor (otherwise, Msg 240 → hence the CAST on Path). All result columns are nullable.
Not allowed in the recursive memberSELECT DISTINCT, GROUP BY, HAVING, PIVOT, scalar aggregation, TOP (Msg 461), LEFT/RIGHT/OUTER JOIN (Msg 462; INNER JOIN is allowed), subqueries and hints on the recursive reference. The CTE appears only once in its FROM.
Analytic functionsROW_NUMBER and similar ones in the recursive part operate on the set of each level, not on the whole CTE.
PlatformsSQL Server, Azure SQL and SQL DB in Fabric: yes. Fabric Warehouse, SQL analytics endpoint and Synapse: no.
Memorize: MAXRECURSION → default 100 · range 0–32767 · 0 = unlimited · exceeding = Msg 530 and statement rollback.
Cycles: if the data has cycles (A→B→A), the recursion does not end on its own; MAXRECURSION only breaks the loop (with an error). To avoid this, accumulate the path traversed and discard nodes already visited.
Learn vs docs: the unit generates a Numbers table from 1 to 1000 with OPTION (MAXRECURSION 366); it fails with Msg 530 (tested): MAXRECURSION counts iterations (1000 rows = 999 levels) and filtering in the outer CTE does not stop the recursion. You need ≥ 999, or limit with the WHERE of the recursive member.
Exam (knowledge check): “all employees who report to a manager at any level” → recursive CTE (not self-joins per level or window functions).
Sources: Learn · Organize queries with common table expressions · Docs · Recursive queries using CTEs · Docs · Query hints (MAXRECURSION) · Docs · GENERATE_SERIES

OVER clause: partition, order, frame and WINDOW SQL Server 2012+ Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

A window function calculates over a set of related rows without collapsing the result. General form: function(args) OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] [ORDER BY …] [ROWS | RANGE frame] ).

SELECT OrderID, CustomerID, OrderDate, Total,
       SUM(Total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID
                        ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID
                        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS RunningTotal,
       AVG(Total) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID
                        ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID
                        ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)         AS Mov2
FROM dbo.Orders;
SELECT v,
  SUM(v) OVER (ORDER BY v)                          AS def_range,  -- 1,5,5,8 (default frame = RANGE: ties together)
  SUM(v) OVER (ORDER BY v ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS rows_run,   -- 1,3,5,8
  LAST_VALUE(v) OVER (ORDER BY v)                   AS lv_default, -- 1,2,2,3 (= current row)
  LAST_VALUE(v) OVER (ORDER BY v
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS lv_full  -- 3,3,3,3
FROM (VALUES (1),(2),(2),(3)) AS t(v);
SELECT OrderID, CustomerID, Total,
       SUM(Total)   OVER w AS Running,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER w AS rn,
       COUNT(*)     OVER (w ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS cnt  -- extends the named window
FROM dbo.Orders
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY OrderDate, OrderID)  -- before the final ORDER BY
ORDER BY CustomerID, OrderID;
SituationEffective frame / rule
Without ORDER BYThe whole partition (and without PARTITION BY, the whole result set).
ORDER BY without ROWS/RANGEFor functions that accept a frame (aggregates, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE): RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
Short formROWS 5 PRECEDING = ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
ROWSPhysical offset in rows; supports n PRECEDING/FOLLOWING.
RANGEBy value: CURRENT ROW includes all the ties of the ORDER BY. Only UNBOUNDED and CURRENT ROW (with n PRECEDING → Msg 4194).
RequirementsROWS/RANGE require ORDER BY. Ranking, LAG/LEAD, NTILE, PERCENT_RANK and CUME_DIST do not accept a frame.
Not allowedDISTINCT inside an aggregate with OVER (Msg 10759). Window functions in WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING (Msg 4108: only SELECT and ORDER BY) → filter with a CTE or subquery.
WINDOWDetails
SyntaxWINDOW window_name AS ( [ reference_window_name ] [ PARTITION BY … ] [ ORDER BY … ] [ ROWS | RANGE … ] ) [ , …n ] — goes after WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING and before the ORDER BY.
UsageOVER w or OVER (w ROWS …). What is defined in WINDOW cannot be redefined in OVER (adding what is missing is allowed).
ReferencesA window can reference another (backward or forward); non-cyclic; only one reference per window.
AvailabilitySQL Server 2022 (16.x)+, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, SQL database in Fabric. Requires compat level ≥ 160; with a lower level the engine does not recognize WINDOW (Msg 102 in the test with 150).
Memorize: default with ORDER BY = RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING → CURRENT ROW. That is why LAST_VALUE “fails” (returns the current row) until you add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.
Performance: nonclustered index with the PARTITION BY columns and then the ORDER BY columns (same order/direction) + INCLUDE of the aggregated column. Window Aggregate operators can run in batch mode (columnstore, or rowstore with compat ≥ 150).
Sources: Learn · Apply window functions for analytics · Docs · OVER clause · Docs · WINDOW clause

Window functions: ranking, offset and analytic SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

Cheat table with signature, return type and behavior with ties/NULL. The ORDER BY in the OVER is required in all of them except the aggregates.

FunctionSignatureReturnsNotes (ties · NULL · frame)
ROW_NUMBERROW_NUMBER() OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] ORDER BY … )bigint1,2,3… unique even if there are ties (the order among ties is not deterministic: add a tiebreaker). Without ORDER BY → Msg 4112.
RANKRANK() OVER ( … )bigintTies = same rank and skips numbers (1,1,3).
DENSE_RANKDENSE_RANK() OVER ( … )bigintTies = same rank, no gaps (1,1,2).
NTILENTILE( integer_expression ) OVER ( … )bigintpositive n (int/bigint). If it does not divide evenly, the larger groups come first: 53 rows in 5 groups → 11,11,11,10,10.
LAGLAG( scalar_expression [ , offset [ , default ] ] ) [ IGNORE NULLS | RESPECT NULLS ] OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] ORDER BY … )Type of scalar_expressionoffset positive integer, default 1 (not negative). default = value if there is no row (omitted → NULL), compatible type. No frame. RESPECT NULLS is the default.
LEADLEAD( scalar_expression [ , offset [ , default ] ] ) [ IGNORE NULLS | RESPECT NULLS ] OVER ( … )Type of scalar_expressionSame as LAG but looks at following rows.
FIRST_VALUEFIRST_VALUE( [ scalar_expression ] ) [ IGNORE NULLS | RESPECT NULLS ] OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] ORDER BY … [ rows_range_clause ] )Type of the expressionFirst row of the frame.
LAST_VALUELAST_VALUE( [ scalar_expression ] ) [ IGNORE NULLS | RESPECT NULLS ] OVER ( … [ rows_range_clause ] )Type of the expressionLast row of the frame; with the default frame = current row → add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.
PERCENT_RANKPERCENT_RANK() OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] ORDER BY … )float(53)(rank − 1) / (rows − 1): 0 on the first row, 1 on the last; ties = same value; NULL counts as the lowest value; no frame.
CUME_DISTCUME_DIST() OVER ( … )float(53)Rows with value ≤ current ÷ total rows; range (0, 1]; no frame.
SUM · AVG · COUNT · MIN · MAXagg( expr ) OVER ( [PARTITION BY …] [ORDER BY … [frame]] )The aggregate's usual typeOptional ORDER BY: without it = the whole partition; with it = cumulative. No DISTINCT.
IGNORE NULLS / RESPECT NULLSAfter the parentheses of LAG/LEAD/FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE—SQL Server 2022+, Azure SQL DB and MI. Default RESPECT NULLS. (Fix in 2022 CU4 for LAG/LEAD + IGNORE NULLS.)
 
SELECT v,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY v DESC) AS rn,    -- 1,2,3,4,5
       RANK()       OVER (ORDER BY v DESC) AS rk,    -- 1,1,3,4,5
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY v DESC) AS drk,   -- 1,1,2,3,4
       NTILE(3)     OVER (ORDER BY v DESC) AS nt     -- 1,1,2,2,3
FROM (VALUES (100),(100),(90),(80),(70)) AS t(v);
SELECT ts, val,
       LAST_VALUE(val) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY ts
              ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS filled,         -- 10,10,10,40
       LAG(val, 1, -1) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY ts)          AS prev_non_null   -- -1,10,10,10
FROM (VALUES (1,10),(2,NULL),(3,NULL),(4,40)) AS t(ts, val)
ORDER BY ts;
WITH r AS
(
    SELECT CustomerID, OrderID, Total,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY Total DESC) AS rn
    FROM dbo.Orders
)
SELECT * FROM r WHERE rn <= 3;        -- ROW_NUMBER() cannot be used in the WHERE
NeedUse
Running total keeping the detailSUM() OVER (ORDER BY … ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) (with ROWS, ties are not added together).
Compare with the previous/next rowLAG / LEAD (better than a self-join or correlated subquery).
Exactly N rows per groupROW_NUMBER() in a CTE + WHERE rn <= N.
N per group including tiesRANK o DENSE_RANK.
Quartiles / percentilesNTILE(4), PERCENT_RANK, CUME_DIST.
Fill NULLs with the last known valueLAST_VALUE(x) IGNORE NULLS … ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
Exam (knowledge check): “running total ordered by date showing each order” → aggregate with OVER (ORDER BY …); not a correlated subquery, not a recursive CTE, not a self-join.
Watch out: the ORDER BY inside OVER does not sort the final result; add an ORDER BY to the SELECT. In ORDER BY ASC, NULLs are the lowest values.
Sources: Learn · Apply window functions for analytics · Docs · Ranking functions · Docs · NTILE · Docs · LAG · Docs · FIRST_VALUE · Docs · LAST_VALUE · Docs · PERCENT_RANK · Docs · CUME_DIST

JSON in T-SQL: function cheat table SQL Server 2016 / 2022 / 2025 Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

Full signature, return type and NULL behavior. What is marked 2025 exists only in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL MI (with the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy) and SQL database in Fabric.

FunctionSignatureReturnsNULL · modes · notes
ISJSONISJSON ( expression [ , json_type_constraint ] )
constraint: VALUE | ARRAY | OBJECT | SCALAR (2022+)		int 1/0; NULL if expression is NULLWithout constraint: 1 only for object or array (RFC 4627). VALUE accepts any JSON value (RFC 8259). Does not validate duplicate keys; never raises an error.
JSON_VALUEJSON_VALUE ( expression , path [ RETURNING data_type ] )nvarchar(4000) (input collation); with RETURNING, that typeScalars only. Object/array or nonexistent path → NULL (lax) / error (strict). JSON null → NULL. Value > 4000 chars → NULL (lax) / error (strict): use OPENJSON. RETURNING (2025) only if the input is json (with nvarchar/varchar → Msg 102 Incorrect syntax near 'RETURNING', tested); types: tinyint, smallint, int, bigint, decimal, numeric, float, real, (n)char, (n)varchar and their max variants, date, time, datetime2, datetimeoffset.
JSON_QUERYJSON_QUERY ( expression [ , path ] [ WITH ARRAY WRAPPER ] )nvarchar(max)Object/array only. path default $. Scalar or nonexistent → NULL (lax) / error (strict). WITH ARRAY WRAPPER (wildcards, ranges, last) documented only for json input. FOR JSON does not escape its result.
JSON_MODIFYJSON_MODIFY ( expression , path , newValue )
path: [append] [lax|strict] $.path		nvarchar (updated JSON)lax + NULL deletes the key; strict + NULL sets it to null. Only one change per call (nest calls). newValue does not accept text.
JSON_PATH_EXISTSJSON_PATH_EXISTS ( value_expression , sql_json_path )int 1/0; NULL if the input is NULLNever returns an error; supports [*]. SQL Server 2022+.
OPENJSONOPENJSON ( jsonExpression [ , path ] ) [ WITH ( colName type [ column_path ] [ AS JSON ] [ , …n ] ) ]Table key, value, type or the WITH oneCompat level ≥ 130. See the OPENJSON topic.
JSON_OBJECTJSON_OBJECT ( [ key : value [ , …n ] ] [ NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL ] [ RETURNING json ] )nvarchar(max) (json with RETURNING json)Default NULL ON NULL. JSON_OBJECT() → {}. 2022+ (RETURNING: 2025).
JSON_ARRAYJSON_ARRAY ( [ value [ , …n ] ] [ NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL ] [ RETURNING json ] )nvarchar(max) (or json)Default ABSENT ON NULL. JSON_ARRAY() → []. 2022+.
JSON_OBJECTAGGJSON_OBJECTAGG ( key : value [ NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL ] [ RETURNING json ] )nvarchar(max) (or json)Aggregate. Default NULL ON NULL. 2025; works with GROUPING SETS.
JSON_ARRAYAGGJSON_ARRAYAGG ( value_expression [ ORDER BY column_list ] [ NULL ON NULL | ABSENT ON NULL ] [ RETURNING json ] )nvarchar(max) (or json)Aggregate. Default ABSENT ON NULL. The inner ORDER BY sets the order of the elements (without it, the order is not guaranteed). 2025.
JSON_CONTAINSJSON_CONTAINS ( target_expression , search_value_expression [ , path_expression ] [ , search_mode ] )int 1 / 0 / NULLSee the JSON_CONTAINS and indexes topic. 2025; not in Fabric Warehouse.
modify methodjson_column.modify ( path , newValue )—Only on the json type (UPDATE t SET Body.modify('$.a', 1), SET @j.modify(…)); edits in place when it can; supports append.
FOR JSONFOR JSON { AUTO | PATH } [ , ROOT [ ( 'RootName' ) ] ] [ , INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES ] [ , WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER ]JSON text in a columnSQL Server 2016+. See the Building JSON topic.
Available sinceFunctions / features
SQL Server 2016 · Azure SQL · FabricISJSON(expr), JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, JSON_MODIFY, OPENJSON (compat 130), FOR JSON. Path as a variable: 2017+ and Azure SQL.
SQL Server 2022 (16.x)ISJSON(expr, constraint), JSON_PATH_EXISTS, JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAY.
SQL Server 2025 (17.x) · Azure SQL DB · MI* · SQL DB in Fabricjson type, JSON index, JSON_OBJECTAGG, JSON_ARRAYAGG, JSON_CONTAINS, RETURNING (in JSON_VALUE and constructors), WITH ARRAY WRAPPER, wildcards [*]/ranges/last, .modify(). Docs: json type and JSON index are GA; none of the above is listed as Preview (Oct 2026) and none requires PREVIEW_FEATURES or a specific compat level (tested from 130; only OPENJSON requires ≥ 130).
Memorize (defaults of the NULL clause): JSON_OBJECT → NULL ON NULL · JSON_ARRAY → ABSENT ON NULL · JSON_OBJECTAGG → NULL ON NULL · JSON_ARRAYAGG → ABSENT ON NULL. (Objects keep the key with null; arrays discard the element.)
Learn vs docs: the unit says that JSON_OBJECT/JSON_ARRAY/JSON_ARRAYAGG are in “SQL Server 2022 and later”. According to the current docs, JSON_ARRAYAGG and JSON_OBJECTAGG are from SQL Server 2025 (2022 only includes JSON_OBJECT/JSON_ARRAY). *MI: only with the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy.

JSON_VALUE vs JSON_QUERY vs JSON_MODIFY, paths and json type SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL GA

DECLARE @j nvarchar(max) = N'{"customer":{"id":12345,"name":"Contoso","active":true},
  "items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":5},{"sku":"B2","qty":3}],"tags":["sql","azure"]}';

SELECT JSON_VALUE(@j, '$.customer.name')      AS v_name,    -- Contoso
       JSON_VALUE(@j, '$.items[1].sku')       AS v_arr,     -- B2 (0-based arrays)
       JSON_VALUE(@j, '$.customer')           AS v_obj,     -- NULL (lax: not a scalar)
       JSON_QUERY(@j, '$.tags')               AS q_arr,     -- ["sql","azure"]
       JSON_VALUE(@j, 'lax $.nope')           AS v_missing, -- NULL
       JSON_PATH_EXISTS(@j, '$.items[*].sku') AS has_sku,   -- 1
       ISJSON(@j)                             AS is_json;   -- 1
-- JSON_VALUE(@j, 'strict $.nope') → Msg 13608 (the property does not exist)
DECLARE @info nvarchar(100) = N'{"name":"John","skills":["C#","SQL"]}';
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, '$.name', 'Mike');            -- updates
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, '$.surname', 'Smith');        -- inserts (lax)
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, 'append $.skills', 'Azure');  -- appends to the array
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, '$.surname', NULL);           -- lax + NULL = deletes the key
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, 'strict $.name', NULL);       -- strict + NULL = sets null
SET @info = JSON_MODIFY(@info, '$.tags', JSON_QUERY('["x","y"]'));  -- JSON_QUERY prevents it from being escaped as text
SELECT @info;  -- {"name":null,"skills":["C#","SQL","Azure"],"tags":["x","y"]}
CriterionJSON_VALUEJSON_QUERY
ExtractsA scalar (string, number, true/false)An object or array (valid JSON fragment)
Return typenvarchar(4000) (or RETURNING in json)nvarchar(max)
Path points to the wrong typeNULL (lax) / error (strict)NULL (lax) / error (strict)
Inside FOR JSONRegular text (it is escaped)Not escaped → JSON_QUERY(col) (without path) to embed existing JSON
IndexingComputed column + index, or JSON index (json)—
JSON_MODIFY · newValueThe path existslax (default)strict
NOT NULLYesUpdates the valueUpdates the value
NOT NULLNoTries to create the key (it may fail)Error
NULLYesDeletes the propertySets the value to null
NULLNoNo action (returns the input)Error
JSON pathRule
Mode and pathlax (default) or strict at the start: 'strict $.a.b'. The path can be a variable (SQL Server 2017+ and Azure SQL).
Keys$ = root; keys with spaces, dots or $ in double quotes: $."my key".
Arrays0-based ($.items[0]). Wildcard [*], range [0 to 2], list [0, 2] and [last] only with json input (ranges in ascending order; [last, 0] is invalid).
Duplicate keysJSON_VALUE/JSON_QUERY return the first one; OPENJSON returns all of them.

Native json type SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB / MI* SQL DB in Fabric GA

CREATE TABLE dbo.Docs (DocID int IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, Body json NOT NULL);
INSERT dbo.Docs (Body) VALUES ('{"user":"ann","tags":["sql","azure"]}');

UPDATE dbo.Docs SET Body.modify('$.user', 'ann2') WHERE DocID = 1;   -- in-place editing
SELECT CAST(Body AS nvarchar(max)) FROM dbo.Docs;                    -- json → text: explicit
AspectValue
StoragePre-parsed binary; strings in UTF-8 (Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8). Available at all compat levels.
Valid inputOnly object {} or array [] (or NULL). Scalars, true, null, empty string → Msg 13609. Duplicate keys: keeps the first.
Conversionsjson → char/varchar/nchar/nvarchar: explicit (implicit → Msg 257). char/nchar/varchar/nvarchar/vector → json: implicit or explicit. Other types (incl. sql_variant) are not allowed.
IndexesCannot be the key of a standard index (Msg 1978); can be an INCLUDE column or appear in the WHERE of a filtered index. JSON index available.
Limits2 GB · 32,000 unique keys · 7,998 bytes per key · 536,870,911 bytes per string value · 65,535 properties per object · 65,535 elements per array · 128 levels.

*Azure SQL MI: with the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy. Metadata for json requires drivers with JSONSUPPORT (SqlClient ≥ 6.0, JDBC ≥ 13.2.0); otherwise, the client sees varchar/nvarchar.

Exam: scalar to filter/compare → JSON_VALUE; keep structure (object/array) → JSON_QUERY; change a value → JSON_MODIFY (or .modify() if the column is json); property that “must exist” → strict; “may be missing” → lax (default).
Index without a JSON index: computed column + index: ALTER TABLE t ADD Cat AS CAST(JSON_VALUE(Data,'$.category') AS nvarchar(100)) PERSISTED; CREATE INDEX ix ON t(Cat);. Narrow the type with CAST: JSON_VALUE returns nvarchar(4000) = 8,000 bytes and the nonclustered key limit is 1,700 bytes (warning).
