OPENJSON: JSON → rows SQL Server 2016+ (compat 130) Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

Table-valued function that exposes a JSON document as a rowset. Without WITH it returns the default schema; with WITH you define columns, types and paths.

DECLARE @j nvarchar(max) = N'{"s":"John","n":45,"b":true,"z":null,"arr":["a","b"],"obj":{"o":1}}';
SELECT [key], value, type FROM OPENJSON(@j);
-- s|John|1 · n|45|2 · b|true|3 · z|NULL|0 · arr|["a","b"]|4 · obj|{"o":1}|5
DECLARE @j nvarchar(max) = N'{"orders":[{"id":1,"customer":{"name":"Ann"},"lines":[{"sku":"A"}],"total":10.5},
                                {"id":2,"customer":{"name":"Bob"},"lines":[],"total":7}]}';
SELECT * FROM OPENJSON(@j, '$.orders')
WITH (OrderID  int           '$.id',
      Customer nvarchar(50)  '$.customer.name',
      Total    decimal(10,2) '$.total',
      Lines    nvarchar(max) '$.lines' AS JSON);   -- AS JSON ⇒ the type must be nvarchar(max)
SELECT d.DocID, i.sku, i.qty
FROM dbo.Docs AS d
CROSS APPLY OPENJSON(d.Body, '$.items')            -- OUTER APPLY keeps the documents without items
     WITH (sku nvarchar(10) '$.sku', qty int '$.qty') AS i;
ItemRule
SyntaxOPENJSON ( jsonExpression [ , path ] ) [ WITH ( colName type [ column_path ] [ AS JSON ] [ , …n ] ) ]
Default schemakey nvarchar(4000) (BIN2 collation) · value nvarchar(max) · type int. Only first-level properties; in an array, key = index (0-based).
type codes0 null · 1 string · 2 number · 3 true/false · 4 array · 5 object
With WITHkey/value/type disappear. Columns are matched by exact name (case-sensitive, BIN2) or by column_path; no match → NULL (lax).
AS JSONReturns the fragment (like JSON_QUERY); the type must be nvarchar(max) (Msg 13618). Without AS JSON it returns a scalar (like JSON_VALUE: NULL in lax / error in strict if it is an object or array).
Compat level≥ 130 (with a lower level: Msg 208 Invalid object name; the other JSON functions work at any level). Does not apply if ALLOW_BUILTIN_TVF_IN_ALL_COMPAT_LEVELS = ON (Preview; Azure SQL DB and SQL DB in Fabric).
Exam: CROSS APPLY OPENJSON discards rows whose JSON is NULL, empty or has no elements; OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs. To join JSON with tables: OPENJSON … WITH + JOIN (module lab).
Sources: Learn · Process JSON data with built-in functions · Docs · OPENJSON · Docs · ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION

Building JSON: JSON_OBJECT, JSON_ARRAY, JSON_*AGG and FOR JSON SQL Server 2022 / 2025 Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

SELECT JSON_OBJECT('a':1, 'b':NULL)                 AS o_default,  -- {"a":1,"b":null}
       JSON_OBJECT('a':1, 'b':NULL ABSENT ON NULL)  AS o_absent,   -- {"a":1}
       JSON_ARRAY(1, NULL, 'x')                     AS a_default,  -- [1,"x"]        (ABSENT ON NULL)
       JSON_ARRAY(1, NULL, 'x' NULL ON NULL)        AS a_null,     -- [1,null,"x"]
       JSON_OBJECT('o':JSON_OBJECT('x':1), 'l':JSON_ARRAY(1,2)) AS nested; -- {"o":{"x":1},"l":[1,2]}
-- JSON_OBJECT() → {}   JSON_ARRAY() → []   RETURNING json → json type instead of nvarchar(max)
SELECT CustomerID,
       JSON_OBJECT('customer':CustomerID,
                   'orders':JSON_ARRAYAGG(OrderID ORDER BY OrderID)) AS j   -- {"customer":10,"orders":[1,2,3]}
FROM dbo.Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;

SELECT JSON_OBJECTAGG(k:v ABSENT ON NULL) AS obj                -- {"a":1,"c":3}
FROM (VALUES ('a',1),('b',NULL),('c',3)) AS t(k, v);
SELECT TOP (2) OrderID AS 'order.id', CAST(NULL AS int) AS Note
FROM dbo.Orders ORDER BY OrderID
FOR JSON PATH, ROOT('orders'), INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES;
-- {"orders":[{"order":{"id":1},"Note":null},{"order":{"id":2},"Note":null}]}
FOR JSONEffect
AUTOThe structure comes from the SELECT and its joins (tables nested per join).
PATHFull control; aliases with dots create nested objects ('order.customer.id').
ROOT('x')Wraps in {"x":[…]}; ROOT without a name → "root".
INCLUDE_NULL_VALUESIncludes null properties (omitted by default).
WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPERRemoves the [ ]: a single object.
OutputA text column; a large result set is split into several rows (concatenate on the client). In Fabric Warehouse it must be the last operator (not in subqueries).
CriterionFOR JSONJSON_OBJECT / JSON_ARRAY / *AGG
ScopeConverts the whole result set (at the end of the query)Build JSON values inside the SELECT, per row or per group (composable)
FormArray of objects; keys = column names/aliasesExplicit key : value pairs; NULL control per function
Nesting 1-NFOR JSON subqueries + JSON_QUERY, or AUTOJSON_ARRAYAGG inside JSON_OBJECT
VersionSQL Server 2016+2022+ (OBJECT/ARRAY) · 2025+ (*AGG, RETURNING json)
Exam (knowledge check): “nested JSON with an array of lines per customer from grouped rows” → JSON_OBJECT + JSON_ARRAYAGG. In versions prior to 2025, the alternative is FOR JSON PATH with subqueries.
Watch out: without ORDER BY inside JSON_ARRAYAGG, the order of the elements is not guaranteed. The constructors convert types like FOR JSON does (bit → true, date → ISO text, decimal → number) and escape special characters.

JSON_CONTAINS and JSON index SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB / MI* SQL DB in Fabric GA Not in Fabric Warehouse

DECLARE @j json = '{"tags":["sql","azure"],"a":1,"s":"hello world","o":{"x":[1,2,{"y":5}]}}';
SELECT JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 'sql',    '$.tags[*]')   AS in_array,   -- 1  (for arrays the [*] wildcard is required)
       JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 'python', '$.tags[*]')   AS not_in,     -- 0
       JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 1,        '$.a')         AS num,        -- 1  (the SQL type of the value matters)
       JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 'hello%', '$.s', 1)      AS like_mode,  -- 1  (search_mode 1 = LIKE)
       JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 5,        '$.o.x[*].y')  AS nested,     -- 1
       JSON_CONTAINS(@j, 'x',      '$.missing')   AS no_path;    -- NULL (nonexistent path)
-- Returns int: in WHERE it is compared → WHERE JSON_CONTAINS(Body, 'sql', '$.tags[*]') = 1
SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON;                                      -- required (Msg 1934 otherwise)
CREATE JSON INDEX ix_docs_body ON dbo.Docs (Body);            -- the whole document

CREATE JSON INDEX ix_docs2_body ON dbo.Docs2 (Body)
    FOR ('$.user', '$.tags')                                  -- only these paths (non-overlapping)
    WITH (OPTIMIZE_FOR_ARRAY_SEARCH = ON);                    -- default OFF
JSON_CONTAINS parameterDetails
target_expressionDocument to search. Docs: json or string with JSON. In SQL Server 2025 (17.0.1145) it only accepted json: nvarchar/varchar → Msg 8116; use CAST(x AS json) (verify on your build).
search_value_expressionSQL scalar (numeric, string, bit) or json; it is compared by its SQL type (unlike a predicate with JSON_VALUE, which always returns text). It does not accept json or the result of JSON_QUERY as the searched value.
path_expressionDocs: optional (default $); in practice required (without path → NULL). If it points to an array, wildcard [*] (auto-unwrap of the first level only). Supports lax/strict and variables.
search_mode0 (default) equality · 1 LIKE semantics (only with a string value).
Returnint 1 / 0 / NULL: NULL if any argument is NULL or the path does not exist.
CREATE JSON INDEXDetails
SyntaxCREATE JSON INDEX name ON table ( json_column ) [ FOR ( sql_json_path [ , …n ] ) ] [ WITH ( <option> [ , …n ] ) ] [ ON { filegroup | "default" } ]. Without FOR = $ (everything, up to 128 levels).
OptionsOPTIMIZE_FOR_ARRAY_SEARCH (default OFF) · FILLFACTOR (1–100; 0 = 100) · DROP_EXISTING (OFF) · ONLINE = OFF (ON → error) · ALLOW_ROW_LOCKS/ALLOW_PAGE_LOCKS (ON) · MAXDOP (accepted but uses 1 CPU) · DATA_COMPRESSION (appears in the syntax and also as “not supported” → verify).
RequirementsTable with a clustered PRIMARY KEY (< 32 columns, key < 128 bytes; heap → Msg 13672) and QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON.
Limits1 JSON index per json column (Msg 13681) · up to 249 per table · not on computed json columns, views, table variables or memory-optimized tables · non-overlapping paths ($.a and $.a.b → Msg 13683) · offline only (Sch-M) · not in index hints · changing paths = recreate.
Predicates it usesJSON_VALUE (=, also with RETURNING), JSON_PATH_EXISTS and JSON_CONTAINS. LIKE and IS [NOT] NULL: not supported.
Permissions · catalogALTER on the table, or sysadmin / db_ddladmin / db_owner · sys.json_indexes.
Statusjson type and JSON indexes: GA in SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL DB, MI (SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy) and SQL DB in Fabric.
CriterionComputed column + B-tree indexJSON index
VersionAny version with JSON functions (2016+)2025 / Azure SQL (GA)
Columnnvarchar/varchar (or json)Only json
CoversOne scalar property per computed columnThe whole document or chosen paths; arrays (OPTIMIZE_FOR_ARRAY_SEARCH)
PredicatesWHERE col = valueJSON_VALUE =, JSON_PATH_EXISTS, JSON_CONTAINS
Learn vs docs: the unit's example JSON_CONTAINS(@json, '"sql"', '$.tags') declares @json NVARCHAR(MAX) → Msg 8116 on 17.0.1145 (compilation error); with @json json it returns 0 (tested): the searched value is a SQL scalar ('sql', without JSON quotes) and the path to an array needs a wildcard ('$.tags[*]'). Also, JSON_CONTAINS returns int, not boolean (compare with = 1), unlike REGEXP_LIKE.
Sources: Learn · Process JSON data with built-in functions · Docs · JSON_CONTAINS · Docs · CREATE JSON INDEX

REGEXP_* functions: cheat table SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB / MI* SQL DB in Fabric GA

Five scalar + two table-valued functions, on the RE2 engine (Google). Optional parameters are chained from the right: to pass flags in REGEXP_SUBSTR you must supply start and occurrence first.

FunctionFull signatureReturnsDefaults · NULL · notes
REGEXP_LIKEREGEXP_LIKE ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , flags ] )boolean (predicate)Only in WHERE, CHECK, CASE WHEN, NOT REGEXP_LIKE(…); = 1 gives a syntax error (Msg 102). SARGable only if the pattern starts with ^. Requires compat 170.
REGEXP_REPLACEREGEXP_REPLACE ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , string_replacement [ , start [ , occurrence [ , flags ] ] ] ] )stringstring_replacement = ''; start = 1; occurrence = 0 (all). In the replacement: \1…\9 = group n (n > no. of groups → empty), \\ = literal backslash, & = the whole match according to the docs (see “Verify” below). No match or start > length → returns the original.
REGEXP_SUBSTRREGEXP_SUBSTR ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , start [ , occurrence [ , flags [ , group ] ] ] ] )stringstart = 1; occurrence = 1; group = 0 (the whole match; n = nth capture group). No match or start > length → NULL.
REGEXP_INSTRREGEXP_INSTR ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , start [ , occurrence [ , return_option [ , flags [ , group ] ] ] ] ] )intreturn_option: 0 = start (default), 1 = end (position after the last character); any other value → error. No match or start > length → 0.
REGEXP_COUNTREGEXP_COUNT ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , start [ , flags ] ] )intstart = 1 (< 1 → error, Msg 19301); start > length → 0.
REGEXP_MATCHES (TVF)REGEXP_MATCHES ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , flags ] )Table: match_id bigint · start_position int · end_position int · match_value (input type or varchar) · substring_matches jsonOne row per match; no matches → 0 rows. substring_matches = capture groups [{"value","start","length"}]. Requires compat 170.
REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE (TVF)REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE ( string_expression, pattern_expression [ , flags ] )Table: value (input type or varchar) · ordinal bigint (1-based)The pattern is the delimiter. No match → 1 row with the whole string. Requires compat 170.
ArgumentRule
string_expressionchar, nchar, varchar, nvarchar; (n)varchar(max) up to 2 MB per docs (see “Verify” below). A NULL argument → NULL result (tested on SUBSTR/REPLACE/INSTR/COUNT).
pattern_expressionchar, nchar, varchar, nvarchar; maximum 8,000 bytes.
flagsvarchar/char, max. 30 characters, can be combined ('ims'): i case-insensitive · c case-sensitive (default; '' = c) · m multi-line (^ and $ also per line) · s the . also matches \n. Contradictory flags: the last one wins ('ic' → case-sensitive; 'ci' → case-insensitive). Any other character → Msg 19303.
startint/bigint, 1-based, ≥ 1 (otherwise, error).
occurrencePositive integer: nth match (in REGEXP_REPLACE, 0 = all).
groupint ≥ 0 and ≤ no. of capture groups; 0 = the whole pattern.
Platform / requirementStatus
SQL Server 2025 (17.x)Available (GA). Do not exist in SQL Server 2022 or earlier.
Azure SQL Database · SQL database in FabricAvailable.
Azure SQL Managed InstanceOnly with the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy.
Fabric Data WarehouseScalars in Preview; the TVFs (REGEXP_MATCHES, REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE) are not supported.
Compatibility level170 for REGEXP_LIKE and the 2 TVFs; the other scalars work at any level (with compat < 170: Msg 195 / Msg 208). ALLOW_BUILTIN_TVF_IN_ALL_COMPAT_LEVELS (Preview, Azure SQL DB and SQL DB in Fabric) avoids it for the TVFs.
PREVIEW_FEATURESNot needed (regex is GA in SQL Server 2025). In SQL Server 2025 only the following require PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON: fuzzy matching (4 functions), CREATE VECTOR INDEX/VECTOR_SEARCH, half-precision vectors and change event streaming.
LimitationsNot in natively compiled stored procedures. Regex does not use collation (it matches by pattern/Unicode properties): it can differ from LIKE, especially on indexed columns with a linguistic collation. {n,m} counts ≤ 1,000.
Verify (RTM-GDR 17.0.1145 vs current docs): (1) the docs say that in string_replacement, & inserts the whole match; in the local build & came out literal ('[&]' → a[&]c) and \& did insert the match (\0 comes out literal). (2) The docs say all REGEXP_* functions accept (n)varchar(max) (≤ 2 MB); the local build gave Msg 19304 on REGEXP_REPLACE, REGEXP_MATCHES and REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE (LIKE/COUNT/SUBSTR/INSTR did work). It may depend on the installed CU.
Memorize: occurrence in REGEXP_REPLACE = 0 → all; in SUBSTR/INSTR = 1 → the first. group = 0 → full match. return_option 0 = start · 1 = end.
Exam: validate/filter → REGEXP_LIKE; extract → REGEXP_SUBSTR (with group for a part); clean/mask → REGEXP_REPLACE; count → REGEXP_COUNT; position → REGEXP_INSTR; all matches as rows (with groups in json) → REGEXP_MATCHES; split by pattern → REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE.

Regex in practice: RE2 dialect, verified examples and TVFs SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

SELECT CASE WHEN REGEXP_LIKE('ABC', 'abc', 'i') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END           AS like_i,  -- 1
       REGEXP_REPLACE('123-456-7890', '(\d{3})-(\d{3})-(\d{4})', '(\1) \2-\3') AS repl,    -- (123) 456-7890
       REGEXP_REPLACE('a1b2c3', '\d', 'X', 1, 2)                                AS repl2,   -- a1bXc3 (2nd match)
       REGEXP_SUBSTR('ana@contoso.com', '@(.+)$', 1, 1, 'i', 1)                 AS domain,  -- contoso.com (group 1)
       REGEXP_INSTR('abc123def45', '\d+', 1, 1, 1)                              AS end_pos, -- 7 (start would be 4)
       REGEXP_COUNT('banana', 'a')                                              AS cnt;     -- 3
SELECT match_id, match_value, start_position, end_position
FROM REGEXP_MATCHES('Learning #AzureSQL #AzureSQLDB', '#([A-Za-z0-9_]+)');
-- 1 | #AzureSQL | 10 | 18      2 | #AzureSQLDB | 20 | 30

SELECT p.PersonID, t.value AS Tag, t.ordinal
FROM dbo.People AS p
CROSS APPLY REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE(p.Tags, '\s*[,;]\s*') AS t;   -- 'python, sql ;c#' → python | sql | c#
CREATE TABLE dbo.Contacts
(
    Email varchar(320) CHECK (REGEXP_LIKE(Email, '^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$')),
    Phone varchar(20)  CHECK (REGEXP_LIKE(Phone, '^\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}$'))
);
RE2 elementSupported syntax
Classes. · [xyz] · [^xyz] · \d \D \s \S \w \W (ASCII only) · POSIX [[:alpha:]] · Unicode \pN, \p{Greek}
Anchors^ $ (with m: per line) · \A · \z · \b · \B (ASCII word boundary)
Repetitions* + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} and lazy *? +? ?? {n,m}?; counts ≤ 1,000
Groups(re) numbered · (?P<name>re) named · (?:re) non-capturing · (?i) inline flags
Not supportedLookahead/lookbehind (?=…) (?!…) and backreferences \1 inside the pattern → Msg 19300 (invalid perl operator / invalid escape sequence)
Learn vs docs (3 discrepancies): (1) the unit says it uses ECMAScript syntax; the engine is RE2 and does not support lookaround (its card-masking example with (?=…) fails). (2) The unit replaces with '$1 $2'; the correct form is '\1 \2' (tested: '($1) $2-$3' is returned literally). (3) The unit writes REGEXP_LIKE(…) = 1; it is a predicate and = 1 gives a syntax error.
Performance: to just check for a match, use REGEXP_LIKE (do not extract substrings). To make it use an index, anchor with ^ and use simple classes/quantifiers. Hints ASSUME_FIXED_MIN_SELECTIVITY_FOR_REGEXP / ASSUME_FIXED_MAX_SELECTIVITY_FOR_REGEXP adjust the cardinality of REGEXP_LIKE; CE feedback applies them on its own (trace flag 16268 disables it).
Sources: Learn · Match patterns with regular expressions · Docs · Regular expressions (RE2) · Docs · REGEXP_LIKE

Fuzzy string matching Preview SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB / MI* SQL DB in Fabric

Four functions that measure character similarity between two strings (typos, omitted or transposed letters, abbreviations). The documentation marks them Preview on all platforms.

FunctionFull signatureReturnsScale · notes
EDIT_DISTANCEEDIT_DISTANCE ( character_expression, character_expression [ , maximum_distance ] )intMinimum no. of insertions, deletions, substitutions and transpositions (Damerau-Levenshtein / OSA, per docs). 0 = identical. maximum_distance (int, optional): can cut the calculation short; if the actual distance exceeds it, it returns maximum_distance + 1; omitted or negative → actual distance; NULL → NULL.
EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITYEDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY ( character_expression, character_expression )int0–100, 100 = identical: (1 − edit_distance / GREATEST(len1, len2)) × 100. ('Colour','Color') → 83.
JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCEJARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE ( character_expression, character_expression )float0–1: 0 = identical, 1 = nothing in common. Favors the common prefix. ('Colour','Color') → 0.0333.
JARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITYJARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITY ( character_expression, character_expression )int0–100, 100 = identical. ('Colour','Color') → 97.
AspectRule
ArgumentsCharacter constant, variable or column; not varchar(max)/nvarchar(max) (Msg 8116). Tested on 17.0.1145: both arguments must be of the same type (varchar/char with varchar/char, or nvarchar/nchar with nvarchar/nchar); mixing them → Msg 8116 (use CAST). Any NULL → NULL.
Enable (SQL Server 2025)ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON; (default OFF; not recommended in production; it also exists in Azure SQL DB and SQL DB in Fabric). Without it: Msg 195 not a recognized built-in function name. They do not require a specific compat level (tested from 130).
CollationsDocs: supports Windows and binary collations (BIN/BIN2); non-binary SQL_* ones are not supported → apply COLLATE to the arguments. Mixing different collations → Msg 468.
Platforms (Applies to)SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL MI (update policy SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date), SQL database in Fabric and SQL analytics endpoint/Warehouse in Fabric.
 
ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON;   -- required in SQL Server 2025 (Preview)
GO   -- separate batch: the function name is resolved when the batch is compiled

SELECT EDIT_DISTANCE('Colour', 'Color')            AS ed,      -- 1
       EDIT_DISTANCE('Chocolate', 'Sweets')        AS ed_full, -- 8
       EDIT_DISTANCE('Chocolate', 'Sweets', 2)     AS ed_max,  -- docs: 3 (= max + 1); on build 17.0.1145 it returned 2
       EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY('Colour', 'Color') AS eds,     -- 83
       JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE('Colour', 'Color')    AS jwd,     -- 0.0333333333333333 (distance: 0 = identical)
       JARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITY('Colour', 'Color')  AS jws;     -- 97
DECLARE @q nvarchar(100) = N'John Smith';

SELECT CustID, FullName,
       EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY(@q, FullName) AS sim
FROM dbo.Cust
WHERE FullName LIKE N'J%'                           -- 1) sargable filter / equality on an indexed column
  AND EDIT_DISTANCE(@q, FullName) <= 3               -- 2) absolute threshold (or sim >= 70 as a percentage)
ORDER BY sim DESC;
ScenarioChooseThreshold used in the docs examples
Typos in short/medium text (products, addresses, duplicates)EDIT_DISTANCE (absolute threshold) or EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY (%, normalizes by length)EDIT_DISTANCE <= 2 · EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY >= 75
People's names (the common prefix weighs more)JARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITY / JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCEJARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITY > 90 · JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE <= .05
Equivalence of meaning (synonyms)Not fuzzy → embeddings / vector search—
Validating a formatNot fuzzy → REGEXP_*—
Exam (knowledge check): “find 'John Smith' when the database has 'Jon Smyth'” → JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE (optimized for names, weights the common prefix); not LIKE '%ohn%', nor SOUNDEX, nor REGEXP_LIKE. Watch out: the unit presents it as a similarity; in the docs it is a distance (0 = identical).
Learn vs docs: the unit treats JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE as a similarity (“1 = identical”, MARTHA/MARHTA ≈ 0.96). Per docs it is a distance (0 = identical; MARTHA/MARHTA → 0.0389); the similarity is JARO_WINKLER_SIMILARITY (int 0–100 → 96). The unit also does not mention that they are Preview or PREVIEW_FEATURES, and presents EDIT_DISTANCE only as Levenshtein.
Verify (local build SQL Server 2025 17.0.1145 RTM-GDR): with maximum_distance exceeded it returned maximum_distance (not +1) and with 0 it returned the actual distance; ('ab','ba') gave 2 even though the docs mention transpositions; 'SQL' vs 'sql' gave 3 even with a CI collation. That is why the example filters with EDIT_DISTANCE(a,b) <= n and it is best to normalize with LOWER()/UPPER().
Performance: each call traverses both strings (O(n·m) cost). Reduce candidates first (equality on indexed columns, LIKE 'Jo%', same postal code) and apply fuzzy only to that subset.

SQL Graph: AS NODE/AS EDGE, MATCH and SHORTEST_PATH SQL Server 2017+ (SHORTEST_PATH 2019+) Azure SQL DB / MI SQL DB in Fabric GA Not in Fabric Warehouse

CREATE TABLE dbo.Person (PersonID int PRIMARY KEY, Name nvarchar(50)) AS NODE;
CREATE TABLE dbo.friendOf (since date) AS EDGE;      -- also: CREATE TABLE dbo.likes AS EDGE;

INSERT dbo.friendOf ($from_id, $to_id, since)        -- the edge stores $node_id, not the business key
SELECT a.$node_id, b.$node_id, '2024-01-01'
FROM dbo.Person AS a, dbo.Person AS b
WHERE a.Name = N'Alice' AND b.Name = N'John';
-- Alice's friends (the arrow goes from p1 to p2; equivalent to MATCH(p2<-(f)-p1))
SELECT p2.Name
FROM dbo.Person AS p1, dbo.friendOf AS f, dbo.Person AS p2
WHERE MATCH(p1-(f)->p2) AND p1.Name = N'Alice';

-- Friends of friends: a different edge alias per hop
SELECT DISTINCT p3.Name
FROM dbo.Person AS p1, dbo.friendOf AS f1, dbo.Person AS p2, dbo.friendOf AS f2, dbo.Person AS p3
WHERE MATCH(p1-(f1)->p2-(f2)->p3) AND p1.Name = N'Alice';
SELECT p1.Name AS StartName,
       STRING_AGG(p2.Name, '->') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path,       -- John | Jacob->Mary | …
       LAST_VALUE(p2.Name)       WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS LastName,
       COUNT(p2.Name)            WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Hops
FROM dbo.Person AS p1,
     dbo.friendOf FOR PATH AS fo,                          -- FOR PATH on the tables in the repeated pattern
     dbo.Person   FOR PATH AS p2
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(p1(-(fo)->p2){1,3}))             -- {1,n} = 1 to n hops; + = 1 or more
  AND p1.Name = N'Alice';
SELECT p1.Name, STRING_AGG(p2.Name, '->') WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH) AS Path, r.Name AS Restaurant
FROM dbo.Person AS p1, dbo.friendOf FOR PATH AS fo, dbo.Person FOR PATH AS p2,
     dbo.likes AS l, dbo.Restaurant AS r
WHERE MATCH(SHORTEST_PATH(p1(-(fo)->p2){1,5}) AND LAST_NODE(p2)-(l)->r)
  AND p1.Name = N'Alice';

CREATE TABLE dbo.worksAt                              -- edge constraint: only Person → Restaurant
(CONSTRAINT ec_works CONNECTION (dbo.Person TO dbo.Restaurant)) AS EDGE;
TopicRule
Pseudo-columnsNode: $node_id. Edge: $edge_id, $from_id, $to_id. When inserting edges, $from_id/$to_id are supplied (values of $node_id). UPDATE is not possible on them (Msg 271): delete and reinsert.
MATCHOnly with node/edge tables, in the WHERE of a SELECT. “ASCII art” pattern: node-(edge)->node or node<-(edge)-node; the direction is always explicit.
RepetitionsThe alias of a node can be repeated; that of an edge cannot (Msg 13903). No OR/NOT with MATCH (Msg 13905); AND is allowed with other predicates and between patterns: MATCH(a-(e1)->c AND b-(e2)->c).
No resultsThe arrow almost always goes the opposite way from how $from_id/$to_id were inserted.
SHORTEST_PATHOnly inside MATCH. Quantifiers: only + (1 or more) and {1,n} (n a positive integer; there is no *). Returns one shortest path (the first one found) per pair, without weights; it does not return all paths. With many hops, try OPTION (HASH JOIN) and/or OPTION (MAXDOP 1).
FOR PATHRequired on each node/edge table of the repeated pattern (otherwise, Msg 13948). Their columns cannot be projected directly (Msg 13961): use path aggregates.
Path aggregatesSTRING_AGG, LAST_VALUE (nodes only), SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX + WITHIN GROUP (GRAPH PATH). COUNT(*) does not exist (syntax error).
LAST_NODE(alias)Chains a second pattern from the last node of the path (or merges two paths). Only inside SHORTEST_PATH/MATCH.
Edge constraintCONNECTION ( node_table TO node_table [ , … ] ) [ ON DELETE { NO ACTION | CASCADE } ]; inserting a disallowed edge → Msg 547.
LimitationsNot allowed: temporary (#/##), table types/variables, system-versioned, memory-optimized or external. No cross-database queries on graph objects. Pseudo-columns cannot be used as the order column of an ordered clustered columnstore.
PlatformsDoes not exist in SQL Server 2016 or in Fabric Data Warehouse. Allowed in SQL database in Fabric, but node/edge tables are not mirrored to OneLake.
Exam: many-to-many relationships, multiple parents, variable depth or “shortest path” → graph + MATCH/SHORTEST_PATH. Simple single-parent hierarchy → recursive CTE (or hierarchyid). Fixed one-level relationships and attribute filters → relational joins with indexes.
Sources: Learn · Traverse relationships with graph queries · Docs · MATCH (SQL Graph) · Docs · SHORTEST_PATH · Docs · CREATE TABLE (SQL Graph) · Docs · SQL Graph architecture (limitations)

Correlated subqueries, EXISTS and APPLY SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

A correlated subquery (repeating subquery) references columns of the outer query: logically it is evaluated once for each outer row (the optimizer usually rewrites it as a join).

SELECT p.ProdID, p.Price
FROM dbo.Prod AS p
WHERE p.Price > (SELECT AVG(p2.Price) FROM dbo.Prod AS p2 WHERE p2.CatID = p.CatID);

SELECT p.ProdID,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.Prod AS q                 -- must return ONE value per row (aggregate / TOP 1)
        WHERE q.CatID = p.CatID AND q.Price > p.Price) AS higher
FROM dbo.Prod AS p;
SELECT c.CatID FROM dbo.Cat AS c
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Prod AS p WHERE p.CatID = c.CatID);        -- categories with products

SELECT c.CatID FROM dbo.Cat AS c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.Prod AS p WHERE p.CatID = c.CatID);    -- without products

SELECT c.CatID FROM dbo.Cat AS c
WHERE c.CatID NOT IN (SELECT p.CatID FROM dbo.Prod AS p);   -- 0 rows if any p.CatID is NULL
SELECT c.CatID, t.ProdID, t.Price
FROM dbo.Cat AS c
CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP (2) p.ProdID, p.Price        -- categories with no rows disappear
             FROM dbo.Prod AS p
             WHERE p.CatID = c.CatID
             ORDER BY p.Price DESC) AS t;            -- with OUTER APPLY they are kept (NULL columns)
NeedUse
Compare each row with a value calculated for its groupCorrelated subquery in WHERE (or AVG() OVER (PARTITION BY …))
Does a related row exist / not exist?EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (NULL-safe)
Top-N per groupCROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP (n) … ORDER BY …) o ROW_NUMBER()
Previous / next rowLAG / LEAD (simpler than a correlated TOP 1 … ORDER BY)
Invoke a TVF per row (OPENJSON, REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE, STRING_SPLIT)CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY
Columns from several tables with no per-row calculationJOIN
RuleDetails
Single valueWith an unmodified comparison operator (=, <, >…) or in the SELECT list, the subquery must return one value (otherwise, Msg 512). With ANY/ALL/IN it can return a list.
ORDER BYOnly with TOP/OFFSET (otherwise, Msg 1033). No COMPUTE/INTO/FOR BROWSE. Up to 32 nesting levels.
EXISTSReturns TRUE/FALSE; the column list is ignored (by convention, SELECT 1 or *).
NOT IN + NULLIf the subquery returns any NULL, NOT IN returns no rows. Fix: NOT EXISTS or WHERE col IS NOT NULL. <> ALL is equivalent to NOT IN.
Name resolutionAn unqualified column that is not in the subquery's table is resolved against the outer query without error: WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM T2) with a only in T1 returns all rows of T1. Always qualify with aliases.
APPLYleft_source { CROSS | OUTER } APPLY right_source. The right side can use columns from the left (TVF or derived table); not the other way around. CROSS: no rows on the right → the left row is discarded. OUTER: it is kept with NULLs.
PerformanceIndex on the correlation columns (e.g. (CatID, Price)); check the plan (SET STATISTICS IO ON). Docs: there is normally no performance difference between a subquery and its equivalent without one; sometimes a join improves the existence check.
Learn vs docs: the unit claims that EXISTS “typically outperforms” IN. The documentation only says there is normally no difference between equivalent formulations; the verifiable difference is semantic (NOT IN with NULL).
Exam: “customers without orders” → NOT EXISTS; “products above the average of their category” → correlated subquery or window; “the 3 most expensive in each category” → CROSS APPLY … TOP (3) or ROW_NUMBER().
Sources: Learn · Compare rows with correlated subqueries · Docs · Subqueries · Docs · FROM clause (APPLY) · Docs · EXISTS

TRY…CATCH and ERROR_* functions SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

BEGIN TRY
    SELECT 1/0;                                -- Msg 8134
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH                                    -- END TRY must be immediately followed by BEGIN CATCH
    SELECT ERROR_NUMBER()    AS num,           -- 8134
           ERROR_SEVERITY()  AS sev,           -- 16
           ERROR_STATE()     AS st,            -- 1
           ERROR_PROCEDURE() AS proc_name,     -- NULL (did not occur inside an SP/trigger)
           ERROR_LINE()      AS ln,
           ERROR_MESSAGE()   AS msg;           -- Divide by zero error encountered.
END CATCH;
FunctionReturnsNote
ERROR_NUMBER()intError number (e.g. 2627 = PK violation).
ERROR_SEVERITY()intSeverity.
ERROR_STATE()intState.
ERROR_PROCEDURE()nvarchar(128)NULL if the error did not occur inside a stored procedure or trigger.
ERROR_LINE()intLine within the routine that caused the error.
ERROR_MESSAGE()nvarchar(4000)Full text with the parameters substituted.
Memorize: the ERROR_* functions return NULL outside a CATCH, but work from anywhere in the CATCH scope (including a stored procedure called from it) and inside natively compiled procs. In a nested CATCH they return those of the current CATCH.
Caught by TRY…CATCHNOT caught
SeverityExecution errors with severity > 10 that do not close the connection (≥ 20 only if the connection is still alive)Notices/messages with severity ≤ 10; severity ≥ 20 that terminates the session
Connection—Attention (the client cancels or the connection is broken); KILL by an administrator
CompilationIf it occurs at a lower level than the TRY (EXEC('…'), sp_executesql, called SP)At the same level: syntax/compilation errors, statement-level recompilation and object name resolution (e.g. SELECT * FROM NonexistentTable → Msg 208 reaches the caller)
RuleDetails
StructureBEGIN TRY … END TRY BEGIN CATCH … END CATCH [;]. It cannot span multiple batches (GO) or blocks (BEGIN…END, IF…ELSE). Not supported in user-defined functions (Msg 443).
NestingA TRY or a CATCH can contain another TRY…CATCH. An error inside a CATCH without a nested TRY propagates to the caller.
Flow controlExecution continues after END CATCH (if it is the last thing in an SP/trigger, it returns to the caller). GOTO can jump within the same block or out of it, but not into it.
To the appThe caught error does not reach the application: rethrow it with THROW (or return it with RAISERROR/SELECT).
RAISERROR in TRYSeverity 11–19 → jumps to the CATCH; severity ≤ 10 → no (the TRY continues).
Exam: “what does TRY…CATCH NOT catch?” → syntax/compilation and name resolution errors at the same level, severity ≥ 20 that closes the connection, attention, KILL, severity ≤ 10.
Sources: Learn · Handle errors with TRY…CATCH · Docs · TRY…CATCH · Docs · ERROR_NUMBER · Docs · ERROR_PROCEDURE · Docs · ERROR_MESSAGE

THROW vs RAISERROR, XACT_ABORT, XACT_STATE() and the rollback pattern SQL Server Azure SQL SQL DB in Fabric GA

SET XACT_ABORT, NOCOUNT ON;                       -- recommended in stored procedures
BEGIN TRY
    BEGIN TRANSACTION;
        UPDATE dbo.Prod   SET Price = Price * 1.05 WHERE CatID = 1;
        UPDATE dbo.Orders SET Total = Total * 1.05 WHERE CustomerID = 10;   -- if it fails, the 1st is also rolled back
    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;       -- without the IF: Msg 3903 if there is no transaction
    THROW;                                        -- rethrows the original error (number, severity, message, line)
END CATCH;
THROW 51000, N'The record does not exist.', 1;    -- Msg 51000, Level 16, State 1
GO   -- each statement in its own batch: THROW aborts the batch

RAISERROR (N'Insufficient stock for "%s". Available: %d, ordered: %d', 16, 1, N'Widget', 5, 10);  -- Msg 50000
GO

DECLARE @m nvarchar(2048) = FORMATMESSAGE(N'Value %d out of range', 42);
THROW 50010, @m, 1;                               -- THROW + FORMATMESSAGE = formatting with THROW
SET XACT_ABORT ON;
BEGIN TRY
    BEGIN TRANSACTION;
        INSERT dbo.Cat (CatID, Name) VALUES (1, N'Duplicada');   -- violates the PK (example)
    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    IF XACT_STATE() = -1 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;    -- uncommittable (XACT_ABORT ON + error): can only be rolled back
    ELSE IF XACT_STATE() = 1 COMMIT TRANSACTION;  -- committable: business decision
    THROW;
END CATCH;
CriterionTHROWRAISERROR
SyntaxTHROW [ { error_number | @var } , { message | @var } , { state | @var } ] [ ; ]RAISERROR ( { msg_id | msg_str | @local_variable } , severity , state [ , argument [ , …n ] ] ) [ WITH option [ , …n ] ]
Error no.int, 50,000–2,147,483,647; does not need sys.messages (any other number → Msg 35100)msg_id from sys.messages (> 50,000, via sp_addmessage); with msg_str the number is 50000
Messagenvarchar(2048); no printf formatting (use FORMATMESSAGE); % reserved (write %%)printf (%d %i %s %u %o %x %X, flags/width/precision); ≤ 2,047 characters; ≤ 20 arguments
SeverityAlways 16; THROW; in a CATCH keeps that of the original errorParameter: 0–18 any user; 19–25 only sysadmin/ALTER TRACE and WITH LOG (otherwise, Msg 2754); ≥ 20 fatal (closes the connection); ≤ 10 informational (does not trigger CATCH)
Statetinyint 0–2550–255 (negative → 1)
SET XACT_ABORT ONHonors it: rolls back the transaction and aborts the batchDoes not honor it: the batch continues and the transaction stays open (outside TRY; tested nuance: inside a TRY with XACT_ABORT ON, RAISERROR with severity 16 also leaves the transaction uncommittable, XACT_STATE() = −1)
OtherTHROW; without parameters only inside a CATCH (Msg 10704 outside it). The previous statement must end in ; (otherwise, Msg 102)Options WITH LOG (up to 440 bytes in the error log), NOWAIT (sent immediately), SETERROR. In Azure SQL DB/MI there is no sp_addmessage
Recommended useNew codeCompatibility / formatted messages
ItemBehavior
SET XACT_ABORT { ON | OFF }ON: an execution error terminates and rolls back the whole transaction. OFF (default for statements; in triggers the default is ON): sometimes only the statement is rolled back and the transaction continues (depending on severity, it may be rolled back entirely). Does not affect compilation errors. Applied at execution time, not at parse time.
XACT_STATE() → smallint1 active, committable transaction · 0 no transaction · −1 active but uncommittable transaction (reads only or a full ROLLBACK; no COMMIT or savepoint). It rolls back by itself when the batch ends.
@@TRANCOUNTBEGIN TRAN +1 · COMMIT −1 · ROLLBACK (without savepoint) → 0. Does not detect uncommittable transactions; XACT_STATE does not detect nested transactions.
Memorize: THROW → number ≥ 50000 · state 0–255 · severity 16 · ; before it · honors XACT_ABORT. RAISERROR → severity 0–18 unrestricted, 19–25 with WITH LOG · printf · does not honor XACT_ABORT. IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK before rethrowing.
Learn vs docs: (1) the unit says that with XACT_ABORT ON the transaction is “normally already rolled back” on reaching the CATCH; inside a TRY it is left uncommittable (XACT_STATE() = −1, @@TRANCOUNT stays at 1; tested): an explicit ROLLBACK is required. (2) It says that THROW “always includes a stack trace”; the documentation does not mention it: THROW only sets the line and procedure, with severity 16. (3) It says that after THROW/RAISERROR the ERROR_* functions return NULL; tested: after RAISERROR inside the CATCH they still return the original error, and after THROW; the batch ends. (4) It says that state ranges from 1 to 255; the THROW doc allows 0–255.
Exam (knowledge check): “procedure that updates several tables and fails after the first one” → TRY…CATCH with IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK in the CATCH and rethrow with THROW. XACT_ABORT alone is not enough, nor is checking @@ERROR after each statement, nor savepoints per table.
Sources: Learn · Handle errors with TRY…CATCH · Docs · THROW · Docs · RAISERROR · Docs · SET XACT_ABORT · Docs · XACT_STATE · Docs · @@TRANCOUNT

Exact file paths, admin toggles, requirements and order of steps are tested.

Skills measured covered:

Map of AI tools for SQL: what to use where SSMS 22+ Fabric

Two assistants: GitHub Copilot (in the IDE: SSMS, VS Code + MSSQL extension, Visual Studio) and Copilot in Fabric (in the Fabric portal). MCP gives them access to the real schema, queries and resources. Common capabilities: code completion, natural language → T-SQL, explain, optimize and error assistance.

Security (1/2): what data travels and what controls exist

Prompts and context are sent to cloud models. Before enabling, evaluate: data classification (PII, financial, health), compliance, intellectual property (a proprietary schema can be a trade secret) and access control (align licenses with DB permissions).

ToolWhat is sent to the modelRetention / training
GitHub CopilotYour prompt, the code you edit, relevant open files, schema and SQL version when there is a connection, query/tool resultsSSMS: does not retain prompts, responses or metadata and does not train models (GitHub Copilot Trust Center)
Copilot in FabricPrompt, meta-prompt, structure (schema) and conversation history; table contents only if you direct itAzure OpenAI managed by Microsoft; no training and no sharing between customers; no retention for abuse monitoring
Copilot in SQL databaseSession messages, executed queries, error messages and schemasOnly accesses the schema visible to the user
ControlWhereDetails
Copilot policiesGitHub → enterprise/org → AI controlsApply to users with a Business/Enterprise license. The enterprise sets the policy or lets the orgs decide; between orgs in the same company, the least restrictive one usually wins
MCPMCP servers in Copilot and Restrict MCP access to registry servers policies (AI controls → MCP)Per-server allowlist/denylist in managed-settings.json (copilot/ folder of the .github-private repo): allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, with matchers serverUrl (supports *), serverCommand (exact command + args) or serverName (not a security control). Deny wins; with an allowlist, anything not listed is blocked. Applies in VS Code, Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app (changelog 2026-08-06); SSMS 22.7+ honors the allow list from AI controls → MCP
ModelsEditor preview features policy (Preview policy)In Business/Enterprise the admin must enable it for certain models in VS Code/SSMS
Filtering and public code (Learn)Org policies in GitHubLearn: content filtering prevents harmful patterns (e.g. SQL injection) and org policies control which repos use Copilot and whether suggestions can match public code
Content exclusionRepo / Org / Enterprise → Copilot → Content exclusionOnly Business and Enterprise. Paths in YAML (fnmatch). SSMS 22.4.1+ honors it (completions and chat)
AuditingAudit log → action:copilotChanges to plan/licenses/policies and agent activity on GitHub.com; retention 180 days
Content exclusion is not absolute: GitHub's matrix shows for VS Code → Chat ✔, Edit ✘, Agent ✘; Copilot CLI and Agent mode in IDEs do not support it; it is not guaranteed with third-party MCP servers either, it does not apply to symlinks or to repos on remote file systems, and Copilot can use indirect semantic information from the IDE (types, hovers). Do not use it as the only control for secrets.
Auditing: the GitHub audit log does not include the prompts of local sessions (you need your own logging, e.g. hooks). It records licenses, policies and agents on GitHub.com.
Exam: “organization with regulated data” → review classification/compliance/IP/access, use policies and content exclusion (Business/Enterprise), an MCP allowlist and least-privilege DB accounts. Never trained on your prompts (Copilot in SSMS and Copilot in Fabric).
Sources: Learn · Interpret security impact · Docs · Admin controls (SSMS) · Docs · Content exclusion (GitHub) · Docs · Audit logs (GitHub) · Docs · Privacy and security of Copilot in Fabric

Security (2/2): minimum permissions, execution, prompt injection and secrets

Memorize: Copilot approval is not a security boundary; the boundary is the SQL Server permission system. Copilot runs with your login (no extra permissions). In Ask mode (SSMS) it classifies the query as read-only before running it, but that is not a boundary either. SSMS Agent mode is READ_ONLY by default.
RiskHow it happensMitigation
Exposed credentialsPasswords or connection strings in prompts, in instruction files or in a committed mcp.jsonEnvironment variables, inputs with "password": true, .env outside Git, Key Vault; review before committing
Excessive privilegeThe tool uses a login with more permissions than neededDedicated read-only account (schema only if sufficient); agentExecuteAsUser; never sa/dbo; separate dev/test/prod
Insecure generated SQLBroad GRANT/REVOKE, concatenated dynamic SQL, SELECT that exposes too much, DROP/TRUNCATEReview everything: least privilege, sp_executesql with parameters, views/SPs to limit columns; test outside production
Prompt injectionUntrusted text (comments, tool results, web) with commands like “IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS”Two-step URL approval, review diffs, Workspace Trust (Restricted Mode), sandbox, do not chain tools without reviewing
ExfiltrationData from one tool sent to another tool or to third partiesLimit active tools (tools picker), server allowlist, private network
Data sampling (Learn)Some MCP configurations send data samples to the model to improve suggestionsKnow what is transmitted and align it with the data policy; if the schema is enough, do not grant data read access
Untrusted MCP server / rug-pullA local server runs code with your permissions or changes its tools after they are approvedReview publisher/command; trust prompts; Visual Studio resets approvals on notifications/tools/list_changed; sandboxEnabled (macOS/Linux only)
Auto-approvalAllow always, Allow all, AutopilotApprove per session; disable by policy (ChatToolsAutoApprove in VS Code)

Network and operations: client IP allowed in the Azure SQL firewall, private endpoints/VPN in sensitive environments, service principals for automated or shared access, and monitoring of MCP server usage.

Exam: “the AI only needs the schema” → dedicated read-only account with no data read permissions. “How to protect credentials” → environment variables / input prompts and never paste them into prompts or save them in files the AI can see. “Always review” GRANT/REVOKE, dynamic SQL and data exposure.

Enable GitHub Copilot: SSMS, VS Code and administration SSMS 22+

SSMS: installation and sign-in

  1. Open the Visual Studio Installer, choose the SSMS installation → Modify.
  2. On the Workloads tab check AI Assistance (all the workloads it enables are required) → Modify.
  3. In SSMS click the GitHub Copilot badge (top right) → Open Chat Window to Sign In → Sign in (or Sign up for Copilot Free).
  4. Verify: connect a query editor, open the chat (Ctrl+\, Ctrl+C or View → GitHub Copilot Chat) and ask “What tables are in this database?”.

Status badge (top right): active (signed in with Copilot access) · inactive (not signed in, no subscription or expired credentials → Add another account / Open Chat Window to Sign In / Refresh your GitHub credentials) · unavailable (network, service failure or expired plan) · not installed (workload missing → Install Copilot).

What Copilot offers in SQL database (portal) and limits

Features

  • Chat pane: NL → T-SQL and Q&A about documentation
  • Code completion: Tab accepts; a leading -- comment gives context
  • Quick actions: Fix and Explain on the highlighted query
  • From SSMS 22 / MSSQL ext: completions, chat and execution plan analysis

Limitations

  • Does not modify an existing query in the editor (only iterates on what it generated before inserting it)
  • Only sees the schema, not the data
  • Chat pane not available with Private Link enabled and Public Access disabled
  • Does not run queries on its own; in SSMS/VS Code Agent mode asks for approval
Fabric Copilot capacity: ≥ F2/P1 and only in the home region; the Fabric admin authorizes and the capacity admin assigns users; one per user (the most recent one) and it takes precedence over the workspace capacity; does not support Fabric AI functions.
Exam: “Copilot does not appear” → trial SKU? capacity < F2/P1? region outside the US/EU boundary without the cross-geo setting? tenant switch off or limited to another security group? Pro/PPU workspace without a Copilot capacity? Enabling it for the whole tenant without planning raises capacity consumption: use security groups.

Complete instruction files for T-SQL (ready to copy)

# T-SQL project guidelines

## Environment
- Local: SQL Server 2025 (17.x) in a container. Cloud: Azure SQL Database.
- All T-SQL must run on both. Avoid features unavailable in Azure SQL Database.

## Naming
- Tables: PascalCase, singular (Customer, OrderDetail). Columns: PascalCase.
- Procedures: usp_ActionEntity (usp_GetCustomerOrders). Views: vw_EntityName.
- Constraints: PK_Table, FK_Child_Parent. Indexes: IX_TableName_ColumnName.

## T-SQL style
- Always schema-qualify objects (dbo.Customer). Never use SELECT *.
- ANSI JOIN syntax only. Use EXISTS instead of COUNT(*) for existence checks.
- Procedures: SET NOCOUNT ON; TRY...CATCH with THROW; explicit transaction for DML.

## Security
- Never generate GRANT to public. Never concatenate user input: use sp_executesql with parameters.
- Never include passwords, keys or connection strings; use placeholders.
- Do not generate DROP or TRUNCATE unless explicitly requested.
---
applyTo: "**/*.sql"
---
# T-SQL conventions

## File template
Every .sql file MUST begin with:
-- Author: <name> | Created: <YYYY-MM-DD> | Purpose: <description>
SET ANSI_NULLS ON;
GO
SET QUOTED_IDENTIFIER ON;
GO

## Conventions
- NVARCHAR for text, BIGINT for keys, DATETIME2(7) for timestamps.
- Every table has createdAt and updatedAt: DATETIME2(7) NOT NULL DEFAULT GETUTCDATE().
- Name constraints: PK_table, FK_child_parent, UQ_table_column, CK_table_column, DF_table_column.

## Avoid
- Deprecated syntax (no *= joins). Do not generate stored procedures unless asked.
---
description: 'Generate a T-SQL stored procedure that follows team standards'
agent: 'ask'
---
Create a stored procedure named ${input:procedureName:usp_ActionEntity}.
Purpose: ${input:purpose}

Requirements:
- SET NOCOUNT ON, TRY...CATCH with THROW, explicit transaction for data changes.
- Schema-qualified objects, explicit column lists, parameters typed like the columns.
- Follow [T-SQL conventions](../instructions/tsql.instructions.md).
  • What to include: target platform/version, naming, schema-qualify, error handling template, security rules (no GRANT to public, parameterize, no secrets), performance (indexes, EXISTS), what not to generate and an example of the pattern.
  • Showing the pattern is more effective than describing it; vague instructions (“use good names”) give vague results.
Discrepancy with Learn: the Learn prompt file example uses {{procedureName}} and says to reference it with #. The documented VS Code syntax is ${input:variableName} (optional ${input:var:placeholder}) and it is invoked as /name. On the exam, the idea is: prompt file = .prompt.md in .github/prompts, a reusable template with parameters.
Memorize: repo-wide .github/copilot-instructions.md · path-specific .github/instructions/*.instructions.md + applyTo · prompts .github/prompts/*.prompt.md · front matter applyTo, excludeAgent, agent, model, tools.
Sources: Learn · Create and configure instruction files · Docs · Custom instructions for T-SQL (MSSQL ext) · Docs · Prompt files in VS Code

SSMS: database instructions, CONSTITUTION.md and execution context SSMS 22.3+ / 22.7+ Azure SQL Fabric

The instructions live inside the database as extended properties (AGENTS.md format) and travel with it; they apply to any Copilot user in that DB. Available in SQL Server, Azure SQL DB, MI and SQL database in Fabric (sp_addextendedproperty).

MechanismExact property nameScopeNotes
Database instructionAGENTS.mdObject (schema, table, column…)Only one per object; SSMS 22.3+
Database constitutionCONSTITUTION.mdThe database (class 0)Highest precedence; can include agentExecuteAsUser front matter (SSMS 22.7+)
 
EXECUTE sp_addextendedproperty
    @name = N'AGENTS.md',
    @value = N'Revenue is defined as SUM(NetAmount) excluding refunds recorded in Finance.Refunds.',
    @level0type = N'SCHEMA', @level0name = N'Finance',
    @level1type = N'TABLE',  @level1name = N'CompanyRevenue';
USE SalesDB;
-- 1) Dedicated user without login and with minimum permissions
CREATE USER GHCP_DB_User WITHOUT LOGIN;
GRANT SELECT  ON SCHEMA::Sales TO GHCP_DB_User;
GRANT EXECUTE ON SCHEMA::Sales TO GHCP_DB_User;
-- 2) Whoever uses Copilot needs IMPERSONATE on that user
GRANT IMPERSONATE ON USER::GHCP_DB_User TO [CONTOSO\dbdev];
-- 3) Constitution: YAML front matter (---) at the start of the value
EXECUTE sp_addextendedproperty
    @name = N'CONSTITUTION.md',
    @value = N'---
agentExecuteAsUser: GHCP_DB_User

---
## Coding standards
- Always use explicit column lists. Do not use SELECT *.
- Use schema-qualified names (Sales.Orders).
### Restricted operations
- Do not generate TRUNCATE TABLE statements.
- Do not generate DROP statements without an existence check.';
SELECT name, CAST(value AS NVARCHAR(MAX)) AS ConstitutionContent
FROM sys.extended_properties
WHERE class = 0 AND name = N'CONSTITUTION.md';

EXECUTE sp_updateextendedproperty @name = N'CONSTITUTION.md',
    @value = N'---
agentExecuteAsUser: New_GHCP_User

---
Updated constitution content.';

EXECUTE sp_dropextendedproperty @name = N'CONSTITUTION.md';
Rule / limitDetails
Size@value is sql_variant ≤ 7,500 bytes (≈ 3,750 NVARCHAR characters): concise instructions
Names@name must be exactly AGENTS.md or CONSTITUTION.md; the front matter is delimited by --- and the rest is the body
Permissions to create themdb_owner or db_ddladmin (the latter not on the database itself); or ALTER/CONTROL on the object
Ask modeCannot modify the DB: Copilot generates the sp_addextendedproperty and you run it
Extended property limitationsNot on memory-optimized tables; not replicated after the initial synchronization
agentExecuteAsUserDatabase user (granular, per database) or SQL login (server-wide). Per-object AGENTS.md cannot override it. EXECUTE AS is used; the connected user needs IMPERSONATE (without it, Copilot does not work: this is by design and is used to block users). Do not use sa/dbo
Default modeAgent mode is READ_ONLY; the docs say it can be changed to READ_WRITE “in the mcp.json” without giving the key. In SSMS 22.9 the mcp.json of the sql-tools server (…\Common7\IDE\Extensions\Microsoft\SSMS.CopilotUiTools\McpServer\) defines "env": { "SQLtools__ExecutionMode": "READ_ONLY" } (the binary also contains READ_WRITE). It is not officially documented and the 22.10.2 release notes say that execution permissions now depend on the connected SQL account → Verify in your version. Always limited by SQL permissions
Exam: “business rules that travel with the DB” → extended property AGENTS.md; “standards for the whole DB and run as a low-privilege account” → CONSTITUTION.md + agentExecuteAsUser + IMPERSONATE. The security boundary is still the SQL permission, not the constitution.
Memorize: AGENTS.md (object, 1 per object) · CONSTITUTION.md (database, highest precedence) · agentExecuteAsUser · 7,500 bytes · SSMS 22.3 (DB instructions) / 22.7 (execution context).

MCP: architecture, transports and mcp.json configuration

Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets an assistant discover and call external tools and data. Client-server model: MCP host (VS Code, SSMS, Visual Studio, Claude…) → MCP client (connector inside the host) → MCP server (exposes tools and, optionally, resources and prompts). Transports: stdio (local process) and streamable HTTP (remote; sse as a fallback). Key messages: tools/list and tools/call.

Key (VS Code format)ScopeValues / notes
serversrootMap of name → configuration (camelCase, no spaces, unique)
inputsrootSecrets: id, type (promptString | pickString | command), description, password (default false), default, options. They are used as ${input:id} and stored in the secure store
typeserverstdio | http | sse
command, args, cwd, env, envFilestdiocommand required; env accepts strings, numbers or null; do not use docker -d (it must run in the foreground)
url, headers, oauth.clientIdhttp/sseurl required; http tries streamable HTTP and falls back to SSE; with oauth VS Code opens the browser on the first connection
dev, sandboxEnabled, sandboxstdioDevelopment mode (watch, debug); sandbox on macOS/Linux only, and with it tool confirmations are auto-approved
ClientFileRoot key
VS Code (workspace).vscode/mcp.jsonservers
VS Code (user)Profile mcp.json (MCP: Open User Configuration)servers

      "password": true
    }
  ]
}
Watch out: in VS Code, Visual Studio and SSMS the root is servers; portable files and other clients (e.g. Claude Desktop, Fabric npx examples) use mcpServers. When copying an example, change the key. The ${input:…} variables are not forwarded to portable Copilot harness sessions. (Learn shows the header value masked; the usual value is Bearer <token>.)
Exam: MCP needs Agent mode; when you add a server, its tools stay disabled in SSMS/Visual Studio until you check them; go to the tools list and verify the server status. If the server “does not appear” → JSON syntax error in mcp.json.
Security: Visual Studio subscribes to notifications/tools/list_changed and, if the server changes its tools, resets the approvals (anti rug-pull); VS 2026 18.7+ asks for re-trust when the configuration or the capabilities change. A local stdio server runs code on your machine: review the publisher and command.

MCP for SQL Server / Azure SQL: SQL MCP Server (Data API builder) SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL SQL database in Fabric DAB 2.0 GA

SQL MCP Server is Microsoft's open-source solution (included in Data API builder ≥ 1.7; use 2.0) that exposes entities (tables, views, stored procedures) as 7 typed DML tools with RBAC, caching, OTEL telemetry and health checks. It is configured with dab-config.json; requires .NET 9+ according to the quickstart (the CLI installation page still says .NET 8). It does not support NL2SQL (“NL2DAB” model: deterministic SQL generated by DAB's Query Builder) and does not perform DDL (data only). MCP protocol 2025-06-18; streamable HTTP and stdio transports.

ToolToggle runtime.mcp.dml-tools.*What it does / parameters
describe_entitiesdescribe-entitiesEntities and operations allowed for the role (reads the config, not the DB). nameOnly, entities. Returns field names/descriptions, no types or PK
create_recordcreate-recordINSERT (tables): entity, data
read_recordsread-recordsSELECT on table/view: entity, select, filter (OData), orderby (array), first, after. No JOIN; cached result
update_recordupdate-recordUPDATE by PK: entity, keys, fields
delete_recorddelete-recordDELETE by PK: entity, keys
execute_entityexecute-entityStored procedure: entity, parameters
aggregate_recordsaggregate-records2.0+ only: function (count/sum/avg/min/max), field ("*" for count), filter, distinct, groupby, having, orderby, first, after; query-timeout 1–600 s (default 30)
PropertyDefaultNotes
runtime.mcp.enabledtrueDefault true in the runtime reference; but the stdio page says that if the mcp block is missing or enabled is false, dab start --mcp-stdio does not start → set "mcp": { "enabled": true } explicitly
runtime.mcp.path"/mcp"HTTP only (ignored in stdio)
runtime.mcp.descriptionnullSent as instructions in initialize
runtime.mcp.dml-toolstrueBoolean or an object per tool; a globally disabled tool does not appear in list_tools
Entity mcpenabled{"dml-tools": false} excludes the entity; {"custom-tool": true} (stored procedures only) registers the SP as a named tool
runtime.host.authentication.providerUnauthenticated (2.0)Everything runs as anonymous; authenticated/custom roles are never activated
 
dab init --database-type mssql --connection-string "@env('MSSQL_CONNECTION_STRING')" --host-mode Development --config dab-config.json
dab add Products --source dbo.Products --permissions "anonymous:read" --description "Toy store products with inventory, price, and cost."
dab update Products --fields.name Id --fields.primary-key true --fields.description "Product Id"
dab update Products --fields.name Price --fields.description "Retail price"
dab start --config dab-config.json
dab start --mcp-stdio role:anonymous --config dab-config.json
{
  "data-source": { "database-type": "mssql", "connection-string": "@env('MSSQL_CONNECTION_STRING')" },
  "runtime": {
    "mcp": {
      "enabled": true,
      "path": "/mcp",
      "description": "Product catalog (read-only)",
      "dml-tools": {
        "describe-entities": true,
        "create-record": false,
        "read-records": true,
        "update-record": false,
        "delete-record": false,
        "execute-entity": true,
        "aggregate-records": { "enabled": true, "query-timeout": 30 }
      }
    }
  },
  "entities": {
    "GetBookById": {
      "source": { "type": "stored-procedure", "object": "dbo.get_book_by_id" },
      "mcp": { "custom-tool": true },
      "permissions": [ { "role": "anonymous", "actions": [ "execute" ] } ]
    }
  }
}
{
  "servers": {
    "sql-mcp-server": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "dab",
      "args": ["start", "--mcp-stdio", "role:anonymous", "--loglevel", "error", "--config", "${workspaceFolder}/dab-config.json"]
    },
    "sql-mcp-http": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:5000/mcp" }
  }
}
Path to SQLWhat it isIdentity and limits
MSSQL ext (VS Code)Tools the extension contributes to Agent mode (not a server you configure)The ext's connection profile; each tool asks for approval; DDL possible depending on your permissions
SSMS Agent modeBuilt-in local MCP server sql-tools (22.7+)Your login or agentExecuteAsUser; READ_ONLY by default
SQL MCP Server (DAB)Server you host: typed CRUD over entitiesDAB role (role:<name> in stdio; JWT/Entra over HTTP; OBO in 2.0); no DDL or NL2SQL
Azure MCP ServerMicrosoft MCP server for Azure resourcesEntra ID + Azure RBAC; for Azure SQL there are 13 control-plane tools (create/delete/update/rename DB and server, firewall rules, elastic pools, Entra admins): does not run T-SQL
Exam: “connect an agent to SQL in a secure and governed way” → SQL MCP Server (entities + RBAC + descriptions), stdio locally and HTTP in the cloud (e.g. Azure Container Apps: https://<fqdn>/mcp, health at /health). “Explore/change schema locally” → MSSQL ext / SSMS, not SQL MCP Server. For production: Entra ID authentication (not anonymous), managed identity, Key Vault, CORS and rate limiting.
Watch out: without fields/descriptions the agent only sees entity names and guesses columns: describe purpose, units, format and valid values (dab update … --fields.description). orderby must be an array. The per-tool toggle exists only at the global level; read_records does no JOIN (use a view or SP). The SQL MCP hub page says “six” tools and the reference says “seven”: there are 7 (the 7th, aggregate_records, is 2.0+). Learn says the Azure MCP Server lets you “query your databases”, but its Azure SQL tools are for management.
DAB 2.0 (GA): aggregate_records, custom tools, Unauthenticated provider by default, On-Behalf-Of (Entra ID, mssql only) and role inheritance named-role → authenticated → anonymous. In stdio: role:<name> (default anonymous), auth forced to Simulator, request max. 1 MB.

MCP for Fabric lakehouse: data agent, Warehouse/SQL endpoint, Core and local Fabric DW MCP: Preview

For a lakehouse, the Learn route is to publish a Fabric data agent as an MCP server and connect the client with its URL. Depending on the task, there are other Fabric servers:

ServerEndpoint / installationWhat it exposesWhen
Data agent as MCPhttps://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/workspaces/{WorkspaceId}/dataagents/{DataAgentId}/agent1 tool = the agent itself (its description is the tool's description); responses grounded in OneLake dataNatural-language questions about lakehouse, warehouse, semantic model, KQL DB…
Data Warehouse MCP Previewhttps://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/dataPlane/sqlEndpoint (global) · …/dataPlane/workspaces/<workspace-id>/items/<item-id>/sqlEndpoint (item-scoped)1 tool: executeSQL (T-SQL with approval); Warehouse and SQL analytics endpointRun T-SQL against the SQL analytics endpoint
Fabric Core MCPhttps://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/coreWorkspaces, items, roles, folders, capacities, shortcuts and OneLake data access rolesCreate/manage resources; does not query lakehouse tables
Fabric MCP (local)VS Code extension fabric.vscode-fabric-mcp-server or npx -y @microsoft/fabric-mcp@latest server start --mode allOffline API docs/specs, OneLake (files), core and Data FactoryDevelopment; upload/download OneLake files

Data agent as MCP server

  • F2+ or P1+ capacity with Fabric enabled; cross-geo AI settings (processing and storing) depending on region.
  • At least one source with data (warehouse, lakehouse, semantic model, KQL DB, mirrored database or ontology) and read permission.
  • Published data agent: a URL built by hand also fails if it is not published.
  1. Create the data agent, add the lakehouse and write a clear, specific description (it will be the tool's description).
  2. Publish the data agent.
  3. Agent → Settings → Model Context Protocol tab: copy the MCP server URL (it also shows the server name, the tool name and description, and lets you download mcp.json).
  4. VS Code: create .vscode/mcp.json → Add Server → HTTP → paste the URL → name → Allow and sign in with your Microsoft account.
  5. Enable Agent mode, choose the model and ask; the server appears among the tools.
{
  "servers": {
    "fabric-lakehouse-agent": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/workspaces/<WorkspaceId>/dataagents/<DataAgentId>/agent"
    },
    "fabric-dw-global": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/dataPlane/sqlEndpoint"
    },
    "fabric-core": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/core"
    },
    "fabric-mcp-local": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@microsoft/fabric-mcp@latest", "server", "start", "--mode", "all"]
    }
  }
}
ServerAuthentication
Data agentFabric Bearer token in Authorization (user or service principal), scope https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/.default; client with streamable HTTP. No dynamic client registration: clients that depend on it do not connect. Long questions: MCP tasks (tasks/get, tasks/cancel)
CoreOAuth 2.0 with Microsoft Entra ID (browser flow); operates with the identity's Fabric permissions (does not grant extra permissions)
Data WarehouseUser identity with its Fabric/SQL permissions (sign-in with your Microsoft account); each executeSQL requires approval
Localaz login or service principal with AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID and AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH (or AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET); the offline docs tools do not require auth. Toolsets: fabricMcp.enabledServices = core, docs, onelake, datafactory (empty = all); fabricMcp.serverMode = single | namespace | all (default all; equivalent to the --mode flag); fabricMcp.readOnly (default false) disables the operations that modify resources
Exam: “connect an assistant to a Fabric Lakehouse” → publish a data agent as an MCP server and use the MCP endpoint URL (not the MSSQL ext, nor Blob Storage connection strings, nor GitHub Actions). “T-SQL on the SQL analytics endpoint” → Data Warehouse MCP (executeSQL). “Create workspace/lakehouse” → Core MCP.
Compliance: data agent responses consumed via MCP can leave the Fabric compliance boundary/region and are processed under the MCP client's terms. Core uses the identity's RBAC: an autonomous client can take destructive actions → least privilege and review every tool call. The local server does not emit Fabric audit logs on its own.
Discrepancy with Learn: Learn cites the ms-fabric.vscode-fabric-mcp-server extension; the Marketplace and the current docs use fabric.vscode-fabric-mcp-server. Fabric's npx examples use mcpServers: in VS Code/Visual Studio use servers. Status: Data Warehouse MCP = Preview (its doc title); data agent: the concept page says generally available while the “Release status of AI and Copilot in Fabric” table lists it as Preview; Core and local show no status label in their docs → Verify.
