Module 5Domain 2 · 35–40%

Implement data security and compliance with SQL

Defense in depth for SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL and SQL database in Fabric: encryption (Always Encrypted, cell-level, TDE), Dynamic Data Masking, Row-Level Security, permissions, passwordless access (Microsoft Entra / Managed Identity), auditing and security of model and API endpoints (REST, GraphQL, MCP). The exam tests choosing the right technique and knowing syntax, permissions and limitations.

Skills measured covered:
  • Design and implement data encryption, including Always Encrypted and column-level encryption
  • Design and implement Dynamic Data Masking
  • Design and implement Row-Level Security (RLS)
  • Design and implement object-level permissions
  • Implement secure database access, including passwordless
  • Implement auditing
  • Secure model endpoints, including Managed Identity
  • Secure GraphQL, REST, and MCP endpoints

Which technique to use when: AE vs cell-level vs TDE vs DDM vs RLS vs permissions

Each layer covers a different threat and they can be combined (e.g. TDE as a baseline + Always Encrypted on the most sensitive columns + RLS + auditing).

Encryption: TDE vs cell-level vs Always Encrypted

CriterionTDECell-level (ENCRYPTBYKEY)Always Encrypted (AE)
Protects againstTheft of data/log files and backups (at rest)Reading specific columns without access to the keyDBA, cloud operator or malware on the server (the engine never receives the key)
Who encryptsThe engine, transparently, at page level (I/O)The engine, with T-SQL (ENCRYPTBYKEY/DECRYPTBYKEY)The client driver; the server only sees ciphertext (with an enclave, it operates inside the enclave)
KeysDEK in the DB protected by a certificate in master (Azure SQL: TDE protector = managed certificate or key in Key Vault)In the DB: DMK → certificate/asymmetric key → symmetric keyCMK outside the DB (Key Vault, cert store, HSM) + encrypted CEK in the DB
User with permissionsSees plaintext (TDE does not prevent it)Sees plaintext only if they can open the keyWithout access to the CMK, sees only ciphertext
App changesNoneThe T-SQL changes (open key, functions, varbinary column)Driver with Column Encryption Setting=Enabled and typed parameters
QueriesAllMust decrypt; ciphertext is not indexed in a useful wayDeterministic: =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, equi-JOIN; randomized: none (with enclave: ranges, LIKE, ORDER BY…)
AvailabilitySQL Server; Azure SQL DB/MI (ON by default); Fabric SQL DB: managed at-rest encryptionSQL Server, Azure SQL DB/MI, Fabric SQL DBSQL Server 2016+, Azure SQL DB/MI. Not in Fabric SQL DB

DDM vs RLS vs GRANT/DENY

CriterionDynamic Data MaskingRow-Level SecurityPermissions (GRANT/DENY)
What it doesObfuscates values in the query resultFilters (FILTER) or blocks (BLOCK) rowsAllows/denies actions on objects and columns
Data on diskUnchanged (plaintext)UnchangedUnchanged
Who bypasses itUNMASK or CONTROL (db_owner, sysadmin); inference via ad hoc queriesNobody: also applies to dbo/db_owner unless the predicate allows itsysadmin and object owners cannot be denied
GranularityColumn (UNMASK: DB, schema, table, column)Row, per table and per DML operationDB → schema → object → column
Ideal forSupport, development, reporting without full valuesMulti-tenant, salesperson/manager, hierarchiesLeast privilege, separation by schemas and roles

If the scenario says… → choose

ScenarioTechnique
Encrypt files and backups without touching the appTDE
The DBA / cloud operator must not see SSN or cardsAlways Encrypted
Decrypt with T-SQL, keys inside the DB, no special driverCell-level (symmetric key)
Equality / JOIN on an encrypted column, without enclaveAE deterministic + _BIN2 collation
LIKE, ranges or ORDER BY on encrypted dataAE with secure enclaves + randomized
Support only sees the last 4 digitsDDM partial()
Each tenant / salesperson only sees their rowsRLS (FILTER + BLOCK AFTER INSERT/UPDATE)
A role reads the table but not one columnDENY SELECT on the column / view / per-column GRANT
Who read what and whenAuditing
Multi-year logs, DBA-proof (Azure SQL)Azure SQL auditing to Blob Storage with immutable storage policy (Allow protected append writes)
App Service → Azure SQL without secretsManaged identity (system-assigned) + Microsoft Entra authentication
AI agent / API: only certain tablesRole with minimum permissions (DAB: per-entity/field permissions; MCP read-only)
Exam: TDE does not protect against users with permissions; AE does protect against the DBA; DDM is not a strong security control (it can be inferred with ad hoc filters); RLS applies even to db_owner/dbo; DDM and AE cannot be combined on the same column.
Sources: Learn · Protect data with encryption · Docs · Always Encrypted · Docs · Dynamic data masking · Docs · Row-level security

Always Encrypted: keys (CMK/CEK) and DDL SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Client-side encryption: the driver encrypts and decrypts; the engine only stores ciphertext and key metadata. Two keys: the CEK encrypts the column data; the CMK encrypts one or more CEKs and lives in an external key store. T-SQL cannot generate keys or encrypt/decrypt data (only exception: in-place encryption with an enclave via ALTER COLUMN): use SSMS, PowerShell (SqlServer module) or sqlpackage.

  1. Create the CMK in the key store (Key Vault, Windows certificate store, HSM).
  2. CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY: metadata only (provider + path).
  3. Generate the CEK on the client, encrypt it with the CMK and register it with CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY.
  4. Encrypt the columns (ENCRYPTED WITH); existing data is encrypted outside the engine (or in place with an enclave).
  5. The app connects with Column Encryption Setting=Enabled.
CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY MyCMK
WITH (
    KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAME = 'AZURE_KEY_VAULT',
    KEY_PATH = 'https://myvault.vault.azure.net/keys/MyCMK/abc123'  -- Key URL
);

CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY MyCEK
WITH VALUES (
    COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = MyCMK,
    ALGORITHM = 'RSA_OAEP',
    ENCRYPTED_VALUE = 0x01700000016C006F00  -- generated by the tool; never in plaintext
);

CREATE TABLE dbo.Employees (
    EmployeeID int PRIMARY KEY,
    SSN char(11) COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2
        ENCRYPTED WITH (COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = MyCEK,
                        ENCRYPTION_TYPE = DETERMINISTIC,
                        ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256') NOT NULL,
    Salary money
        ENCRYPTED WITH (COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = MyCEK,
                        ENCRYPTION_TYPE = RANDOMIZED,
                        ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256') NOT NULL
);

Key store providers and KEY_PATH format

KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAMEStoreKEY_PATH
'AZURE_KEY_VAULT'Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM (RSA key)Key URL: https://vault.vault.azure.net/keys/name/version (the CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY doc shows it with a port: …vault.azure.net:443/keys/…)
'MSSQL_CERTIFICATE_STORE'Windows Certificate Store (CurrentUser or LocalMachine)CurrentUser/My/<thumbprint> o LocalMachine/My/<thumbprint>
'MSSQL_CSP_PROVIDER'HSM with CryptoAPI (CAPI)ProviderName/KeyIdentifier
'MSSQL_CNG_STORE'HSM with CNGProviderName/KeyIdentifier
'MSSQL_JAVA_KEYSTORE'Java Key Store (JDBC driver)Depends on the provider
Custom providerAny other store (registered in the driver)The name cannot start with MSSQL_

Rules and values to memorize

ItemDetails
CEK256-bit plaintext; only 1–2 ENCRYPTED_VALUE in the DB (2 during a rotation). ALGORITHM = 'RSA_OAEP' for system providers.
Column algorithmOnly value: 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256' (AES-256-CBC + HMAC-SHA-256, encrypt-then-MAC).
CMK in Key VaultMust be an RSA key. App: access policy get, unwrapKey, verify; admin: create, get, list, sign, unwrapKey, wrapKey, verify. With RBAC: role Key Vault Crypto User (Managed HSM: Managed HSM Crypto User).
CMK in cert storeCertificate with a private key (≥ 2048 bits recommended). The driver does not validate expiration or the CA chain. In LocalMachine each user needs read permission.
ENCLAVE_COMPUTATIONS (SIGNATURE = 0x…)Marks the CMK as enclave-enabled; SSMS/PowerShell generate the signature.
Views / SPssys.column_master_keys, sys.column_encryption_keys, sys.column_encryption_key_values, sys.columns (encryption_type_desc, column_encryption_key_id), sp_describe_parameter_encryption; after changing an encrypted column: sp_refresh_parameter_encryption.

AE database permissions

PermissionPurpose
ALTER ANY COLUMN MASTER KEYCreate/delete CMK metadata
ALTER ANY COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEYCreate/delete CEK metadata
VIEW ANY COLUMN MASTER KEY DEFINITIONRead CMK metadata: needed to query encrypted columns
VIEW ANY COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY DEFINITIONRead CEK metadata: needed to query encrypted columns
Watch out: in SQL Server the public role already has both VIEW ANY …; in Azure SQL Database it does not: an explicit GRANT is required to work with encrypted columns. In SQL database in Fabric, AE is not supported (tables with AE cannot be created). The sys.columns page mentions SHA_512: it is a typo, the valid value is AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256.
Exam: the server never has the CMK; whoever has access to the CMK (not the server) can decrypt. To protect against DBAs, do not give them access to the CMK or to the plaintext CEK.
Sources: Learn · Protect data with encryption · Docs · CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY · Docs · CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY · Docs · Create and store column master keys

Always Encrypted: deterministic vs randomized and limitations GA

CriterionDETERMINISTICRANDOMIZED
Same plaintextSame ciphertext (IV derived from the value with HMAC-SHA-256)Different ciphertext every time (random 128-bit IV)
Without enclave= (point lookup), IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, equi-JOIN (only if both columns use the same CEK)No operations on the server (store and read only)
Indexes, PK, UNIQUE, FK, statisticsSupportedNo (with enclave: nonclustered indexes)
With secure enclaveEquality only=, <, >, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, DISTINCT, JOIN, ORDER BY, GROUP BY
SecurityReveals patterns: with few possible values (True/False, regions) the data can be inferredStronger; with enclave + index it can reveal the order
Typical useGovernment ID searched by parameterCredit card, salary, data that is not searched
Memorize: encrypted string columns must use a _BIN2 collation (the BIN2 variant of the DB's family; Latin1_General_BIN2). With an enclave in SQL Server 2022 / Azure SQL, a UTF-8 collation is also accepted for confidential queries.

Which columns can NOT be encrypted with AE

xmltimestamp / rowversionimagentexttextsql_varianthierarchyidgeographygeometryvectoralias / UDTFILESTREAMIDENTITYROWGUIDCOLsparseDEFAULT constraintCHECK constraintpartition columnfull-textDDM maskcomputed (if the expression is not compatible)CDCPK with change trackingnon-BIN2 string

Query limitations

LimitationDetails
Parameters, not literalsValues for encrypted columns only via parameters; T-SQL literals or variables fail (Msg 206 Operand type clash).
Do not mix plaintext and encryptedComparing with a plaintext column or literal; UPDATE, BULK INSERT, SELECT INTO, INSERT…SELECT between plaintext and encrypted.
Parameter typeMust match the column: AE does not convert between encrypted types (nchar → char, datetime → date).
OtherNo TVPs into encrypted columns, no FOR XML / FOR JSON.
Does not work withReplication (transactional, merge, snapshot), linked servers / OPENROWSET / OPENDATASOURCE, cross-DB joins on encrypted columns. Always On and other physical replicas do work.
Exam: “search by equality / JOIN / GROUP BY” → deterministic; “maximum secrecy, no queries” → randomized; “LIKE or ranges” → randomized + enclave. Encrypting existing data requires taking it out of the DB (or an enclave to do it in-place).
Sources: Learn · Protect data with encryption · Docs · Always Encrypted (Limitations) · Docs · Always Encrypted cryptography · Docs · CREATE TABLE (ENCRYPTED WITH)

Always Encrypted with secure enclaves SQL Server 2019+ (Windows) Azure SQL DB Fabric SQL DB GA

The enclave is a protected memory region inside the engine process where plaintext is processed without exposing it to the rest. It provides in-place encryption (encrypt, re-encrypt or decrypt with ALTER TABLE…ALTER COLUMN) and confidential queries (comparisons, LIKE, ranges, sorting, grouping) with indexes.

PlatformEnclaveAttestationNotes
SQL Server 2019+ (Windows only)VBSHGS or Nonesp_configure 'column encryption enclave type' = 1 + restart
Azure SQL DB (non-DC-series, DTU)VBSNone (no attestation)preferredEnclaveType = VBS property
Azure SQL DB (vCore DC-series)Intel SGXMicrosoft Azure Attestation (required)SGX end of support: Oct 31, 2027 (automatic migration to non-DC + VBS)
 
-- SQL Server: 0 = no enclave (default), 1 = VBS
EXECUTE sp_configure 'column encryption enclave type', 1;
RECONFIGURE;   -- changes require restarting the instance
# Portal / SSMS: "Enable secure enclaves" = ON
New-AzSqlDatabase -ResourceGroupName rg1 -ServerName srv1 -DatabaseName db1 -PreferredEnclaveType VBS
Set-AzSqlDatabase -ResourceGroupName rg1 -ServerName srv1 -DatabaseName db1 -PreferredEnclaveType VBS
# CLI: az sql db create ... --preferred-enclave-type VBS

Operations inside the enclave (require randomized and compat level ≥ 160)

OperationAzure SQL DBSQL Server 2022SQL Server 2019
=, <, >, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, DISTINCTYesYesYes
JOINYesYesNested loop only
ORDER BY, GROUP BYYesYesNo
 
CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY MyEnclaveCMK
WITH (
    KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAME = 'AZURE_KEY_VAULT',
    KEY_PATH = 'https://myvault.vault.azure.net/keys/MyEnclaveCMK/abc123',
    ENCLAVE_COMPUTATIONS (SIGNATURE = 0x1A2B3C)   -- signature generated by SSMS/PowerShell
);

-- Connection with AE + enclave enabled
ALTER TABLE dbo.Employees
ALTER COLUMN SSN char(11) COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2
ENCRYPTED WITH (COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = CEK1,   -- CEK enclave-enabled
                ENCRYPTION_TYPE = DETERMINISTIC,
                ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256') NOT NULL
WITH (ONLINE = ON);
ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION CLEAR PROCEDURE_CACHE;   -- recompiles affected plans
ALTER COLUMN in-placeEffect
With ENCRYPTED WITH, plaintext columnEncrypts
With ENCRYPTED WITH, another encryption type or a different CEKRe-encrypts (switch deterministic ↔ randomized, rotate CEK)
Without ENCRYPTED WITH, encrypted columnDecrypts (goes back to plaintext)
RulesDo not combine with other changes except NULL/NOT NULL and collation (same code page). The connection must have AE + enclave. Invoke-Sqlcmd and sqlcmd do not support it.

Connection string (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient)

KeywordValues / effect
Column Encryption SettingEnabled: enables AE on the connection
Attestation ProtocolHGS (SQL Server + Host Guardian Service), AAS (Azure SQL DB with SGX + Microsoft Azure Attestation), None (VBS without attestation; the only option for VBS in Azure SQL DB; SqlClient 4.1+). If omitted, the enclave stays disabled on the connection.
Enclave Attestation URLAttestation service endpoint; not needed with None
Minimum driversODBC 17.4+ (18.1+ for None), JDBC 8.2+ (12.2+ for None), .NET Framework 4.6 / .NET Core 2.1 (SqlClient 4.1+ for None)

Specific limitations

  • No clustered index, PK, FK or UNIQUE on randomized enclave-enabled columns; computed columns cannot operate on them; they cannot be used in in-memory tables.
  • Enclave-enabled CMK: only in Windows Certificate Store or Azure Key Vault.
  • LIKE without escape characters; with nchar/nvarchar n > 3967 or char/varchar/binary n > 7935 indexes are ignored (scan).
  • Enable ADR before creating the first index on a randomized enclave-enabled column (ON by default in Azure SQL, not in SQL Server).
  • After restoring a DB with VBS the enclave must be reconfigured; in HA/DR all replicas must support enclave; in BACPAC those indexes are removed first; in an elastic pool the DB inherits the pool's enclave.
Security: VBS protects against attacks inside the VM but not against privileged host accounts; SGX also protects against the host. Randomized with ranges/index can reveal the order of the data. Do not share CMK/CEK with the DBAs.
Exam: “VBS in Azure SQL DB” → Attestation Protocol=None; “SGX/DC-series” → Microsoft Azure Attestation (AAS); “SQL Server” → VBS with HGS or None. Rich operations require randomized + enclave-enabled CEK.

Always Encrypted: client, parameters and key rotation GA

SqlConnection.RegisterColumnEncryptionKeyStoreProviders(
    new Dictionary<string, SqlColumnEncryptionKeyStoreProvider>
    {
        { "AZURE_KEY_VAULT", new SqlColumnEncryptionAzureKeyVaultProvider(new DefaultAzureCredential()) }
    });

var cs = "Server=tcp:myserver.database.windows.net,1433;Database=mydb;" +
         "Authentication=Active Directory Default;Encrypt=True;" +
         "Column Encryption Setting=Enabled";
using var conn = new SqlConnection(cs);
await conn.OpenAsync();
using var cmd = new SqlCommand("SELECT EmployeeID FROM dbo.Employees WHERE SSN = @ssn", conn);
cmd.Parameters.Add(new SqlParameter("@ssn", SqlDbType.Char, 11) { Value = "795-73-9838" });  // same type as the column
API / setting (.NET)Purpose
Column Encryption Setting=EnabledEncrypts parameters and decrypts results. Without it, parameters against encrypted columns fail and results arrive as encrypted byte[].
SqlCommandColumnEncryptionSettingPer command: Enabled, ResultSetOnly (no encrypted parameters, only decrypts results), Disabled (does not touch encrypted columns).
SqlConnection.ColumnEncryptionKeyCacheTtlTime the plaintext CEK stays cached in the app: 2 hours by default.
ColumnEncryptionTrustedMasterKeyPathsList of trusted key paths: protects against a compromised server that returns fake paths.
SqlParameter.ForceColumnEncryptionRequires that parameter to be encrypted; fails if the server says it is not needed.
Key Vault providerNuGet Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.AlwaysEncrypted.AzureKeyVaultProvider (not included in SqlClient; supports Vault and Managed HSM).
SSMSConnection options → Enable Always Encrypted (column encryption) and enable Parameterization for Always Encrypted; in SSMS variables must be parameterized.
Gotcha: in .NET a string maps to nvarchar; against an encrypted char/varchar column it fails. Use DbType.AnsiStringFixedLength / SqlDbType.Char and SqlDbType.Date (not DateTime) to match the exact type.

CMK rotation (re-encrypts the CEKs, does not touch the data)

  1. Create the new CMK in the key store (the SqlServer module does not do this).
  2. New-SqlColumnMasterKey: creates the new CMK's metadata.
  3. Invoke-SqlColumnMasterKeyRotation: each CEK ends up with two encrypted values (old and new CMK).
  4. Deploy the new CMK to all apps that query the columns.
  5. Complete-SqlColumnMasterKeyRotation: removes the values encrypted with the old CMK (do not run it before migrating the apps).
  6. Remove-SqlColumnMasterKey on the old one. Keep the old CMK in the key store: you need it to restore backups taken before the rotation.
ALTER COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY MyCEK
ADD VALUE (COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = NewCMK, ALGORITHM = 'RSA_OAEP', ENCRYPTED_VALUE = 0x01700000016C006F00);

-- when all apps use NewCMK:
ALTER COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY MyCEK
DROP VALUE (COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = OldCMK);
CriterionRotate CMKRotate CEK
What changesThe key that protects the CEKsThe key that encrypts the data: decrypt and re-encrypt the column
Separation of rolesPossible (Security Admin + DBA; New-SqlColumnEncryptionKeyEncryptedValue)No: access to the keys and the DB is needed
With enclaveSameIn-place: ALTER COLUMN … ENCRYPTED WITH (new enclave-enabled CEK)
Sources: Docs · Using Always Encrypted with SqlClient · Docs · Rotate Always Encrypted keys · Docs · ALTER COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY

Column-level (cell-level) encryption with symmetric keys SQL Server Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Explicit encryption with T-SQL: the keys live inside the DB and you decide who can open them. Hierarchy: SMK (DPAPI in SQL Server; managed by Azure in SQL DB/MI) → DMK → certificate / asymmetric key → symmetric key → data (varbinary).

CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<password>';   -- in Azure SQL DB the password is optional
CREATE CERTIFICATE SensitiveDataCert WITH SUBJECT = 'Cell-level encryption';
CREATE SYMMETRIC KEY SensitiveDataKey
    WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256
    ENCRYPTION BY CERTIFICATE SensitiveDataCert;

ALTER TABLE dbo.CustomerData ADD CardEncrypted varbinary(160);   -- the ciphertext is varbinary
OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY SensitiveDataKey DECRYPTION BY CERTIFICATE SensitiveDataCert;

UPDATE dbo.CustomerData
SET CardEncrypted = ENCRYPTBYKEY(KEY_GUID('SensitiveDataKey'), CardNumber,
                                 1, HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', CONVERT(varbinary, CustomerID)));  -- authenticator

SELECT CustomerID,
       CONVERT(varchar(19), DECRYPTBYKEY(CardEncrypted,
                                         1, HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', CONVERT(varbinary, CustomerID)))) AS CardNumber
FROM dbo.CustomerData;

CLOSE SYMMETRIC KEY SensitiveDataKey;
Function / statementDetails
ENCRYPTBYKEY(key_GUID, cleartext [, add_authenticator, authenticator])Returns varbinary of up to 8,000 bytes. NULL if the key is not open or does not exist. add_authenticator must be 1 if you use an authenticator (prevents swapping encrypted values between rows).
DECRYPTBYKEY(ciphertext [, add_authenticator, authenticator])Returns varbinary (max. 8,000 bytes). Requires the key to be open in the session; NULL if it is not open. The authenticator must be the same as when encrypting.
OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY … DECRYPTION BY CERTIFICATE | ASYMMETRIC KEY | PASSWORD | SYMMETRIC KEYStays open per session (not per security context) until CLOSE SYMMETRIC KEY or the end of the session; sys.openkeys.
Other functionsENCRYPTBYPASSPHRASE, ENCRYPTBYCERT, ENCRYPTBYASYMKEY and their DECRYPTBY… counterparts, DECRYPTBYKEYAUTOCERT (opens the key with a certificate).

CREATE SYMMETRIC KEY: options and permissions

ItemValues / rules
ALGORITHMAES_128 | AES_192 | AES_256 recommended. DES, TRIPLE_DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, RC4_128, DESX are deprecated (only with compat level ≤ 120; RC4 only at 90/100).
ENCRYPTION BYCERTIFICATE, PASSWORD (a TRIPLE DES key is derived: weak link), SYMMETRIC KEY, ASYMMETRIC KEY; you can list several.
Temporary keysName with a single #; KEY_SOURCE / IDENTITY_VALUE to derive the key and the GUID from a phrase.
PermissionsALTER ANY SYMMETRIC KEY on the DB; VIEW DEFINITION on the certificate; for OPEN: some permission on the key, no DENY VIEW DEFINITION, and CONTROL on the certificate. Only Windows/SQL logins and application roles can be owners (not groups or roles).
CREATE MASTER KEYRequires CONTROL on the DB; encrypted with AES_256; password required in SQL Server, optional in Azure SQL DB.
Compat level 170Keys encrypted by a certificate/asymmetric key use OAEP-256 padding (encryptor_type = CERTIFICATE_OAEP_256).
Gotchas: CONVERT to the same original type (varchar vs nvarchar) or you will get garbage; with ANSI_PADDING OFF the encryption functions can lose data; back up the DMK and the certificate or you will lose the data; OPEN leaves the key open after a context switch (EXECUTE AS).
Exam: TDE encrypts files and decrypts when reading into memory; cell-level keeps the data encrypted until DECRYPTBYKEY and allows GRANT/DENY per key. AE is the only one that protects against a DBA without access to the key.
Sources: Learn · Protect data with encryption · Docs · Encrypt a column of data · Docs · ENCRYPTBYKEY · Docs · DECRYPTBYKEY · Docs · CREATE SYMMETRIC KEY · Docs · OPEN SYMMETRIC KEY

Transparent Data Encryption (TDE): for comparison with AE and cell-level SQL Server Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Encrypts data files, the log and backups at rest, in real time and at the page level. The app does not change. Protects the physical media, not authorized users or traffic (that is TLS).

USE master;
CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<password>';
CREATE CERTIFICATE MyServerCert WITH SUBJECT = 'My DEK Certificate';
BACKUP CERTIFICATE MyServerCert TO FILE = 'C:\certs\MyServerCert.cer'
    WITH PRIVATE KEY (FILE = 'C:\certs\MyServerCert.pvk', ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<password>');

USE AdventureWorks2022;
CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256
    ENCRYPTION BY SERVER CERTIFICATE MyServerCert;
ALTER DATABASE AdventureWorks2022 SET ENCRYPTION ON;    -- OFF to decrypt

SELECT DB_NAME(database_id) AS db, encryption_state, percent_complete
FROM sys.dm_database_encryption_keys;
ItemDetails
HierarchyDPAPI → SMK → DMK (in master) → certificate (in master) → DEK (in the user DB). DEK: AES_128 | AES_192 | AES_256 (TRIPLE_DES_3KEY deprecated).
What it does not encryptmaster/model/msdb, FILESTREAM, traffic. tempdb is encrypted only when some DB on the instance uses TDE (it is not encrypted directly).
encryption_state0 no DEK · 1 unencrypted · 2 encryption in progress · 3 encrypted · 4 key change in progress · 5 decryption in progress · 6 protection change in progress
Scan (2019+)encryption_scan_state 0–4; ALTER DATABASE … SET ENCRYPTION SUSPEND | RESUME
PermissionsCREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY: CONTROL on the DB + VIEW DEFINITION on the certificate. To read the DMV: VIEW SERVER STATE (SQL Server ≤ 2019 and MI) · VIEW SERVER SECURITY STATE (SQL Server 2022+) · VIEW DATABASE STATE (Azure SQL DB; on Basic/S0/S1 and elastic pools: server admin, Entra admin or the ##MS_ServerStateReader## role; Fabric: VIEW DATABASE STATE or any workspace role).
RestrictionsDuring the initial encryption, key change or decryption you cannot drop a file, drop/take offline/detach the DB or set it to READ ONLY; a READ ONLY filegroup makes the operation fail; there is no instant file initialization; after changing the DEK twice, a log backup is required before changing it again.
BackupsBackups are also encrypted with the DEK: restoring requires the certificate and its private key. If you run CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY with a certificate that has not been backed up, SQL Server issues warning 33091 (run BACKUP CERTIFICATE immediately). Never delete the certificate from master: the DB would become inaccessible.

Azure SQL Database / Managed Instance

TopicDetails
DefaultNew DBs are created encrypted (service-managed). Not encrypted by default: SQL DBs from before May 2017 and MIs from before Feb 2019. Restore/geo-replication/copy inherit the source's status.
Service-managedBuilt-in certificate per server, AES-256 CBC, rotated by Microsoft every year.
Customer-managed (BYOK)TDE protector = asymmetric key in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM; set at the server/instance level (inherited by the DBs) and also at the DB level. If the server loses access to the key, the DB becomes inaccessible.
T-SQLALTER DATABASE … SET ENCRYPTION ON | OFF (admin or dbmanager role in master). The TDE protector cannot be changed with T-SQL: portal, PowerShell or CLI.
Othertempdb is always encrypted with a Microsoft key; a BACPAC exported from a TDE DB is not encrypted; MI does not allow manual COPY_ONLY of a DB with service-managed TDE.

SQL database in Fabric

  • Everything is encrypted at rest with Microsoft-managed keys (service-side encryption of the storage).
  • Optional: customer-managed keys at the workspace level (Azure Key Vault) → TDE is enabled automatically on all the SQL DBs in the workspace (and tempdb). Without access to the key, the DB becomes Inaccessible in ≤ 10 min; if it recovers in ≤ 30 min it self-heals. Verify with sys.dm_database_encryption_keys (encryptor_type = ASYMMETRIC_KEY).
Discrepancy: on the limitations page for SQL database in Fabric, the “Database level limitations” bullet says that CMK and TDE “are not supported”, but its own feature table marks TDE = Yes and the encryption page documents workspace CMK with automatic TDE (RSA or RSA-HSM key of 2,048 or 3,072 bits; not 4,096). The encryption page wins; verify in your tenant. Learn (unit 2) adds that in Fabric column encryption is designed with Always Encrypted or symmetric keys, but the current docs state that Always Encrypted is not supported in Fabric SQL DB (only cell-level with symmetric keys).
Exam: “encryption-at-rest compliance with no app changes” → TDE; “protect from DBAs” → AE. They can be combined (baseline TDE + AE on critical columns).
Sources: Learn · Protect data with encryption · Docs · TDE (SQL Server) · Docs · TDE (Azure SQL) · Docs · Data encryption in SQL database in Fabric

Dynamic Data Masking (DDM) SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Limits the exposure of sensitive data by obfuscating the query result for users without UNMASK. The stored data does not change and the app is not modified.

FunctionResult and rules
default()Full mask by type: strings XXXX (fewer X if the field length is < 4); numeric 0; date/time 1900-01-01 00:00:00.0000000; binary one ASCII 0 byte (the Azure SQL docs say “empty value” for binary/varbinary/image). In Azure SQL: XML <masked />; sql_variant uses the default value of its type.
email()First letter + XXX@XXXX.com (e.g. aXXX@XXXX.com; the Azure SQL docs write aXX@XXXX.com).
random(start, end)Random number within the range, different for each query; numeric types only. If start = end, it is constant.
partial(prefix, "padding", suffix)Custom string: shows prefix characters at the start, the padding and suffix at the end. If the value is short, part of the prefix/suffix is hidden. partial(1,"XXXXXXX",0): 555.123.1234 → 5XXXXXXX.
datetime("Y"|"M"|"D"|"h"|"m"|"s")Masks the year, month, day, hour, minute or second in date, datetime, datetime2, datetimeoffset, smalldatetime, time. SQL Server 2022+, Azure SQL, Fabric SQL DB.
REGEXP_REPLACE("pattern", "replacement") PreviewAzure SQL DB only and T-SQL only. char/nchar/varchar/nvarchar and LOB up to 2 MB; pattern ≤ 8,000 bytes; start = 1, occurrence = 0 (all), fixed 'c' flags. Anything that does not match the pattern stays unmasked. Do not use in production.
Portal: “Credit card”Equivalent to partial(0,"XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-",4) (shows the last 4 digits).
 
CREATE TABLE dbo.Customers (
    CustomerID int PRIMARY KEY,
    LastName   varchar(100) NOT NULL,
    Email      varchar(100) MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'email()') NULL,
    Phone      varchar(20)  MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'partial(3, "-XXX-XX", 2)') NULL,
    CardNumber varchar(19)  MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'partial(0, "XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-", 4)') NULL,
    Income     decimal(18,2) MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'random(10000, 100000)') NULL,
    SSN        char(11)     MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'default()') NULL,
    BirthDate  date         MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'datetime("Y")') NULL
);

ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN LastName ADD MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'partial(2,"xxxx",0)');   -- add
ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN LastName varchar(100) MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'default()');     -- change
ALTER TABLE dbo.Customers ALTER COLUMN LastName DROP MASKED;                                           -- remove
GRANT UNMASK TO DataAnalyst;                            -- whole DB
GRANT UNMASK ON SCHEMA::Sales TO SalesManager;          -- schema
GRANT UNMASK ON dbo.Customers TO CustomerService;       -- table
GRANT UNMASK ON dbo.Customers (Phone) TO Telemarketing; -- column
REVOKE UNMASK ON dbo.Customers (Phone) FROM Telemarketing;

-- Test the mask (Learn exercise)
CREATE USER MaskedViewer WITHOUT LOGIN;
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.Customers TO MaskedViewer;
EXECUTE AS USER = 'MaskedViewer';
SELECT LastName, Email, CardNumber, Income FROM dbo.Customers;   -- masked values
REVERT;

SELECT c.name, t.name AS table_name, c.is_masked, c.masking_function
FROM sys.masked_columns AS c
JOIN sys.tables AS t ON c.object_id = t.object_id;
Permission / roleWhat it allows
UNMASKView unmasked data. Granular at DB, schema, table or column level (SQL Server 2022+, Azure SQL, Fabric SQL DB). Always needs SELECT; on its own it does not even reveal metadata.
ALTER ANY MASK + ALTER on the tableAdd, change or remove masks (security officer role).
CONTROLIncludes ALTER ANY MASK and UNMASK: db_owner and sysadmin see everything. In Azure SQL, also the server admin and Entra admin.
Create table with maskOnly CREATE TABLE and ALTER on the schema.
Portal / PowerShell / RESTAzure roles: SQL Security Manager, SQL DB Contributor, SQL Server Contributor (action Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases/dataMaskingPolicies/*). MI and Fabric SQL DB: T-SQL only.

Limitations and behavior

  • A mask cannot be defined on Always Encrypted columns, FILESTREAM, COLUMN_SET/sparse in the column set, or PolyBase external tables; nor on a computed column (but a computed column that depends on a masked column returns the masked value). A masked column cannot be the key of a full-text index.
  • Adding a mask is a schema change: it fails if there are dependencies (computed columns, indexes): remove the dependency, mask, and re-create it.
  • Any expression that projects a masked column is always masked with default(), regardless of the original function.
  • SELECT INTO, INSERT INTO and export/import (BACPAC) copy already-masked data if the user does not have UNMASK. Cross-database comparisons/joins on masked columns give incorrect results. Not supported with indexed views on the base table.
  • The mask does not prevent UPDATE: control write permissions. In Fabric SQL DB EXECUTE AS USER does not exist: test by connecting as another user.
Inference: with ad hoc query permission, WHERE Salary > 99999 AND Salary < 100001 reveals the value even if 0 is displayed. DDM prevents accidental exposure, not a deliberate attack: combine it with minimal permissions, RLS, encryption and auditing.
Exam: Learn mentions “four functions”, but the current docs have five (default, email, random, partial, datetime) + regex in preview. Learn also says that SELECT + ALTER lets you bypass the mask; the docs require ALTER ANY MASK + ALTER on the table.
Sources: Learn · Configure dynamic data masking · Docs · Dynamic data masking · Docs · DDM in Azure SQL · Docs · Regex-based DDM (preview)

Row-Level Security (RLS) SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Controls access to rows based on the user context. Two parts: a predicate (inline table-valued function that returns a row if there is access) and a security policy that binds it to a table.

CREATE SCHEMA Security;
GO
CREATE FUNCTION Security.fn_TenantPredicate(@TenantID int)
RETURNS TABLE
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
RETURN SELECT 1 AS fn_result
WHERE @TenantID = CAST(SESSION_CONTEXT(N'TenantID') AS int);
GO
CREATE SECURITY POLICY Security.TenantPolicy
    ADD FILTER PREDICATE Security.fn_TenantPredicate(TenantID) ON dbo.Orders,
    ADD BLOCK  PREDICATE Security.fn_TenantPredicate(TenantID) ON dbo.Orders AFTER INSERT,
    ADD BLOCK  PREDICATE Security.fn_TenantPredicate(TenantID) ON dbo.Orders AFTER UPDATE
WITH (STATE = ON, SCHEMABINDING = ON);
GO
-- The app, after authenticating the user:
EXEC sp_set_session_context @key = N'TenantID', @value = 42, @read_only = 1;
CREATE FUNCTION Security.fn_RegionFilter(@SalesRegion nvarchar(20))
RETURNS TABLE
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
RETURN SELECT 1 AS AccessGranted
WHERE @SalesRegion = CASE USER_NAME() WHEN 'WestSalesRep' THEN 'West' WHEN 'EastSalesRep' THEN 'East' ELSE @SalesRegion END
   OR IS_MEMBER('db_owner') = 1;   -- db_owner sees everything
GO
CREATE SECURITY POLICY CustomerRegionPolicy
    ADD FILTER PREDICATE Security.fn_RegionFilter(SalesRegion) ON dbo.Customers
WITH (STATE = ON);

CREATE USER WestSalesRep WITHOUT LOGIN;
GRANT SELECT ON dbo.Customers TO WestSalesRep;
EXECUTE AS USER = 'WestSalesRep';
SELECT * FROM dbo.Customers;   -- only 'West' rows
REVERT;
Fail-open: the ELSE @SalesRegion in the exercise lets any unlisted user see all regions. In production, make the predicate fail-closed (user→region mapping table or SESSION_CONTEXT; no match, no rows).
-- CREATE SECURITY POLICY [schema.]policy
--   { ADD [FILTER|BLOCK] PREDICATE schema.tvf(column|expression [,...n]) ON schema.table
--       [AFTER {INSERT|UPDATE} | BEFORE {UPDATE|DELETE}] } [,...n]
--   [WITH (STATE = {ON|OFF} [, SCHEMABINDING = {ON|OFF}])] [NOT FOR REPLICATION]

ALTER SECURITY POLICY Security.TenantPolicy WITH (STATE = OFF);   -- disable (diagnostics)
ALTER SECURITY POLICY Security.TenantPolicy
    ADD FILTER PREDICATE Security.fn_TenantPredicate(TenantID) ON dbo.Shipments;
ALTER SECURITY POLICY Security.TenantPolicy
    ALTER FILTER PREDICATE Security.fn_TenantPredicate_v2(TenantID) ON dbo.Orders;
ALTER SECURITY POLICY Security.TenantPolicy DROP FILTER PREDICATE ON dbo.Shipments;

SELECT p.name, p.is_enabled, pr.predicate_type_desc, pr.operation_desc, pr.predicate_definition
FROM sys.security_policies p
JOIN sys.security_predicates pr ON pr.object_id = p.object_id;
PredicateEffect
FILTERSilently filters data on read: affects SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE (no error; returns an empty set). INSERT is still allowed.
BLOCK … AFTER INSERTError if the inserted row violates the predicate (prevents inserting for another tenant).
BLOCK … AFTER UPDATEError if the UPDATE leaves the row with a value that violates the predicate.
BLOCK … BEFORE UPDATEError if the current row already violates the predicate.
BLOCK … BEFORE DELETEBlocks DELETE of rows that violate the predicate.
BLOCK with no operationApplies to all write operations. In sys.security_predicates.operation: NULL = all, 1 AFTER INSERT, 2 AFTER UPDATE, 3 BEFORE UPDATE, 4 BEFORE DELETE.

Rules, permissions and limitations

TopicDetails
One predicate per operationAt most one per DML operation and table. Several policies only if they do not overlap; on the same operation, only one enabled at a time.
SCHEMABINDINGThe policy uses SCHEMABINDING = ON by default: functions must be created WITH SCHEMABINDING, neither the function nor the referenced columns can be altered, and users do not need permissions on the predicate's tables/functions. With OFF they do need them (SELECT/EXECUTE). ALTER SECURITY POLICY does not change SCHEMABINDING: DROP and CREATE.
STATEInconsistent docs: the argument text of CREATE SECURITY POLICY says that without STATE the policy is enabled, but its example A leaves it disabled and the RLS article says “The STATE must be set to ON to enable the policy”. Always write STATE = ON.
PermissionsCreate/alter/drop a policy: ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY (+ ALTER on the schema to create/drop). For each predicate: SELECT and REFERENCES on the function, REFERENCES on the table and on each column used as an argument. The policy manager does not need SELECT on the table.
Who it applies toTo everyone, including dbo, db_owner and the table owner. If sysadmin/db_owner must see everything, the predicate must allow it.
User contextUSER_NAME(), DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID(), IS_MEMBER() for DB users; SESSION_CONTEXT() with a middle-tier app. sp_set_session_context: key ≤ 128 bytes, sql_variant value ≤ 8,000 bytes, total context ≤ 1 MB; @read_only = 1 prevents changing the value until the connection is closed (returned to the pool).
UPDATEIt is split into BEFORE and AFTER: you cannot block “raising the salary” by comparing old and new; for that, use a trigger with INSERTED/DELETED. AFTER UPDATE is not evaluated if the predicate columns do not change. BULK INSERT honors AFTER INSERT.
CompatibilityFILESTREAM ✗; indexed views on tables with a policy ✗; memory-optimized: function WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION + SCHEMABINDING; partitioned views: no BLOCK (FILTER is allowed); temporal: the policy is not replicated to the history table (add the predicate to both); CDC/change tracking can leak rows or PKs; DBCC SHOW_STATISTICS only for owner, sysadmin, db_owner, db_ddladmin; columnstore compatible (may lose batch mode).
PlatformsFabric Data Warehouse / SQL analytics endpoint and Synapse: FILTER only. The RLS article says “Microsoft Fabric and Azure Synapse Analytics support filter predicates only” and its Applies to includes SQL database in Fabric (same engine as Azure SQL DB): Verify whether the latter accepts BLOCK.

Best practices and risks

  • Separate schema (Security) for functions and policies; avoid type conversions, recursion and excessive joins (performance).
  • Do not depend on SET options (DATEFORMAT, LANGUAGE, DATEFIRST, ANSI_WARNINGS, ARITHABORT, CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL): use CONVERT with an explicit style.
  • Side-channel: queries such as SELECT 1/(Salary-100000) … leak information through errors; a malicious policy manager can exfiltrate data with a custom TVF: audit changes to policies and functions.
  • READ UNCOMMITTED can see transient values because BLOCK predicates are evaluated after the DML.
Diagnostics: if a result looks odd, disable the policy (STATE = OFF) and compare. Documented alternative to AFTER UPDATE with a single-user app: DENY UPDATE on the predicate column.
Sources: Learn · Implement row-level security · Docs · Row-level security · Docs · CREATE SECURITY POLICY · Docs · ALTER SECURITY POLICY

Object-level permissions: GRANT/DENY/REVOKE, roles and schemas SQL Server Azure SQL Fabric SQL DB GA

Hierarchy: server → database → schema → object → column; permissions granted higher up flow down. GRANT … ON SCHEMA:: also covers objects created later.

CREATE SCHEMA Sales AUTHORIZATION dbo;
CREATE ROLE SalesReaders;
GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA::Sales TO SalesReaders;                  -- includes future objects
DENY  SELECT ON Sales.Customers (CreditLimit) TO SalesReaders;  -- protected column
GRANT EXECUTE ON SCHEMA::Reports TO ReportingUsers;
GRANT INSERT, UPDATE ON dbo.Orders TO OrderProcessing;
ALTER ROLE SalesReaders ADD MEMBER [alice@contoso.com];
REVOKE INSERT ON dbo.Orders FROM OrderProcessing;               -- removes the GRANT, does not deny
StatementSyntax and rules
GRANTGRANT perm [,…n] ON securable TO principal [WITH GRANT OPTION] [AS principal]. Removes a prior DENY/REVOKE at the same scope. ALL is deprecated.
DENYDENY perm [,…n] ON securable TO principal [CASCADE] [AS principal]. Wins over any GRANT (even one inherited through a role). Does not apply to sysadmin or object owners. Fails without CASCADE if the permission was given WITH GRANT OPTION.
REVOKEREVOKE [GRANT OPTION FOR] perm ON securable FROM principal [CASCADE] [AS principal]. Removes a GRANT or a DENY; it does not block access that comes through another GRANT or role.
PrecedenceDENY > GRANT; REVOKE is neutral. Historical exception: a table-level DENY does not override a column-level GRANT.
Who can grantWhoever has the permission with GRANT OPTION or a higher one (CONTROL on the DB → db_owner; CONTROL on the schema → any object in that schema).

Fixed database roles

RoleCapacity
db_ownerCONTROL DATABASE: everything, and DROP of the DB in SQL Server
db_securityadminManages permissions and membership of custom roles; can escalate privileges
db_accessadminALTER ANY USER, CREATE SCHEMA, CREATE USER (grants or removes access to the DB)
db_backupoperatorBACKUP DATABASE, BACKUP LOG, CHECKPOINT
db_ddladminAny DDL; can escalate privileges
db_datareaderSELECT on all user tables and views (any schema except sys and INFORMATION_SCHEMA)
db_datawriterINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all user tables
db_denydatareader / db_denydatawriterDENY SELECT (and hides metadata) / DENY INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
publicAll users; in SQL Server it has VIEW ANY COLUMN MASTER/ENCRYPTION KEY DEFINITION and SELECT on system views (revocable)
dbmanager, loginmanagerAzure SQL DB only (virtual master): create/drop DBs and logins

The permissions of fixed roles cannot be changed (except public); all roles have CONNECT; roles can be nested; server permissions cannot be given through DB roles; a user cannot be removed from public.

Mediate access with modules

MechanismRule
Ownership chainingIf the calling object and the referenced one have the same owner, permissions on the referenced object are not checked (the chain breaks if the owner changes). Does not apply to dynamic SQL (EXEC(...)/sp_executesql) inside the module. The default owner is the schema's owner. The user only needs EXECUTE on the module.
EXECUTE AS in modules{ CALLER | SELF | OWNER | 'user_name' }; CALLER is the default. Permissions on referenced objects are checked against the specified user (ownership chaining still applies). Whoever creates the module needs IMPERSONATE on the principal; OWNER must be an account, not a role; the principal cannot be dropped while a module uses it.
EXECUTE AS USER = 'x' / REVERTTo test permissions (requires IMPERSONATE). Not supported in Fabric SQL DB.
 
SELECT prin.name AS principal, perm.permission_name, perm.state_desc, perm.class_desc,
       OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(perm.major_id) AS schema_name, OBJECT_NAME(perm.major_id) AS object_name
FROM sys.database_permissions AS perm
JOIN sys.database_principals AS prin ON perm.grantee_principal_id = prin.principal_id
WHERE prin.name = N'SalesAnalyst';

SELECT * FROM fn_my_permissions('Sales.Orders', 'OBJECT');   -- effective permissions of the current user
Exam: user in two roles, one with GRANT and the other with DENY → DENY wins. REVOKE is not the same as denying. Least privilege: roles by function, schema-level permissions, views/SPs instead of direct table access, avoid db_owner. Combine permissions with RLS and DDM.
Sources: Learn · Manage permissions and secure access · Docs · GRANT · Docs · DENY · Docs · Database-level roles · Docs · EXECUTE AS clause

Passwordless access: Microsoft Entra ID and Managed Identity Azure SQL DB/MI SQL Server 2022+ (Arc) Fabric SQL DB GA

Replaces username/password with Entra ID tokens: there are no secrets to steal or rotate. For apps in Azure, managed identity is the most secure option.

Authentication=IdentityNotes
Active Directory Managed Identity (o Active Directory MSI)System-assigned (without User Id) or user-assigned (User Id= client ID; in SqlClient 2.1 it was the object ID, since 3.0 it is the client ID)Preferred in Azure; no secrets (SqlClient 2.1+)
Active Directory DefaultDefaultAzureCredential chain: environment variables, workload identity, managed identity, VS, CLI, PowerShell, azdIdeal for development; the 1st connection can be slow → in production use a specific mode (SqlClient 3.0+)
Active Directory Workload IdentityFederated token (AKS, GitHub Actions)SqlClient 5.2+
Active Directory Service PrincipalClient ID (User ID) + secret (Password)Not recommended (secret); with a certificate use AccessTokenCallback
Active Directory InteractiveUser with MFAFor people; never in unattended services
Active Directory Integrated / Device Code FlowFederated IWA / sign-in on another deviceDevice Code: SqlClient 2.1+
Active Directory PasswordEntra username and passwordDeprecated and without MFA: do not use
Sql PasswordSQL authenticationNot Entra
 
Server=tcp:myserver.database.windows.net,1433;Database=mydb;Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity;Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=False;
// user-assigned: add  ;User Id=UAMI_CLIENT_ID
  1. Enable the identity: system-assigned on the resource (App Service, Functions, VM, Container Apps) or user-assigned (reusable by several apps: fewer users in the DB).
  2. Set the Microsoft Entra admin of the logical server (az sql server ad-admin create): a single object (user, group, SP or MI); use a group for several administrators.
  3. Recommended: enable Microsoft Entra-only authentication (next topic).
  4. Connect as the Entra admin (or with ALTER ANY USER) and create the contained user.
  5. Assign minimal permissions through DB roles; configure the connection string without credentials.
CREATE USER [my-app-service] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;      -- MI or service principal: DisplayName
CREATE USER [alice@contoso.com] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;   -- user: UPN
CREATE USER [Data Analysts] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;       -- group: DisplayName
ALTER ROLE db_datareader ADD MEMBER [my-app-service];
ALTER ROLE db_datawriter ADD MEMBER [my-app-service];
TopicDetails
User nameThe DB user for a managed identity uses the identity's DisplayName (the system-assigned identity of an App Service is named after the app). A user-assigned one can be shared across several apps with a single user in the DB.
SQL Server 2022+Entra auth via Azure Arc (app registration). SQL Server 2025 with Arc (Windows Server only): system-assigned managed identity (primary) for inbound and outbound connections.
Fabric SQL DBEntra only (no SQL authentication or logins). The Read permission on the item in Fabric is required; service principals require the tenant setting Service principals can use Fabric APIs.
Secrets and networkConnection strings in Key Vault or environment variables; Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=False; firewall and private endpoints; SP secrets in Key Vault with rotation (certificate > shared secret).
Exam: “Azure app without credentials” → managed identity + CREATE USER … FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER. Getting a token does not grant database permissions: the user must exist in the DB with permissions. “Several apps with the same permissions” → user-assigned MI.
Sources: Learn · Manage permissions and secure access · Docs · Microsoft Entra authentication with SqlClient · Docs · Configure Entra authentication (Azure SQL) · Docs · Authentication in SQL database in Fabric

Microsoft Entra: principals, Graph permissions and Entra-only authentication Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

TopicDetails
Contained userCREATE USER [x] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER: portable with the DB; sys.database_principals.type = E (user or app) or X (group); the SID is the Entra object ID.
Login (server principal)CREATE LOGIN [x] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER + CREATE USER [x] FROM LOGIN [x]: the user inherits permissions from the login (GA in Azure SQL DB, MI and SQL Server 2022+). Avoid a contained user with the same name as a login: they get mixed up.
Duplicate namesEntra allows duplicate DisplayNames; SQL does not (error 33131). CREATE USER [alias] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER WITH OBJECT_ID = 'guid' (also in CREATE LOGIN): the alias = original name + suffix (e.g. myapp2ba6c); if the object ID does not exist in the tenant, error 37545. It is a workaround for duplicate service principals, not for general use. Preview according to the Azure SQL guide (authentication-aad-configure); the dedicated article and the CREATE USER reference list it without a label for SQL Server 2025+, Azure SQL DB/MI and Fabric SQL DB: Verify the status.
Entra adminSingle property (not a list); it is db_owner in all DBs and the first identity that can create Entra principals. Removing it disables all Entra authentication. Afterwards it can grant ALTER ANY USER to others.
Microsoft Graph permissionsIf CREATE USER/LOGIN is run by a service principal or MI, the server identity (SMI/UMI) needs Application.Read.All (SP/MI), User.Read.All (users) and GroupMember.Read.All (groups), or the Directory Readers role. In MI: Directory Readers for the instance identity. An Entra user (human) who runs the command needs nothing extra.
No Azure RBACEntra authentication does not integrate with Azure RBAC: the SQL Server Contributor / SQL DB Contributor roles manage resources and do not grant data access. Each identity must exist as a principal in the DB.
LimitUsers or SPs in more than 2,048 security groups cannot connect.
AuditingWith Entra, failed sign-ins do not appear in the SQL audit log: check them in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

Entra-only authentication (disables SQL authentication)

az sql server ad-only-auth enable  --resource-group myresource --name myserver
az sql server ad-only-auth disable --resource-group myresource --name myserver
az sql server ad-only-auth get     --resource-group myresource --name myserver
az sql mi ad-only-auth enable      --resource-group myresource --name myinstance   # Managed Instance
# PowerShell: Enable-AzSqlServerActiveDirectoryOnlyAuthentication -ServerName myserver -ResourceGroupName myresource
  • All other forms of authentication are disabled, including the SQL admin and SQL accounts (in MI also Windows authentication). The SQL accounts are not deleted: they just can no longer connect.
  • Requires the Entra admin to be already configured. Owner, Contributor and SQL Security Manager can enable it; neither SQL Server Contributor nor SQL Managed Instance Contributor can (separation of duties).
  • It is governed with Azure Policy; Entra users with permissions can still create SQL logins, but these will not be able to connect.
-- Connected as an Entra user (requires the Directory Readers role)
CREATE USER [alice@contoso.com] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;

-- Connected as a service principal: FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER does not work; use SID (binary(16)) + TYPE
CREATE USER [HRApp] WITH SID = 0x0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF, TYPE = E;   -- E = user/SP/MI, X = group
Memorize (Fabric): SID = object ID of the user/group, or application (client) ID of the service principal, converted to binary(16); Fabric does not validate the ID against Entra.
Sources: Docs · Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure SQL · Docs · Microsoft Entra-only authentication · Docs · CREATE USER · Docs · Managed identities for Azure SQL

Auditing: SQL Server Audit, Azure SQL auditing and Fabric SQL Server Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

SQL Server Audit uses Extended Events. A server audit defines the destination; the specifications define what to capture: one server audit specification per audit (instance events) and one database audit specification per DB and audit.

CriterionSQL ServerAzure SQL DatabaseAzure SQL MIFabric SQL DB
ConfigurationT-SQL: CREATE SERVER AUDIT + specificationsPortal, PowerShell, CLI, REST, ARM, Azure Policy (server or DB level)T-SQL (CREATE SERVER AUDIT) + diagnostic settingsFabric portal (Security → Manage SQL auditing) or REST
DestinationsFILE, APPLICATION_LOG, SECURITY_LOGStorage (.xel blobs), Log Analytics, Event Hubs (combinable)URL (blob), EXTERNAL_MONITOR (Event Hubs / Log Analytics)OneLake (read-only, immutable)
Readsys.fn_get_audit_filefn_get_audit_file / _v2, KQL, SSMS Merge Audit Filesfn_get_audit_file, KQLsys.fn_get_audit_file_v2
RetentionMAXSIZE, MAX_ROLLOVER_FILES, MAX_FILESDays in Storage: 0 = unlimited (default)RETENTION_DAYS, default 0 = unlimitedIndefinite by default; configurable; deleted along with the item
 
CREATE SERVER AUDIT SecurityAudit
TO FILE (FILEPATH = 'C:\AuditLogs\', MAXSIZE = 100 MB, MAX_ROLLOVER_FILES = 10)
WITH (QUEUE_DELAY = 1000, ON_FAILURE = CONTINUE);
ALTER SERVER AUDIT SecurityAudit WITH (STATE = ON);          -- starts disabled

CREATE SERVER AUDIT SPECIFICATION ServerAuditSpec
FOR SERVER AUDIT SecurityAudit
ADD (FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP), ADD (SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUP),
ADD (SERVER_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUP)
WITH (STATE = ON);

USE MyDatabase;
CREATE DATABASE AUDIT SPECIFICATION DatabaseAuditSpec
FOR SERVER AUDIT SecurityAudit
ADD (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON dbo.SensitiveData BY public),
ADD (EXECUTE ON SCHEMA::dbo BY public),
ADD (DATABASE_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP)
WITH (STATE = ON);

SELECT event_time, action_id, succeeded, session_server_principal_name, object_name, statement
FROM sys.fn_get_audit_file('C:\AuditLogs\*.sqlaudit', DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
WHERE event_time > DATEADD(day, -7, GETUTCDATE());
CREATE SERVER AUDIT optionValues and defaults
TOFILE | APPLICATION_LOG | SECURITY_LOG | URL | EXTERNAL_MONITOR. URL does not exist in SQL Server; in MI only URL or EXTERNAL_MONITOR.
FILE (…)FILEPATH; MAXSIZE min. 2 MB (default UNLIMITED); MAX_ROLLOVER_FILES (default UNLIMITED) or MAX_FILES (when the limit is reached, audited actions fail); RESERVE_DISK_SPACE (default OFF).
QUEUE_DELAYMilliseconds before forcing the write; 1000 is the minimum and the default; 0 = synchronous.
ON_FAILURECONTINUE (default; some activity may go unaudited) · SHUTDOWN (shuts down the instance; the login needs SHUTDOWN) · FAIL_OPERATION (audited actions fail).
OtherAUDIT_GUID (mirroring/AG), OPERATOR_AUDIT (MI only: Microsoft support operations), RETENTION_DAYS (MI and Azure SQL DB only), WHERE (predicate ≤ 3,000 characters).
PermissionsServer audit/specification: ALTER ANY SERVER AUDIT or CONTROL SERVER. Database audit specification: ALTER ANY DATABASE AUDIT (or ALTER/CONTROL on the DB). Reading files: CONTROL SERVER (≤ 2019) or VIEW SERVER SECURITY AUDIT (2022+); Azure SQL DB: CONTROL DATABASE according to the fn_get_audit_file reference (the auditing guide says VIEW DATABASE SECURITY AUDIT); Fabric: VIEW DATABASE SECURITY AUDIT.

Azure SQL Database: key points

  • Server-level applies to all DBs; database-level coexists with it (both are audited). With many DBs and heavy load, it is better to switch to per-DB auditing (logs are easier to query).
  • Default policy: BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP, SUCCESSFUL_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP, FAILED_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUP. With Log Analytics/Event Hubs, a diagnostic setting is created with the SQLSecurityAuditEvents category.
  • Authentication to Storage: Managed Identity (recommended) or Storage Access Keys. Container sqldbauditlogs; GPv2 if the Storage is behind a VNet/firewall. Immutable logs: Allow protected append writes = Append blobs (or Block and append blobs); Storage retention must be shorter than SQL Auditing retention, and SQL retention = 0 is not supported with a Storage policy.
  • Auditing prioritizes availability and performance: under extreme load it may skip events. Failed Entra logins are not audited here (you see them in Entra); FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP does not apply to Azure SQL DB.
  • Changing retention from 0 to N only affects new logs. When configuring it from the portal, the Storage and the Event Hub must be in the same region as the server/DB (with other methods they can be in any region).

Common action groups

SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUPFAILED_LOGIN_GROUPSUCCESSFUL_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUPFAILED_DATABASE_AUTHENTICATION_GROUPSERVER_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUPDATABASE_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUPDATABASE_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUPDATABASE_PRINCIPAL_CHANGE_GROUPSCHEMA_OBJECT_ACCESS_GROUPSCHEMA_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUPDATABASE_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUPBATCH_COMPLETED_GROUPSENSITIVE_BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP (2022+)AUDIT_CHANGE_GROUPUSER_DEFINED_AUDIT_GROUP (sp_audit_write)
CREATE CREDENTIAL [https://mystorage.blob.core.windows.net/sqlaudit]
WITH IDENTITY = 'SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE', SECRET = '<SAS KEY>';
CREATE SERVER AUDIT MiBlobAudit TO URL (PATH = 'https://mystorage.blob.core.windows.net/sqlaudit', RETENTION_DAYS = 90);

CREATE SERVER AUDIT MiMonitorAudit TO EXTERNAL_MONITOR;   -- + diagnostic settings to Event Hubs / Log Analytics
SELECT event_time, action_id, succeeded, server_principal_name, client_ip, statement
FROM sys.fn_get_audit_file_v2(
       'https://mystorage.blob.core.windows.net/sqldbauditlogs/myserver/mydb/',
       DEFAULT, DEFAULT, '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z', '2026-10-08T00:00:00Z');   -- v2: time filters
AzureDiagnostics
| where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents" and TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| summarize count() by client_ip_s, server_principal_name_s

SQL database in Fabric

  • Immutable, read-only logs in OneLake: https://onelake.blob.fabric.microsoft.com/{workspace_id}/{artifact_id}/Audit/sqldbauditlogs/.
  • By default Audit everything (batch completed + successful and failed authentications). Preconfigured scenarios: Permission Changes & Login Attempts, Data Reads and Writes, Schema Changes; or custom action groups; T-SQL predicate expression to exclude events (e.g. WHERE statement NOT LIKE '%select%').
  • Manage with the workspace Contributor role or higher, or with ALTER ANY DATABASE AUDIT. After a restore, it must be re-enabled (Manage SQL auditing → Save). SQL Server Audit (T-SQL) is not supported: use the portal or the REST API.
Discrepancy with Learn: the unit shows ALTER DATABASE AUDIT SPECIFICATION AzureAuditSpec … for Azure SQL DB and the Fabric output as “Purview/activity logging”. In Azure SQL DB, auditing is not configured with T-SQL specifications (portal/PowerShell/CLI/REST/ARM), and in Fabric SQL DB the logs go to OneLake (the Purview doc does not replace them).
Best practices: audit a limited set of actions (BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP generates high volume); store the logs outside the audited DB, with immutable storage and retention according to regulations; create alerts (login failures, permission changes, anomalous access). To audit administrators, audit the dbo user. Complements: Microsoft Defender for SQL (Vulnerability Assessment + Advanced Threat Protection) and the role of Entra logs for failed logins.
Sources: Learn · Implement auditing · Docs · SQL Server Audit · Docs · CREATE SERVER AUDIT · Docs · Auditing for Azure SQL Database · Docs · Auditing for SQL MI · Docs · Auditing for SQL database in Fabric · Docs · Audit action groups

Secure model endpoints: Managed Identity, credentials and permissions Azure SQL DB/MI SQL Server 2025 Fabric SQL DB

Calling Azure OpenAI / Foundry from the DB (sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint, CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL + AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS) can take data out of the DB and incur cost. Controls: authentication without API keys (Managed Identity), least-privilege authorization (RBAC + DB permissions), restricted network and monitoring.

  1. Enable the server's managed identity (system-assigned, or user-assigned as primary).
  2. In Azure RBAC on the Azure OpenAI resource, assign that identity the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role (inference with Entra ID).
  3. Master key: in Azure SQL DB it is created automatically when you create the credential; in SQL Server, run CREATE MASTER KEY first.
  4. Create the DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL with IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity' and the resource id (audience) in SECRET.
  5. Use it in @credential or in CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL … CREDENTIAL, and grant permissions only to whoever must use AI.
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL [https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com]
    WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity', SECRET = '{"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"}';

CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL MyEmbeddingModel
WITH (
    LOCATION = 'https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/text-embedding-3-small/embeddings?api-version=2024-02-01',
    API_FORMAT = 'Azure OpenAI',
    MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS,
    MODEL = 'text-embedding-3-small',
    CREDENTIAL = [https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com]
);

GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::MyEmbeddingModel TO [app-service-identity];   -- use the model in AI functions
GRANT CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL TO [ai-admin];                                      -- or ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL
GRANT EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT TO [app-service-identity];
GRANT REFERENCES ON DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL::[https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com] TO [app-service-identity];

DECLARE @response nvarchar(max);
DECLARE @payload  nvarchar(max) = JSON_OBJECT('input': 'hello world');
EXEC sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint
    @url = 'https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/text-embedding-3-small/embeddings?api-version=2024-02-01',
    @method = 'POST',
    @credential = [https://my-aoai.openai.azure.com],
    @payload = @payload,
    @response = @response OUTPUT;
SELECT JSON_QUERY(@response, '$.result.data[0].embedding');   -- the result goes under $.result
TopicDetails
IDENTITY of the REST credentialHTTPEndpointHeaders (secret {"api-key":"…"} plain JSON, goes in headers) · HTTPEndpointQueryString · Managed Identity (secret {"resourceid":"…"}) · SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE. For external data sources: USER IDENTITY (Entra pass-through, Azure SQL DB and Fabric SQL DB) and DATABASE MANAGED IDENTITY (Azure SQL DB, preview).
Resource id (audience)Azure OpenAI / AI Services: https://cognitiveservices.azure.com · Event Hubs: https://eventhubs.azure.net · a function protected with Entra: the APP_ID/client ID of its registration.
Credential nameMust be a valid URL on an allowed domain, with no query string; protocol + FQDN identical to those of the called URL (scheme and host case-insensitive; the rest case-sensitive); each path segment must match and the credential must be more generic than the URL.
Which identity is usedWith IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity': if there are one or more user-assigned, the primary is used; if not, the system-assigned; if both exist, the user-assigned. SQL Server 2025 (Arc): sp_configure 'allow server scoped db credentials', 1 + Arc primary MI.
Azure OpenAI rolesCognitive Services OpenAI User: inference with Entra ID. OpenAI Contributor: the above + deployments, fine-tuning. Cognitive Services Contributor: manages resources and keys but does not do inference with Entra ID.
DB permissionsEXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT (for the SP) · REFERENCES on the credential · CREATE/ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL · EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::name · CONTROL on the DB to create credentials.
Enablementsp_configure 'external rest endpoint enabled', 1; RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; on SQL Server 2025 and MI (with the SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date update policy; disabled by default; requires ALTER SETTINGS). Azure SQL DB and Fabric SQL DB: enabled by default.
NetworkHTTPS/TLS only. In Azure SQL DB/MI, only allowed domains (*.openai.azure.com, *.cognitiveservices.azure.com, *.azurewebsites.net, *.search.windows.net, *.vault.azure.net, graph.microsoft.com…); for others, API Management. Reinforce with firewall, private endpoints and outbound firewall rules (Restrict outbound networking, by FQDN).
Limits@timeout 1–230 s (default 30); @retry_count 0–10 (also "sql_rest_options": {"retry_count": n} in the model's PARAMETERS); payload ≤ 100 MB; URL ≤ 8 KB; headers ≤ 8 KB; @url nvarchar(4000); concurrency ≤ 15% of workers (max. 175), errors 10928/10936.
MonitoringWait type HTTP_EXTERNAL_CONNECTION; log table with ORIGINAL_LOGIN(), auditing and alerts for call spikes or unexpected principals.
Discrepancies in the Learn unit (the docs win): (1) role “Cognitive Services User” → the sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint doc uses Cognitive Services OpenAI User (inference with Entra ID) and the CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL one (SQL Server 2025 + Arc) asks for Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor for the identity: for sp_invoke_…, User is enough (least privilege); for CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL in SQL Server 2025 the doc requires Contributor and does not confirm that User is enough: Verify. (2) Secret {"resourceId": "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/"} and a credential named AzureOpenAICredential → doc: {"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"} and a credential with a URL name. (3) CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE … TYPE = REST and sys.dm_external_provider_certificate_store do not appear in the docs for these functions: do not use them. (4) JSON_VALUE(@response,'$.data[0].embedding') → the response is under $.result and arrays are read with JSON_QUERY. (5) Learn says Fabric has no credentials/MI; the doc shows sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint and CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL available in Fabric SQL DB, with a USER IDENTITY credential by default in external data sources.
Exam: “do not store API keys in the DB” → Managed Identity + RBAC on the AI resource; the credential uses IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity'; limit who can invoke with EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT / EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL / REFERENCES on the credential; the local ONNX model (API_FORMAT = 'ONNX Runtime') only with models from trusted sources.
Sources: Learn · Configure secure access to AI services · Docs · sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint · Docs · CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL · Docs · CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL · Docs · Azure OpenAI RBAC · Docs · Outbound firewall rules

Secure REST, GraphQL and MCP endpoints with Data API builder (DAB) Azure SQL SQL Server Fabric GraphQL API DAB 2.0 GA

DAB exposes tables, views and stored procedures as REST, GraphQL and MCP from a dab-config.json. Three pillars: authentication (who calls), authorization (what they can do) and transport (TLS). Secure by default: an entity without permissions is accessible to no one, and objects that are not in the config are ignored. (General configuration details: DAB module.)

authentication.providerWhenNotes
Unauthenticated (default)DAB behind a trusted front-end (APIM, gateway)Does not validate JWTs: everything runs as anonymous; the authenticated and custom roles are never activated (notice at startup)
EntraID (alias AzureAD)Apps with Microsoft EntraRequires jwt.audience + jwt.issuer
CustomJWT from Okta, Auth0, KeycloakRequires jwt.audience + jwt.issuer
AppService / StaticWebAppsEasyAuth: the platform injects headers (X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL)Without jwt
SimulatorDevelopment and testingOnly with host.mode = "development"; in production DAB does not start
OBO (user-delegated)SQL must see the real user (RLS, auditing)DAB 2.0, only mssql + Entra: data-source.user-delegated-auth
 
{
  "data-source": {
    "database-type": "mssql",
    "connection-string": "@env('SQL_CONNECTION_STRING')"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "rest":    { "enabled": true, "path": "/api" },
    "graphql": { "enabled": true, "path": "/graphql", "allow-introspection": false },
    "mcp":     { "enabled": true, "path": "/mcp", "dml-tools": { "delete-record": false } },
    "host": {
      "mode": "production",
      "cors": { "origins": ["https://app.contoso.com"], "allow-credentials": false },
      "authentication": {
        "provider": "EntraID",
        "jwt": { "audience": "api://my-api", "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0" }
      }
    }
  }
}
"Order": {
  "source": "dbo.Orders",
  "permissions": [
    { "role": "anonymous", "actions": [
        { "action": "read", "policy": { "database": "@item.IsPublic eq true" } } ] },
    { "role": "authenticated", "actions": [
        { "action": "read",
          "fields": { "include": ["OrderID", "OrderDate", "Status"], "exclude": ["InternalNotes", "CostPrice"] },
          "policy": { "database": "@item.OwnerId eq @claims.userId" } } ] },
    { "role": "inventory-manager", "actions": ["create", "read", "update"] },
    { "role": "admin", "actions": ["*"] }
  ]
}
dab init --database-type mssql --connection-string "@env('SQL_CONNECTION_STRING')" \
  --auth.provider EntraID --auth.audience "api://my-api" \
  --auth.issuer "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0" \
  --host-mode production --cors-origin "https://app.contoso.com"
dab add Order --source dbo.Orders --permissions "authenticated:read" \
  --fields.exclude "InternalNotes,CostPrice" --policy-database "@item.OwnerId eq @claims.userId"
dab configure --runtime.graphql.allow-introspection false
dab configure --show-effective-permissions

Roles and authorization

ConceptRule
Effective role (JWT)Without a token or X-MS-API-ROLE → anonymous. Valid token without header → authenticated. Valid token + header with a role that is in the roles claim → that role; if it is not → 403. Invalid token → 401. Only one role is evaluated per request.
Inheritance (DAB 2.0)named-role → authenticated → anonymous: an unconfigured role inherits from the next broader one. dab configure --show-effective-permissions shows the result.
Actionscreate | read | update | delete (tables and views), execute (stored procedures); * = all of that type (for SPs, only execute).
Fieldsfields.include / fields.exclude inside the action object (not at the permission level). Requesting an excluded field rejects the request.
Database policyOData predicates (eq ne gt ge lt le and or) with @item.field and @claims.type; only read, update, delete (not create or execute); translated to a WHERE; if the claim is missing → 403; the claim name is case-sensitive.
SQL RLS with DABdata-source.options.set-session-context: true (or dab init --set-session-context true): DAB calls sp_set_session_context with the claims and native RLS filters (disables the cache for that source). Or OBO: the DB authenticates the real user; requires user-delegated-auth.database-audience (e.g. https://database.windows.net), runtime.cache disabled and the variables DAB_OBO_CLIENT_ID, DAB_OBO_TENANT_ID, DAB_OBO_CLIENT_SECRET; separate connection pools per user.

Runtime hardening

SettingDefault and recommendation
runtime.graphql.allow-introspectionDefault true → set it to false in production (hides the schema).
runtime.graphql.depth-limitDefault null (no limit): set an integer to curb nested queries (DoS). CLI: --runtime.graphql.depth-limit.
runtime.host.max-response-size-mbDefault 158 (MB): maximum size of a response from the DB.
runtime.host.modeDefault production; development only for testing (enables Simulator).
rest.enabled / graphql.enabled / mcp.enabledAll true: disable the protocol you do not use.
runtime.host.corsorigins default []; allow-credentials default false: list explicit origins.
Paginationruntime.pagination.default-page-size = 100; max-page-size = 100,000. Lower the maximum to limit exfiltration and DoS.
Secrets@env('NAME') or @azure('key-vault-uri'); never passwords in dab-config.json.
To the DBManaged identity: Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity; (system-assigned) or …;User Id=CLIENT_ID_UAMI; (user-assigned); it uses DefaultAzureCredential. Give that identity only the DB permissions the entities need.
TransportHTTPS only; TLS 1.2+ and disable legacy TLS in the OS (Kestrel delegates to the OS; do not pin versions).
Azure SQL networkServer firewall (sp_set_firewall_rule in master, max. 256 rules), DB firewall (sp_set_database_firewall_rule), Allow Azure services and resources = 0.0.0.0 rule (AllowAllWindowsAzureIps, counts as 1 rule; Azure SQL Database only), Private Link / private endpoints; security changes take up to ~5 min.

MCP (SQL MCP Server)

  • Two authentication directions: inbound (client → DAB: runtime.host.authentication, a single configuration per instance; for two IdPs, two instances) and outbound (DAB → DB: connection string with managed identity).
  • API keys are not directly supported: put a gateway (Azure API Management) in front. Foundry: custom MCP tool (https://host/mcp) with Unauthenticated, Entra (OAuth identity passthrough) or key-based via gateway.
  • Seven DML tools: describe_entities, create_record, read_records, update_record, delete_record, execute_entity, aggregate_records (timeout 30 s, range 1–600). DML only, never DDL. Enable only the ones you need (--runtime.mcp.dml-tools.delete-record false) or per entity (mcp.dml-tools).
  • MCP is role-aware: it exposes only the entities, operations and fields that the effective role can use; it reuses permissions, fields and policies from REST/GraphQL. Least privilege: read-only role for agents.
  • Stored procedures as tools: --mcp.custom-tool true on a stored-procedure entity.
  • stdio transport (dab start --mcp-stdio role:ROLE): default role anonymous, uses the Simulator, requests ≤ 1 MB. Streamable HTTP for normal hosting.
  • Prompt injection: do not run AI-generated SQL without validating it; DAB avoids NL2SQL (it generates deterministic T-SQL from the entity layer). If you did it in SQL, use allow-lists, not block-lists.

Fabric: API for GraphQL

  • Requires Microsoft Entra (the registered app needs the GraphQLApi.Execute.All permission). Two data access modes, which cannot be mixed in one API: Single sign-on (the user needs the Run Queries and Mutations permission on the API and access to the source) or Saved credentials (the user only needs the API; required for Azure sources such as Azure SQL).
  • Limits: page 100 (default), 100,000 max. when paginating, response 64 MB, timeout 100 s, query depth 10.
Discrepancies in the Learn unit: the authentication block goes in runtime.host.authentication (not at the root level); fields goes inside each action (not in the permission); the recommended provider is called EntraID (AzureAD still works). The unit's mcpServers / allowedOperations / deniedTables / maxRowsReturned config is not DAB's: in DAB it is limited with per-entity permissions, dml-tools, fields and policies. Validating SQL by LIKE '%INSERT%' patterns is fragile: use allow-lists and minimal permissions. Learn does not mention that in DAB 2.0 the default provider is Unauthenticated. Small inconsistency in the docs: the help for dab init --auth.provider says every provider except Unauthenticated, StaticWebApps and Simulator requires audience/issuer, but the AppService how-to states that it does not need them (and the runtime reference requires jwt only for EntraID/AzureAD/Custom).
Exam: “hide the GraphQL schema” → allow-introspection: false; “restrict columns by role” → fields.exclude inside the action; “each user sees their rows” → database policy with @claims (or SQL RLS + session context/OBO); “read-only AI agent” → role with read only and minimal dml-tools; “API key for MCP” → gateway (APIM), not DAB.

Common traps

  • DENY wins over GRANT; REVOKE is not DENY; a table-level DENY does not override a column-level GRANT.
  • RLS applies to db_owner/dbo; DDM does not (db_owner has UNMASK via CONTROL). RLS policy: write STATE = ON; add BLOCK to prevent out-of-scope writes.
  • TDE does not protect against users with permissions and does not encrypt in transit; AE does hide data from the DBA; AE does not exist in SQL database in Fabric, requires parameters (not literals) and identical types.
  • DDM and AE are incompatible on a column; DDM can be inferred with filters; UNMASK needs SELECT.
  • Entra-only requires a prior Entra admin; SQL Server Contributor cannot enable it; Entra does not use Azure RBAC for data; failed Entra logins do not show up in the SQL audit.
  • Credential for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint: name = URL; IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity'; role Cognitive Services OpenAI User; permissions EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT + REFERENCES on the credential.
  • DAB: fields inside the action; policies do not apply to create/execute; Simulator only in development; allow-introspection is true by default.

Optimize database performance

Choose the tier, compute and configuration of Azure SQL Database; protect consistency with isolation levels and locking; and diagnose/resolve performance issues with execution plans, DMVs, Query Store, Query Performance Insight, blocking and deadlocks.

Skills measured covered:
  • Recommend database configurations
  • Preserve data integrity and consistency by using transaction isolation levels and concurrency controls
  • Evaluate query performance by using query execution plans, dynamic management views (DMVs), Query Store, and Query Performance Insight
  • Identify and resolve query performance issues, including blocking and deadlocks

Resource models and service tiers: vCore vs DTU · GP / BC / Hyperscale Azure SQL DB GA

vCore: you choose tier, compute and hardware separately (recommended for new deployments and migrations). DTU: fixed bundle of CPU + memory + I/O (Basic / Standard / Premium).

Decision rule: latency < 2 ms + free read replica → Business Critical; > 4 TB, fast growth, fast restore/scaling or several read replicas → Hyperscale; generic workload on a budget (5–10 ms) → General Purpose; migration from on-premises → vCore model.
Memorize: avg_dtu_percent = MAX(avg_cpu_percent, avg_data_io_percent, avg_log_write_percent). Basic, S0, S1 and S2 offer < 1 vCore (for CPU-intensive workloads use S3+). GP/BC storage: you choose the maximum (1 GB–4 TB, 1 GB steps; +30% of log billed).
Measure consumption and limits: sys.dm_db_resource_stats (one row every 15 s, ~1 h), sys.resource_stats in master (5-min averages, 14 days) and sys.dm_user_db_resource_governance (actual DB limits).
Learn vs docs: Learn describes Hyperscale as “suitable for the widest variety of workloads” and summarizes it in its table as “large databases, flexible scaling”; the current documentation (vCore model) presents it as “the recommended and default service tier for all new and modernizing OLTP and HTAP workloads” (not only for huge DBs) and no longer offers Azure Hybrid Benefit on new Hyperscale DBs (since Dec 2023). On the exam: “> 4 TB / growth / fast restore and scaling” → Hyperscale; the docs also recommend it by default.
