SqlPackage /Action:Publish /SourceFile:bin/Release/MyDb.dacpac \
  /TargetConnectionString:"Server=tcp:myserver.database.windows.net,1433;Initial Catalog=mydb;Authentication=Active Directory Default;Encrypt=True;Connection Timeout=30;"
SqlPackage /Action:Script       /SourceFile:MyDb.dacpac /TargetConnectionString:"..." /DeployScriptPath:Deployment.sql
SqlPackage /Action:DeployReport /SourceFile:MyDb.dacpac /TargetConnectionString:"..." /OutputPath:report.xml
SqlPackage /Action:DriftReport  /TargetConnectionString:"..." /OutputPath:drift.xml
SqlPackage /Action:Extract /SourceConnectionString:"..." /TargetFile:MyDbProject /p:ExtractTarget=SchemaObjectType

Authentication to the target (connection string)

  • SQL authentication (User ID + Password) · Windows · Entra ID: Authentication=Active Directory Password, integrated, universal (/UniversalAuthentication:True, MFA).
  • Managed identity: Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity — recommended method in automated environments (no credentials at runtime).
  • Service principal: Authentication=Active Directory Service Principal with User Id=<AppId> + Password=<secret> (SqlPackage renews the token), or an explicit token with /at:.
  • Authentication=Active Directory Default: used by the azure/login (OIDC) + azure/sql-action pattern, with no user or password.
  • Permissions: Publish on an existing DB requires db_owner; creating a new DB requires the CREATE DATABASE permission.
Exam: “see exactly which T-SQL will run before production” → Script. “Summary of creates/alters/drops to parse in the pipeline (alert on TableDataMotion or drops)” → DeployReport. “What changed in a registered DB since its registration” → DriftReport.
Watch out: .dacpac and .bacpac are compressed but not encrypted (they can contain data if extracted with data): protect them. On Windows, SqlPackage comes with the hosted images; on ubuntu-latest (24.04) it no longer does, so install it in the workflow.
Memorize: /a action · /sf source file · /tcs target connection string · /scs source connection string · /tf target file · /p property · /v SQLCMD variable · /pr profile · /at access token · /dsp deploy script path · /drp deploy report path · /op output path.
Sources: Learn · Create, build, and validate SQL database projects · Docs · SqlPackage · Docs · SqlPackage Publish · Docs · SqlPackage Script · Docs · Deploy Report and Drift Report · Docs · SqlPackage Extract · Docs · Download and install SqlPackage

Update the project and deploy changes: procedure and Publish properties GA

  1. git checkout -b feature/add-customer-email and edit the object's .sql: declare the final state, one object per file (a column change touches only Tables/Customers.sql).
  2. Rename or move objects with Rename Symbol (VS Code) or Refactor → Rename… (Visual Studio) so that the .refactorlog gets updated. Without it, the deploy is DROP + CREATE (data loss). SSMS is not integrated: create the entry by hand.
  3. Data to migrate before removing or changing a column → pre-deployment; reference data → post-deployment.
  4. dotnet build (validates references and syntax) + code analysis if enabled.
  5. Preview against the target with Script and DeployReport; look for Drop, TableDataMotion and clustered index rebuilds.
  6. Pull request → checks (build + tests) → merge to main.
  7. Pipeline: Publish dev → test → prod with approvals; the same .dacpac in all environments.
  8. Verify (the DeployReport of a second run must come out empty = idempotent) and, if there was a manual hotfix, run a drift check.
<DeploymentReport xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/dac/DeployReport/2012/02">
  <Alerts />
  <Operations>
    <Operation Name="Create">
      <Item Value="[dbo].[Products].[IX_Products_CategorySlug]" Type="SqlIndex" />
    </Operation>
    <Operation Name="Alter">
      <Item Value="[dbo].[Customers]" Type="SqlTable" />
    </Operation>
  </Operations>
</DeploymentReport>
Publish property (/p:)DefaultWhat it does
BlockOnPossibleDataLossTrueAborts at schema validation on changes with possible data loss (DROP COLUMN, less precision, type change with cast), even if there is no data. With False it can still fail at runtime if there is non-convertible data
DropObjectsNotInSourceFalseDrops objects from the target that are not in the .dacpac (takes precedence over DropExtendedProperties)
DoNotDropObjectTypes · ExcludeObjectTypes—List separated by ; (Users;Permissions;RoleMembership…); the repeatable singular forms DoNotDropObjectType / ExcludeObjectType exist
DropIndexesNotInSource · DropConstraintsNotInSource · DropDmlTriggersNotInSource · DropStatisticsNotInSource · DropExtendedPropertiesNotInSourceTrueTable children not in the project do get dropped
DropPermissionsNotInSource · DropRoleMembersNotInSourceFalsePermissions and role members outside the project are kept
GenerateSmartDefaultsFalseSupplies a default value when adding a NOT NULL column to a table with data
AllowTableRecreationTrueAllows the table to be re-created (keeps data; may have a performance impact)
IncludeTransactionalScriptsFalseUses transactions when possible
CreateNewDatabaseFalseDrops and re-creates the DB instead of updating it
RegisterDataTierApplication · BlockWhenDriftDetectedFalse · TrueRegisters the schema (enables DriftReport) · blocks updating a DB whose schema no longer matches its registration
AllowIncompatiblePlatformFalsePublishes even if the target platform does not match the target
ScriptDatabaseOptionsTrueApplies the project's DB options; False leaves them intact
VerifyDeploymentTruePreliminary checks that stop the publish if something will block it
IgnorePreDeployScript · IgnorePostDeployScriptFalseDoes not attach the pre/post script from the .dacpac to the plan (since SqlPackage 170.1)
IncludeCompositeObjectsFalseIncludes in the publish the objects of references to the same DB
BackupDatabaseBeforeChangesFalsePrior backup; does not apply to Azure SQL Database
CommandTimeout · LongRunningCommandTimeout · DatabaseLockTimeout60 · 0 · 60 s0 = wait with no limit; lock timeout -1 = indefinite
What is lost with drift: by default, tables/views/procedures that are not in the project are not dropped (DropObjectsNotInSource=False), but table-child indexes, constraints, and triggers are (default True). The module warns that a column added by hand in production would be lost in the next deploy; with BlockOnPossibleDataLoss=True the publish aborts instead of losing data.
Exam: “the publish stops because of possible data loss” → do not set BlockOnPossibleDataLoss=False blindly: migrate the data in a pre-deployment or use refactorlog. “Add a NOT NULL column to a table with rows” → define a DEFAULT or use GenerateSmartDefaults.
Sources: Learn · Detect and resolve schema drift · Docs · SqlPackage Publish (properties) · Docs · Refactor overview

Pre/post-deployment scripts and reference data (static data) in source control GA

The schema is declarative, but reference data (statuses, regions, default configuration) is also part of the “product”. It goes in the repo as pre/post-deployment scripts: they travel inside the .dacpac but are neither compiled nor validated in the model and run on every deployment.

CriterionPre-deploymentPost-deployment
When it runsBefore the deployment plan (but the plan is already computed when it runs)After the plan finishes
Typical useDrop constraints, migrate/back up data before the schema changePopulate lookups, application default values
How many per projectAt most one of each type; for several files, use SQLCMD :r from that single entry point
Skipped with/p:IgnorePreDeployScript=True/p:IgnorePostDeployScript=True
 
<ItemGroup>
  <PreDeploy Include="Scripts\PreDeployment\prep-db.sql" />
  <PostDeploy Include="PostDeploy.sql" />
</ItemGroup>
<ItemGroup>
  <Build Remove="Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-statuses.sql" />
  <None Include="Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-statuses.sql" />
</ItemGroup>
:r .\Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-statuses.sql
:r .\Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-regions.sql
:r .\Scripts\PostDeployment\seed-app-settings.sql
MERGE INTO [dbo].[OrderStatuses] AS target
USING (VALUES
    (1, N'Pending'), (2, N'Processing'), (3, N'Shipped'),
    (4, N'Delivered'), (5, N'Cancelled')
) AS source ([StatusID], [StatusName])
ON target.[StatusID] = source.[StatusID]
WHEN MATCHED THEN
    UPDATE SET [StatusName] = source.[StatusName]
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT ([StatusID], [StatusName])
    VALUES (source.[StatusID], source.[StatusName]);
StrategyIdempotentDeletes rows it does not ownWhen
Plain INSERTNo: the 2nd deploy fails because of a duplicate keyNoNever in post-deployment
INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTSYesNoInitial insert; does not update existing values
MERGE (MATCHED → UPDATE, NOT MATCHED → INSERT)YesNoControlled lookup whose values can change
MERGE … WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETEYesYes (full synchronization)Only if the table is 100% static (Fabric example)

SQLCMD variables (different values per environment)

  • They are declared with <SqlCmdVariable Include="EnvironmentName"> (DefaultValue + Value = $(SqlCmdVar__1)) and used as $(EnvironmentName) in objects and scripts: IF '$(EnvironmentName)' = 'testing' …
  • The value is set at deployment: sqlpackage /Action:Publish … /v:EnvironmentName=production or in the publish profile. /v: variables take precedence over those in the profile.
  • Predefined DacFx variables (e.g. $(DatabaseName)): Verify — the SQL projects doc does not list them; it only documents the ones you declare with SqlCmdVariable.
Docs discrepancy: the SQL projects page says that, without /v or a profile, the variables are left empty; the Publish reference says that an error occurs if a value is missing. Always pass all the values. The DefaultValue is not compiled into the .dacpac.
Best practices: one file per reference table, referenced with :r; every script idempotent; validate the result by inspecting the .dacpac (rename it to .zip: it contains the single combined .sql for pre and for post). Do not put secrets in these scripts: pass them with /v: from the secret store.
Memorize: max. 1 pre + 1 post · :r to include · Build Remove + None Include (otherwise the file is compiled as an object and the build fails) · MERGE instead of INSERT.

Source control, branching, pull requests, and conflicts GA

Each object is a file, so Git versions at the object level: a commit that changes Customers and a procedure shows exactly those two files, not a migration script of hundreds of lines.

cd MyDatabaseProject
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit of database project"

Version

  • .sqlproj and all the .sql files (one object per file)
  • Pre/post-deployment scripts and reference data
  • .refactorlog, .scmp, global.json
  • Publish profiles without credentials
  • Workflows, pipeline YAML, and CODEOWNERS

Ignore (.gitignore)

bin/
obj/
*.dacpac
*.user

The .dacpac is regenerated on every CI build. Do not version connection strings with passwords, tokens, or .bacpac/.dacpac with data either. dotnet new sqlproj -g adds a complete .gitignore.

Branching and pull requests

Three principles (module and Azure Repos guide): one feature branch per change, integrate into main only through a PR, and keep main always deployable. Short branches = fewer conflicts; long branches that diverge from main are harder to merge. (GitFlow with develop/release/hotfix or trunk-based are general alternatives; the module only describes this one.)

git checkout -b feature/add-customer-email
git add .
git commit -m "Add Email column to Customers table"
git push origin feature/add-customer-email

PR review questions:

  • Does the change break existing queries or procedures?
  • Do the names follow the project conventions?
  • Does it require updating a post-deployment script?
  • Is there data loss, or does it need a migration?

CI on the PR: GitHub → workflow with pull_request targeting main + required status check; Azure DevOps → Build validation policy (in Azure Repos Git, PR triggers are implemented with branch policies, and draft PRs do not trigger the build).

Resolve conflicts

  1. Bring main into your branch: git checkout feature/add-customer-phone and git pull origin main.
  2. Git marks the conflicting sections: open the file and review both versions.
  3. Edit to keep both changes with valid syntax (e.g. Phone and Address columns in the same CREATE TABLE).
  4. git add Tables/Customers.sql and git commit; then rebuild: dotnet build MyDatabaseProject.sqlproj.
Watch out: a clean text merge does not guarantee a valid schema (one branch renames a column and another adds a procedure that uses the old name): always rebuild after resolving. With SDK-style, adding files does not touch the .sqlproj (globbing), which reduces conflicts in that file; the PreDeploy/PostDeploy/Build Remove items do live in it.
Sources: Learn · Configure source control and manage reference data · Learn · Manage branching, pull requests, and conflict resolution · Docs · About branches and branch policies · Docs · Azure Repos Git (PR triggers)

Schema drift: detect and resolve (Schema Compare, Extract, DeployReport, DriftReport) GA

Drift = difference between what the project defines and what exists in the live DB. Causes: manual changes (ALTER TABLE in a query window), emergency hotfixes that do not make it back into the project, and third-party tools (monitoring agents, ORMs). The danger is the next deploy: it computes the diff against the project and may revert the hotfix. It must be detected before deploying; the goal is not to avoid it altogether but to resolve it early.

TechniqueWhat it comparesRequirementsResult / use
Schema Compare (.scmp)DB, project, or .dacpac in any combination and directionVS, VS Code, SSMS (SDK-style SSDT in VS 2022: without DB → project)Grid by action; you exclude differences and update the target or generate a script. DB → project = find drift; project → DB = preview a deploy
Extract + git statusLive schema extracted to files vs what is versionedProject under Git; /p:ExtractTarget=SchemaObjectTypeNo. of changed files = “drift count”; suitable for a scheduled job
DeployReport / ScriptProject .dacpac vs live DB.dacpac + connectionWhat the next deploy would change (XML or T-SQL)
DriftReportDB vs its DAC registrationDB registered with /p:RegisterDataTierApplication=True in a previous publishXML of changes since registration
  • Comparison options: Ignore whitespace · Ignore column order · Ignore partition schemes · Drop indexes not in source · Block on possible data loss; also, which object types to include (tables, procedures, indexes, permissions, UDTs…).
  • .scmp file: XML with source/target, options, and excluded types. Commit it to repeat the same comparison across the whole team.
  • Resolve: if the production hotfix was correct, import it into the project (Schema Compare lets you pick differences: accept the index, discard the agent's temporary table) and open a PR; otherwise, publish the project again.
rm -rf MyDatabaseProject
sqlpackage /Action:Extract /SourceConnectionString:"{connection string}" /TargetFile:MyDatabaseProject /p:ExtractTarget=SchemaObjectType
git status --porcelain | wc -l     # no. of changed files = drift
Practical notes (inference): the recipe deletes the project folder, so git status would also count .sqlproj and scripts as deleted; also, the SchemaObjectType structure (schema/type folders) must match the repo's. Extract to a separate folder or rely on DeployReport/Schema Compare. And Extract uses IgnorePermissions=True by default: permissions drift is not visible except with /p:IgnorePermissions=False.
Exam: “a DBA added an index in production and the project does not have it” → schema drift, detected with schema comparison (not with dotnet build, Git, or Publish). “Scheduled, automated check” → SqlPackage /Action:Extract in a job with schedule.
Memorize: DriftReport only works with a registered DB (RegisterDataTierApplication, default False); BlockWhenDriftDetected (default True) blocks updating a DB whose schema no longer matches its registration (literal text from the doc: “…or is unregistered”).
Sources: Learn · Detect and resolve schema drift · Docs · Schema comparison overview · Docs · Deploy Report and Drift Report · Docs · Data-tier applications (DAC)

Testing strategy: build, unit tests, and integration tests SQL Server unit tests (SSDT)

A project that compiles does not prove that a procedure calculates correctly. Three layers, each slower and more expensive, but each detects what the previous one cannot.

LevelWhat it detectsHowIn the pipeline
Build validationSyntax and broken references (only validates the structure)dotnet buildFirst step, also on every PR
Unit testsLogic errors in SPs/functions with known inputsSQL Server unit tests (SSDT) or tSQLtAfter build and deployment to a test DB
Integration testsEnd-to-end scenarios: sequences of SPs, triggers, views after related changesDedicated DB with the project deployed + seed dataBefore promoting to staging/production

SSDT SQL Server unit tests (Visual Studio)

  • Three phases per test: pre-test (prepare data), test (runs the SP/query), and post-test (clean up); the T-SQL is validated with test conditions.
  • Create: open the project → SQL Server Object Explorer → right-click the object → Create Unit Tests → C# test project → connection to the development DB → check Automatically deploy the database project before unit tests are run.
Test conditionFails if…
Row Countthe result set does not have the expected no. of rows
Scalar Valuea specific cell does not equal the expected value (default null)
Expected Schemathe result set's columns or types do not match the defined ones
Data Checksumthe checksum differs (do not use with generated dates or identity: it changes on every run)
Empty ResultSet · Not Empty ResultSetthe result set is not empty · is empty
Execution Timethe test script takes longer than the limit (default 30 s; only the test script counts, not pre/post)
Inconclusivealways (Inconclusive result); it is the default condition of each test: delete it when you add the real ones
 
[TestMethod()]
[ExpectedSqlException(Severity = 16, MatchFirstError = false, State = 1)]
public void Sales_uspCancelOrder_FilledOrder_Test()

The test passes only if the procedure raises an error with that severity/state (MessageNumber = nnnnn also exists; the parameters you omit are ignored); if it finishes without an error, it fails. MatchFirstError is true by default (only looks at the first error); with false it matches any of the SqlErrors. The attribute goes in the generated .cs in Solution Explorer.

# Azure DevOps
- task: VSTest@2
  inputs:
    testAssembly: '**\*Tests.dll'
    searchFolder: '$(System.DefaultWorkingDirectory)'
# GitHub Actions
- name: Run database unit tests
  run: dotnet test ./DatabaseTests/DatabaseTests.csproj

Reliable test environment

  • Isolated from production: dedicated test instance or DB; never run tests against production.
  • Known state before each run: post-deployment or cleanup scripts; automatic deployment of the project before the tests.
  • Connection strings externalized in configuration (local and CI point to different DBs without changing code).
  • A failed test stops the pipeline: the change does not reach staging or production.
Verify: the SSDT documentation only describes creating and running SQL Server unit tests in Visual Studio (C# test project). The module uses dotnet test (GitHub Actions) and VSTest@2 (Azure DevOps) without documenting the runner or the agent (Windows?): on Linux or containers the practical option is tSQLt (next topic).
Exam: “an SP must raise an error when a parameter is missing” → attribute [ExpectedSqlException] (not [ExpectedException], [TestMethod], or [ShouldThrow]). “Validate no. of rows / specific value / columns and types” → Row Count / Scalar Value / Expected Schema.
Sources: Learn · Design and implement a testing strategy · Docs · Verify database code by using SQL Server unit tests · Docs · Use test conditions

tSQLt (unit tests in T-SQL) and integration tests in CI with a SQL Server container SQL Server

tSQLt is an open-source unit testing framework written in T-SQL: each test runs inside a transaction that is rolled back when it finishes, tests are grouped by schema (test class), and the output can be text or XML (useful in CI). Test procedures must be named test…; if the class has a SetUp procedure, it runs before each test.

EXEC tSQLt.NewTestClass 'testFinancialApp';
GO
CREATE PROCEDURE testFinancialApp.[test ConvertCurrency uses the given rate]
AS
BEGIN
    DECLARE @actual MONEY, @expected MONEY = 2.4;
    SELECT @actual = FinancialApp.ConvertCurrency(1.2, 2.00);   -- (rate, amount)
    EXEC tSQLt.AssertEquals @expected, @actual;
END;
GO
EXEC tSQLt.Run 'testFinancialApp';   -- one class, or 'Class.[test name]'
EXEC tSQLt.RunAll;                   -- all classes in the DB
ProcedureSyntax and notes
tSQLt.NewTestClass'name' creates the schema of the test class
tSQLt.FakeTable'schema.table' [, @Identity = 1] [, @ComputedColumns = 1] [, @Defaults = 1]: replaces the table with an empty one without constraints (accepts tables, views, and synonyms; not #temp tables). @SchemaName is deprecated: the tutorial still uses the old form ('schema', 'table')
tSQLt.AssertEquals · AssertEqualsTable@Expected, @Actual [, @Message] (values) · @Expected, @Actual [, @Message] [, @FailMsg] with table names (compares the content; AssertEqualsTableSchema compares only the schema)
tSQLt.ExpectException[@ExpectedMessage] [@ExpectedSeverity] [@ExpectedState] [@Message] [@ExpectedMessagePattern] [@ExpectedErrorNumber]: all optional; call it before the code that fails; only once per test; if no error is raised, the test fails
tSQLt.SpyProcedure · ApplyConstraint · FailReplaces an SP and logs its parameters in <proc>_SpyProcedureLog · applies a specific constraint to a fake table · fails the test with a message
tSQLt.Run · tSQLt.RunAll[@testName] [, @TestResultFormatter]; with no parameter it repeats the last call. If something fails they raise Msg 50000, Level 16, State 10 + Test Case Summary: N test case(s) executed, X succeeded, Y failed, Z errored. → the pipeline step fails
  • Installation: PrepareServer.sql (enables CLR and installs a certificate; requires SA permissions, once per server) and tSQLt.class.sql in the development/test DB.
  • Never install tSQLt in production. Compatible with SQL Server 2005 SP2+ (all editions) and certified for SQL Server on Linux (release notes: applies to the container). It uses CLR, which Azure SQL Database does not support: it is not listed as supported on Azure SQL Database (the README does not mention it; open issues #70, #188, and #207 on GitHub); in Azure, test against a test SQL Server or a container.
  • XML output for CI: EXEC tSQLt.SetTestResultFormatter 'tSQLt.XmlResultFormatter'; or directly EXEC tSQLt.RunWithXmlResults; (formatters: DefaultResultFormatter, XmlResultFormatter, NullTestResultFormatter).

Integration tests in GitHub Actions with an ephemeral SQL Server

Pattern from the official Azure SQL blog (CI/CD, part 3), with a 2025 image and MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD (SA_PASSWORD is deprecated). Before the first step, add a wait until the container accepts connections (the blog uses a loop with sqlcmd).

jobs:
  integration-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      mssql:
        image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest
        env:
          ACCEPT_EULA: "Y"
          MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SQL_TEST_SA_PASSWORD }}
        ports:
          - 1433:1433
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Create DB and enable CLR
        uses: azure/sql-action@v2.4
        with:
          connection-string: "Server=localhost;Initial Catalog=master;User ID=sa;Password=${{ secrets.SQL_TEST_SA_PASSWORD }};Encrypt=False;"
          path: ./setups/setupDatabase.sql
      - name: Publish test project (with tSQLt)
        uses: azure/sql-action@v2.4
        with:
          connection-string: "Server=localhost;Initial Catalog=testingDB;User ID=sa;Password=${{ secrets.SQL_TEST_SA_PASSWORD }};Encrypt=False;"
          path: ./TestsSQLServer/TestsSQLServer.sqlproj
          action: publish
          arguments: /p:IncludeCompositeObjects=True
      - name: Run tSQLt (script with EXEC tSQLt.RunAll;)
        uses: azure/sql-action@v2.4
        with:
          connection-string: "Server=localhost;Initial Catalog=testingDB;User ID=sa;Password=${{ secrets.SQL_TEST_SA_PASSWORD }};Encrypt=False;"
          path: ./TestsSQLServer/myTests/runAllTests.sql
Exam: tests in CI without touching production → container or isolated test instance, project deployed before each run, and seed data via post-deployment; the failed test stops the pipeline. “tSQLt in production” → never.
Container password: minimum 8 characters and three of the four categories (uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols). The 2025-latest image exists on MCR alongside 2022-latest; stopping and removing the container loses its data (exactly what we want in CI).
Sources: Learn · Design and implement a testing strategy · Docs · tSQLt quick start · Docs · tSQLt tutorial · Docs · tSQLt ExpectException · Docs · Azure SQL CI/CD part 3: tSQLt · Docs · SQL Server container images · Docs · tSQLt on GitHub (README, release notes, issues)

GitHub Actions: build → deploy pipeline with azure/sql-action and OIDC Azure SQL GA

Two stages: Build (compiles the project and produces the .dacpac) and Deploy (publishes that same artifact per environment). Workflows live in .github/workflows/. A single workflow covers CI (PR: build only) and CD (push to main: build + deploy with approval from the environment).

name: Build and Deploy SQL Project
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build SQL project (validates references and syntax)
        run: dotnet build ./Database/Database.sqlproj -c Release -o ./output
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dacpac
          path: ./output/Database.dacpac
  deploy:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'    # PR = CI only
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production          # reviewers, wait timer, deployment branches
    permissions:
      id-token: write                # required for OIDC
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dacpac
      - run: dotnet tool install -g microsoft.sqlpackage   # ubuntu-latest no longer includes it
      - uses: azure/login@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - uses: azure/sql-action@v2.4
        with:
          connection-string: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING }}
          path: ./Database.dacpac
          action: publish
Approve with evidence: before the environment with reviewers, add a plan job (same azure/login + SqlPackage installed) that runs sqlpackage /Action:Script … /DeployScriptPath:deploy.sql and /Action:DeployReport … /OutputPath:report.xml with env: SQL_CONN: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING }} and uploads both with actions/upload-artifact: the approvers review the exact T-SQL (the module's pattern). Pass the secret through env, not inline in the command.
azure/sql-action inputDefaultNotes
connection-stringrequiredIncludes DB and authentication; store it as a secret
pathrequired.sql (supports glob), .dacpac, or .sqlproj (must use the Microsoft.Build.Sql SDK; the action builds it with dotnet build)
actionrequired except with .sqlPublish · Script · DeployReport · DriftReport
arguments—Properties/parameters of SqlPackage (/p:DropObjectsNotInSource=true, /Profile:, /Variables:) or of go-sqlcmd (-v in scripts)
build-arguments—dotnet build options for .sqlproj (-c Release)
sqlpackage-path · skip-firewall-check— · falseSqlPackage path · skips the server access check (both since v2.3)
summary · comment-pr · github-tokentrue · auto (off|auto|always) · workflow tokenSummary in the job summary and comment on the PR (requires pull-requests: write). Only on the master branch: the action.yml of the v2.3 and v2.4 tags does not have them (no release as of 2026-10-30)
Outputschanges-detected · objects-changed · deployment-report-path · deployment-script-path (also only on master, not on v2.4)
  • Authentication in the connection string: SQL auth, Entra password, service principal, or Entra default (v1.x only supported SQL auth). .sql scripts are run with go-sqlcmd.
  • Firewall (Azure SQL Database): with “Allow Azure services” nothing is needed; otherwise, put azure/login first: the action opens and closes a temporary rule for the runner's IP, and the identity needs the SQL Security Manager role or a custom role with Microsoft.Sql/servers/firewallRules/write and delete. Managed Instance: network connectivity to the endpoint (public = port 3342); SQL Server: network access or a self-hosted runner.
Watch out — filters and status checks: if you add paths or branches to a workflow that is a required check and gets skipped (also by commit message), its checks stay Pending and block the merge: do not require workflows that can be skipped. Job names must be unique across workflows.
Discrepancies with the module: its YAML uses azure/login@v2 without permissions: id-token: write (required for OIDC). Versions as of 2026-10-30: azure/login v3 (v2 in maintenance), azure/sql-action v2.4 (the module uses @v2.3 and the SQL projects doc @v2; watch out: the v2 tag does not float, it points to the original 2022 commit, without sqlpackage-path or skip-firewall-check: pin @v2.4), actions/checkout v7, upload-artifact v7, download-artifact v8, setup-dotnet v6; the YAMLs above use the module's major versions (v4), which still exist. For hardening, pin a full SHA.
Sources: Learn · Implement CI/CD pipelines · Docs · Azure/sql-action · Docs · sql-action connection guide · Docs · SQL projects automation · Docs · SqlPackage in development pipelines · Docs · Troubleshooting required status checks

Azure DevOps: YAML pipeline with SqlAzureDacpacDeployment@1 Azure SQL GA

Same pattern: the Build stage publishes the .dacpac as a pipeline artifact and the Deploy stage uses a deployment job with environment (that is where Approvals and checks are evaluated). A deployment job does not clone the repo (use checkout: self if you need it) and automatically downloads the current run's artifact, only in the deploy hook, into $(Pipeline.Workspace)/<artifact>.

trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]
  paths:
    include: [Database/*]
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: build
    pool:
      vmImage: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
      inputs:
        command: build
        projects: Database/Database.sqlproj
        arguments: -c Release -o $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)
    - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
      inputs:
        targetPath: $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/Database.dacpac
        artifact: dacpac
- stage: Deploy
  dependsOn: Build
  jobs:
  - deployment: deploy_prod
    environment: production       # approvals and checks (configured in the UI)
    pool:
      vmImage: windows-latest     # the task requires a Windows agent
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: SqlAzureDacpacDeployment@1
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: sc-sql-prod
              AuthenticationType: servicePrincipal
              ServerName: myserver.database.windows.net
              DatabaseName: mydb
              deployType: DacpacTask
              DeploymentAction: Publish
              DacpacFile: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/dacpac/Database.dacpac
          - script: dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.SqlPackage
            displayName: Install SqlPackage
          - script: |
              sqlpackage /Action:Publish \
                /SourceFile:"$(Pipeline.Workspace)/dacpac/Database.dacpac" \
                /TargetConnectionString:"$SQL_CONN"
            displayName: Publish
            env:
              SQL_CONN: $(ConnectionString)   # secret: it must be mapped explicitly
Task inputValues / default
azureSubscription (alias ConnectedServiceNameARM)ARM service connection (required with azureConnectionType = ConnectedServiceNameARM, the default)
AuthenticationTypeserver (default) · aadAuthenticationPassword · aadAuthenticationIntegrated · connectionString · servicePrincipal. ServerName and DatabaseName are required except with connectionString; SqlUsername/SqlPassword only with server (mark the variable as secret)
deployTypeDacpacTask (default) · SqlTask (SqlFile) · InlineSqlTask (SqlInline)
DeploymentActionPublish (default) · Extract · Export · Import · Script · DriftReport · DeployReport
DacpacFileRequired with Publish, Script, and DeployReport (BacpacFile for Import)
PublishProfile · AdditionalArgumentsProfile XML (if it has secrets, upload it to Secure files and download it with DownloadSecureFile) · SqlPackage arguments (/p:IgnoreAnsiNulls=True, /DiagnosticsFile:…) that take precedence over the profile
IpDetectionMethod · DeleteFirewallRuleAutoDetect (default) or IPAddressRange (+ StartIpAddress/EndIpAddress) · true (default): deletes the rule when it finishes
Exam: PR validation in Azure Repos Git is the Build validation policy (its PR triggers are implemented with branch policies). Approvals and checks are not in the YAML: they are managed by the resource administrators (environment, service connection…) from the UI, so whoever edits the YAML cannot remove them.
Discrepancies with the module: its example has a single stage, with PublishBuildArtifacts@1 and AuthenticationType: server + $(SqlPassword) (it stores a password): here PublishPipelineArtifact@1, a deployment job with environment, and servicePrincipal are used (the principal of the ARM service connection must exist as a DB user). On Linux agents the task does not work (it requires Windows): use SqlPackage. Passing $(ConnectionString) on the command line exposes it: the secret variables guide recommends mapping it to an environment variable (env:); they are not decrypted on their own.
Sources: Learn · Implement CI/CD pipelines · Docs · SqlAzureDacpacDeployment@1 · Docs · Deployment jobs · Docs · SQL projects automation · Docs · Set secret variables

Secrets management and pipeline authentication: secrets, OIDC, service principal, managed identity, and Key Vault Azure SQL GA

A connection string with a password in the YAML is a breach waiting to happen. Rules: no credentials in the repo, secrets injected at runtime, least privilege, and, better still, no secrets (OIDC or managed identity).

MethodStored secretWhen
SQL auth (user/password)Yes: connection string in a secretLegacy / SQL Server; avoid in production. Rotate with Key Vault (+ Azure Functions to automate the rotation)
Service principal + client secretYes: client secret that expires (creds of azure/login or Authentication=Active Directory Service Principal)If OIDC is not possible
OIDC / federated credentialsNo (only non-sensitive IDs)Recommended in GitHub Actions: azure/login with client-id, tenant-id, subscription-id
Managed identityNoRunner/agent in Azure with an assigned identity: Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity. Avoid it on self-hosted runners for public repos
Azure DevOps: ARM service connection with workload identity federationNoRecommended in ADO (automatic app registration or managed identity)

OIDC with GitHub Actions: procedure

  1. Create an app registration (or a user-assigned managed identity) and its service principal.
  2. Entra admin center → App registrations → Certificates & secrets → Federated credentials → Add credential → scenario GitHub actions deploying Azure resources → Organization, Repository, and Entity type (Environment, Branch, Pull request, or Tag).
  3. Issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com · Audience api://AzureADTokenExchange · Subject depending on the entity type (next table).
  4. Grant access to the DB (SQL below) and, if you use the temporary firewall rule, the SQL Security Manager role or a custom role.
  5. GitHub: store AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID as secrets; in the workflow, permissions: id-token: write + azure/login (see the GitHub Actions topic).
Entity typeSubject (sub) that must match exactly
Environmentrepo:ORG/REPO:environment:ENV-NAME
Branchrepo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH-NAME
Pull requestrepo:ORG/REPO:pull_request
Tagrepo:ORG/REPO:ref:refs/tags/TAG-NAME
 
-- As the Entra admin of the target DB
CREATE USER [sample-app-registration] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;
ALTER ROLE [db_ddladmin] ADD MEMBER [sample-app-registration];   -- example from the guide (may require more roles)
-- Connection string (secret/variable): Server=<srv>.database.windows.net;Initial Catalog=<db>;
--   Authentication=Active Directory Default;Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=False;Connection Timeout=30;
Subject trap: if the job declares environment:, the token carries the environment in the subject (not the branch or pull_request); the credential must be of type Environment. An incorrect subject is created without error and fails later (AADSTS700213, no matching federated identity record). Limits: 20 credentials per app or user-assigned managed identity, no wildcards (flexible federated credentials, in preview, support claims-matching expressions), unique issuer + subject. Without permissions: id-token: write there is no OIDC token (the module's YAML omits it). Publish documents db_owner on an existing database.

Where to store secrets

  • GitHub: repository, environment and organization secrets (the lowest level wins). They are referenced with ${{ secrets.NAME }} and must be passed explicitly to the step. Names: alphanumeric and _, no GITHUB_ prefix, cannot start with a number, case-insensitive. Limits: 1,000 org secrets, 100 per repo, 100 per environment; 48 KB each. Environment secrets are released to the job only when the protection rules (reviewers) pass. 
    gh secret set AZURE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING                      # repository
gh secret set AZURE_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING --env production     # environment
  • Azure Key Vault (centralize and rotate): in ADO, the AzureKeyVault@2 task (azureSubscription, KeyVaultName, SecretsFilter default *, RunAsPreJob default false) or a variable group linked to the vault; the identity needs Get and List permissions on secrets. In GitHub: azure/login + az keyvault secret show --vault-name … --name … --query value -o tsv and echo "::add-mask::$VALUE".
  • ADO: secret variables are not automatically decrypted into environment variables; map them with env: and never pass them on the command line.
  • Variables (non-sensitive): in GitHub, ${{ vars.NAME }} can be used for configuration values such as server names; azure/login@v3 masks the client-id by default (mask-client-id: true) even if it comes from vars. Use one environment per stage (dev/test/prod), each with its own secrets.

Authorization (users, roles, permissions) as code

  • DacFx treats Users, DatabaseRoles, RoleMembership and Permissions as object types: they can live in the project and be excluded with DoNotDropObjectTypes/ExcludeObjectTypes. By default Publish does not drop permissions or role members that are not in the source (DropPermissionsNotInSource/DropRoleMembersNotInSource = False) and IgnorePermissions=False; Extract ignores them (IgnorePermissions=True).
  • Passwords for SQL users created in a post-deployment: SQLCMD variables passed with /v: from the secret store, never in the .sql. When extracting a database with SQL users, SqlPackage replaces the password with a different one: change it after publishing.
Exam: “authenticate the pipeline without storing passwords” → OIDC with federated credentials (azure/login). “Secrets accessible only to the production job” → environment secrets. “Centralize and rotate credentials” → Azure Key Vault.
Sources: Learn · Implement CI/CD pipelines · Docs · sql-action connection guide · Docs · Azure/login · Docs · Federated identity credentials · Docs · GitHub OIDC reference · Docs · GitHub secrets reference · Docs · AzureKeyVault@2 · Docs · ARM service connection

Deployment pipeline controls: branch policies, triggers, approvals and code owners

A pipeline that deploys to production on every push with no review is risky for database changes. Control layers: protect the branch (PR + checks + code owners), protect the environment (approvals, allowed branches) and protect the credentials (secrets per environment, branch control). Separate the environments (dev/test/prod) with one environment per stage, each with its own rules and secrets.

NeedGitHubAzure DevOps
Protect mainBranch protection rule or rulesetBranch policies (a branch with required policies cannot be deleted and every change goes through a PR)
Minimum reviewersRequire pull request reviews (no. of approvals)Require a minimum number of reviewers
The build must passRequire status checks to pass before mergingBuild validation (Required/Optional)
Reviewers by code areaCODEOWNERS + Require review from Code OwnersAutomatically included reviewers (path filters)
Resolved commentsRequire conversation resolution before mergingCheck for comment resolution
Approve a deploymentEnvironment → Required reviewersEnvironment → Approvals (UI, not YAML)
Which branches can deployEnvironment → Deployment branches and tagsBranch control check (refs/heads/main)
Delay / windowWait timerBusiness hours check · deferred approvals
Triggerson: push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, schedule (+ paths)trigger: (CI) + Build validation (PR)

GitHub: branch protection, environments and CODEOWNERS

Require pull request reviewsRequire status checksRequire conversation resolutionRequire signed commitsRequire linear historyRequire merge queueRequire deployments to succeedLock branchDo not allow bypassingRestrict who can pushAllow force pushesAllow deletions

By default a protection rule disables force pushes and deletions and does not apply to admins (unless Do not allow bypassing). Status checks strict = Require branches to be up to date before merging (default when requiring checks); loose = without that requirement.

CriterionBranch protection ruleRuleset
Apply at the same timeOnly one per branchSeveral: they are aggregated and the most restrictive version wins
StatusActive or deletedActive / Disabled without deleting
Who manages / views itAdmins (or roles with “edit repository rules”)Anyone with read access can view the active rulesets
Extras—Push rulesets (paths, extensions, size); up to 75 per repo; org-wide with Enterprise
Environment (GitHub)Values and limits
Required reviewersUp to 6 users or teams (with at least read access); one approval is enough; Prevent self-review stops whoever triggered the deployment from approving
Wait timerInteger from 1 to 43,200 minutes (30 days); does not count as billable time. The GitHub docs define it as a delay of the job after it is triggered; Learn describes it as a delay between approval and execution
Deployment branches and tagsNo restriction · Protected branches only · Selected branches and tags (fnmatch pattern against GITHUB_REF; * does not match /)
Bypass · custom rulesAllow administrators to bypass enabled by default · custom rules with GitHub Apps (public preview); maximum 6 active rules per environment
Secrets and variablesAccessible only to jobs that use the environment and after the rules pass. The environment name: ≤ 255 characters, unique per repo, case-insensitive
PlansWith Free/Pro/Team, reviewers, wait timer, bypass and custom rules exist only in public repos (they are not available in private repos); deployment branches and environment variables do work in private repos with Pro/Team
 
/Database/   @contoso/db-team
*.sql        @contoso/db-team @contoso/dba-lead
/.github/    @contoso/platform-owners
  • Location: .github/, root or docs/ (the first one found is used); must be on the PR's base branch; < 3 MB.
  • gitignore-style pattern (without ! or [ ]) + @username/@org/team on the same line; the last match wins; owners need write access.
  • It only requests a review (not on a draft PR; Learn says the file “requires” the review, which is imprecise). To make it mandatory, enable Require review from Code Owners; the approval of one of the owners is enough. Protect the file itself (/.github/ with an owner).
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['Database/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:            # manual deployment
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1-5'       # scheduled drift check (UTC)

Azure DevOps: branch policies and approvals & checks

  • Branch policies (all Off by default): minimum number of reviewers (options: Allow requestors to approve their own changes, Prohibit the most recent pusher from approving, vote reset when the branch changes), linked work items, comment resolution, limit merge types, Build validation, status checks and Automatically included reviewers.
  • Build validation: trigger Automatic (when the PR is created or updated) or Manual; requirement Required or Optional; expiration Immediately when <branch> is updated · After <n> hours · Never; optional path filter.
  • Approvals and checks (on environments, service connections, repos, variable groups, secure files and agent pools) run in this order: (1) static checks (Branch control, Required template, Evaluate artifact) → (2) pre-check approvals → (3) dynamic checks (Approval, Invoke Azure Function, Invoke REST API, Business Hours, Query Azure Monitor alerts) → (4) post-check approvals → (5) Exclusive lock. They are managed through the UI (not in the YAML); if they expire, the stage is skipped; with a group as approver, one member is enough; only a resource admin can Bypass.
  • Branch control (on the service connection or the environment): list of allowed branches in full format refs/heads/main and, optionally, require them to be protected. Even if someone edits the pipeline in a feature branch, the production connection rejects the request.
az repos policy approver-count create --repository-id <repo-id> --branch main \
  --blocking true --enabled true --minimum-approver-count 2 \
  --allow-downvotes false --creator-vote-counts false --reset-on-source-push true
“Authentication tables” (verbatim from the study guide): confirmed with a search on 2026-10-30: the phrase appears only in the study guide (Skills measured); it is not in the module or in the Learn, GitHub or Azure DevOps documentation. Under “deployment pipeline controls” the module covers environment protection rules (required reviewers, wait timers, deployment branches), branch policies, CODEOWNERS / automatically included reviewers and branch control checks; authentication is covered separately (secrets/OIDC). Most reasonable interpretation: pipeline authentication to the target (OIDC, service principal, managed identity, secrets per environment) and, if it refers to data, application authentication/authorization tables (users, roles, permissions) treated as code: schema in the project, seed data (roles, never passwords) in an idempotent post-deployment (MERGE) and no secrets in the repo. Coverage here: (1) pipeline authentication → topic “Secrets and authentication”; (2) approvals, environments and checks → this topic; (3) users, roles and permissions as code → authorization section of “Secrets and authentication” and the pre/post-deployment topic.
Exam: “only main can deploy to production” → deployment branches (GitHub) / branch control check (ADO). “The database team must review every *.sql” → CODEOWNERS + Require review from Code Owners / automatically included reviewers. “Manual approval” → the environment's required reviewers.
Sources: Learn · Implement CI/CD pipelines · Docs · GitHub deployments and environments · Docs · About protected branches · Docs · About rulesets · Docs · About code owners · Docs · Branch policies · Docs · Approvals and checks

SQL database in Fabric: Git integration and deployment pipelines Fabric

SQL database in Fabric uses the same engine as Azure SQL Database and reuses SQL projects, but Fabric manages source control and promotion: you do not set up the SqlPackage pipeline yourself. Prerequisites: a Fabric capacity and the Git integration tenant setting enabled.

CriterionAzure SQL / SQL Server (module)SQL database in Fabric
Source of truthRepo with your .sqlprojRepo connected to the workspace (one branch per workspace; Azure DevOps or GitHub). Fabric generates and maintains the SQL project (<db>.SQLDatabase)
Validate and applydotnet build + SqlPackage Publish in CIUpdate from source control = project build + publish
Promote between environmentsCI/CD pipeline + environmentsFabric deployment pipelines: Development → Test → Production (3 stages by default; editable)
Publish optionsYou choose themFixed: /p:ScriptDatabaseOptions=false · /p:DoNotAlterReplicatedObjects=false · /p:IncludeTransactionalScripts=true · /p:GenerateSmartDefaults=true
Static dataProject post-deployment scriptPost-deployment from Shared Queries
Collation and compatibility levelDefaultCollation, CompatibilityMode in the projectNot included in source control or deployment pipelines: adjust them with T-SQL after deployment
  1. Commit: Source control panel → select the database → Commit; Fabric reads the definitions and writes them to the repo.
  2. Update: after a PR, the workspace database does not change until you click Update in the panel. Branch workspace: Branches tab → Branch out to new workspace.
  3. Static data: query in the editor with MERGE … WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE → rename it to Post-Deployment-StaticData.sql → move it to Shared Queries → … menu → Set as Post-deployment Script. It runs on every Update and every deployment pipeline.
Watch out: Fabric generates the .sqlproj (it excludes .sharedQueries from the build, takes the pre/post scripts from there and references system objects through a package reference): your edits are overwritten on the next commit. To build locally, add the reference to master.dacpac. A syntax error or an unsupported feature makes the Update fail: revert manually in source control. After an Update, the database can appear Uncommitted because of unintended differences (e.g. inline column attributes): commit from Fabric. If a change involves data loss, the deployment pipeline requires doing it manually.
Memorize: the SqlDbFabric DSP is listed as preview in the target platform docs (the template labels it “Fabric mirrored SQL database (preview)”); the pipelines compare by object (like a schema compare).
Sources: Docs · Fabric SQL database source control integration · Docs · SQL database deployment pipelines · Docs · Package references (system databases)

If the scenario says…Choose…
CI on Linux/macOS or containers; new projectSDK-style (Microsoft.Build.Sql) + dotnet build (.NET 8+)

SQL database in Fabric: promote dev → test → prodFabric deployment pipelines; static data with a post-deployment in Shared Queries
Memorize: pipeline = Build (dotnet build → .dacpac) + Deploy (the same artifact across environments). Review beforehand: Script/DeployReport. Publish defaults: BlockOnPossibleDataLoss=True · DropObjectsNotInSource=False · CreateNewDatabase=False · RegisterDataTierApplication=False · CommandTimeout=60.

Integrate SQL solutions with Azure services

Data API builder (DAB 2.x): complete structure of dab-config.json, REST/GraphQL entities, dab CLI, deployment to Azure, Azure Monitor and change detection (CES, CDC, Change Tracking, Azure Functions, Logic Apps). Exact configuration, default values and decision criteria are tested.

Skills measured covered:
  • Create configuration files for Data API builder (DAB)
  • Configure entities for REST and GraphQL, including data caching, pagination, searching, and filtering
  • Configure REST or GraphQL endpoints
  • Expose database objects, stored procedures, and views, including GraphQL relationships
  • Configure and implement DAB deployment
  • Recommend Azure Monitor configurations, including Application Insights and Log Analytics

Structure of dab-config.json and data-source DAB 2.x GA SQL Server 2016+ Azure SQL SQL in Fabric

DAB is an open-source (MIT) engine that publishes tables, views and stored procedures as REST, GraphQL and MCP endpoints from a single JSON. Latest stable version: 2.1.5 (2026-10-01); 2.0 is GA. CLI: dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.DataApiBuilder (docs: .NET 8+; 2.1.x targets net10.0 and needs .NET 10, 2.0.x uses net8.0). Official image: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-databases/data-api-builder.

Root keyValueNotes
$schemaURIRequired. https://github.com/Azure/data-api-builder/releases/latest/download/dab.draft.schema.json or versioned …/releases/download/v2.1.5/dab.draft.schema.json. Provides validation/IntelliSense
data-sourceobjectRequired. Database connection (next table)
data-source-filesstring[]Other config files, each with its own data-source
runtimeobjectGlobal behavior: pagination, rest, graphql, mcp, host, cache, compression, telemetry, health (and embeddings in the 2.1.5 schema, not yet documented)
entitiesobjectEntity name → definition. Required unless you use autoentities
autoentitiesobjectPattern-based rules that expose objects automatically (mssql only, DAB 2.0)
azure-key-vaultobjectendpoint (required) + retry-policy: mode exponential|fixed (default exponential), max-count 3, delay-seconds 1, max-delay-seconds 60, network-timeout-seconds 60. Enables @akv()

data-source

KeyValuesDefault / notes
database-typemssql · dwsql · postgresql · mysql · cosmosdb_nosql · cosmosdb_postgresqlRequired. mssql = SQL Server 2016+, Azure SQL DB/MI and SQL database in Fabric; dwsql = Synapse, Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint. (The 2.1.5 JSON schema lists only 5 values: it does not include cosmosdb_postgresql)
connection-stringstringRequired. Use @env('VAR') or @akv('secret'). dab init leaves it "" if you do not pass it
options.set-session-contextbool (mssql/dwsql only)Sends the JWT claims to SESSION_CONTEXT() (RLS, auditing). If omitted, the default is true (docs and code); dab init writes false. With true the response cache is disabled
health.enabled · .name · .threshold-msbool · string · inttrue · value of database-type · 1000
user-delegated-auth.*enabled · provider (EntraId) · database-audienceOBO (2.0, mssql only): false · EntraId · required if enabled (e.g. https://database.windows.net). Requires runtime.cache to be disabled and env vars DAB_OBO_CLIENT_ID, DAB_OBO_TENANT_ID, DAB_OBO_CLIENT_SECRET; uses one connection pool per user
Authentication to SQLConnection string fragmentNotes
Local developmentAuthentication=Active Directory Default;Uses DefaultAzureCredential. If it expires: az login --scope https://database.windows.net//.default
MI system-assignedAuthentication=Active Directory Managed Identity;No User Id or Password
MI user-assignedAuthentication=Active Directory Managed Identity; User Id=<client-id>;User Id = the identity's client ID
Transient errorsExponential backoff: 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, 32 s5 retries

Secrets, environments and multiple files

  • @env('VAR') reads variables from the process or from a .env next to the config (the .env wins over the process; add it to .gitignore). An unquoted pattern (@env(VAR)) is treated as a literal.
  • @akv('secret') is resolved at startup using azure-key-vault.endpoint.
  • DAB_ENVIRONMENT=<Env>: dab-config.<Env>.json overrides dab-config.json (you only repeat what changes); the CLI generates dab-config.<Env>.merged.json. Without the variable → Production environment.
  • data-source-files: each file needs data-source + entities/autoentities; only the root file applies runtime; entity names unique across files; there are no relationships between files.
{
  "$schema": "https://github.com/Azure/data-api-builder/releases/latest/download/dab.draft.schema.json",
  "data-source": {
    "database-type": "mssql",
    "connection-string": "@env('DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING')"
  },
  "runtime": { "host": { "mode": "production" } },
  "entities": {}
}
{
  "data-source": { "connection-string": "@env('DEV_CONNECTION_STRING')" },
  "runtime": { "host": { "mode": "development" } }
}
Exam: credentials outside the JSON → @env() (or @akv()); never in the file, nor Base64, nor a credentials.json. The safest option: a passwordless managed identity.
Learn vs current docs: (1) the unit says that dab start --config dab-config.production.json merges files; the merge is triggered by DAB_ENVIRONMENT (--config points to a specific file). (2) Its $schema v1.1.7 and the StaticWebApps provider are only an example, specific to SWA. (3) set-session-context: the data-source docs list true as the default (the DAB 2.1.5 code does too), but dab init explicitly writes false: check the actual value in your file.
Sources: Learn · Create configuration files for data API builder · Docs · Configuration schema · Docs · Data source · Docs · Environments · Docs · @env()

runtime: REST, GraphQL and pagination (values and defaults) GA

Global endpoint configuration. Docs: paths do not support subpaths (/api/data is invalid); the 2.1.5 release notes and its code already accept multi-segment paths (e.g. /api/v2). If runtime.rest.enabled/graphql.enabled is false, each entity's enabled does not matter.

KeyValuesDefault / notes
pagination.default-page-sizeint > 0 or -1100. -1 = max-page-size. Must be less than the maximum
pagination.max-page-sizeint > 0 or -1100000. 0 and values < -1 not supported
pagination.next-link-relativeboolfalse → absolute nextLink; true → relative (/api/users?$after=…)
rest.enabledbooltrue
rest.pathstring/api
rest.request-body-strictboolDefault true if omitted (docs and code). true → extra fields in the body = 400; false → they are ignored (lets you reuse the same POCO). Watch out: dab init writes false if you do not pass the option (and the 2.1.5 schema lists false as the default)
graphql.enabledbooltrue
graphql.pathstring/graphql
graphql.allow-introspectionbooltrue. Setting false in production hides the schema
graphql.depth-limitint | nullnull = no limit. Prevents abusive nested queries (the Learn unit uses 8)
graphql.multiple-mutations.create.enabledboolfalse. Enables createUsers(input: [ … ]) in a single transaction (requires the create permission)
graphql.enable-aggregationbooltrue (2.1.x schema): groupBy, sum, avg, min, max, count in mssql/dwsql
 
"runtime": {
  "pagination": { "default-page-size": 100, "max-page-size": 100000, "next-link-relative": false },
  "rest": { "enabled": true, "path": "/api", "request-body-strict": true },
  "graphql": {
    "enabled": true,
    "path": "/graphql",
    "allow-introspection": false,
    "depth-limit": 8,
    "multiple-mutations": { "create": { "enabled": false } }
  }
}
Memorize: page 100 / maximum 100000; REST /api; GraphQL /graphql; introspection true; depth-limit null; -1 = “use the maximum”.
GraphQL mutations: they need an active connection pool. If the connection string has Pooling=False or MultipleActiveResultSets=False, they fail with “Implicit distributed transactions have not been enabled”.
Exam: “hide the GraphQL schema in production” → allow-introspection: false; “limit nested queries” → depth-limit; “adjust page size” → runtime.pagination.
Sources: Learn · Create configuration files · Learn · Define entities for REST and GraphQL · Docs · Runtime · Docs · GraphQL endpoints

runtime: host, authentication, health, compression and MCP GA

MCP (SQL MCP Server) is available from DAB 1.7 and the /health endpoint from 1.5; compression, Unauthenticated, role inheritance, OBO and autoentities arrive with 2.0.

KeyValuesDefault / notes
host.modeproduction | developmentproduction. development enables Nitro (GraphQL IDE), Swagger UI at /swagger, /openapi/{role}, anonymous health and Debug logs
host.max-response-size-mbint > 0 (schema: 1–158)158 (limit per result; measures size, not rows)
host.cors.originsstring[][] ("*" is valid)
host.cors.allow-credentialsboolfalse (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header)
host.authentication.providersee tableUnauthenticated (2.0+)
host.authentication.jwt.audience · .issuerstringBoth required with EntraID, AzureAD or Custom
compression.leveloptimal | fastest | noneoptimal. Negotiated with Accept-Encoding: gzip or br (Brotli)
health.enabledbooltrue (endpoint /health)
health.rolesstring[]null. Required in production (otherwise → 403); ["anonymous"] makes it public
health.cache-ttl-seconds · .max-query-parallelismint · int (1–8)5 · 4
mcp.enabled · .pathbool · stringtrue · /mcp
mcp.description · .allowed-hostsstring · string[]null · [] (loopback always allowed; "*" disables Host/Origin validation: not recommended)
mcp.dml-toolsbool or objecttrue. Object: describe-entities, create-record, read-records, update-record, delete-record, execute-entity (all true) and aggregate-records (bool or { enabled, query-timeout }; query-timeout default 30, range 1–600 s)
ProviderIdentityWhenjwt
UnauthenticatedNone: everything runs as anonymousDAB behind an APIM/gateway that authenticates (default 2.0+)No
EntraID (AzureAD)Microsoft Entra ID JWTProduction apps with Microsoft identityYes
CustomExternal IdP JWT (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak)Third-party IdPYes
AppServiceApp Service EasyAuth headersDAB on App Service with authentication enabledNo
StaticWebAppsStatic Web Apps headersSWA database connections only (retired)No
SimulatorSimulatedLocal testing; only with mode: development (otherwise DAB does not start)No
  • Role selection: X-MS-API-ROLE header (all providers except Simulator). If omitted → system role authenticated.
  • With Unauthenticated, the entities' authenticated and custom roles are never activated (DAB warns at startup).
  • Check endpoints: / (always public: status/version/app-name) and /health (full report; in production it requires health.roles).
  • MCP: dab start --mcp-stdio role:<role> serves it over stdin/stdout (forces Simulator, no HTTP port). At entity level: mcp.dml-tools (true) and mcp.custom-tool (SP only, false).
"host": {
  "mode": "production",
  "max-response-size-mb": 158,
  "cors": { "origins": ["https://app.contoso.com"], "allow-credentials": false },
  "authentication": {
    "provider": "EntraID",
    "jwt": {
      "audience": "<application-id>",
      "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0"
    }
  }
}
Watch out: before 2.0 the default provider of dab init was StaticWebApps; now it is Unauthenticated. The Learn unit's examples with StaticWebApps are only valid for Static Web Apps.
Exam: “DAB runs on App Service with Easy Auth” → AppService; “Okta/Auth0 tokens” → Custom + jwt; “test roles locally” → Simulator + development; “health in production returns 403” → health.roles is missing.
