Entities: source, fields, rest and graphql GA

Each key in entities is a logical name (case-sensitive) that maps a database object and defines how it is published. Shortcut: "source": "dbo.Books" is equivalent to a table.

KeyValuesDefault / notes
descriptionstring2.0+. Appears in OpenAPI/GraphQL and in MCP discovery
source.objectstringRequired. dbo is optional; brackets are supported [dbo].[Users]
source.typetable | view | stored-procedureRequired in the object (dab add → table)
source.parametersarray [{ name, required, default, description }]SP only. Only needed for parameters with a default. The dictionary format { "id": 0 } is deprecated in 2.0
source.key-fieldsstring[]Deprecated in 2.0 → fields[].primary-key. Required on views if you do not use fields
fields[]{ name, alias, description, primary-key }Replaces mappings + key-fields; the schema forbids mixing them in the same entity. primary-key default false
mappings{ "column": "alias" }Deprecated in 2.0 → fields[].alias. The alias must follow the GraphQL naming rules; clients use the alias
restbool or object { enabled, path, methods }enabled true; path /<entity> (2.0: supports /, e.g. shopping-cart/item); methods SP only: lowercase array get|post|put|patch|delete, default post
graphqlbool or object { enabled, type, operation }enabled true; type string (singular) or object { singular, plural }; operation SP only: mutation (default) | query
permissions · relationships · cache—Next topics
health{ enabled, first, threshold-ms }true · 100 (1–500, ≤ max-page-size) · 1000. SPs are excluded
mcpbool or { dml-tools, custom-tool }true · false (custom-tool SP only; on a table/view it gives a configuration error)
OperationREST (/api)GraphQL (/graphql)
ListGET /api/Product → { "value": [ … ] }products { items { … } }
By keyGET /api/Product/id/123 (composite: /orderId/100/productId/50)product_by_pk(id: 123)
CreatePOST /api/ProductcreateProduct(item: { … })
UpdatePATCH (partial) or PUT (replacement) /api/Product/id/123updateProduct(id: 123, item: { … })
DeleteDELETE /api/Product/id/123deleteProduct(id: 123)
Stored procedureGET (query string) / POST (JSON) /api/<entity>execute<Entity>(…)
 
"Book": {
  "description": "Book catalog",
  "source": { "object": "dbo.books", "type": "table" },
  "fields": [
    { "name": "id", "primary-key": true },
    { "name": "sku_title", "alias": "title", "description": "Display title" }
  ],
  "rest": { "enabled": true, "path": "/library/books" },
  "graphql": { "enabled": true, "type": { "singular": "Book", "plural": "Books" } },
  "permissions": [ { "role": "anonymous", "actions": ["read"] } ]
}

autoentities (DAB 2.0, mssql only; structure autoentities.<definition>.patterns|template|permissions)

KeyTypeDefault / notes
patterns.include · .excludestring[] (T-SQL LIKE on schema.object)["%.%"] · null
patterns.namestring"{schema}_{object}" (must yield unique names)
template.rest.enabled · graphql.enabled · health.enabled · mcp.dml-toolsbooltrue
template.cache.enabled · .ttl-seconds · .levelbool · int · L1|L1L2false · null · L1L2
permissionsarrayAs in a regular entity

They are re-evaluated on every startup (new matching tables are exposed automatically). An explicit entity with the same name wins. In 2.0 dab auto-config only covers tables; preview with dab auto-config-simulate (-o results.csv).

Learn vs current docs: (1) the unit uses mappings (deprecated) and shows rest.methods on tables as an object { "get": true, "put": false }; the real schema is a lowercase array and only for stored procedures. (2) graphql.operation does not apply to views or tables either. (3) It says GraphQL exposes product/products; in reality they are products (list) and product_by_pk.
Exam: “rename columns in the API without touching the database” → fields[].alias (formerly mappings); “change the GraphQL type name” → graphql.type; “change the REST path” → rest.path; “do not expose in GraphQL” → graphql.enabled: false. For tables, verb control is done with permissions.
Sources: Learn · Define entities for REST and GraphQL · Docs · Entities · Docs · GraphQL endpoints · Docs · What's new in 2.0

Permissions: roles, actions, fields and policy.database GA

Each entity lists permissions = role + actions. System roles: anonymous (no token) and authenticated (valid token); plus custom roles that the client selects with the X-MS-API-ROLE header. With no rules (own or inherited) for the role, there is no access.

Object typeValid actionsNotes
table · viewcreate · read · update · delete · ** expands to all four
stored-procedureexecute · ** expands only to execute. Using update on an SP fails in dab validate
API operationRequired actionNotes
REST GET · GraphQL queryread
REST POST · createXcreate
REST PUT/PATCHcreate + updateThey are upserts (if the key does not exist, they insert); with an IDENTITY key, a PUT/PATCH to a nonexistent key returns 404: use POST
REST DELETE · deleteXdelete
SPexecute
  • Role inheritance (2.0): named role → authenticated → anonymous. If you define only anonymous: read, all other roles can read too. Check: dab configure --show-effective-permissions.
  • Forms of actions: array of strings (["read"], ["*"]) or objects { "action", "fields", "policy" }; the bare string form ("actions": "*") is valid only for stored procedures.
  • fields.include / fields.exclude (inside the action): limits visible columns (["*"] = all); reflected in OpenAPI.
  • policy.database: OData-style predicate injected into the SQL query. Operators eq ne and or gt lt; @item.<field> (uses the alias if there is one) and @claims.<type>. Only for read, update and delete (not create or execute).
"permissions": [
  {
    "role": "anonymous",
    "actions": [ { "action": "read", "fields": { "include": ["*"], "exclude": ["UnitCost"] } } ]
  },
  { "role": "authenticated", "actions": ["create", "read", "update", "delete"] },
  {
    "role": "auditor",
    "actions": [ { "action": "read", "policy": { "database": "@item.OwnerId eq @claims.userId" } } ]
  }
]
dab add Book --source dbo.Books --permissions "anonymous:read" --fields.exclude "UnitCost"
dab update Book --permissions "authenticated:create,read,update,delete"
dab update Book --permissions "auditor:read" --policy-database "@item.OwnerId eq @claims.userId"
Exam (knowledge check): “read-only” → permissions with only read. source.type: view does not block writes by itself, and anonymous does not imply read-only. “Hide a column” → fields.exclude; “each user sees their own rows” → policy.database with @claims.
Watch out: DAB permissions are an API layer; the SP or query runs with the permissions of the connection, not the end user. Grant the DAB identity only what is needed (db_datareader/db_datawriter, EXECUTE) and use set-session-context + RLS, or OBO, if the DB must see the real user. --policy-request is still in the CLI but is not listed in the 2.1.5 JSON schema.
Memorize: role → actions; * on SP = execute; PUT/PATCH = create + update; policy only on read/update/delete.
Sources: Learn · Define entities · Learn · Knowledge check · Docs · Entities (permissions) · Docs · Permission-aware OpenAPI · Docs · dab validate

Data caching: runtime.cache and entities.<n>.cache GA (L2 since 2.0)

The cache stores query results to reduce round trips to the DB. There is a double switch: global (runtime.cache.enabled) and per entity (cache.enabled); if the global one is false, the entity one does not matter.

KeyValuesDefault / notes
runtime.cache.enabledboolfalse
runtime.cache.ttl-secondsint5 (default TTL for entities)
runtime.cache.level-2.enabledboolfalse
level-2.providerredisredis (the only one supported)
level-2.connection-stringstringnull (use @env())
level-2.partitionstringnull. Prefixes the Redis keys and the backplane channel; only containers with the same partition share a cache
entities.<n>.cache.enabledboolfalse
entities.<n>.cache.ttl-secondsintInherits the global TTL
entities.<n>.cache.levelL1 | L1L2L1L2. If L2 is not enabled globally, L1L2 behaves like L1
  • L1 = process memory (fast, not shared across instances). L1L2: request → L1 → L2 (Redis) → DB → written to L2 and L1; allows sharing and keeping the cache “warm” after recycling containers.
  • REST request header Cache-Control: no-cache (skips L1/L2 and refreshes) or no-store (does not store). REST only; ignored if the cache is disabled. DAB does not emit cache headers in the response.
{
  "runtime": {
    "cache": {
      "enabled": true,
      "ttl-seconds": 30,
      "level-2": {
        "enabled": true,
        "provider": "redis",
        "connection-string": "@env('REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING')",
        "partition": "prod-api"
      }
    }
  },
  "entities": {
    "Product": { "cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl-seconds": 60, "level": "L1L2" } }
  }
}
dab configure --runtime.cache.enabled true --runtime.cache.ttl-seconds 30
dab update Product --cache.enabled true --cache.ttl-seconds 60 --cache.level L1L2
Learn vs current docs: the unit puts cache inside graphql and says REST/GraphQL behave differently. Per the docs, cache is a sibling key of rest/graphql at the entity level. The L1 doc says it applies only to REST (and Cache-Control too), while the repo's design doc (docs/design/query-caching.md) talks about REST GET and GraphQL queries → Verify for GraphQL. The cache is not used with set-session-context: true (docs) and must be disabled with OBO (user-delegated-auth). Verify: in the 2.1.5 code, an entity without cache.enabled inherits the global value, although the docs say each entity must enable it.
Exam: “several replicas must share a cache” → L2 Redis + entity on L1L2 + same partition; “nearly static data” → long TTL; “inventory counters” → short TTL or no cache.
Memorize: global false / TTL 5; entity false, inherits TTL, level L1L2.
Sources: Learn · Define entities · Docs · Level 1 cache · Docs · Level 2 cache · Docs · Cache-Control

Queries: pagination, search and filtering in REST vs GraphQL GA

Nothing has to be configured per field: filtering, sorting, projection and pagination are available automatically for the exposed fields. Only runtime.pagination adjusts the sizes. REST paths and parameters are case-sensitive.

ConceptRESTGraphQL
Endpoint/api/{entity}POST /graphql (everything)
List response{ "value": [ … ], "nextLink": "…" }items { … } + hasNextPage + endCursor
By key/api/Book/id/1010. If it does not exist → 200 with value: []book_by_pk(id: 1010). If it does not exist → error “Could not find item…”
Projection$select=id,title (nonexistent/inaccessible field → 400)Selection set (there is no SELECT *)
Filter$filter= eq ne gt ge lt le and or not ( )filter: { field: { op: value } }; and: [ … ] / or: [ … ]. Ops: eq neq gt gte lt lte contains notContains startsWith endsWith in isNull
Nullseq null / ne nullisNull: true|false
Text searchNo contains/startswith in $filtercontains (LIKE '%x%'), startsWith, endsWith, notContains
Order$orderby=year desc, title ascorderBy: { year: DESC, title: ASC } (no and/or; null ignores the field)
Page size$first=Nfirst: N
Continuation$after=<token> (or follow nextLink)after: "<endCursor>"
DatesISO 8601 UTC without quotes: 2025-01-01T00:00:00ZString ISO 8601 UTC: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
 
GET /api/products?$select=id,name,price&$filter=price gt 100 and stockQuantity gt 0&$orderby=price desc&$first=10
GET /api/products?$first=10&$after=eyJQcm9kdWN0SUQiOjEwfQ==
GET /api/products/id/123
GET /api/book?$filter=year ge 1970 or title eq 'Dune'
GET /api/books?$filter=published_on ge 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z and rating eq null
query {
  products(
    filter: { and: [ { price: { gt: 100 } }, { name: { contains: "USB" } } ] }
    orderBy: { price: DESC }
    first: 10
    after: "<endCursor of the previous page>"
  ) {
    items { id name price category { name } }
    hasNextPage
    endCursor
  }
}
  • Default sort order: ascending primary key (if you sort by another field, the PK fields are added as a tiebreaker). Pagination is keyset (cursor), not offset.
  • $after/after tokens are opaque (Base64): do not build them; changing the schema or sort order invalidates them.
  • $first/first: omitted → default-page-size (100); -1 → max-page-size; 0, < -1 or greater than the maximum → 400 (confirmed in the code, RuntimeConfig.GetPaginationLimit; the note in the runtime doc that talks about “trimming” is incorrect).
  • Stored procedures: do not support pagination, filtering or sorting (first result set only).
Different names: REST ne ge le ↔ GraphQL neq gte lte. REST nulls with eq null ↔ GraphQL isNull. REST $orderby ... desc ↔ GraphQL ASC/DESC.
Text search: the operators contains, notContains, startsWith and endsWith exist only in GraphQL; REST $filter does not have them. For filters that cannot be expressed with the standard operators, expose a view or an SP that encapsulates the logic (Learn tip).
Exam: “paginate without offset” → $first + $after / first + after (keyset); “know whether there are more pages in GraphQL” → hasNextPage; “clients receive 100 rows” → default-page-size.
Sources: Learn · Define entities · Docs · REST endpoints · Docs · $filter · Docs · filter (GraphQL) · Docs · $first · Docs · after · Docs · orderBy

Exposing views, stored procedures and GraphQL relationships GA

View (view)

  • DAB does not detect its key: define fields[].primary-key: true (formerly source.key-fields)
  • Permissions like a table (read, and create/update/delete only if the view is updatable and you grant them)
  • No key → dab validate fails
  • Views do not support relationships (limitation from the docs)

Stored procedure

  • Action execute (or *)
  • REST methods (default post); GraphQL operation (default mutation)
  • Parameters: array { name, required, default, description }

Relationship

  • Navigable only in GraphQL
  • cardinality: one | many
  • M:N with linking.*
"ProductInventory": {
  "source": { "object": "dbo.ProductInventory", "type": "view" },
  "fields": [ { "name": "ProductID", "primary-key": true } ],
  "rest": { "enabled": true, "path": "/inventory" },
  "permissions": [ { "role": "anonymous", "actions": ["read"] } ]
},
"CreateOrder": {
  "source": {
    "object": "dbo.CreateOrder",
    "type": "stored-procedure",
    "parameters": [
      { "name": "CustomerID", "required": true },
      { "name": "Quantity", "required": false, "default": 1 }
    ]
  },
  "rest": { "methods": ["post"] },
  "graphql": { "operation": "mutation" },
  "permissions": [ { "role": "authenticated", "actions": ["execute"] } ]
}
GET  /api/products/by-price-range?MinPrice=10&MaxPrice=50          (SP with rest.methods ["get"])
POST /api/CreateOrder     {"CustomerID": 7, "Quantity": 2}           (JSON in the body)

query    { executeGetProductsByPriceRange(MinPrice: 10, MaxPrice: 50) { ProductID ProductName } }
mutation { executeCreateOrder(CustomerID: 7, Quantity: 2) { OrderID } }
  • SP limits: only the first result set is returned; no pagination, filtering, sorting or relationships; they cannot be requested by key; there is no per-parameter authorization; DAB reads metadata with sys.dm_exec_describe_first_result_set; they are excluded from health checks.
  • GraphQL arguments are the SP's parameter names (without @); operation only changes where executeXxx appears (Query or Mutation).
  • REST verbs of an SP: the docs say “only GET and POST” (default POST), although the CLI, schema and code accept get|post|put|patch|delete (a verb that is not configured → 405); for the exam, stick with GET/POST. With rest: false, REST is disabled for that SP.

Relationships

"Category": {
  "relationships": {
    "products": { "cardinality": "many", "target.entity": "Product",
                  "source.fields": ["CategoryID"], "target.fields": ["CategoryID"] }
  }
},
"Product": {
  "relationships": {
    "category": { "cardinality": "one", "target.entity": "Category",
                  "source.fields": ["CategoryID"], "target.fields": ["CategoryID"] }
  }
},
"Book": {
  "relationships": {
    "authors": {
      "cardinality": "many", "target.entity": "Author",
      "source.fields": ["id"], "target.fields": ["id"],
      "linking.object": "dbo.books_authors",
      "linking.source.fields": ["book_id"], "linking.target.fields": ["author_id"]
    }
  }
}
query {
  products(first: 10) {
    items { name price category { CategoryName } }
  }
  categories {
    items { CategoryName products(first: 3) { items { name } hasNextPage } }
  }
}
dab update Product  --relationship category --target.entity Category --cardinality one  --relationship.fields "CategoryID:CategoryID"
dab update Category --relationship products --target.entity Product  --cardinality many --relationship.fields "CategoryID:CategoryID"
dab update Book --relationship authors --target.entity Author --cardinality many --relationship.fields "id:id" \
  --linking.object "dbo.books_authors" --linking.source.fields "book_id" --linking.target.fields "author_id"
  • The keys have literal dots ("target.entity", "source.fields", "target.fields", "linking.object", "linking.source.fields", "linking.target.fields"); cardinality and target.entity are required.
  • It is defined on both sides (the inverse is not created automatically). one = many→one (Product→Category) or 1:1; many = one→many or N:M. The relationship name is unique per entity and is the name of the GraphQL field; many relationships return a connection (items).
  • The number of linking.* fields must match the keys; with an existing FK, DAB can infer source.fields/target.fields (relationships doc); dab validate checks that the target entity and the linking.object exist. There are no relationships across different config files.
Learn vs current docs: (1) the unit writes parameters as a “rename” dictionary ("MinPrice": "minPrice"); it does not rename: the dictionary format (name → default value) is deprecated and the array is used. (2) For N:M it suggests chaining entities by hand; DAB supports linking.object. (3) It says operation: query prevents mutations on a view; operation applies only to SPs (it is the permissions that limit writes).
Exam: “view without PK” → fields[].primary-key; “SP that inserts data” → execute + operation: mutation; “fetch order + customer + lines in one call” → GraphQL relationships; “many-to-many with a junction table” → cardinality: many + linking.object.
Sources: Learn · Expose database objects, stored procedures, and views · Docs · Entities (relationships) · Docs · Stored procedures (REST) · Docs · dab update

CLI dab: installation, init, configure, validate, start, export GA

dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.DataApiBuilder    # docs: .NET 8+; 2.1.x requires .NET 10
dotnet tool update  --global Microsoft.DataApiBuilder
dab --version
dotnet new tool-manifest                                  # alternative: pinned local tool
dotnet tool install microsoft.dataapibuilder --version <version>
dotnet tool run dab start
CommandPurposeNotes
dab initCreates dab-config.jsonOverwrites if it exists (does not merge). Only --database-type is required
dab add <entity>Adds an entityRequired: -s/--source and --permissions
dab update <entity>Modifies entity / relationshipsOne role per --permissions run
dab configureChanges data-source and runtime (not entities)All-or-nothing; anything not specified is kept. App Insights/OpenTelemetry → dab add-telemetry
dab add-telemetryTelemetry (App Insights, OpenTelemetry)See the DAB telemetry topic
dab auto-config · auto-config-simulateDefines / previews autoentitiesMSSQL only; -o exports CSV
dab validateValidates without startingOnly accepts -c/--config; exit 0 OK, ≠ 0 error
dab startStarts the runtimeHTTP 5000 / HTTPS 5001 by default
dab export --graphql -o <dir>Exports the GraphQL schema-g name (default schema.gql); --generate + sampling for Cosmos DB NoSQL only

dab init

OptionValuesDefault
--database-typemssql, dwsql, mysql, postgresql, cosmosdb_postgresql, cosmosdb_nosqlRequired
--connection-stringstring (supports @env('…'))""
--set-session-contextbool (mssql)false
--host-modeDevelopment | ProductionProduction
--cors-origincomma-separated list—
--auth.providerUnauthenticated, StaticWebApps, EntraID, AzureAD, AppService, Simulator, CustomUnauthenticated
--auth.audience · --auth.issuerJWTRequired if the provider is not Unauthenticated/StaticWebApps/Simulator

--graphql.enabled · --graphql.path · --graphql.multiple-mutations.create.enabledbool · string · booltrue · /graphql · false
--mcp.enabled · --mcp.path · --mcp.aggregate-records.query-timeoutbool · string · inttrue · /mcp · 30 (1–600)

-c, --configfile namedab-config.json

--rest.disabled, --graphql.disabled and --mcp.disabled are deprecated: use --*.enabled false and do not mix both forms. At least one endpoint (REST, GraphQL or MCP) must remain enabled. dab init 2.x also adds a telemetry.open-telemetry block bound to @env('OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT'), @env('OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS') and @env('OTEL_SERVICE_NAME').

dab configure (option families)

FamilyOptions (prefix --)
data-sourcedata-source.database-type, .connection-string, .options.set-session-context, .health.enabled|name|threshold-ms, .user-delegated-auth.enabled|provider|database-audience, data-source-files
REST / GraphQLruntime.rest.enabled|path|request-body-strict · runtime.graphql.enabled|path|depth-limit|allow-introspection|multiple-mutations.create.enabled
Pagination / cacheruntime.pagination.max-page-size|default-page-size|next-link-relative · runtime.cache.enabled|ttl-seconds · runtime.compression.level

Health / MCPruntime.health.enabled|cache-ttl-seconds|max-query-parallelism|roles · runtime.mcp.enabled|path|description|dml-tools[.describe-entities|create-record|read-records|update-record|delete-record|execute-entity|aggregate-records[.query-timeout]]

Telemetryruntime.telemetry.log-level, .azure-log-analytics.*, .file.*
Diagnostics--show-effective-permissions (permissions resolved with inheritance)

dab validate: stages (if one fails, the following ones are skipped)

  1. Schema: JSON conforming to the schema, valid enums, no unexpected properties.
  2. Config properties: at least one endpoint enabled, paths with a leading / and no collision, JWT with issuer and audience.
  3. Permissions: non-empty roles, valid actions per type (SP: execute), * or explicit ones but not both.
  4. Database connection: parseable connection string, valid credentials, the DB exists.
  5. Entity metadata: source object exists, view keys, SP parameters, relationships and linking.object, policies, non-negative TTL.

dab start y dab export

  • dab start: -c/--config (default dab-config.json, or dab-config.<DAB_ENVIRONMENT>.json if it exists), --LogLevel <level>, --verbose (= Information), --no-https-redirect, --mcp-stdio [role:<role>]. In a container only HTTP 5000 is published.
  • dab export --graphql -o ./schema-out [-g custom.gql] [-c config]: starts a temporary runtime (tries https://localhost:5001 and then http://localhost:5000); without --graphql it fails.
dab init --database-type mssql --connection-string "@env('DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING')" --host-mode development
dab add Category --source dbo.Categories --permissions "anonymous:read"
dab validate
dab start        # http://localhost:5000/api/Category  ·  http://localhost:5000/graphql
Exam: “generate the base file without editing JSON” → dab init; “add a table with anonymous read” → dab add … --permissions "anonymous:read"; “validate in CI without starting” → dab validate (exit code); “change CORS/introspection/pagination” → dab configure.
Watch out: dab init overwrites the existing file. In the lab, for Azure SQL with your identity use Authentication=Active Directory Default; if you see “DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token”, repeat az login --scope https://database.windows.net//.default.

Inconsistent documentation: the dab update page lists --cache.ttl, but the CLI code defines --cache.ttl-seconds for add and update. The dab add page says --source.key-fields ends in fields, but its example (and the Learn lab) show source.key-fields: in the v2.1.5 code, dab add writes source.key-fields (deprecated, valid in the schema) and dab update converts it to fields[].primary-key.
Memorize: --permissions "role:action1,action2"; for views the key; for SPs --rest.methods + --graphql.operation; relationships only with dab update.

Complete and verified example of dab-config.json DAB 2.1.5

The 4 parts are independent JSON objects; when merged (deep-merge) they form a single file that validates without errors against dab.draft.schema.json v2.1.5. Scenario: catalog with a table, a 1:N relationship, a view and a stored procedure, Microsoft Entra ID authentication and telemetry.

{
  "$schema": "https://github.com/Azure/data-api-builder/releases/latest/download/dab.draft.schema.json",
  "data-source": {
    "database-type": "mssql",
    "connection-string": "@env('DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING')",
    "options": { "set-session-context": false },
    "health": { "enabled": true, "name": "catalog-sql", "threshold-ms": 1000 }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "pagination": { "default-page-size": 100, "max-page-size": 100000, "next-link-relative": false },
    "rest": { "enabled": true, "path": "/api", "request-body-strict": true },
    "graphql": {
      "enabled": true,
      "path": "/graphql",
      "allow-introspection": false,
      "depth-limit": 8,
      "multiple-mutations": { "create": { "enabled": false } }
    },
    "mcp": {
      "enabled": true,
      "path": "/mcp",
      "dml-tools": {
        "describe-entities": true, "create-record": false, "read-records": true,
        "update-record": false, "delete-record": false, "execute-entity": true,
        "aggregate-records": { "enabled": true, "query-timeout": 30 }
      }
    }
  }
}
{
  "runtime": {
    "host": {
      "mode": "production",
      "max-response-size-mb": 158,
      "cors": { "origins": ["https://app.contoso.com"], "allow-credentials": false },
      "authentication": {
        "provider": "EntraID",
        "jwt": {
          "audience": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
          "issuer": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0"
        }
      }
    },
    "cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl-seconds": 30, "level-2": { "enabled": false } },
    "compression": { "level": "optimal" },
    "telemetry": {
      "application-insights": {
        "enabled": true,
        "connection-string": "@env('APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING')"
      },
      "open-telemetry": {
        "enabled": true,
        "endpoint": "@env('OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT')",
        "service-name": "dab-catalog",
        "exporter-protocol": "grpc"
      },
      "log-level": { "default": "warning" }
    },
    "health": { "enabled": true, "roles": ["monitoring"], "cache-ttl-seconds": 5, "max-query-parallelism": 4 }
  }
}
{
  "entities": {
    "Product": {
      "description": "Product catalog",
      "source": { "object": "dbo.Products", "type": "table" },
      "fields": [
        { "name": "ProductID", "alias": "id", "primary-key": true },
        { "name": "ProductName", "alias": "name" },
        { "name": "UnitPrice", "alias": "price" }
      ],
      "rest": { "enabled": true, "path": "/products" },
      "graphql": { "enabled": true, "type": { "singular": "Product", "plural": "Products" } },
      "permissions": [
        { "role": "anonymous",
          "actions": [ { "action": "read", "fields": { "exclude": ["UnitsInStock"] } } ] },
        { "role": "authenticated", "actions": ["create", "read", "update", "delete"] },
        { "role": "inventory-admin",
          "actions": [ { "action": "read" },
                       { "action": "update", "policy": { "database": "@item.Discontinued eq false" } } ] }
      ],
      "relationships": {
        "category": { "cardinality": "one", "target.entity": "Category",
                      "source.fields": ["CategoryID"], "target.fields": ["CategoryID"] }
      },
      "cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl-seconds": 60, "level": "L1" }
    }
  }
}
{
  "entities": {
    "Category": {
      "source": { "object": "dbo.Categories", "type": "table" },
      "permissions": [ { "role": "anonymous", "actions": ["read"] } ],
      "relationships": {
        "products": { "cardinality": "many", "target.entity": "Product",
                      "source.fields": ["CategoryID"], "target.fields": ["CategoryID"] }
      }
    },
    "ProductCatalog": {
      "source": { "object": "dbo.ProductCatalogView", "type": "view" },
      "fields": [ { "name": "ProductID", "primary-key": true } ],
      "rest": { "path": "/catalog" },
      "graphql": { "type": { "singular": "CatalogItem", "plural": "CatalogItems" } },
      "permissions": [ { "role": "anonymous", "actions": ["read"] } ]
    },
    "GetProductsByPriceRange": {
      "source": {
        "object": "dbo.GetProductsByPriceRange",
        "type": "stored-procedure",
        "parameters": [
          { "name": "MinPrice", "required": true, "description": "Minimum price" },
          { "name": "MaxPrice", "required": false, "default": 1000 }
        ]
      },
      "rest": { "path": "/products/by-price-range", "methods": ["get", "post"] },
      "graphql": { "operation": "query" },
      "permissions": [ { "role": "authenticated", "actions": ["execute"] } ]
    }
  }
}
GET /api/products?$filter=price gt 100&$orderby=price desc&$first=5
GET /api/catalog
GET /api/products/by-price-range?MinPrice=10&MaxPrice=50          (authenticated role + X-MS-API-ROLE if applicable)
POST /graphql   { Products(first: 5) { items { name price category { CategoryName } } hasNextPage endCursor } }
POST /graphql   { executeGetProductsByPriceRange(MinPrice: 10, MaxPrice: 50) { ProductID ProductName } }
  • graphql.type.plural is the exact name (case-sensitive) of the root field: Products, not products.
  • With fields[].alias, clients use the alias (id, name, price); in policy, use the alias too if it exists.
  • Run dab validate before deploying: it checks schema, permissions, connection and metadata.
  • set-session-context is set to false on purpose: with true, the response cache (part 2) is disabled.
Best practice: connection string and keys only via @env()/@akv(); mode: production, allow-introspection: false and explicit health.roles in production; mcp.dml-tools only with the tools you need.
Sources: Learn · Define entities for REST and GraphQL · Docs · Configuration schema · Docs · dab.draft.schema.json (v2.1.5)

StatusGAGARetired on Nov 30, 2025

Other options from the DAB deployment index: Azure Container Instances, Azure Kubernetes Service (see health checks), local Docker (docker run -p 5000:5000; the image is amd64 only, no ARM64), local CLI, from source, air-gapped environments and Hosted MCP in a connector namespace (Logic Apps, SQL pivot).

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/azure-databases/data-api-builder:latest
COPY dab-config.json /App/dab-config.json
az acr build --registry <acr> --image dab:1 .
az containerapp create \
  --name dab-api --resource-group <rg> --environment <aca-env> \
  --image <acr>.azurecr.io/dab:1 \
  --ingress external --target-port 5000 \
  --system-assigned --min-replicas 0 --max-replicas 5 \
  --env-vars DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING="Server=tcp:<srv>.database.windows.net,1433;Initial Catalog=<db>;Authentication=Active Directory Managed Identity;Encrypt=True;"
# with SQL auth: --secrets dbconn="<connection-string>"  and  --env-vars DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING=secretref:dbconn
# private registry: add --registry-server / --registry-identity (or username and password)
CREATE USER [dab-api] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER;           -- identity name (container app / web app)
ALTER ROLE [db_datareader] ADD MEMBER [dab-api];
ALTER ROLE [db_datawriter] ADD MEMBER [dab-api];
GRANT EXECUTE ON SCHEMA::dbo TO [dab-api];               -- only if you expose stored procedures
  • Multiple environments: image with ARG ENVIRONMENT=production, COPY dab-config.${ENVIRONMENT}.json /App/dab-config.${ENVIRONMENT}.json and ENV DAB_ENVIRONMENT=${ENVIRONMENT} (the file name must match the value of DAB_ENVIRONMENT).
  • Probes: liveness on / (public: status/version); the DB probe can be a lightweight query (/api/Product?$first=1) or /health (in production it requires health.roles; otherwise, 403).
  • CI/CD: workflow that triggers on changes to dab-config*.json/Dockerfile: dab validate → build/push to ACR → update the Container App. Never store secrets in the repo.
  • App Service (code): the .NET stack includes the runtime, not the SDK: restore DAB on your machine (dotnet tool restore), package dab/ and use startup.sh with LF (not CRLF): exec dotnet ./dab/Microsoft.DataApiBuilder.dll start --config ./dab-config.json.

Static Web Apps “database connections” Retired

  • The SWA doc warns: “Database Connections for Static Web Apps ends November 30, 2025”; it is no longer listed in the DAB deployment index.
  • How it worked: DAB managed by SWA; endpoints at /data-api/* (fixed prefix); staticwebapp.database.config.json file in swa-db-connections (or data_api_location in the workflow); swa db init --database-type mssql; swa start ./src --data-api-location swa-db-connections (proxy on port 4280); provider StaticWebApps; roles via X-MS-API-ROLE; the DB firewall had to allow Azure services; SWA forced mode: production and overwrote the connection string.
  • CLI (extension, preview): az staticwebapp dbconnection create --name <swa> --resource-group <rg> --db-resource-id <id> [--db-name] [--mi-system-assigned | --mi-user-assigned | --username --password].
Learn vs current docs: the unit still presents SWA as an option and uses az staticwebapp dbconnection create --db-type mssql (--db-type does not exist) and the file staticwebapps.database.config.json (with an “s”; the real one is staticwebapp.database.config.json). Its App Service example uses the container image; the current DAB guide for App Service deploys the runtime as code (ZIP + startup.sh).
Exam (knowledge check): “managed identity + request-based autoscaling” → Azure Container Apps with system-assigned MI. Azure Functions is not a DAB host; VMs do not provide managed scaling; SWA DB connections is retired. “Secrets” → variables/secrets (secretref, Key Vault), never in the JSON.

Dynamic thresholds do not fire until enough history is collected. Metric alerts are stateful: they fire once and resolve with a resolved notification. Notifies via action groups (email, SMS, webhook, ITSM).

Current monitoring recommendation: Database watcher (Preview) retires on Apr 30, 2027 and will not reach GA; from Nov 9, 2026, watchers can no longer be created or edited. Migrate to Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric (Preview; Fabric Free license, no Fabric capacity; requires the Reader role on the subscription). Azure SQL Analytics (preview, via Log Analytics) is in archived docs, with no active development. Query Performance Insight (Query Store) is still available in the current docs.
Exam: “alert when CPU > 90%” → metric alert; “send deadlocks/errors to a SIEM” → diagnostic setting → Event Hubs; “query with KQL and correlate” → Log Analytics; “cheap long-term retention” → Storage; “logs do not appear” → missing diagnostic setting (none by default).

(3) On App Service, App Insights can suffer double instrumentation; it works better in containers, Container Apps or AKS.

Change detection: CES vs CDC vs Change Tracking vs Azure Functions vs Logic Apps CES Preview rest GA

CriterionCESCDCChange TrackingFunctions SQL triggerLogic Apps SQL trigger
StatusPreviewGAGAGAGA
PlatformSQL Server 2025 (not on Linux), Azure SQL DB, MI (SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date policy), SQL database in FabricSQL Server, MI, Azure SQL DB (any vCore; DTU ≥ S3)SQL Server, Azure SQL DB, MI, SQL database in FabricAzure SQL DB, MI, SQL Server (on top of CT)SQL Server, Azure SQL DB, MI
What it captures / granularityINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE as CloudEvent (JSON or Avro) with schema, new and old values. No DDL or initial snapshotI/U/D with before/after values in change tables; LSN; DDL in cdc.ddl_historyOnly PK + operation + version (+ column mask). No old valuesPer row: Item (current value) + Operation (Insert/Update/Delete)Managed: row created / modified (INSERT+UPDATE, no DELETE). Built-in: insert/update/modified/delete
MechanismPush from the log, near real-time (no polling)Asynchronous log read (capture job); small latency, not zeroSynchronous with the transaction; the consumer queries (pull)Polling: PollingIntervalMs 1000, batches MaxBatchSize 100Scheduled polling (Frequency/Interval)
TargetAzure Event Hubs or Fabric Eventstreamcdc.<instance>_CT tables in the same DBInternal tables; CHANGETABLE()Your function (C#, Java, JS, PowerShell, Python)Workflow actions
RequirementsFULL recovery; db_owner/CONTROL; Event Hubs; SQL 2025: PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON; no PK requireddb_owner (Azure SQL DB); in SQL Server/MI sp_cdc_enable_db requires sysadmin and sp_cdc_enable_table db_owner; SQL Server Agent (in Azure SQL DB a scheduler does this); PK/unique index only for net changesPK required; compat. ≥ 90; snapshot isolation recommendedCT on DB and table + PK; permissions; az_func schemaManaged: IDENTITY (created) / ROWVERSION (modified). Built-in: Change Tracking
RetentionNo storage of its own; the log is not truncated while changes are pending3 days by default (cleanup job)CHANGE_RETENTION (e.g. 2 DAYS)Inherits CT retention—
Not compatible / watch outCDC, transactional replication, Fabric mirroring and Synapse Link in the same DB; views; TRUNCATEMax. 2 capture instances per table; not with CESDoes not keep value historyDoes not use CDC. In-process model: end of support Nov 10, 2026Resetting/truncating the identity makes “created” skip rows; V1 deprecated
Decision rules:
  • Auditing/compliance with before and after values, batch load → CDC.
  • Only knowing which rows changed (incremental sync, caches, offline apps) → Change Tracking.
  • Stream to Event Hubs/Fabric Eventstream without polling, real-time analytics, microservices → CES (Preview).
  • Serverless code per row change → Azure Functions SQL trigger (needs Change Tracking, not CDC).
  • Notify/approve/integrate without code → Logic Apps.
  • CDC + CES in the same DB → not supported. CT + CES is supported; CT + CDC is supported.
Learn vs current docs: (1) the unit shows CREATE EVENT STREAMING GROUP … TARGET_TYPE='eventhub': that syntax does not exist; CES is configured with sys.sp_enable_event_stream, sys.sp_create_event_stream_group and sys.sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group (next topic). (2) It claims “sub-second” and “millions of events per second”: the docs only say near real-time. (3) It recommends combining CDC (auditing) with Functions triggers (which use CT): that is indeed possible; what cannot be done is CDC + CES in the same DB. (4) It says DAB integrates with these mechanisms through Functions triggers: DAB does not detect changes. (5) “CDC requires SQL Server Agent” only applies to SQL Server/MI.
Memorize: CES = push to Event Hubs (Preview, FULL recovery) · CDC = change tables with before/after (3 days) · CT = only PK + operation (PK required) · Functions = polling over CT · Logic Apps = IDENTITY / ROWVERSION or CT.
Sources: Learn · Handle changes with event-driven patterns · Docs · Change event streaming · Docs · CDC · Docs · CDC in Azure SQL Database · Docs · Change Tracking · Docs · Azure SQL trigger · Docs · SQL Server connector (Logic Apps)

Exact commands: enable CES, CDC and Change Tracking CES Preview SQL Server Azure SQL

Change event streaming (CES)

-- Requirements: FULL recovery model; db_owner or CONTROL DATABASE
ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON;     -- SQL Server 2025 only

CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<Password>';
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL EhCred WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity';
-- with SAS: WITH IDENTITY = '<policy name (Send)>', SECRET = '<key>'

EXEC sys.sp_enable_event_stream;

EXEC sys.sp_create_event_stream_group
    @stream_group_name      = N'myStreamGroup',
    @destination_type       = N'AzureEventHubs',     -- SQL DB and Fabric; MI/SQL 2025: N'AzureEventHubsApacheKafka'
    @destination_location   = N'myns.servicebus.windows.net:9093/myhub',
    @destination_credential = EhCred,
    @max_message_size_kb    = 256,
    @partition_key_scheme   = N'None';

EXEC sys.sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group N'myStreamGroup', N'dbo.Orders';
ParameterValuesDefault / notes
@destination_typeAzureEventHubs | AzureEventHubsApacheKafka | AzureEventHubsAmqpSQL DB and Fabric: only AzureEventHubs (Kafka). MI and SQL 2025: AzureEventHubsApacheKafka (AMQP deprecated)
@destination_location<ns>.servicebus.windows.net:9093/<eventhub>Port 9093 (Kafka). Fabric Eventstream: custom endpoint
@max_message_size_kb128 – 1024256; align with the destination (Event Hubs: 1 MB). The event is split into chunks; columns > 1 MB are silently truncated
@partition_key_schemeNone | StreamGroup | Table | ColumnNone (round-robin). Column requires @partition_key_column_name (schema.column)
@encodingJSON | BinaryJSON (Binary = Avro)
sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group@include_all_columns · @include_old_values · @include_old_lob_values1 · 1 · 0. Tables only
  • Event Hubs access: Microsoft Entra with MI (role Azure Event Hubs Data Sender, better at the instance level; in SQL Server 2025 requires CU3 and Azure Arc or an Azure VM) or SAS policy with the Send right; SQL database in Fabric has no Entra. Public endpoints only (no private endpoints).
  • Operations: sp_remove_object_from_event_stream_group, sp_drop_event_stream_group, sp_disable_event_stream; status with sys.databases.is_event_stream_enabled, sp_help_change_event_stream_groups, sp_help_change_event_stream_tables, sys.dm_change_feed_errors, sys.dm_change_feed_log_scan_sessions.
  • AMQP deprecated: from Aug 15, 2026, new groups in Azure SQL DB and Fabric must use AzureEventHubs (otherwise: error @destination_type is invalid. Allowed values: AzureEventHubs). Existing AMQP groups work until April 2027: recreate them (remove/add tables and sp_drop_event_stream_group) after first checking that there are no pending changes in sys.dm_change_feed_log_scan_sessions.
  • Limits: up to 4,096 groups and 40,000 tables per group; a table in a single group; no renaming tables/columns, adding/dropping PKs, or TRUNCATE/SWITCH PARTITION; no clustered columnstore, temporal/ledger history, Always Encrypted, In-Memory OLTP, graphs or external tables; omitted types: geography, geometry, image, json, rowversion, sql_variant, text/ntext, vector, xml and UDT. RLS and masks do not apply to the stream.
  • Log: delivery is guaranteed, so the log is not truncated while there are unpublished changes (errors, destination throttling, long transactions) and, if it fills up, writes fail: monitor the log size and errors.

Change data capture (CDC)

EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db;                               -- sysadmin in SQL Server/MI, db_owner in Azure SQL DB; no prior "cdc" schema/user
EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table
    @source_schema        = N'dbo',
    @source_name          = N'Orders',
    @role_name            = NULL,                         -- access role (NULL = no gating role)
    @capture_instance     = N'dbo_Orders',                -- default: <schema>_<table>
    @supports_net_changes = 1;                            -- requires PK or @index_name (unique index)

DECLARE @from binary(10) = sys.fn_cdc_get_min_lsn('dbo_Orders'),
        @to   binary(10) = sys.fn_cdc_get_max_lsn();
SELECT * FROM cdc.fn_cdc_get_all_changes_dbo_Orders(@from, @to, N'all');
-- __$operation: 1 = delete, 2 = insert, 3 = update (before), 4 = update (after); N'all' does not return 3, use N'all update old'
  • Objects: change table cdc.<capture_instance>_CT, fn_cdc_get_all_changes_<ci> and (with @supports_net_changes = 1) fn_cdc_get_net_changes_<ci>. Metadata columns: __$start_lsn, __$seqval, __$operation, __$update_mask. @captured_column_list limits columns.
  • Default retention 3 days; maximum 2 capture instances per table; query sys.databases.is_cdc_enabled.
  • SQL Server/MI use SQL Server Agent jobs (capture and cleanup); Azure SQL DB uses its own scheduler. Azure SQL DB: any vCore tier; DTU only S3 or higher.

Change Tracking (CT)

ALTER DATABASE SalesDb
SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON (CHANGE_RETENTION = 2 DAYS, AUTO_CLEANUP = ON);       -- DAYS | HOURS | MINUTES

ALTER TABLE dbo.Orders ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING WITH (TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED = ON); -- PK required; default OFF

DECLARE @last_sync bigint = 0;                            -- last version already processed
IF @last_sync < CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION(OBJECT_ID('dbo.Orders'))
    RAISERROR('Stale version: must reinitialize', 16, 1);

SELECT CT.OrderId, P.Status, CT.SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION, CT.SYS_CHANGE_VERSION, CT.SYS_CHANGE_COLUMNS
FROM dbo.Orders AS P
RIGHT OUTER JOIN CHANGETABLE(CHANGES dbo.Orders, @last_sync) AS CT ON P.OrderId = CT.OrderId;
SELECT CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION();                 -- save this version for the next round
  • SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION: I, U, D. Use RIGHT OUTER JOIN (or LEFT reversed) so deleted rows are not lost.
  • Only the PK values are stored; the current data is read from the table. Any DML counts as a change even if the value does not change.
  • To disable: first ALTER TABLE … DISABLE CHANGE_TRACKING on all tables and then SET CHANGE_TRACKING = OFF; sys.change_tracking_tables lists them. SQL Server 2025 uses adaptive “shallow” cleanup (disabled with trace flag 8273).
Exam: “error when enabling CT on a table” → missing PK; “offline consumer > retention” → CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION indicates it must reinitialize; “CES does not start on SQL Server 2025” → PREVIEW_FEATURES, FULL recovery or Event Hubs credential/permissions.

Azure Functions with SQL trigger binding and Logic Apps triggers GA Azure SQL SQL Server

using Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker;
using Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker.Extensions.Sql;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

public static class ToDoTrigger
{
    [Function("ToDoTrigger")]
    public static void Run(
        [SqlTrigger("[dbo].[ToDo]", "SqlConnectionString")] IReadOnlyList<SqlChange<ToDoItem>> changes,
        FunctionContext context)
    {
        var log = context.GetLogger("ToDoTrigger");
        foreach (SqlChange<ToDoItem> c in changes)      // c.Operation: Insert | Update | Delete
            log.LogInformation("{op}: {id}", c.Operation, c.Item.Id);
    }
}
ItemValueDefault / notes
[SqlTrigger] attributeTableName, ConnectionStringSetting (required), LeasesTableName (optional)NuGet package Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker.Extensions.Sql. In function.json: "type": "sqlTrigger", "direction": "in"
host.json → extensions.SqlMaxBatchSize · PollingIntervalMs · MaxChangesPerWorker100 · 1000 ms · 1000
App settingsSql_Trigger_MaxBatchSize · Sql_Trigger_PollingIntervalMs · Sql_Trigger_MaxChangesPerWorkerSame defaults. The table in the docs lists Sql_Trigger_BatchSize, but in the extension code that is the old name (compatibility): Sql_Trigger_MaxBatchSize is valid
Internal stateaz_func schema: leases table Leases_{FunctionId}_{TableId} and GlobalStateThe trigger creates them if they do not exist
RetriesException in the function → the batch is retried after 60 s5 consecutive failures of a row → that row is ignored in the future
ScalingTarget-based scaling (Consumption and Premium)In Premium, enable Runtime Scale Monitoring; Consumption requires extension ≥ v3.1.284
 
ALTER DATABASE [SampleDatabase] SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON (CHANGE_RETENTION = 2 DAYS, AUTO_CLEANUP = ON);
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[ToDo] ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING;          -- the table needs a PK

-- identity permissions (db_datareader/db_datawriter are NOT enough)
GRANT CREATE TABLE TO [<identity>];
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA TO [<identity>];
GRANT SELECT ON [dbo].[ToDo] TO [<identity>];
GRANT VIEW CHANGE TRACKING ON [dbo].[ToDo] TO [<identity>];
CREATE SCHEMA az_func;
GRANT ALTER ON SCHEMA::az_func TO [<identity>];
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON SCHEMA::az_func TO [<identity>];
  • Changes are processed in order, grouped by row: if a row changes several times between iterations, only one entry arrives (the difference between the last processed state and the current one).
  • Always Encrypted/TDE: the change is detected but the trigger does not decrypt the encrypted columns.

Logic Apps: SQL Server connector

TriggerWhereRequirement / behavior
When an item is created (V2)Managed (Consumption and Standard)IDENTITY column: uses the last identity as a threshold; if the identity is reset/truncated, the flow skips new rows
When an item is modified (V2)ManagedROWVERSION column; fires on INSERT and UPDATE (no DELETE)
When a row is inserted | updated | modified | deletedBuilt-in (Standard only)Requires Change Tracking on the table; permissions VIEW CHANGE TRACKING and schema az_func/GlobalState
  • It uses polling: you choose Frequency and Interval in the managed trigger. Optional OData parameters: $filter, $top, $orderby, $select. V1 triggers are deprecated.
  • On-premises in Consumption: on-premises data gateway. The built-in connector authenticates with MI, Microsoft Entra or a connection string and can access virtual networks without a gateway.
Learn vs current docs: the unit's code uses [FunctionName] + ILogger (in-process model), whose support ends on Nov 10, 2026; the current form is [Function] + FunctionContext (isolated worker). It correctly states that the trigger uses Change Tracking, not CDC.
Exam: “function that reacts to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on a table” → SQL trigger + Change Tracking on DB and table. “Workflow with email/Teams” → Logic Apps. “Table without PK” → neither CT nor the SQL trigger can be used. “Function down for 3 days with retention of 2” → lost changes (CT retention).

Module 9Domain 3 · 25–30%

Design and implement models and embeddings with SQL

Register an AI endpoint as a database object (CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL), generate chunks and embeddings in T-SQL (AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS), store them in vector columns and keep them in sync. The exam tests: exact syntax and options, choosing a model, which columns/chunks to embed and which maintenance method fits the scenario.

Skills measured covered:
  • Evaluate external models, including multimodal, multilanguage, sizes, and structured output
  • Create and manage external models
  • Choose an embedding maintenance method, including table triggers, Change Tracking, Azure Functions with SQL trigger binding, Azure Logic Apps, CDC, CES, and Microsoft Foundry
  • Identify which columns to include in embeddings
  • Design and implement chunks for embeddings
  • Generate embeddings

End-to-end flow and availability by platform SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB

An external model is a database object that stores endpoint metadata (URL, API format, credential, parameters). It is not a model that runs inside the engine: the AI_* functions use it to call the external service without putting URLs or secrets in the code.

  1. Enable outbound REST: external rest endpoint enabled defaults to ON in Azure SQL DB and Fabric SQL DB; in SQL Server 2025 and MI it defaults to OFF (sp_configure + RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; requires ALTER SETTINGS).
  2. Master key + DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL (Managed Identity or API key).
  3. CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL (MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS) y GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::….
  4. (Optional) AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS: splits long text; uses no network or credential.
  5. AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(text USE MODEL …) → array of floats that is assigned to vector(n).
  6. Store in a vector(n) column (better in a separate 1-N table) and query with VECTOR_DISTANCE / VECTOR_SEARCH (another module), combining with relational filters (hybrid search).
  7. Keep the vectors in sync: hash/model version + trigger, Change Tracking, CDC, Functions, Logic Apps or CES.

Exam (knowledge check): external model = object with endpoint metadata (it does not run in the engine nor is it a copy of the model); chunking = splitting long text to respect token limits; data type for embeddings = VECTOR; in RAG, embeddings represent data as vectors to compare semantic similarity.
Watch out: AI_ANALYZE_SENTIMENT, AI_CLASSIFY, AI_EXTRACT, AI_FIX_GRAMMAR, AI_GENERATE_RESPONSE, AI_SUMMARIZE and AI_TRANSLATE exist only in Warehouse / SQL analytics endpoint in Fabric. In SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL DB/MI and Fabric SQL DB the available AI_* functions are AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS and AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS.
MI and status (discrepancy between pages): CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS and the vector type cite only the Always-up-to-date policy; AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS, VECTORPROPERTY and sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint cite SQL Server 2025 or Always-up-to-date. In “What's new in SQL Server 2025” (Language › Artificial intelligence), CREATE/ALTER/DROP EXTERNAL MODEL, AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS and AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS appear without the Requires PREVIEW_FEATURES mark that CREATE VECTOR INDEX, VECTOR_SEARCH and CES do carry: in SQL Server 2025 they are treated as GA; the local ONNX runtime, float16, vector index/VECTOR_SEARCH and CES are Preview.
Sources: Learn · Create and manage external models in SQL · Docs · AI Functions · Blog · GA of AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS and EXTERNAL MODEL · Docs · What's new Azure SQL DB · Docs · Limitations SQL database in Fabric

Evaluate models: modality, language, size and structured output

Learn evaluates four characteristics before integrating a model; the tool to compare them is the Microsoft Foundry Models catalog (capabilities, benchmarks, version and lifecycle status).

Modality (multimodal)

  • Text vs image/audio/structured data: depends on the data you store and the use case.
  • AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS only accepts character types (char, varchar, nchar, nvarchar) → text embeddings.
  • Multimodal example in Foundry: Cohere embed-v-4-0 (text of 512 tokens + images of up to 2 M pixels; 256/512/1024/1536 dims).
  • Design pattern (not a SQL function): describe the image with a multimodal LLM via REST and embed that text, or generate the vector outside the engine and store it in vector.

Language (multilanguage)

  • Needed if users or content span several languages.
  • Compare multilingual retrieval benchmarks: MIRACL — ada-002 31.4 · 3-small 44.0 · 3-large 54.9. MTEB (English) — 61.0 · 62.3 · 64.6.
  • Cohere embed-v-4-0: en, fr, es, it, de, pt-br, ja, ko, zh-cn, ar.

Size and capacity

  • Large models: better reasoning, but more tokens, latency and cost. Small models are enough for focused tasks like embeddings.
  • Each model limits tokens per request (e.g. 8,000 or 128,000) and is billed per token → this affects chunking and context in RAG.
  • In embeddings, more dimensions = more compute, memory and storage.

Structured output

  • Models that return JSON conforming to a schema are easy to process in T-SQL (OPENJSON, JSON_VALUE).
  • In the catalog, look at the Response formats column (Text, JSON).
  • Structured outputs (json_schema + strict: true) ≠ JSON mode (only guarantees valid JSON, not the schema).
If the scenario says…Choose
Multilingual semantic searchtext-embedding-3-large (best MIRACL); 3-small if cost/latency matter
High volume, tight cost/latencytext-embedding-3-small (1,536 dims)
Catalog with images + textMultimodal embeddings model (e.g. Cohere embed-v-4-0) outside AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS, or an LLM that describes the image
Production on Azure SQL DB/MI with Entra / Managed IdentityAzure OpenAI (*.openai.azure.com): Azure billing and SLA, role Cognitive Services OpenAI User. Direct OpenAI (api.openai.com) is not in the Azure SQL DB/MI allow list: only SQL Server 2025 or behind API Management
Data that cannot leave / local developmentOllama (https://localhost…) or ONNX Runtime (SQL Server 2025, Windows, Preview)
Extract fields as JSON with a schemaChat model with structured outputs via sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint (not EXTERNAL MODEL)
Compare benchmarks, versions and retirementsFoundry Models catalog
 
{
  "model": "<deployment-name>",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Extract the event information."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Alice and Bob are going to a science fair on Friday."}
  ],
  "response_format": {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
      "name": "CalendarEventResponse",
      "strict": true,
      "schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "name": {"type": "string"},
          "date": {"type": "string"},
          "participants": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
        },
        "required": ["name", "date", "participants"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      }
    }
  }
}
Memorize: MODEL_TYPE only accepts EMBEDDINGS. Chat/vision models are not registered as EXTERNAL MODEL; they are called via REST (details in the RAG module). Chat Completions uses response_format; the Responses API uses text.format. With function calling and structured outputs, parallel_tool_calls must be false.
Lifecycle: Microsoft does not recommend preview models in production (they do not follow the standard lifecycle). And there is no “upgrade” between embedding models: changing the model means regenerating all the vectors.
Sources: Learn · Understand and evaluate models · Docs · Foundry Models sold by Azure · Docs · Structured outputs · Docs · AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS

Azure OpenAI embedding models: dimensions, limits and dimensions

Criteriontext-embedding-ada-002text-embedding-3-smalltext-embedding-3-large
Max. tokens per input8,192 (v2) · 2,046 (v1)8,1928,192
Default dimensions1,5361,5363,072
dimensions parameterNoYesYes
MIRACL / MTEB31.4 / 61.044.0 / 62.354.9 / 64.6
Does it fit in vector(n) float32 (≤ 1,998)?YesYesNot by default: use dimensions ≤ 1,998 or float16
