-- Option A: reduce dimensions in the model (≤ 1,998 for float32)
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL EmbLarge
WITH (
    LOCATION   = 'https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/<deployment>/embeddings?api-version=2024-10-21',
    API_FORMAT = 'Azure OpenAI',
    MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS,
    MODEL      = 'text-embedding-3-large',
    CREDENTIAL = [https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/],
    PARAMETERS = '{"dimensions":1536}'
);
GO
-- Option B: override per query (wins over the model value)
DECLARE @p json = N'{"dimensions":1024}';
SELECT AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(N'sample text' USE MODEL EmbLarge PARAMETERS @p);
GO
-- Option C: keep 3,072 dims with half-precision (Azure SQL DB/MI/Fabric: GA)
CREATE TABLE dbo.Doc3072 (id int PRIMARY KEY, emb vector(3072, float16) NULL);
  • Maximum items per request to the embeddings endpoint: 2,048 (relevant if you call via REST with arrays of texts).
  • Query and data must use the same model and the same dimensions; the returned dimensions must match the column's n (error 42204 otherwise).
Memorize: 1,536 = ada-002 and 3-small · 3,072 = 3-large · float32 ≤ 1,998 · float16 ≤ 3,996 · only the 3rd generation accepts dimensions.
Watch out: you cannot “upgrade” from ada-002 to 3-large; all embeddings must be regenerated (and VECTOR(n) reviewed). The docs examples use api-version=2024-02-01/2023-05-15; the Learn lab uses 2024-10-21 (GA).
Sources: Docs · Foundry Models sold by Azure (Embeddings) · Docs · vector data type · Docs · AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS · Learn · Lab 09

DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL and authentication to the AI endpoint Azure SQL DB/MI SQL Server 2025

-- A) Managed Identity (recommended in Azure SQL Database)
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL [https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/]
    WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity',
         SECRET   = '{"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"}';

-- B) API key in HTTP headers (Azure SQL DB and SQL Server 2025)
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL [https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/]
    WITH IDENTITY = 'HTTPEndpointHeaders',
         SECRET   = '{"api-key":"<your-api-key>"}';
IDENTITYWhat it sendsSECRET
'Managed Identity'Entra token of the managed identity (in Azure SQL DB, that of the logical server){"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"} — fixed value (OAuth audience of Cognitive Services)
'HTTPEndpointHeaders'HTTP headersPlain JSON: {"api-key":"…"} (Azure OpenAI) · {"Bearer":"…"} (OpenAI)
'HTTPEndpointQueryString'Query stringPlain JSON, e.g. {"code":"…"}
'SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE'SASSAS token (without the leading ?)

Managed Identity in Azure SQL DB: steps

  1. Portal → SQL server (the logical server, not the DB) → Security > Identity → System assigned managed identity = On. If there is a user-assigned identity, the primary one is used; if both system- and user-assigned identities exist, the user-assigned one wins.
  2. Azure OpenAI resource → Access control (IAM) → assign the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role to that identity (it can take up to ~5 min).
  3. Create the Managed Identity credential with the fixed resourceid.
  4. Create the EXTERNAL MODEL with CREDENTIAL = […].

Credential name rules

  • Valid URL, without a query string, and its domain must be in the allow list (in Azure SQL DB/MI).
  • Protocol + FQDN identical to those of the called URL; each path segment must match completely.
  • The credential must point to a more generic path than the request URL (e.g. https://host/ works for https://host/openai/...).
  • Maximum name length: 128 characters; it cannot start with #.
RequirementDetails
Create the credentialCONTROL permission on the database
Database master keyRequired before creating credentials; in Azure SQL DB it is created automatically (random password) when the first credential is created; in SQL Server you must create it
Use the credential with direct RESTGRANT REFERENCES ON DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL::[…]
SQL Server 2025 + Managed IdentityAzure Arc with primary managed identity + sp_configure 'allow server scoped db credentials', 1; RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE;
Allowed endpoints (Azure SQL DB/MI)*.openai.azure.com, *.cognitiveservices.azure.com, *.api.cognitive.microsoft.com, *.azure-api.net… (full list in the sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint docs)
Watch out — Foundry endpoint: use the URL from the OpenAI tab (*.openai.azure.com) or *.cognitiveservices.azure.com. The *.services.ai.azure.com URL from the Foundry tab is not in the allow list and the Learn lab says it does not work with these functions. For providers outside the list, publish them behind API Management (*.azure-api.net).
Role discrepancy: Learn (unit 3 and lab) requires Cognitive Services OpenAI User for Azure SQL DB; the CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL docs (SQL Server 2025 with Arc) mention Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor. User is the minimum for inference (OpenAI Contributor includes everything in User; by contrast, Cognitive Services Contributor, without “OpenAI”, does not allow inference with Entra ID); follow the role the question names. Verify (Fabric SQL DB): the EXTERNAL MODEL docs apply to it, but Learn only describes Managed Identity for Azure SQL DB; verify the supported method before assuming it.
Memorize: Managed Identity → resourceid = https://cognitiveservices.azure.com (not your endpoint). API key → IDENTITY = 'HTTPEndpointHeaders' with {"api-key":"…"}. Avoid keys in T-SQL code.
Sources: Learn · Create and manage external models · Learn · Lab 09 · Docs · CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL · Docs · sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint · Docs · CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL

CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL: syntax, options and examples SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Creates the object with the location, authentication method and purpose of the inference endpoint. It does not invoke the model: URL/credential errors usually show up on the first call to AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS.

CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL external_model_object_name
[ AUTHORIZATION owner_name ]
WITH
  ( LOCATION   = '<prefix>://<path>[:<port>]'
  , API_FORMAT = '<Azure OpenAI | OpenAI | Ollama | ONNX Runtime>'
  , MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS
  , MODEL      = 'text-embedding-model-name'
  [ , CREDENTIAL = <credential_name> ]
  [ , PARAMETERS = '{"valid":"JSON"}' ]
  [ , LOCAL_RUNTIME_PATH = 'path to the ONNX Runtime files' ]
  );
OptionValueNotes
AUTHORIZATIONowning user or roleBy default, the current user; others need explicit permission to use the model
LOCATIONHTTPS URL (local folder with ONNX)Only endpoints with HTTPS + TLS
API_FORMATAzure OpenAI · OpenAI · Ollama · ONNX RuntimeRequired; defines the message format
MODEL_TYPEEMBEDDINGSOnly accepted value
MODELmodel name (text-embedding-3-small)Required; the deployment goes in the URL
CREDENTIALDATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIALOptional (the Ollama and ONNX examples do not use it)
PARAMETERSValid JSON that is added to the request body{"dimensions":n} · {"sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":0–10}}; can be combined in the same JSON
LOCAL_RUNTIME_PATHONNX Runtime folderOnly with ONNX Runtime
 
Azure OpenAI : https://{endpoint}/openai/deployments/{deployment-id}/embeddings?api-version={date}
OpenAI       : https://{server_name}/v1/embeddings
Ollama       : https://localhost:{port}/api/embed
ONNX Runtime : local path of the folder containing model.onnx and tokenizer.json
-- Azure OpenAI with API key (HTTPEndpointHeaders credential) and PARAMETERS
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL MyAzureOpenAIModel
AUTHORIZATION CRM_User                      -- explicit owner (optional)
WITH (
    LOCATION   = 'https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/deployments/text-embedding-3-small/embeddings?api-version=2024-02-01',
    API_FORMAT = 'Azure OpenAI',
    MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS,
    MODEL      = 'text-embedding-3-small',
    CREDENTIAL = [https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com/],
    PARAMETERS = '{"dimensions":725, "sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":5}}'
);
GO
-- OpenAI: the key goes in a header; credential name = protocol + FQDN of LOCATION
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL [https://api.openai.com]
    WITH IDENTITY = 'HTTPEndpointHeaders', SECRET = '{"Bearer":"<openai-key>"}';
GO
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL MyOpenAIModel
WITH (LOCATION = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings', API_FORMAT = 'OpenAI',
      MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS, MODEL = 'text-embedding-ada-002',
      CREDENTIAL = [https://api.openai.com]);
GO
-- Ollama locally (development; requires HTTPS)
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL MyOllamaModel
WITH (LOCATION = 'https://localhost:11435/api/embed', API_FORMAT = 'Ollama',
      MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS, MODEL = 'all-minilm');

Local ONNX Runtime Preview SQL Server 2025 · Windows

  1. ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON; and EXECUTE sp_configure 'external AI runtimes enabled', 1; RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE; (requires SQL Server Machine Learning Services).
  2. Folder with onnxruntime.dll (ONNX Runtime ≥ 1.19) and tokenizers_cpp.dll; the model (model.onnx + tokenizer.json) in a subfolder; grant FullControl to the MSSQLLaunchpad account.
  3. Register and test:
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL myLocalOnnxModel
WITH (
    LOCATION   = 'C:\onnx_runtime\model\all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx',   -- model.onnx + tokenizer.json
    API_FORMAT = 'ONNX Runtime',
    MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS,
    MODEL      = 'allMiniLM',
    PARAMETERS = '{"valid":"JSON"}',                               -- placeholder required in SQL Server 2025
    LOCAL_RUNTIME_PATH = 'C:\onnx_runtime\'
);
SELECT AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(N'Test Text' USE MODEL myLocalOnnxModel);
Discrepancy: the GA blog (May 2026) cites only Azure OpenAI and OpenAI as API_FORMAT; the current reference lists four (Ollama = local development; ONNX Runtime = Preview, Windows only). On the exam, valid values: Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Ollama, ONNX Runtime. The ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL page lists only three (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Ollama) and shows LOCATION/API_FORMAT/MODEL_TYPE/MODEL without brackets even though its example only changes MODEL. The OpenAI docs use a credential [https://openai.com] with URL api.openai.com, which contradicts the “identical protocol + FQDN” rule: here the name that meets the rule is used.
Memorize: MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS (only value) · HTTPS only · retry_count 0–10 · the deployment goes in the URL, the model name in MODEL.
Sources: Learn · Create and manage external models · Docs · CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL · Blog · GA of EXTERNAL MODEL

Manage external models: ALTER, DROP, permissions, catalog and errors SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB Fabric SQL DB

-- Changes only what is specified; dependent queries are not rewritten
ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL myAImodel SET ( MODEL = 'text-embedding-3-large' );

SELECT name, api_format, model_type_desc, model, location, credential_id, parameters, create_time, modify_time
FROM sys.external_models;

GRANT CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL    TO [dev_user];                  -- create models
GRANT ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL TO [dev_user];                  -- create/alter any
GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::myAImodel TO [app_user];      -- use it in AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS

-- There is no IF EXISTS in the documented syntax; DROP does NOT remove the credential used
DROP EXTERNAL MODEL myAImodel;
ActionPermission
Create / alter a modelCREATE EXTERNAL MODEL or ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL (database permissions)
Use the model in an AI functionEXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::name (by default only the owner)
Create the credentialCONTROL on the DB
Call sp_invoke_external_rest_endpointEXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT (+ REFERENCES on the credential)
View the model in sys.external_modelsYou only see what you own or have some permission on
  • ALTER modifies one object at a time; concurrent requests on the same model wait. Changing MODEL or dimensions does not regenerate the vectors already stored.
  • A view with SCHEMABINDING that uses AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS prevents dropping the model until the view is modified or dropped.
  • Diagnostics: extended events ai_generate_embeddings_summary (HTTP code, errors, model) and external_rest_endpoint_summary; ONNX: ai_generate_embeddings_airuntime_trace.
  • Columns of sys.external_models: external_model_id, name, principal_id, location, api_format, model_type_id/_desc, model, credential_id, parameters (json), create_time, modify_time.
Observed errorCommon cause
Msg 31630The credential name is not a prefix of LOCATION (or a different path/FQDN)
Msg 33047Managed Identity credential without SECRET with resourceid
Msg 31612Domain outside the allow list (Azure SQL DB/MI)
Msg 15151Missing EXECUTE on the model; also if CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL and its use are in the same batch (separate with GO)
Msg 31742HTTP 401 (incorrect key/role) or 400 (dimensions not supported)
Msg 42204Result dimensions ≠ n of vector(n)
Msg 46556Attempt to drop a credential still used by a model: first DROP EXTERNAL MODEL, then DROP DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL
Source and Verify: the error table comes from tests published by Microsoft (repo microsoft-sql, Azure SQL DB, Aug 2026), not from the docs contract; only 42204 also appears in the vector type docs. Verify: the ALTER/DROP page lists SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL DB and Fabric; it does not mention MI.
Exam: “change the endpoint/credential without touching the code” → ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL. “Give a user permission to generate embeddings” → GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL. Dropping the model leaves the credential orphaned (it must be dropped separately, and only after the model).
Sources: Docs · ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL · Docs · DROP EXTERNAL MODEL · Docs · sys.external_models · Docs · CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL (permissions) · GitHub · microsoft-sql (observed errors)

Generate embeddings: AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS ( source USE MODEL model_identifier [ PARAMETERS optional_json_request_body_parameters ] )

-- 1) SELECT: returns the JSON array of floats
SELECT id, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(large_text USE MODEL MyAzureOpenAIModel) FROM myTable;

-- 2) UPDATE into a vector column
UPDATE t SET myEmbeddings = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(t.text USE MODEL MyAzureOpenAIModel) FROM myTable AS t;

-- 3) Vector variable (embedding of the search query)
DECLARE @qv vector(1536) = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(N'Pink Floyd music style' USE MODEL Ada2Embeddings);

-- 4) Per-query PARAMETERS: overrides what is defined in the model
DECLARE @params json = N'{"dimensions":768, "sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":10}}';
SELECT id, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(large_text USE MODEL MyAzureOpenAIModel PARAMETERS @params) FROM myTable;
ItemDetails
sourceCharacter-type expression: nvarchar, varchar, nchar, char (text only)
model_identifierName of an EXTERNAL MODEL of type EMBEDDINGS
PARAMETERSValid JSON added to the request body; whatever the endpoint supports (dimensions, sql_rest_options.retry_count 0–10)
ResultJSON array of floats; implicitly converted to vector(n) when assigned to a column/variable (n = model dimensions)
Where it is usedSELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE, procedures and triggers
Prerequisitesexternal rest endpoint enabled (ON by default in Azure SQL DB/Fabric) + EXTERNAL MODEL + EXECUTE on the model
Input limitThe model's (8,192 tokens in OpenAI models): you chunk first with AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS
CriterionAI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS + EXTERNAL MODELsp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint
What it isT-SQL function on a DB objectGeneric procedure to call any HTTPS REST endpoint
ModelsEmbeddings only (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Ollama, ONNX)Anything: chat, images, other APIs
Payload / responseHandled by the engine; returns the vectorYou build @payload and parse @response (JSON)
PermissionEXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODELEXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT (+ REFERENCES on the credential)
Retriessql_rest_options.retry_count (0–10)@retry_count (0–10) and @timeout (1–230 s, default 30)
Use it forStandard embeddings, set-basedChat/completions, structured output, unsupported endpoints
Discrepancies (resolved): (1) the “Return types” section of the reference says it returns “a one-column table with JSON arrays”, but the syntax, the GA blog (“scalar-valued … returns a JSON array value”), Learn unit 5 (“the function returns a vector”) and all the examples (SELECT list, SET col =, DECLARE @v vector(n) =) use it as a scalar function: treat it as scalar (no example puts it in FROM/CROSS APPLY; that belongs to AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS). (2) Learn unit 3 calls for granting EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT “to whoever calls external endpoints”; the CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL reference and the GA blog only require EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL for AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS (the model carries the credential; in published tests on Azure SQL DB the other permissions were not needed). Rule: “call sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint” → EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT (+ REFERENCES on the credential); “use the model in AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS” → EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL.
Best practices: filter out NULL and empty strings before calling (a literal NULL gave Msg 8116 in published tests). Each value is one HTTP call (observed), so large batches are processed in rounds (see “End-to-end and batches”). Extended event: ai_generate_embeddings_summary.
Sources: Learn · Generate and maintain embeddings · Docs · AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS · Blog · GA · Docs · sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint

End-to-end: credential → model → chunks → embeddings → vector column (and batches with retries)

  1. Setup (once per DB): outbound REST, master key, credential, model and permission.
  2. Tables 1-N: document → chunks with vector column, hash and model.
  3. Load chunks (no network) with AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS and embed in batches those with Embedding IS NULL.
  4. Query: embedding of the question + VECTOR_DISTANCE.
-- SQL Server 2025 and MI only (already ON in Azure SQL DB and Fabric)
EXECUTE sp_configure 'external rest endpoint enabled', 1;
RECONFIGURE WITH OVERRIDE;
GO
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.symmetric_keys WHERE [name] = '##MS_DatabaseMasterKey##')
    CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = N'<strong-password>';
GO
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL [https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/]
    WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity',
         SECRET   = '{"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"}';
GO
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL MyEmbeddingModel
WITH (
    LOCATION   = 'https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/<deployment>/embeddings?api-version=2024-10-21',
    API_FORMAT = 'Azure OpenAI',
    MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS,
    MODEL      = 'text-embedding-3-small',
    CREDENTIAL = [https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/],
    PARAMETERS = '{"dimensions":1536, "sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":3}}'
);
GO
GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::MyEmbeddingModel TO [app_user];
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.Document
(
    DocID int IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    Title nvarchar(200) NOT NULL,
    Body  nvarchar(max) NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE dbo.DocumentChunk
(
    DocID       int           NOT NULL,
    ChunkNo     int           NOT NULL,
    ChunkOffset int           NOT NULL,
    ChunkText   nvarchar(max) NOT NULL,
    Embedding   vector(1536)  NULL,            -- NULL = pending embedding
    ModelName   nvarchar(100) NULL,
    SourceHash  binary(32)    NOT NULL,        -- SHA2_256 of the document's source text
    EmbeddedAt  datetime2(0)  NULL,
    CONSTRAINT PK_DocumentChunk PRIMARY KEY (DocID, ChunkNo),
    CONSTRAINT FK_DocumentChunk_Document FOREIGN KEY (DocID)
        REFERENCES dbo.Document (DocID) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
GO
INSERT INTO dbo.DocumentChunk (DocID, ChunkNo, ChunkOffset, ChunkText, SourceHash)
SELECT d.DocID, c.chunk_order, c.chunk_offset, c.chunk, HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', d.Body)
FROM dbo.Document AS d
CROSS APPLY AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS(SOURCE = d.Body, CHUNK_TYPE = FIXED, CHUNK_SIZE = 1000, OVERLAP = 10) AS c;
DECLARE @batch int = 30, @n int = 1, @try int = 0, @maxTry int = 3;
WHILE @n > 0
BEGIN
    BEGIN TRY
        UPDATE TOP (@batch) c
           SET c.Embedding  = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(c.ChunkText USE MODEL MyEmbeddingModel),
               c.ModelName  = N'text-embedding-3-small',
               c.EmbeddedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME()
          FROM dbo.DocumentChunk AS c
         WHERE c.Embedding IS NULL;
        SELECT @n = @@ROWCOUNT, @try = 0;
        IF @n > 0 WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:02';      -- respects the deployment's TPM/RPM
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        SET @try += 1;
        IF @try > @maxTry THROW;                  -- retries exhausted: propagate the error
        WAITFOR DELAY '00:00:05';                  -- e.g. 429: wait and retry the batch
    END CATCH
END;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS Total, COUNT(Embedding) AS Embebidos FROM dbo.DocumentChunk;
SELECT TOP (1) VECTORPROPERTY(Embedding, 'Dimensions') AS Dims, DATALENGTH(Embedding) AS Bytes
FROM dbo.DocumentChunk WHERE Embedding IS NOT NULL;     -- 1536 dims · ≈ 6,148 bytes
DECLARE @q vector(1536) = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(N'How do I restore a backup?' USE MODEL MyEmbeddingModel);
SELECT TOP (5) DocID, ChunkNo, VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', @q, Embedding) AS Distance   -- 0 identical … 2 opposite
FROM dbo.DocumentChunk
WHERE Embedding IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY Distance;
Retry / limit layerValue
sql_rest_options.retry_count (model or the query's PARAMETERS)0–10; the query's overrides the model's
sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint@retry_count 0–10 (default 0) · @timeout 1–230 s (default 30; cumulative if there are retries)
Retried HTTP codes408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504; waits Retry-After if present, otherwise exponential backoff (fallback 200 ms)
Outbound concurrency15% of worker threads, max. 175 → error 10928 (10936 in elastic pool)
Deployment quota (TPM/RPM)Exceeding it produces HTTP 429
Pattern: separate “chunking” (cheap, no network) from “embedding” (slow, with network): load the chunks with Embedding = NULL and process in small rounds to avoid holding long transactions. A single statement (INSERT … SELECT AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(c.chunk …) CROSS APPLY AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS) works on small data, but for millions of rows use rounds or an external tool that sends arrays of texts per request.
Watch out: in published tests, CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL and the function that uses it cannot be in the same batch (Msg 15151): separate with GO. The Learn lab uses UPDATE TOP (@batchSize), WAITFOR DELAY and manual retry: it is the expected pattern for batches.
Sources: Learn · Exercise · Learn · Lab 09 · Docs · AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS (example F) · Docs · sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint (limits, retry)

vector type: syntax, dimensions, storage and limitations SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

column_name VECTOR ( <dimensions> [ , <base_type> ] ) [ NOT NULL | NULL ]   -- base_type: float32 (default) | float16

CREATE TABLE dbo.v32 (id int PRIMARY KEY, v vector(1536) NOT NULL);        -- float32 · 4 bytes/dim
CREATE TABLE dbo.v16 (id int PRIMARY KEY, v vector(3072, float16) NULL);   -- float16 · 2 bytes/dim

DECLARE @v vector(3) = '[0.1, 2, 30]';                                      -- string or json → vector (implicit)
SELECT CAST(@v AS nvarchar(max)) AS as_text,                                -- scientific notation
       CAST(@v AS json)          AS as_json;                                -- decimal notation
SELECT VECTORPROPERTY(@v, 'Dimensions') AS dims, VECTORPROPERTY(@v, 'BaseType') AS base_type;
SELECT name, vector_dimensions, vector_base_type, vector_base_type_desc     -- 0 = float32 · 1 = float16
FROM sys.columns WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.v16');
TopicRule
DimensionsMinimum 1; float32 ≤ 1,998; float16 ≤ 3,996. Stored in binary and exposed as a JSON array
Storagefloat32 = 4 bytes/dim (1,536 dims ≈ 6 KB/row; DATALENGTH ≈ 6,148); float16 = 2 bytes/dim
AvailabilityAll compatibility levels. float16: GA in Azure SQL DB/MI/Fabric; Preview in SQL Server 2025 (PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON); not supported on Arm64
ConversionImplicit/explicit from and to char, nchar, varchar, nvarchar, json; the value must be a JSON array of numbers with exactly n elements. Implicit conversion requires declaring the dimensions
float32 ↔ float16Cannot be converted (neither implicitly nor with CAST); VECTOR_DISTANCE does not accept mixed base types. float16: values > 65,504 raise an error
Error codes42204 (no. of elements/dimensions differs) · 13670 (not a JSON array of numbers) · 42211 (target string too short) · 42238 (float32 ↔ float16)
PrecedenceLower than string types: in UNION, CASE, COALESCE the result is the string

Limitations

  • Only NULL/NOT NULL constraints: no DEFAULT, CHECK, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY or UNIQUE on the vector column; no comparison, arithmetic or concatenation operators.
  • Not in memory-optimized tables; no B-tree or columnstore indexes (allowed as an INCLUDE column); the approximate index is a separate object (CREATE VECTOR INDEX).
  • Not with sql_variant, CREATE TYPE (alias) or Always Encrypted; sp_describe_first_result_set shows it as varchar/nvarchar; sp_verify_database_ledger fails if there are vector columns.
  • Native binary transport with TDS 7.4+: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient ≥ 6.1.0 (SqlVector), JDBC ≥ 13.1.0; native float16: JDBC 13.4 / ODBC 18.7.1. Other clients receive it as varchar(max) JSON.
Exam: the type to store embeddings is VECTOR (not NVARCHAR(MAX) or JSON). 3,072-dim model → dimensions ≤ 1,998 or vector(3072, float16). The no. of dimensions must match between the model and the column.
Sources: Learn · Generate and maintain embeddings · Docs · vector data type · Docs · half-precision float · Docs · VECTORPROPERTY

Which columns to include in the embedding and how to compose the text

Embeddings work best with text that carries meaning. Identifiers, numeric values and operational metadata add no semantics: they waste tokens and worsen similarity.

Include

  • Titles and names, descriptions, summaries
  • Category or labels as text
  • Notes, comments, reviews, articles/FAQ
  • Short fields (tags, author, language) consolidated into a single text/JSON

Exclude

  • IDs, GUIDs, SKUs, codes, foreign keys
  • Numeric values (price, quantity), dates, flags and statuses
  • Hashes, URLs, binaries
  • Best practice: PII, repetitive text (legal notices, signatures) and noisy fields
-- CONCAT_WS ignores NULLs (with "+" a NULL nullifies the whole result)
SELECT p.ProductID, CONCAT_WS(N'. ', p.Name, p.Description, c.Name) AS SourceText
FROM dbo.Product AS p
JOIN dbo.Category AS c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID;

-- Short fields → a single JSON → a single embedding
SELECT p.ProductID,
       CAST(JSON_OBJECT('tags': p.Tags, 'author': p.Author, 'language': p.Lang ABSENT ON NULL) AS nvarchar(max)) AS MetaText
FROM dbo.Product AS p;
  • One embedding per long field, in its own table (id, chunk_index, embedding; PK (id, chunk_index)); several tables are combined with LEAST(VECTOR_DISTANCE(…), VECTOR_DISTANCE(…)). Learn: a separate table lets you measure the space the vectors take up and rebuild them without touching the original data.
  • Filter attributes (category, language, date, tenant) stay as regular columns for the WHERE (hybrid search), not just inside the vector.
  • Use the same template when ingesting and regenerating (view/function): changing it invalidates the existing vectors.
Exam: “reduce tokens/cost and improve relevance” → remove IDs, numeric values and operational metadata and embed only descriptive text (title + description + category). Many short fields → consolidate them into a single text/JSON.
Sources: Learn · Design embeddings · Blog · Modeling embeddings · Learn · Lab 09

Chunking: AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS and strategies SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL DB/MI Fabric SQL DB GA

Table-valued function that splits text into fragments. Requires compatibility level ≥ 170 (below that, the engine cannot find the function). It uses no network or credential; the docs define no specific permissions.

AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS ( SOURCE = text_expression
                   , CHUNK_TYPE = FIXED
                   [ , CHUNK_SIZE = numeric_expression ]
                   [ , OVERLAP = numeric_expression ]
                   [ , ENABLE_CHUNK_SET_ID = numeric_expression ] )

-- Fixed size with 10% overlap (CHUNK_SIZE = 1000 → 100 repeated characters)
SELECT d.DocID, c.chunk_set_id, c.chunk_order, c.chunk_offset, c.chunk_length, c.chunk
FROM dbo.Document AS d
CROSS APPLY AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS(SOURCE = d.Body, CHUNK_TYPE = FIXED, CHUNK_SIZE = 1000,
                               OVERLAP = 10, ENABLE_CHUNK_SET_ID = 1) AS c;

-- Chunking + embedding in one statement (pattern from the docs)
INSERT INTO my_embeddings (chunked_text, vector_embeddings)
SELECT c.chunk, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(c.chunk USE MODEL MyAzureOpenAIModel)
FROM table_with_text AS t
CROSS APPLY AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS(SOURCE = t.text_to_chunk, CHUNK_TYPE = FIXED, CHUNK_SIZE = 100) AS c;
ArgumentRule
SOURCECharacter expression (nvarchar, varchar, nchar, char)
CHUNK_TYPELiteral FIXED (only value); cannot be NULL or come from a column
CHUNK_SIZENo. of characters per chunk (tinyint/smallint/int/bigint); not NULL, negative or 0; required with FIXED
OVERLAPPercentage of CHUNK_SIZE repeated from the previous chunk; integer 0–50; default 0
ENABLE_CHUNK_SET_ID1 returns chunk_set_id (omitted, NULL or 0 = not returned)
Returned columnschunk (same type as SOURCE) · chunk_order bigint (1…n) · chunk_offset bigint (1-based) · chunk_length int · chunk_set_id bigint (optional; different per row/document)
StrategyHowProsCons
Fixed sizeFIXED + CHUNK_SIZESimple, fast, T-SQL onlyCuts mid-word/mid-sentence
Fixed + overlapOVERLAP (e.g. 10–20)Preserves context at the edgesMore chunks → more cost and storage
Paragraph / sentenceCustom T-SQL: REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE (compat 170) or STRING_SPLIT(text, sep, 1) (single-character sep; 1 returns ordinal)Respects semantic boundariesMore code; uneven sizes
Semantic / by tokensOutside SQL (app, Function)Better qualityCHUNK_TYPE only supports FIXED
 
SELECT d.DocID, p.ordinal AS ChunkNo, LTRIM(RTRIM(p.value)) AS Chunk
FROM dbo.Document AS d
CROSS APPLY REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE(d.Body, N'(\r?\n){2,}') AS p      -- separator: blank line
WHERE LEN(LTRIM(RTRIM(p.value))) > 0;
  • CHUNK_SIZE counts characters, not tokens: each chunk must stay under the model's limit (8,192 tokens in OpenAI embeddings). Rule of thumb ≈ 4 characters/token in English (varies by language).
  • Trade-off: chunk too large → exceeds the limit or dilutes the semantic focus; too small → loses context and multiplies rows, calls and cost.
  • Unofficial heuristic: start at hundreds–~1,000 characters with OVERLAP 10–20 and adjust by measuring relevance.
Memorize: OVERLAP = % of CHUNK_SIZE (0–50, default 0) · chunk_order and chunk_offset start at 1 · without ENABLE_CHUNK_SET_ID = 1 there is no chunk_set_id · chunks table 1-N: PK (DocID, ChunkNo) + FK to the document.
Watch out: FIXED chunking can split words (see the official example: “stee|p hills”). The CHUNK_SIZE = 100 in the docs examples is a toy value; in production use larger sizes. Example B of the AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS reference uses c.chunk_text, but the returned column is named chunk (example F and the AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS reference use c.chunk).
Sources: Learn · Design embeddings · Docs · AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS · Docs · REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE · Docs · STRING_SPLIT

Keeping text, model and vector aligned: hash, version and re-embedding

An embedding is a snapshot of the text and the model at the moment it is generated. If the text or the model changes, it becomes stale. Store in the embeddings table what is needed to detect it (see the “End-to-end” tables).

ColumnPurpose
SourceHash binary(32)HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', source text): detects real changes in the embedded text, ignoring changes in other columns
ModelName / ModelVersionDetects vectors generated with a different model or dimensions
Embedding IS NULLPending generation (natural queue for the batch)
EmbeddedAtAuditing and reprocessing order
rowversion on the source tableCheap, but changes with any UPDATE (false positives)
 
SELECT d.DocID
FROM dbo.Document AS d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.DocumentChunk AS c WHERE c.DocID = d.DocID)
   OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.DocumentChunk AS c
              WHERE c.DocID = d.DocID
                AND (c.Embedding IS NULL
                     OR c.ModelName <> N'text-embedding-3-small'
                     OR c.SourceHash <> HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', d.Body)));
-- For those returned: DELETE their chunks → INSERT ... AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS (Embedding = NULL) → embeddings batch
When changing modelsHowWhen
In-placeUPDATE … SET Embedding = NULL and let the batch regenerateSame dimensions; while it runs, vectors are mixed
Blue/green (recommended)New column/table (Embedding_v2) + new EXTERNAL MODEL; populate, switch the queries and drop the old oneDimensions change or mixing is not allowed; allows rollback
  • Never mix vectors from different models or dimensions in one column; the query embedding must come from the same model.
  • ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL … SET (MODEL = …) or changing dimensions does not regenerate what is stored; there is no “upgrade” between embedding models: everything is regenerated.
  • If the text template changes (included columns), the hash changes: re-embed.
Exam: “detect which rows really changed and which vectors were made with another model” → source text hash column + model/version column in the embeddings table, and regenerate only those rows (batch).
Sources: Learn · Generate and maintain embeddings · Learn · Lab 09 (stale embeddings) · Docs · Embeddings (no upgrade between models)

Choosing the maintenance method: the 7 options

They all answer two questions: how do I detect that the text changed, and who regenerates the embedding? Choose based on volume, latency, risk to the OLTP transaction and where generation runs.

CriterionTable triggerChange TrackingCDC
What it detectsINSERT/UPDATE/DELETE immediately (inserted/deleted)Which rows changed (PK + version + operation); no previous valuesEach change with before/after values and LSN
ModeSynchronous, inside the transactionRecorded in the transaction; consumed by polling (micro-batches)Asynchronous: reads the transaction log
LatencyImmediateLow (depends on the polling)Medium (captures every 20 s in Azure SQL DB)
RiskCalling the model inside the trigger lengthens/blocks the transaction; if it fails, the DML is rolled backMinimal overheadMore storage; the log is retained until CDC processes it
ComplexityLowMedium (persist last_sync_version)Medium-high
IdealPoC / low concurrency; better to only enqueueLightweight incremental synchronizationHigh volume, ETL, auditing, you need before/after
PlatformAllAll (incl. Fabric)SQL Server, MI, Azure SQL DB · No in Fabric
CriterionAzure Functions (SQL trigger)Azure Logic AppsCESMicrosoft Foundry
What it isServerless function triggered by changes; uses Change TrackingLow-code workflow; SQL trigger via polling (managed) or CT (built-in Standard)Stream of DML changes to Event Hubs / Fabric Eventstream (CloudEvents)Model catalog, hosting and evaluation; does not detect changes
LatencyNear real time (polling 1 s by default)Higher: recurrence intervalNear real timen/a (another process detects)
On the transactionNone (outside the engine)NoneNone; decouples from the engineNone
CodeC#, Python, JS, Java, PowerShellNo codeCustom consumer (e.g. Function)—
ScalingServerless; target-based scalingDepends on plan/connectorHigh; several consumers of the same stream—
StatusGAGAPreviewGA
Decision rule:
  • PoC, T-SQL only, low concurrency → trigger (that only flags/enqueues; do not call the model inside the transaction in heavy OLTP).
  • Knowing which rows changed, lightweight, in batches → Change Tracking.
  • Before/after values, history, high volume/ETL → CDC.
  • Serverless, own code, independent scaling, near real time → Azure Functions with SQL trigger binding.
  • Low-code, integrate with other services → Logic Apps.
  • Decouple from the engine, several consumers, streaming → CES (Preview).
  • Choose/host/evaluate the model that generates the vectors → Foundry; it does not replace a detection mechanism.
Sources: Learn · Generate and maintain embeddings · Blog · Solutions for keeping embeddings updated · Docs · Change Tracking · Docs · CES

Triggers, Change Tracking and CDC: key configuration SQL Server Azure SQL DB/MI

CREATE TABLE dbo.EmbeddingQueue
(
    QueueID  bigint IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    DocID    int NOT NULL,
    QueuedAt datetime2(0) NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME()
);
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER dbo.trg_Document_Enqueue ON dbo.Document
AFTER INSERT, UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    IF UPDATE(Title) OR UPDATE(Body)        -- only columns that feed the embedding (on INSERT, UPDATE() is TRUE)
        INSERT dbo.EmbeddingQueue (DocID) SELECT DocID FROM inserted;
END;
ALTER DATABASE [<db>] SET CHANGE_TRACKING = ON (CHANGE_RETENTION = 2 DAYS, AUTO_CLEANUP = ON);
ALTER TABLE dbo.Document ENABLE CHANGE_TRACKING WITH (TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED = ON);   -- the table needs a PK

DECLARE @last_sync bigint = 0,                                  -- persist across runs
        @current   bigint = CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION();
IF @last_sync < CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION(OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.Document'))
    THROW 50001, N'Stale version: full re-embedding', 1;

SELECT ct.DocID, ct.SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION                        -- I | U | D
FROM CHANGETABLE(CHANGES dbo.Document, @last_sync) AS ct;
-- process and save @current as the new @last_sync
EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_db;                        -- db_owner; reserves the schema and user "cdc"
EXEC sys.sp_cdc_enable_table
     @source_schema = N'dbo', @source_name = N'Document',
     @role_name = NULL,                           -- no gating role
     @captured_column_list = N'DocID, Title, Body',
     @supports_net_changes = 1;                   -- requires a PK or unique index included in the columns
MechanismKey facts
Change TrackingRequires PK. CHANGE_RETENTION (official example: 2 DAYS), AUTO_CLEANUP, TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED (default OFF). last_sync_version is a nullable bigint (variable or literal, not an expression). Several changes to one row = one row; TRUNCATE TABLE is not tracked. Permissions: SELECT on the PK + VIEW CHANGE TRACKING. Columns: SYS_CHANGE_VERSION, SYS_CHANGE_CREATION_VERSION, SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION, SYS_CHANGE_COLUMNS, SYS_CHANGE_CONTEXT
CDCLog-based. Per table: capture instance (cdc.<schema>_<table>_CT, fn_cdc_get_all_changes_*, fn_cdc_get_net_changes_*), max. 2 per table. __$operation: 1 delete · 2 insert · 3 update (before) · 4 update (after). Default retention: 3 days
CDC in Azure SQL DBIts own scheduler (no SQL Server Agent): capture every 20 s, cleanup every hour. Any vCore tier; DTU ≥ S3. A paused serverless DB does not run CDC
TriggerIt is part of the transaction: if it calls the model, duration and blocking grow with the endpoint's latency/429. Azure SQL already uses RCSI by default
Watch out: Fabric SQL database does not support CDC (it does support Change Tracking). With Change Tracking, retention must cover the maximum interval between synchronizations; otherwise, CHANGE_TRACKING_MIN_VALID_VERSION indicates that you must reinitialize (full re-embedding).
Sources: Learn · Generate and maintain embeddings · Docs · Enable Change Tracking · Docs · CHANGETABLE · Docs · CDC in Azure SQL DB · Docs · CDC in SQL Server/MI

Azure Functions, Logic Apps, CES and Foundry: key configuration

Azure Functions with SQL trigger binding GA

[Function("EmbedDocumentChanges")]
public static void Run(
    [SqlTrigger("[dbo].[Document]", "SqlConnectionString")]
    IReadOnlyList<SqlChange<Document>> changes, FunctionContext context)
{
    foreach (SqlChange<Document> change in changes)
    {
        // change.Operation: Insert | Update | Delete · change.Item: the row
        // → re-chunk + AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS (or REST) and UPDATE the vector column
    }
}
{ "version": "2.0", "extensions": { "Sql": { "MaxBatchSize": 100, "PollingIntervalMs": 1000, "MaxChangesPerWorker": 1000 } } }
  • Uses Change Tracking: it must be enabled on the DB and on the table (with PK). Polling loop: takes up to MaxBatchSize changes, invokes the function and waits PollingIntervalMs. Several changes to one row between iterations are consolidated into one.
  • Outside C#, function.json: "type": "sqlTrigger", tableName, connectionStringSetting; optional LeasesTableName (default Leases_{FunctionId}_{TableId}). Internal state in the az_func schema.
  • Permissions: db_datareader/db_datawriter are not enough → CREATE TABLE, CREATE SCHEMA, SELECT and VIEW CHANGE TRACKING on the table, and permissions on az_func.
  • If the function is stopped for longer than CHANGE_RETENTION, changes are lost. If the function throws an exception, the batch is retried after 60 s and, after 5 consecutive failures, that row is ignored. Scaling: Consumption plans (extension ≥ v3.1.284) and Premium with target-based scaling; on Premium enable Runtime Scale Monitoring.

Azure Logic Apps (SQL Server connector) GA

  • Managed triggers (Consumption and Standard) by polling (Frequency/Interval): When an item is created (V2) requires an IDENTITY column (it uses the last value as a threshold; a reseed/truncate causes rows to be skipped); When an item is modified (V2) requires a ROWVERSION column and fires on INSERT and UPDATE.
  • Built-in triggers (Standard only, e.g. When a row is inserted) require Change Tracking on the table.
  • Authentication: managed identity (Logic Apps only), Entra or connection string; on-premises SQL in Consumption → on-premises data gateway.
  • Limitation: the Insert/Update row actions fail if the table has a SQL trigger; use a stored procedure or native query.

Change Event Streaming (CES) Preview

CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = '<password>';                    -- if it does not exist
CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL ces_cred WITH IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity';
EXEC sys.sp_enable_event_stream;
EXEC sys.sp_create_event_stream_group
     @stream_group_name      = N'embeddings_sg',
     @destination_type       = N'AzureEventHubs',      -- only value in Azure SQL DB and Fabric
     @destination_location   = N'<namespace>.servicebus.windows.net:9093/<eventhub>',
     @destination_credential = ces_cred,
     @max_message_size_kb    = 256,                    -- default
     @partition_key_scheme   = N'None';                -- default (round robin)
EXEC sys.sp_add_object_to_event_stream_group N'embeddings_sg', N'dbo.Document';
  • Publishes each INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE as a CloudEvent (schema, previous and new values; JSON or Avro) by reading the log, without adding work to the transactions; several consumers can read the same stream.
  • @partition_key_scheme: None (default) · StreamGroup · Table · Column. Requirements: DB in full recovery, db_owner or CONTROL DATABASE; with Entra, the Azure Event Hubs Data Sender role for the identity.
  • destination_type: Azure SQL DB and Fabric → AzureEventHubs (Kafka); MI and SQL Server 2025 → AzureEventHubsApacheKafka (recommended) or AzureEventHubsAMQP (deprecated: new groups in Azure SQL DB as of Aug 15, 2026; existing AMQP groups work until April 2027). SQL Server 2025 requires PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON.

Microsoft Foundry

  • Used to select, host and evaluate the models that generate embeddings (catalog, benchmarks, versions, lifecycle). Change detection and writing to the DB are handled by another mechanism in this list.
Discrepancy (resolved): the local.settings.json table in Learn says Sql_Trigger_BatchSize, but the example on the same page, the polling loop and the extension docs on GitHub use Sql_Trigger_MaxBatchSize (correct app setting name); in host.json it is MaxBatchSize. The other two app settings: Sql_Trigger_PollingIntervalMs and Sql_Trigger_MaxChangesPerWorker.

Data pointValue
vector float32 / float16≤ 1,998 / ≤ 3,996 dimensions · 4 / 2 bytes per dimension
Default dimensions1,536 (ada-002, 3-small) · 3,072 (3-large)
OpenAI embeddings input8,192 tokens (ada-002 v1: 2,046) · 2,048 elements per request
AI_GENERATE_CHUNKSOVERLAP 0–50% (default 0) · compat ≥ 170 · CHUNK_TYPE = FIXED only
retry_count (model/query/@retry_count)0–10
sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint@timeout 1–230 s (default 30) · payload 100 MB · URL 8 KB (query 4 KB) · headers 8 KB · concurrency 15% of workers, max. 175
Credential name≤ 128 characters · URL without query string
Functions SQL triggerMaxBatchSize 100 · PollingIntervalMs 1000 · MaxChangesPerWorker 1000
CESMessage 256 KB (default) · port 9093 · partition_key_scheme None by default

  • MODEL_TYPE only EMBEDDINGS; AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS only accepts text.
  • Credential name = base URL more generic than LOCATION, without query string; MI → fixed resourceid https://cognitiveservices.azure.com.
  • Endpoint URL: *.openai.azure.com or *.cognitiveservices.azure.com (not *.services.ai.azure.com).
  • 3-large (3,072) does not fit in vector float32: dimensions ≤ 1,998 or float16. float32 ↔ float16 cannot be converted.
  • DROP EXTERNAL MODEL does not drop the credential; ALTER … SET (MODEL …) does not regenerate vectors.
  • Permission to use the model: EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL; to create: CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL/ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL. Learn adds EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT (needed only to call sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint).
  • Synchronous trigger with a model call = risk; CT/CDC/Functions/Logic Apps/CES are asynchronous. CES is Preview and CDC does not exist in Fabric SQL DB.
  • Embeddings and model change together: text hash + model name; do not mix models or dimensions.

Module 10Domain 3 · 25–30%

Design and implement intelligent search with SQL

Choose and combine full-text, vector search (ENN with VECTOR_DISTANCE; ANN with CREATE VECTOR INDEX + VECTOR_SEARCH) and hybrid with RRF. It is the module that changes the most: here the Learn module (units from Jul 2026) is contrasted with the current documentation (Oct 2026) and GA is separated from Preview.

Skills measured covered:
  • Choose from full-text, semantic vector, and hybrid search
  • Implement full-text search
  • Design for vector data, including vector data type, vector indexes, and size
  • Identify when to use vector-related types and functions for semantic searching, including VECTOR_NORMALIZE, VECTOR_DISTANCE, VECTORPROPERTY, and VECTOR_SEARCH
  • Choose between using ANN and ENN for vector search
  • Evaluate vector index types and metrics
  • Implement vector search
  • Implement hybrid search
  • Implement reciprocal rank fusion (RRF)
  • Evaluate performance of vector and hybrid search

Choosing: full-text vs vector (semantic) vs hybrid

Three ways to search text in SQL Server / Azure SQL. The choice depends on how the user searches (exact terms vs a description of a need) and on the precision / recall / latency trade-off.

CriterionFull-textVector (semantic)Hybrid
What it comparesWords and phrases (word breaker, stemmer, stoplist)Embeddings: distance between vectorsThe two ordered lists + fusion (RRF)
Ideal forSKU / “Model XR-500”, error messages, proper names, exact technical termsNatural language (“something to keep drinks cold on a hike”), synonyms, paraphrases; multilingual if the model isCannot predict how the user searches (“XR-500 portable cooler”); RAG
SynonymsNot by default (“MTB” ≠ “mountain bike”) except with a thesaurus; yes for inflections (ride/rode)Yes, by meaningYes
Precision / recallHigh precision, fewer resultsMore recall (discovery); may return items without the key termBetter recall, usually with little loss of precision
RequirementsFull-text index (unique 1-column key)vector column with embeddings from the same model as the queryBoth
T-SQLCONTAINS · FREETEXT · CONTAINSTABLE · FREETEXTTABLEVECTOR_DISTANCE (ENN) · VECTOR_SEARCH (ANN)CTEs + FULL OUTER JOIN + RRF formula
OrderRANK 0–1000 (higher = better)distance (lower = closer)RRF score (higher = better)
LatencyInverted index: very fastENN scans everything; ANN requires a vector indexSum of both branches + fusion (slower than either one)
Decision rule:
  • Code, SKU, literal phrase, technical term → full-text (CONTAINS).
  • The user describes what they need, synonyms, paraphrases → vector.
  • Both patterns, or maximize recall (RAG) → hybrid, fused with RRF.
  • “Combine rankings from different sources without normalizing scores” → RRF.
  • Forms of a word (ride → riding / rode) → full-text (FORMSOF(INFLECTIONAL) or FREETEXT); no vector needed.
Do not confuse: full-text “Semantic Search” (STATISTICAL_SEMANTICS, SEMANTICKEYPHRASETABLE, SEMANTICSIMILARITYTABLE: key phrases and document similarity) is a different feature, documented only for SQL Server. The “semantic” search in this module is vector search.
Sources: Learn · Choose an intelligent search approach · Docs · Full-Text Search · Docs · Vector search and vector indexes

Full-text: catalog, index and population SQL Server Azure SQL DB / MI GA Fabric SQL DB Preview

Full-text = inverted index (token → rows) built with the word breaker and stemmer of each column's language. Steps: (1) catalog, (2) unique single-column index that acts as the key, (3) CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX.

CREATE FULLTEXT CATALOG ftCatalog AS DEFAULT;       -- virtual object: no filegroup

CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products
(
    Name        LANGUAGE 1033,                      -- LCID 1033 = English (en-US)
    Description LANGUAGE 1033
)
KEY INDEX PK_Products                               -- unique, 1 column, NOT NULL (int is best)
ON ftCatalog
WITH (CHANGE_TRACKING = AUTO, STOPLIST = SYSTEM);   -- both are the default values
OptionValuesDefault / notes
KEY INDEXUnique index, a single column, NOT NULLRequired; an integer type is recommended. It is the [KEY] column returned by the *TABLE functions
ON catalogname · (name, FILEGROUP fg)Optional → DEFAULT catalog; if none exists → error. In CREATE FULLTEXT CATALOG, ON FILEGROUP and IN PATH have no effect (virtual catalog)
LANGUAGEAlias from sys.syslanguages, integer LCID or 0x…; 0x0 = neutralDefault: the instance's default full-text language. It is also the default language in queries
CHANGE_TRACKINGAUTO · MANUAL · OFF [, NO POPULATION]Default AUTO (propagates, though not immediately). MANUAL → ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX … START UPDATE POPULATION. WRITETEXT/UPDATETEXT are not detected
STOPLISTOFF · SYSTEM · nameDefault: system stoplist
TYPE COLUMN, STATISTICAL_SEMANTICS, SEARCH PROPERTY LISTDocument extension (.doc, .pdf; only varbinary(max) / image) · Semantic Search · document propertiesSTATISTICAL_SEMANTICS and SEARCH PROPERTY LIST are documented only for SQL Server
 
ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products ENABLE;                         -- ENABLE | DISABLE
ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products SET CHANGE_TRACKING MANUAL;     -- MANUAL | AUTO | OFF
ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products START UPDATE POPULATION;        -- FULL | INCREMENTAL | UPDATE
ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products ADD (Notes LANGUAGE 1033) WITH NO POPULATION;  -- error if CHANGE_TRACKING = AUTO/MANUAL
ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX ON dbo.Products SET STOPLIST = myStoplist;      -- OFF | SYSTEM | name

CREATE FULLTEXT STOPLIST myStoplist FROM SYSTEM STOPLIST;
ALTER FULLTEXT STOPLIST myStoplist ADD N'bike' LANGUAGE 1033;        -- custom stopword

ALTER FULLTEXT CATALOG ftCatalog REORGANIZE;                         -- merges intermediate indexes
ALTER FULLTEXT CATALOG ftCatalog REBUILD;                            -- rebuilds all its indexes
  • Only one full-text index per table / indexed view; up to 1024 columns. Types: char, varchar, nchar, nvarchar, text, ntext, image, xml, varbinary(max).
  • CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX cannot run inside a user transaction.
  • CHANGE_TRACKING + WITH NO POPULATION: with AUTO/MANUAL it is an error; with OFF it is not populated until ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX … START … POPULATION; without NO POPULATION a full population is performed.
  • Catalog: name ≤ 120 characters; not in master/model/tempdb; ACCENT_SENSITIVITY = ON | OFF (default: that of the DB collation; changing it requires a rebuild).
  • INCREMENTAL only works if the table has a timestamp column; otherwise, it performs a full population.
  • Check population: sys.dm_fts_index_keywords_by_document(DB_ID(), OBJECT_ID('dbo.Products')).
  • Status (used by the module lab): OBJECTPROPERTY(OBJECT_ID('dbo.Products'), 'TableFulltextPopulateStatus') → 0 = inactive, 1 = full population in progress, 2 = incremental, 3 = propagating changes, 4 = background update (auto change tracking), 5 = throttled or paused; 'TableHasActiveFulltextIndex' → 1 = an active full-text index exists.
Permissions: CREATE FULLTEXT CATALOG (or db_owner / db_ddladmin). CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX: REFERENCES on the catalog + ALTER on the table (or sysadmin / db_owner / db_ddladmin); if it uses STOPLIST, REFERENCES on the stoplist.
Exam: the full-text index key must be a unique index on one non-null column; CHANGE_TRACKING is AUTO by default; LIKE only matches character patterns, full-text is linguistic (stemming, thesaurus, stopwords).
SQL Server 2025 — version 2 full-text indexes: word breakers, stemmers and filters were rewritten (new languages: Finnish 1035, Hungarian 1038, Estonian 1061; different tokenization, e.g. cat_dog → cat_dog, cat, dog). After an in-place upgrade the indexes remain at index_version = 1 (sys.fulltext_indexes) and their queries/populations fail (v1 binaries removed) → ALTER FULLTEXT CATALOG … REBUILD or recreate. FULLTEXT_INDEX_VERSION (1 | 2, default 2) in ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION sets the version when creating/rebuilding. Azure SQL DB/MI: v1 still supported, phased retirement. The thesaurus (FORMSOF(THESAURUS), XML files) is documented only for SQL Server; Azure SQL DB and SQL database in Fabric do not support third-party filters or word breakers.
Sources: Learn · Implement full-text search · Docs · CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX · Docs · ALTER FULLTEXT INDEX · Docs · CREATE FULLTEXT CATALOG · Docs · Full-text index version upgrade · Docs · Fabric SQL database limitations

Full-text queries: CONTAINS, FREETEXT and the *TABLE functions SQL Server Azure SQL DB / MI GA

Predicates in WHERE (they only filter) and table functions in FROM (they return [KEY] and [RANK]; they are joined to the base table on the full-text index key).

FormWhereReturnsWhat it supports
CONTAINSWHERERows (no rank)Terms, phrases, prefix, FORMSOF, NEAR, ISABOUT, AND/OR/AND NOT
FREETEXTWHERERows (no rank)Free text only: word-break + stemming + thesaurus; no operators, wildcards, FORMSOF, NEAR or WEIGHT; “and” is a stopword. Less precise than CONTAINS
CONTAINSTABLEFROM[KEY], [RANK]Same as CONTAINS
FREETEXTTABLEFROM[KEY], [RANK] (BM25)Same as FREETEXT
 
CONTAINS  ( { col | ( col1, col2 ) | * | PROPERTY ( col, 'prop' ) }, N'<contains_search_condition>' [ , LANGUAGE lang ] )
FREETEXT  ( { col | ( col1, col2 ) | * }, N'free text'                                    [ , LANGUAGE lang ] )

CONTAINSTABLE ( table, { col | ( col1, col2 ) | * }, N'<contains_search_condition>' [ , LANGUAGE lang ] [ , top_n_by_rank ] )
FREETEXTTABLE ( table, { col | ( col1, col2 ) | * }, N'free text'                  [ , LANGUAGE lang ] [ , top_n_by_rank ] )
CONTAINS conditionSyntaxNotes
Term / phrase'aluminum' · '"mountain bike"'Phrase in double quotes, same words and order; case-insensitive; punctuation is ignored
Prefix'"light*"'* inside the double quotes. Without quotes ('light*'), the * is a literal character
Generation'FORMSOF(INFLECTIONAL, ride)' · 'FORMSOF(THESAURUS, metal)'INFLECTIONAL: the language's stemmer (ride / rides / riding / rode); THESAURUS: synonyms from the thesaurus file
Proximity (custom)'NEAR((bike, control), 10, TRUE)'NEAR((t1, t2 [, …]) [, max_distance [, match_order]]). max_distance: integer 0–4294967295 or MAX (default); match_order: TRUE = respects the order, FALSE (default). 2–64 terms
Proximity (generic)'a NEAR b' · 'a ~ b'Marked as deprecated (“will be removed in a future version”): use the custom one
Weighted'ISABOUT(frame WEIGHT(.8), wheel WEIGHT(.4))'WEIGHT 0.0–1.0 (always a decimal point). Affects the RANK of CONTAINSTABLE, not the rows of CONTAINS
BooleansAND / & · OR / | · AND NOT / &!NOT only after AND (neither OR NOT nor a leading NOT). Precedence: NOT, then AND, then OR; parentheses are evaluated first
 
-- CONTAINS: exact word + regular relational filter
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
WHERE CONTAINS(Name, N'mountain')
  AND ListPrice < 500;

-- Prefixes with OR; inflections; ordered proximity (≤ 10 words)
SELECT Name FROM Production.Product WHERE CONTAINS(Name, N'"chain*" OR "full*"');
SELECT Description FROM Production.ProductDescription
WHERE CONTAINS(Description, N'FORMSOF (INFLECTIONAL, ride)');
SELECT Comments FROM Production.ProductReview
WHERE CONTAINS(Comments, N'NEAR((bike,control), 10, TRUE)');

-- FREETEXT: free text; finds ride / rides / biking…
SELECT ProductID, Name
FROM Production.Product
WHERE FREETEXT(Name, N'riding bikes');
-- CONTAINSTABLE with weights; highest rank first
SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name, k.[RANK]
FROM Production.Product AS p
INNER JOIN CONTAINSTABLE(Production.Product, Name,
           N'ISABOUT (frame WEIGHT (.8), wheel WEIGHT (.4), tire WEIGHT (.2))') AS k
        ON p.ProductID = k.[KEY]
ORDER BY k.[RANK] DESC;

-- FREETEXTTABLE (BM25) with language and only the top 5 rows
SELECT d.ProductDescriptionID, d.Description, k.[RANK]
FROM Production.ProductDescription AS d
INNER JOIN FREETEXTTABLE(Production.ProductDescription, Description,
           N'high level of performance', LANGUAGE N'English', 5) AS k
        ON d.ProductDescriptionID = k.[KEY]
ORDER BY k.[RANK] DESC;
Memorize: [KEY] = value of the full-text index's unique key; [RANK] = 0–1000 (higher = more relevant); CONTAINS/FREETEXT do not return rank. Prefix = '"text*"'. *TABLE argument order: table, columns, condition, LANGUAGE, top_n_by_rank.
Exam: inflections (run → running) are found by both CONTAINS … FORMSOF(INFLECTIONAL, …) and FREETEXT. CONTAINS gives full control (phrases, prefix, NEAR, weights, Booleans); FREETEXT is simpler and less precise. Need rank? → CONTAINSTABLE / FREETEXTTABLE. Synonyms/abbreviations (MTB) only with a thesaurus; “ideas” without the words → vector.
Common mistakes:
  • The search condition is nvarchar; it does not support varchar(max) or nvarchar(max). With varchar there is an implicit conversion and no parameter sniffing: declare nvarchar(n).
  • A query made up only of stopwords returns an error. In FREETEXT, “and” is discarded; in CONTAINS, AND is an operator.
  • Predicates work on one table (for several, use JOIN / a derived table). With column_list or *, all columns must have the same language, unless you specify LANGUAGE.
  • top_n_by_rank combined with other filters can return fewer rows than actually satisfy all the filters.
  • CONTAINSTABLE with unsanitized user text can fail with a syntax error; FREETEXTTABLE accepts free text (which is why it is the usual choice in hybrid).
Sources: Learn · Implement full-text search · Docs · CONTAINS · Docs · CONTAINSTABLE · Docs · FREETEXT · Docs · FREETEXTTABLE

Full-text RANK: how it is calculated and why it matters in hybrid SQL Server Azure SQL DB / MI GA

The RANK from CONTAINSTABLE / FREETEXTTABLE is the “keyword” signal that is then fused with the vector ranking.

AspectValueNotes
RangeInteger 0–1000 (MaxQueryRank = 1000)Only relative order within the same query; neither comparable across queries nor stable over time
FREETEXTTABLEOkapi BM25Constants k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75, k3 = 8.0. Inflectional forms and thesaurus synonyms count as independent terms of equal weight
CONTAINSTABLE (term)Rank = min(1000, HitCount × 16 × StatisticalWeight / MaxOccurrence)StatisticalWeight = Log2((2 + IndexedRowCount) / KeyRowCount). Not BM25
ISABOUTWeighted JaccardDefault weight of each term: 1
NEARMore hits (relative to document length) and shorter distance → higher rankWithout an integer max_distance, hits more than 100 terms apart → rank 0
top_n_by_rankOnly the n highest-ranked rows, in descending orderFaster than fetching everything and sorting
Exam: “which algorithm ranks FREETEXTTABLE?” → BM25. CONTAINSTABLE uses a different formula (statistical; Jaccard for ISABOUT). In hybrid, the full-text rank is sorted DESC and the vector distance ASC.
Discrepancy with Learn: unit 6 says that FREETEXTTABLE or CONTAINSTABLE return a BM25 rank. According to the RANK docs, only FREETEXTTABLE uses BM25.
Maintenance: the rank uses statistics from the largest intermediate index, so it varies until they are merged; after large populations run ALTER FULLTEXT CATALOG … REORGANIZE. Since it is an integer 0–1000, ties are frequent: in RRF use RANK() (tie = same rank) or define your own tie-breaker.
Sources: Docs · Limit search results with RANK · Learn · Implement hybrid search and ranking

GA vs Preview: availability matrix (do not mix them up) SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric

Status according to the Oct 2026 documentation. AUP = Azure SQL Managed Instance with the Always-up-to-date update policy; SS2025 policy = MI with the SQL Server 2025 update policy.

FeatureSQL Server 2025Azure SQL DBSQL database in FabricAzure SQL MI
Full-text searchGA (v2 indexes)GAPreviewGA
vector type + functionsGAGAGAGA (AUP and SS2025 policy)
vector(n, float16)Preview (PREVIEW_FEATURES)GAGAGA
CREATE VECTOR INDEX + VECTOR_SEARCHPreview (PREVIEW_FEATURES)GAGAAUP GA · SS2025 policy Preview
Index version 3No (previous version)YesYesAUP yes · SS2025 policy no
ALLOW_STALE_VECTOR_INDEXNot availableYes (previous indexes)Yes (previous indexes)Not documented
AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGSGAGAGAAUP

“Index version 3” = full DML, iterative filtering, optimizer-driven and TOP (N) WITH APPROXIMATE (details in the CREATE VECTOR INDEX topic).

ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON;

SELECT [name], [value]
FROM sys.database_scoped_configurations
WHERE [name] = 'PREVIEW_FEATURES';
Exam: SQL Server 2025 scenario + CREATE VECTOR INDEX / VECTOR_SEARCH / float16 → you must enable PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON (not recommended in production). Not needed in Azure SQL Database and SQL database in Fabric. The vector type and VECTOR_DISTANCE / VECTOR_NORM / VECTOR_NORMALIZE / VECTORPROPERTY are GA on all four platforms.
Learn vs docs: the module units (Jul 2026) describe the previous version of the index: read-only table, TOP_N, clustered int PK, “preview”. The current docs mark it GA in Azure SQL DB / Fabric / MI AUP with the v3 index (GA announced Sep 29, 2026, after the module). In SQL Server 2025 it is still in Preview and, according to the docs, with the previous version of the index (verify on your build / CU). The module lab (Lab 10, Azure SQL DB) runs PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON and ALLOW_STALE_VECTOR_INDEX = ON; according to the current docs, PREVIEW_FEATURES is not needed in Azure SQL DB / Fabric and ALLOW_STALE_VECTOR_INDEX only affects indexes of the previous version.

vector type: dimensions, base type and size SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric GA

Array of numbers in an optimized binary format, exposed as a JSON array. It is declared with the no. of dimensions of the embedding model.

column_name VECTOR ( <dimensions> [ , <base_type> ] ) [ NOT NULL | NULL ]   -- base_type: float32 (default) | float16

CREATE TABLE dbo.Products
(
    ProductID         int           NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    Name              nvarchar(100) NOT NULL,
    Description       nvarchar(max) NULL,
    DescriptionVector vector(1536)  NULL          -- float32: 4 bytes per dimension
);
Base typeBytes / dimensionMax. dimensionsStatus
float32 (default)41,998GA
float16 (half-precision)23,996GA in Azure SQL DB / MI / Fabric; Preview in SQL Server 2025
Size per vectorCalculation (8 B header + dim × bytes)Result
vector(1024)8 + 1,024 × 44,104 B (example from the docs: 1 vector per 8,060 B page)
vector(1536)8 + 1,536 × 46,152 B (≈ 6 KB)
vector(1998)8 + 1,998 × 48,000 B (float32 maximum)
vector(1536, float16)8 + 1,536 × 23,080 B
vector(3996, float16)8 + 3,996 × 28,000 B (float16 maximum)
  • text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-ada-002: 1,536 dimensions.
  • text-embedding-3-large: 3,072 by default (exceeds 1,998) → request fewer dimensions with the model's dimensions parameter (e.g. 1,024 ≈ 4 KB) or use float16. More dimensions = more storage, memory and CPU per distance, with marginal benefit.
  • Embeddings and query must come from the same model (same dimensions and space).
  • The vector type is available at any DB compatibility level. It has lower precedence than string types: in UNION, CASE or COALESCE with a string, the result is the string.
Conversion / literalDetailsError
Literal'[0.1, 2, 30]' · JSON_ARRAY(1.0, 2.0, 3.0) · CAST('[1,2,3]' AS VECTOR(3))No. of elements ≠ dimensions → 42204; not a JSON array of numbers → 13670
vector ⇄ text / jsonImplicit or explicit with char, nchar, varchar, nvarchar, json; not allowed with any other type (not even sql_variant)Target too short → 42211 (does not truncate)
vector → string / jsonString: scientific notation (1.0000000e+000); json: decimal—
float32 ⇄ float16Neither implicit nor CAST/CONVERT42238. In VECTOR_DISTANCE with different base types: “does not support different base types”
 
SELECT name, vector_dimensions, vector_base_type, vector_base_type_desc   -- 0 = float32, 1 = float16
FROM sys.columns
WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('dbo.Products');
Type limitations:
  • Only NULL / NOT NULL constraints: no DEFAULT, CHECK, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY or UNIQUE. There are no comparison, arithmetic or concatenation operators.
  • Not in memory-optimized tables; no B-tree or columnstore indexes on the column (yes as an INCLUDE column); no CREATE TYPE alias; no Always Encrypted; dense vectors only (sparse not supported).
  • sp_describe_first_result_set shows it as varchar/nvarchar; clients without the new TDS receive JSON as varchar(max) (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient ≥ 6.1.0 exposes SqlVector<float>).
  • float16: out-of-range values (> 65,504) → error; not supported on ARM64.
Memorize: 1,998 (float32) · 3,996 (float16) · 4 B vs 2 B per dimension · header 8 B · page 8,060 B · errors 42204 / 13670 / 42211 / 42238.
Sources: Learn · Prepare SQL for vector search · Docs · Vector data type · Docs · Half-precision float · Docs · Vector FAQ · Azure SQL blog · Embedding models and dimensions

Vector functions: VECTOR_DISTANCE, VECTOR_NORM, VECTOR_NORMALIZE, VECTORPROPERTY SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric GA

FunctionSignatureReturns / notes
VECTOR_DISTANCEVECTOR_DISTANCE ( distance_metric , vector1 , vector2 )Scalar float. Always exact: does not use a vector index even if one exists. Error if the metric is not valid or the arguments are not vector
VECTOR_NORMVECTOR_NORM ( vector , norm_type )float: length/magnitude according to the norm
VECTOR_NORMALIZEVECTOR_NORMALIZE ( vector , norm_type )vector with the same direction and length 1 in that norm; NULL input → NULL
VECTORPROPERTYVECTORPROPERTY ( vector , property )'Dimensions' → int; 'BaseType' → sysname
VECTOR_SEARCHTABLE, COLUMN, SIMILAR_TO, METRIC (+ legacy TOP_N)Table function (ANN): table columns + distance. See the VECTOR_SEARCH topic
AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGSAI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS ( source USE MODEL model_identifier [ PARAMETERS json ] )Generates the embedding (JSON array → assignable to vector). Requires an EXTERNAL MODEL of type EMBEDDINGS; external rest endpoint enabled is enabled by default in Azure SQL DB / Fabric
'cosine''euclidean''dot''norm1''norm2''norminf''Dimensions''BaseType'
norm_typeDefinitionExample with [1, 2, 3]
norm1Sum of absolute values6.0
norm2Euclidean norm: square root of the sum of squares (the most common)3.7416573867739413
norminfMaximum absolute value3.0
 
DECLARE @v vector(3) = '[3, 4, 0]';

SELECT VECTOR_NORM(@v, 'norm2')         AS magnitude,  -- 5
       VECTOR_NORMALIZE(@v, 'norm2')    AS unit_vector, -- [0.6, 0.8, 0]
       VECTORPROPERTY(@v, 'Dimensions') AS dims,       -- 3
       VECTORPROPERTY(@v, 'BaseType')   AS base_type;

-- The metric goes FIRST; with [1,1] and [-1,-1] the cosine is 2 (opposite vectors)
DECLARE @a vector(2) = '[1, 1]', @b vector(2) = '[-1, -1]';
SELECT VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', @a, @b) AS cos_dist;
ScenarioFunction
Fewer than ~50,000 vectors, or the WHERE leaves few candidates; exact resultVECTOR_DISTANCE
Hundreds of thousands / millions of vectors with a vector index; speed > perfect accuracyVECTOR_SEARCH
The model does not return normalized vectors (Azure OpenAI does return them normalized); Learn frames it as “varied embedding sources / models”VECTOR_NORMALIZE(v, 'norm2') before storing / comparing
Debug dimension or base type errorsVECTORPROPERTY (+ sys.columns)
Exam: VECTOR_DISTANCE = exact (ENN) and does not use an index; only VECTOR_SEARCH uses a vector index (ANN). Normalizing does not make vectors from different models comparable: use the same model for data and query.
Learn vs docs: unit 5 says that BaseType is “always float”, but float16 now exists; confirm the base type with sys.columns.vector_base_type_desc. The VECTORPROPERTY docs only document “float (32-bit)” as the default.
Sources: Learn · Implement vector search query patterns · Docs · VECTOR_DISTANCE · Docs · VECTOR_NORMALIZE · Docs · VECTOR_NORM · Docs · VECTORPROPERTY · Docs · AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS

Distance metrics: which one to choose SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric GA

MetricMeasuresReturn valueChoose it when
cosineAngle between vectors; ignores magnitude[0, 2]: 0 identical, 2 oppositeCommon option with text embeddings: most models are optimized for cosine
euclideanStraight-line distance (direction + magnitude)[0, +∞): 0 identicalMagnitude carries information, or the model was trained with Euclidean distance
dotNegative dot product(−∞, +∞): more negative = more similarNormalized embeddings or a model trained with inner product
  • Use the metric the embedding model was trained with (see its documentation); if you do not know it, cosine.
  • The same metric in CREATE VECTOR INDEX … METRIC and in VECTOR_SEARCH … METRIC (and the same column). If it does not match, the index is not used: warning + exact kNN. Check sys.vector_indexes.distance_metric.
  • With vectors of length 1 (Azure OpenAI returns them normalized; VECTOR_NORMALIZE(v, 'norm2') for the rest) cosine, dot and euclidean produce the same ordering (a mathematical property).
  • Always ORDER BY distance ascending: lower = more similar, also with dot (it returns the negative). Cosine similarity = 1 − distance.
  • Thresholds (< 0.3) are examples: calibrate with test queries until you see where the relevant results end.
Exam: cosine range = 0 to 2 (not −1..1 or 0..1). dot returns the negative dot product so that “lower = more similar” holds for all three metrics. Supported index type: only DiskANN (sys.vector_indexes.vector_index_type).
Sources: Learn · Prepare SQL for vector search · Docs · VECTOR_DISTANCE (distance metrics) · Docs · sys.vector_indexes

ENN (exact): VECTOR_DISTANCE + ORDER BY SQL Server 2025 Azure SQL Fabric GA

Exact kNN: computes the distance to each candidate row, sorts and takes the best k. Recall 100%. Does not need (or use) a vector index.

DECLARE @qv vector(1536);
SELECT @qv = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(N'lightweight hiking boots' USE MODEL MyEmbeddingModel);

SELECT TOP (10)
       p.ProductID,
       p.Name,
       VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', @qv, p.DescriptionVector) AS distance
FROM dbo.Products AS p
WHERE p.CategoryID = 5                 -- the filter reduces the candidates (and the cost)
ORDER BY distance;                     -- ASC: smaller distance = more similar
SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name,
       VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', @qv, p.DescriptionVector) AS distance
FROM dbo.Products AS p
WHERE VECTOR_DISTANCE('cosine', @qv, p.DescriptionVector) < 0.3   -- example threshold: calibrate it
ORDER BY distance;
  • Linear cost with the no. of candidate rows. Recommended with fewer than ~50,000 vectors; the table can be larger if the predicates reduce the candidates to 50,000 or fewer.
  • Generate the query embedding once (variable) and with the same model as the data; AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS is a REST call to the model.
  • Use the “top-k” pattern (TOP (k) + ORDER BY distance) or the threshold one (WHERE … < x) when you want “everything above a minimum quality”.
Memorize: ENN = VECTOR_DISTANCE(metric, v1, v2) + ascending ORDER BY. Equivalent to exact kNN, which is also obtained with VECTOR_SEARCH + TOP (N) without WITH APPROXIMATE.
Sources: Learn · Implement vector search query patterns · Docs · VECTOR_DISTANCE · Docs · Vector search and vector indexes

CREATE VECTOR INDEX (DiskANN) Azure SQL DB Fabric GA SQL Server 2025 Preview

Approximate index on a vector column for ANN. Based on DiskANN: a graph to navigate to the nearest neighbors using SSD and little memory. Only VECTOR_SEARCH uses it (never VECTOR_DISTANCE).

CREATE VECTOR INDEX index_name
ON object ( vector_column )
[ WITH (
    [ , ] METRIC = { 'cosine' | 'dot' | 'euclidean' }
    [ [ , ] TYPE = 'DiskANN' ]
    [ [ , ] MAXDOP = max_degree_of_parallelism ]
) ]
[ ON { filegroup_name | "default" } ]
[;]

CREATE VECTOR INDEX vec_idx
ON dbo.Products (DescriptionVector)
WITH (METRIC = 'cosine', TYPE = 'DiskANN');   -- METRIC must match the one in VECTOR_SEARCH
OptionValuesDefault / notes
METRIC'cosine' · 'dot' (negative dot product) · 'euclidean'No documented default (in the syntax it appears without brackets inside WITH): always specify it; all the official examples do
TYPE'DiskANN' (case-insensitive)Only supported value and default
MAXDOP0 · 1 · > 1Default 0 (uses the server / DB / workload group config). Limits parallelism and consumption during the build
ON filegroupName or "default"Places the index
AspectPrevious version (2025 preview)Latest version (v3)
DML on the tableRead-only; with ALLOW_STALE_VECTOR_INDEX = ON (Azure SQL DB / Fabric only) writes are allowed but the index becomes stale until DROP + CREATEINSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE with asynchronous background maintenance
FiltersPost-filteringIterative filtering (during the search)
Query syntaxTOP_N = k in VECTOR_SEARCHTOP (N) WITH APPROXIMATE; TOP_N → Msg 42274
PlanUses the index if it matchesThe optimizer chooses DiskANN or kNN based on cost
OtherClustered PK on an int columnAdvanced quantization, transparent (docs: better storage efficiency and faster queries; Mar 2026 blog: faster build at the cost of slightly larger files); minimum 100 rows
WhereSQL Server 2025 and MI with the SQL Server 2025 update policy (Preview)Azure SQL DB, Fabric, Always-up-to-date MI (GA)
  • Base table (not views or temporary tables); column of type vector; ALTER permission on the table. Unique name within the table.
  • Minimum 100 rows with a non-NULL vector (v3); with fewer → Msg 42266. Without an index, VECTOR_SEARCH still works by brute force (kNN).
  • Cannot be partitioned; not replicated to subscribers; TRUNCATE TABLE not allowed (DROP INDEX → TRUNCATE → reload ≥ 100 rows → CREATE); not deployed with DACPAC (BACPAC yes, DacFx ≥ 170.5.96).
  • Deduplicate embeddings before indexing; after an almost complete replacement (e.g. re-embedding with another model) do DROP + CREATE. For the WHERE predicates, also create regular B-tree indexes.
  • Cannot be upgraded “in place”: migrating to v3 = DROP INDEX vec_idx ON dbo.Products; + CREATE VECTOR INDEX (first, update the queries that use TOP_N).
SELECT i.name, vi.vector_index_type, vi.distance_metric,
       JSON_VALUE(vi.build_parameters, '$.Version') AS index_version   -- 3 = latest version
FROM sys.vector_indexes AS vi
INNER JOIN sys.indexes AS i
        ON i.object_id = vi.object_id AND i.index_id = vi.index_id;

SELECT OBJECT_NAME(object_id) AS table_name, index_id,
       graph_catchup_pending_percent,            -- changes waiting to be added to the graph
       last_background_task_succeeded, last_background_task_error_message
FROM sys.dm_db_vector_indexes;                   -- requires VIEW DATABASE STATE
Exam: “the table becomes read-only when the index is created” and “clustered int PK” are limitations of the previous version; it cannot be partitioned in any version. If the question mentions Azure SQL Database / Fabric, assume v3 (full DML).
SQL Server 2025 (Preview): requires PREVIEW_FEATURES = ON. Known issues: the MAXDOP value is ignored in CREATE VECTOR INDEX and VECTOR_SEARCH (it uses the server's max degree of parallelism or the DB's MAXDOP); the warning “The join order has been enforced because a local join hint is used” appears (it can be ignored). A Mar 2026 blog showed the approximate_staleness_percent column; the current DMV docs use graph_catchup_pending_percent.
Verify: the current docs (Oct 2026) document defaults for TYPE (DiskANN) and MAXDOP (0), but not for METRIC (syntax without brackets inside WITH). Do not assume 'cosine': always specify it, and the same one you will use in VECTOR_SEARCH. The Learn units and the lab also always specify it.
Memorize: METRIC / TYPE / MAXDOP options · DiskANN is the only type · 100 rows minimum (Msg 42266) · ALTER on the table · removed with DROP INDEX · catalog sys.vector_indexes · DMV sys.dm_db_vector_indexes.
